title: I Started Blowing Rainbow Farts at My Rival
author: Gu Sanyue
synopsis:
Jiang Qing was a natural-born actor, a child star by trade. But his tongue was far too sharp for his own good, and he managed to offend half the entertainment industry. In the end, he came crashing down spectacularly because of his rival, Lin Xun, toppling straight off his pedestal.
What he didn't expect was that the fall sent him tumbling back three years into the past, and with a bizarre new condition to boot: he stutters whenever he lies.
Since Heaven had seen fit to give him a second chance, he swore he would keep his head down and behave himself.
So his fans were baffled to discover that their beloved idol had not only lost his sharp tongue, he had also developed a stutter, and was now openly gushing about his rival.
Host: "What do you think of Lin Xun, your upcoming co-star?"
Jiang Qing: "He's g-gorgeous, k-kind, and t-talented, his acting is ab-ab-absolutely explosive, I'm his his his his biggest fan."
That day's trending search: #Jiang Qing riding the clout train, hands off our Xun Xun#
Meanwhile, the other party in question was watching the interview clip at home with a furrowed brow: "Who is this guy? I want his full profile in two minutes."
A few years later, when asked the same question again, Jiang Qing answered without a single stutter: "Pfft, you mean that guy with the pretty face and the garbage acting, the garbage talent? The one I could have kneeling in front of me and calling me daddy in ten seconds flat?"
Top trending: #Qingqing's counterattack fails again today! Xun has him locked down!#
Lin Xun saw the post, liked it with deep satisfaction, and went to throw out the kneeling board he kept at home.

chapters.title: I've Been Reborn
chapters.content:
"Jiang Qing."

"Jiang Qing! Jiang Qing!!"

Several urgent, anxious voices rang out beside his ear. Jiang Qing furrowed his brow, swiped his right hand blindly through the air, then snapped his eyes open and gasped, staring around him in alarm.

A hand waved in front of his face. His unfocused eyes locked onto it, and he turned his head to find the hand's owner: his manager, Shu Tong.

"Tong-jie?"

Shu Tong was beside herself with worry. "How do you feel?"

He didn't answer. He looked around. He was lying on a sofa chair. Besides Shu Tong, a number of strangers had gathered around him, chattering nonstop, studying him with panicked expressions.

He mumbled, "I... where is this?"

"Backstage." Shu Tong pressed a hand to his forehead. "You were in the middle of an interview and suddenly fainted. Yiyi went to call an ambulance."

"An interview?!"

He was stunned. Just a moment ago he had gone over a cliff, car and all... what was going on?

A young, stylish woman nearby chimed in, "That's right, the interview was cut short halfway. You gave me quite a scare. I thought I'd asked something absolutely devastating."

Jiang Qing studied her carefully. She looked familiar: a well-known host from some television station, though they'd only worked together once. If he remembered correctly, that collaboration had been three years ago...

Wait. Three years ago?!

He shot upright, looked around in disbelief, rushed to the dressing table nearby, and stared hard at his own face.

His figure was the same, but this face... the skin was fair and smooth, his hair was slightly grown out and tied up in a little knot. His features were refined, his eyes clear and bright; the dark circles were gone, the worn-out look had completely vanished. He looked impossibly young.

Everyone watched his strange behavior. He stared at himself in the mirror and let out a few odd little laughs.

He yanked up his shirt hem, startling several young women into covering their faces before peeking through their fingers.

Jiang Qing looked down at his flat, taut stomach. The faint lines of his abs were just barely visible, and above that... hm? The scar was gone?!

The previous year, while filming an arthouse wuxia project, he'd gotten injured and been left with a fairly prominent scar above his lower abdomen.

But now there wasn't a single mark. What was going on? Had time actually reversed?

After a long moment, he finally found his voice. "What time is it right now?"

Shu Tong answered, "Four-thirty in the afternoon."

"No, I mean what year."

"You don't even know what year it is? Did you hit your head?"

Before she finished speaking, a young woman with a sweet face came running in through the door. It was his assistant, Sang Yi, her expression urgent. "Tong-jie, the ambulance is here... wait, Qing-ge, you're awake?"

Jiang Qing turned around, the corners of his mouth curving up slightly. He nodded. "Yeah, I'm awake."

Shu Tong said worriedly, "We should still go to the hospital for a check-up."

Jiang Qing was fairly certain nothing was seriously wrong with his body, and declined. "It's fine, I just slept for a se— a se-se..."

The word "second" never made it out. Both he and Shu Tong froze at the same time.

Why had that sentence come out so painfully?

Shu Tong's eyes slowly went wide. She looked back and forth between him and Sang Yi, then leaned close to his ear and asked in a voice only the two of them could hear, "Who did you sleep with?"

"A second! One second!" He forced the words out with great difficulty.

Shu Tong glanced at Sang Yi again; she seemed perfectly normal. Somewhat reassured, Shu Tong agreed, reluctantly, to take him to the hospital for an examination.

Jiang Qing couldn't win the argument. On second thought, he figured he might as well get checked out. What if there were side effects?

The host arranged for someone to escort them out. Once they were in the ambulance, Jiang Qing looked at the two women across from him and asked, "What interview was that today?"

Shu Tong's irritation flared at the mention of it. "I think you really did knock yourself stupid. Weren't you just giving a passionate speech on camera? The film you shot with Director Yu last year has come out, and you were invited to sit for an interview with the cast. And what do you do? You go and throw Director Yu right under the bus."

"What?"

Three years ago was hard to remember in detail. But the one thing he could say for certain was that he'd failed, once again, to keep his mouth shut.

Sang Yi, being a woman of few words, simply pulled out her phone, found the clip from the interview, and handed it to him. "Congratulations. Director Yu's fans have officially become anti-fans of yours."

"..."

He hit play and watched carefully.

The host had asked him for his thoughts on the director he frequently collaborated with.

"Director Yu is genuinely talented, but he's gotten a little restless these past few years. His work lacks depth. Though that's not really his fault; the market is what it is. Everyone's doing it, and he has to keep up with the crowd. You can't eat ideals for dinner."

Watching his own smug, spirited face on screen, he felt deeply regretful. He wanted to reach in and drag that version of himself out for a good talking-to.

Did you not know how to be modest and tactful in front of a camera? Do you have any idea how many people you've offended because you can never keep that mouth of yours in check?

Of course he didn't need to scold himself; the netizens had already started in on him.

[Jiang Qing's something else. Doesn't spare anyone when he goes off.]

[Jiang Qing is unreal. Does Director Yu seriously still dare cast him? Serves him right that he has no projects. Playing him out with a nice sendoff.]

[Hasn't he always been like this? Arrogant and shameless, I'll give him that. Bully king of the entertainment industry, well and truly earned.]

[Not gonna lie, I just want to curse Jiang Qing out. What the hell, man!]

Jiang Qing: "..."

Netizens really had such vibrant energy.

"Director Yu, I need to see him." He put down the phone, forgetting he was still in an ambulance, stood up to walk out, then turned back around when he found the door locked.

He made several calls, none of which were answered. Eventually the other party just switched off his phone.

"Is Director Yu really that angry?"

"What. Do. You. Think." Shu Tong said through gritted teeth. "The second the interview wrapped he was gone, didn't even look at you once. What am I supposed to say to you? Talking back to some random traffic idol or flower vase is one thing, but you're even going after directors now. At this rate, are you going to be throwing punches at investors next week?"

"It won't come to that." Jiang Qing smiled shamelessly. "Don't worry, don't worry. I will never recklessly make enemies like that again."

He'd made his debut at six years old in an award-winning film; though only a minor supporting role, his performance had been genuinely noteworthy. He'd been grinding in front of the camera ever since, racking up award after award.

Getting into the industry so early, the people he'd rubbed shoulders with in those formative years were all performers of genuine substance, and that had set the standard for him. So when the market shifted and he watched so many traffic celebrities coasting on fan service instead of doing actual work, he'd been deeply dissatisfied, and had frequently named names.

What he'd underestimated was the power of those fan bases. Once he'd gone through and taken shots at them one by one, the fans of each respective idol turned against him; day after day they came after him, and the hashtag "Jiang Qing Get Out of the Entertainment Industry" stayed stubbornly trending.

A handful of major brand endorsements were collectively boycotted by other fandoms. The endorsements vanished, and his film and television resources took a serious hit.

For two years running, he had no scheduled work at all. When he finally managed to land a new film role, it turned out to be a supporting part opposite his greatest rival, Lin Xun.

Lin Xun had exploded in popularity over the past few years, drowning in resources.

In a low mood, he'd driven out to clear his head. Of all things, a pack of paparazzi and obsessive fans started chasing his car; the road was dark and slick with rain, and when he took a curve, something went wrong and the barrier gave way...

But since Heaven had seen fit to take pity on him, he would roll up his sleeves, keep his head down, and become a decent person again.

Doing the math, at this point in time he could still get booked for jobs, but they were all low-quality. Endorsements had dried up too. He was about as obscure as a person could get.

So this time, no matter what, he had to salvage his image and his reputation. He would break the habit of that sharp tongue and learn to deploy shameless flattery naturally and without a trace.

"Let me see exactly how many people I've offended." He opened his phone again.

"Don't bother looking; Yiyi has a list. I've been keeping track for you!" Shu Tong said irritably. Every time this kid opened his mouth and caused damage, she was the one who spent ages cleaning up the mess.

Jiang Qing was genuinely moved. "Tong-jie, you look so young right now."

"Don't try that with me!"

"I mean it, you really do look so young right now."

After he'd fallen into obscurity in his previous life, Shu Tong had spent years hustling to find him resources, enduring no shortage of cold shoulders, and in just two or three years her hair had started going white. Even Sang Yi, who normally seemed utterly unbothered by everything, had walked around with a long face every day.

This time, whatever it took, he would not let himself or the people around him end up in that same situation again.

After arriving at the hospital and being assigned a series of check-ups, he spent the waiting time scrolling through the trending fan forums of several popular celebrities to study how fans managed to heap such lavish and imaginative praise upon their beloved idols.

The more he read, the more he seethed with envy.

Why did his own fans only ever compliment his acting?

Was his face not a divine masterpiece, the breathtaking product of nature and humanity working in perfect harmony?

Did he not deserve to have his perfectly sculpted, heroic, awe-inspiring physique celebrated to the heavens?

His fans really needed to sit down and take some notes from other fan bases.

No self-respecting fan could afford to give up on rainbow flattery. Die with dignity, but at least die singing your idol's praises.

He scrolled through the trending fan forums and found Lin Xun somewhere in the middle.

At this point, Lin Xun was still a newcomer, fresh on the scene. He'd starred in one idol drama as a CEO character and attracted a decent following of fans who were in it for the looks, but he hadn't yet become the top-tier traffic celebrity he would eventually be.

As for how Lin Xun had managed to rise so quickly to the top...

That was something Jiang Qing had found out by accident, and it was also the reason he had always despised him.

Lin Xun was being kept by a wealthy young heir. It wasn't hard to see where all those resources had come from.

This sort of thing was common enough in the industry, but the previous version of himself had had zero tolerance for it. Especially when it came to a man like this, who was genuinely handsome and, in terms of actual ability... genuinely terrible. What a waste.

He was still lamenting this when his phone buzzed with a push notification: "Jiang Qing Faints During Interview." He tapped it open. It said he had fallen ill and the interview had been cut short.

That had Shu Tong's fingerprints all over it.

The comment section under the video was a sea of gleeful mockery. Any fan who dared post a single word of concern was immediately branded a brainless follower.

And then the hashtags appeared: #JiangQingFaints, #JiangQingCallsOutDirectorYu, #DidJiangQingRetireToday.

"Stop reading." Shu Tong snatched the phone from his hand and tapped the side of his head with one finger. "I'm already in contact with people. It'll be pushed down soon. Let's talk about you fainting. Have you been feeling unwell lately?"

Jiang Qing tried to lie. "Probably just a-a-a— anemia."

There it was again: that peculiar pressure in his throat, compelling him to force out one word at a time.

Shu Tong clearly didn't believe him.

He came clean. "All right, fine. The truth is, I've been reborn."

That came out without a hitch.

Shu Tong: "..."

"Pfft." Sang Yi laughed out loud, then pulled out her somewhat battered PSP and sat down beside him to play.

"I'm serious. In my previous life I fell into obscurity, but you two lovely ladies stood by me through all of it, and I was deeply touched. Please don't worry; I am never going to be the bully king of the entertainment industry ever again!" He got through that whole speech in one breath, and it felt absolutely wonderful.

Shu Tong decided he had genuinely reflected on himself and was simply making up a ridiculous excuse to save face. She played along and asked, "So what's your plan?"

Jiang Qing joked, "Run off with the t-t— two of you to the moon, obviously."

Shu Tong caught a flicker of something off. "Why are you stuttering? Are you hiding something?"

"What are you talking about, you're the one who stu—" Jiang Qing abruptly stopped. He stared at her in horror. For a long moment he couldn't say a word.

After a while, he tried reciting a dish name. It came out fluid and easy, perfectly clear, and he let out a breath of relief. "See, that's perfectly fine."

"Then just now...?"

He was curious about it himself. There had definitely been moments when certain sentences felt stuck, like trying to push words through something thick and unyielding.

He thought carefully back over the sentences where he'd stuttered, and it suddenly hit him: every single one had been a lie.

What did that mean? A side effect of being reborn?

He opened his mouth to test it in disbelief. "I ate two bowls of rice for lunch."

He paused. Nothing. He tried again. "I ch-ch-chipped my g-g-gold tooth."

Stuck.

"Jiang Qing is extremely handsome, exceptionally talented, and he also does his recycling." His eyes grew wider and wider with each phrase. "Everyone lo-loves hi-hi-him."

Oh no, oh no, oh no! What on earth was this! He was a perfectly normal person, and now he had a stutter, just like that. Was the entire rainbow flattery plan going to die before it even got started?!

"Stop throwing a tantrum." Shu Tong hesitated for a moment, then brought up the subject of work. "There's a variety show and a drama series. Will you take them?"

Jiang Qing's eyes lit up, and he immediately set aside the stuttering problem. "Yes, I'll take both!"

Shu Tong quietly exhaled. In the old days, this kid would have refused without a second thought. It seemed he really was determined to change.

"The variety show also has an interview lined up. Do you dare go?"

Jiang Qing swallowed. "Of course I'll go. I'm not the least b-bit nervous."

chapters.title: Required Viewing for Real Men
chapters.content:
The variety show was called "I Am an Actor," a performance competition series with three seasoned industry veterans serving as judges. A group of actors would compete on the same stage, going head to head in their craft, with the goal of crowning the year's finest performer.

This was the first show to feature acting itself as the basis for competition, and during the development and promotional phase it attracted considerable criticism. Getting guest competitors to sign on was proving extremely difficult.

After all, stepping onto this stage meant putting your real acting ability on display in front of a national audience. One slip and you'd be publicly ridiculed.

Jiang Qing, however, had no reason to be afraid, because he'd been invited to join as a judge.

As a judge, outstanding ability alone wasn't enough; you needed to bring some spectacle.

And what spectacle did Jiang Qing bring? Child star. Serious actor. Youngest Best Actor winner. Exceptionally good-looking. Absolutely vicious mouth.

Who on that stage, competitor or fellow judge, was willing to openly tear into someone in front of everyone, no matter what it cost them?

Look across the entire entertainment industry, and Jiang Qing stood alone.

To the production team, he was pure gold. From the very first planning meeting, they'd had their eyes on Jiang Qing, and were absolutely determined to get him on this stage.

In his previous life, Jiang Qing had flatly refused. He wasn't blind; he could see exactly what they were after.

But because he'd turned down variety show invitation after invitation, he'd eventually been blacklisted by every major production team.

This time, being reborn at exactly this moment, perhaps it was fate quietly telling him: it's time to take this show.

Jiang Qing spun his phone in his hand, then remembered there was still something unresolved. He opened his contacts and called Director Yu. No one picked up.

He was really upset, it seemed. Very upset indeed.

Jiang Qing typed out a sincere, carefully worded apology text and sent it. It disappeared into silence without a reply.

Two days later, the three of them finally "discharged" themselves from the hospital and went home.

The variety show production team, seemingly terrified he might change his mind, kept contacting Shu Tong, nailing down a date for the promo shoot and penciling in a brief interview alongside it.

That morning, Jiang Qing was deep in sleep when Shu Tong dragged him up. Sang Yi was already on the sofa playing her games.

"What a fine day it is today, balloons floating in the sky, little birds coming out to play." He hummed cheerfully on his way to the bathroom.

Sang Yi glanced at the grey, rain-streaked sky outside and went back to her game.

In the car on the way over, he started thinking through how to handle the interview.

Taking promotional photos was nothing. The real challenge was keeping himself from tearing into people the way he used to.

Not to mention the inexplicable stutter he'd developed.

When they arrived at the television station, he went to hair and makeup first, then shot the promo photos.

For some reason, he had the persistent feeling the stylist was a little hostile toward him. It wasn't until he caught a glimpse of her phone screen saver, which was a photo of Lin Xun, that it all made sense.

And it didn't stop there. The makeup artist was a fan of another young heartthrob; the runner was a fan of a popular young actress; the camera operator was a longtime collaborator of Director Yu's...

He finally understood what it meant to reap what you sow.

So when he ran into the host backstage, his very first words were, "Hi there. Do you follow any celebrities?"

The host shook her head. "I don't follow individuals. I follow everyone who puts in the work for their roles and gives everything they have for the stage."

What a mouth on her. She'd spoken directly to his heart. He almost wanted to offer her a job on the spot, until he noticed the lavender hair clip pinned to her head.

Lavender: the fan color of Lin Xun's fandom.

Lin Xun's ability to attract fans was even stronger than he'd realized. He'd learned that far too late in his previous life.

The camera operator switched on the equipment. The host took a seat at an angle across from him, and the interview began.

She started with some small talk, asking about recent life, the film that was about to wrap its theatrical run, letting him ease into things naturally before steering toward what she actually wanted to ask.

Host: "Did you go see the new film?"

Jiang Qing: "I did." He'd seen it three years ago.

"There's been a lot of online discussion about what you said in a previous interview regarding Director Yu. What's your take on that?"

He'd expected this question. It was inevitable.

Shu Tong had warned him in the car, but now that the moment was here, she found herself staring at him anyway, bracing for the second he'd lose control and say something catastrophic.

Jiang Qing cleared his throat and said with complete sincerity, "Last time I was having a bit of a, a, ahem, a cold, and the interview ended abruptly before I could finish what I was saying. Let me take this opportunity to clarify: what I meant was that this film appears restless on the surface. It follows a poor young man who disguises himself to enter high society. It's a comedy, but it's actually a satire of the modern spiritual condition..."

Shu Tong looked over at him, her expression shifting to undisguised surprise.

He continued: "And as for not being able to eat ideals for dinner, that's precisely why Director Yu is one of the rare few who can seamlessly integrate market appeal with artistic vision. We've collaborated so many times; we know each other well. I'm sure he understood what I left unsaid."

The host thought: well, this isn't what I was expecting at all.

She pressed further. "You're about to take on a judging role for 'I Am an Actor.' Do you feel you have what it takes?"

She watched him closely as she asked.

Going by Jiang Qing's track record, he'd surely fire off something scathing about all the traffic celebrities, triggering a full-blown online war, which would be absolutely perfect for the show's publicity...

Instead, Jiang Qing gave a perfectly vague, deflecting smile and said, "The production team invited me to be a judge. Isn't that their vote of confidence?"

The host paused, maintaining a polished smile. "Yes. After a very thorough selection process, we unanimously agreed that you are one of the defining representatives of the younger generation of actors, and are absolutely qualified for this role."

"Thank you."

Jiang Qing smiled back at her, and it was so genuine that it caught her off guard for a moment. She almost let herself get distracted by it.

She quickly moved on. "This year has produced quite a few breakout dramas, and a number of new-generation actors have made their names. Who made the biggest impression on you?"

"Lin Xun." The name was out before he'd even thought about it. He blinked at himself.

The host hadn't expected that answer either. The urge to immediately take his side evaporated on the spot, and she could already imagine how he was going to verbally tear apart the idol she'd been secretly rooting for.

She braced herself internally, but asked anyway for the sake of the content. "Why him?"

Jiang Qing also very much wanted to know why he'd gone and said that.

He quickly adjusted his expression, pulled up a smile, and said earnestly, "Well. He's very handsome, his acting is ex-explo-explosive, and I want to c-c— how do you say it, I want to call... I want to cheer him on."

He struggled through it, but every time he got stuck, he either pretended not to know the slang or affected a thoughtful pause, and the host never caught on to the stuttering. She was too busy being floored by the answer itself.

Was she hearing things? Was this Jiang Qing real?

She couldn't stop herself. "There's been an audio clip circulating online from a while back, where you mentioned Lin Xun and said something about his expressionless acting style. Do you remember that?"

Of course he remembered. It had been a private gathering, and someone had asked him what he thought of the newly famous Lin Xun and played him a few clips from one of the dramas, all scenes of the domineering CEO character making an entrance. He'd said what he said off the cuff, and someone had made a recording.

That audio clip was what had landed him in the enemy camp as far as Lin Xun's fans were concerned.

There were plenty of people in the industry who privately resented this newcomer who'd seemingly appeared out of nowhere, but none of them had been as openly critical as Jiang Qing. The war between the two sides had never let up. Even after he'd faded into obscurity, the lavender fans still came to his Weibo to check in on the has-been and spit on him for good measure.

Beside him, Shu Tong saw him suddenly drift off and knew full well how incendiary this question was. She picked up her phone, about to fake an incoming call to derail the topic, when Jiang Qing turned back to the camera and spoke.

"The recording from that gathering was made in a crowded, noisy room. It didn't come out clearly. What I said wasn't expressionless acting." He put a deliberate emphasis on the pause, conveying both correction and barely contained indignation at having been secretly recorded.

"Then what did you say?"

"I said face-to-face acting. You only need to meet him in person to experience the full impact of his performance. The character and the man are one and the same; I imagine that's what his fans mean when they call him a walking CEO."

The host: ...

How did I somehow end up convinced by that?

Shu Tong was speechless, the hand holding her phone trembling faintly.

The host, riding the momentum of his answer, took the opportunity to express some affection for her new favorite. "Lin Xun's performance in his last drama really was exceptional. Fans have been calling him the real CEO, the noble prince."

"Noble prince..." He let his guard slip for just a second, started to push back on instinct, caught the host's wide eyes, and pivoted smoothly mid-sentence. "Prince doesn't even begin to cover it. He's a god, a deity descended to the earthly realm! Yes, a heavenly being, come down among us mortals, the most magnificent man alive. Lin Xun, go, go, go!"

The host: ...

Lin Xun's fans had lost. Their rainbow flattery was nothing compared to this.

On the way back, Shu Tong asked, "Why did you end up complimenting Lin Xun?"

"It just... came out." He paused. "But it's not like I was only talking him up. Give me a microphone and I could blow rainbow smoke over the entire entertainment industry right now."

Shu Tong gave him a look, then let out a small breath of relief. "You did well. It's about time you learned to rein it in. It won't be accepted all at once, but slow progress is still progress."

"Right."

Though, rainbow flattery really was a skill.

To generate buzz for the show, the production team released the short interview clip online ahead of schedule. Just as Shu Tong had predicted, both Jiang Qing's fans and Lin Xun's fans were baffled, and the two sides immediately started fighting.

[Take our Lin back, please. This washed-up actor doesn't need to be riding anyone's coattails. We don't know you, thanks.]

[Massive karma moment. Who was it that said he would never, ever do variety shows or reality TV? I just want to ask, does your face hurt? Got every director blacklisting you, no work to be found, serves you right!]

[He's obviously taking a dig at our brother. Blocked, never speaking again.]

[Lin Xun's fans have some nerve. A senior of Jiang Qing's level actually compliments your guy, and you're going to act like that?]

[Jiang Qing is clearly just using a nobody to get some traction. Have some self-respect.]

[Probably scripted. The production team is probably trying to push Lin Xun. Lin Xun's backing is seriously powerful; didn't he just come out of nowhere to land a male lead role in that last drama?]

[Qingqing, are you okay?? If someone's holding you hostage, blink twice!]

The clip shot up the trending charts within hours.

#JiangQingRidingANewcomer'sCoattails

#JiangQingLinXun

Meanwhile, the other person at the center of it all had no idea any of this was happening. He was at home, soaking his feet.

In his spacious, well-lit living room, a nocturne played softly in the background. Lin Xun had his head tipped back against the sofa, lost in the music, his fingers tracing the melody through the air, a perfectly measured curve at the corners of his mouth.

He'd just dried his hair. The light brown, loosely waved strands lay softly over his head. His features were defined and precise, the bridge of his nose straight and high, the line of his profile tracing a flawless arc.

Past the curve of his thin lips and fair jaw, his throat shifted slightly, moving without thought.

A ringtone cut through the moment. His lashes trembled faintly. His eyes opened, slow and unhurried.

Those bright eyes added another layer of richness to an already arresting face; looked at closely, the irises revealed themselves to be a deep, warm brown.

Profound and opaque, like a night sky.

The pleasant atmosphere broke. He swiped to answer, his voice low. "What is it?"

The call was from another young man, whose voice was bright and high-spirited. "Did you see what I sent you? On WeChat."

"No, I don't really use it."

"Then open it right now. Required viewing for real men!" The other man laughed, clearly pleased with himself.

He hung up, then opened the green-icon app. The first message was from a contact named "MengLiFindsYou," sharing a video clip.

"Boring."

He was about to exit when he noticed the thumbnail: an unfamiliar man, with a few large characters overlaid.

"Lin Xun. The most magnificent man alive."

Lin Xun slowly typed: ?

Curious now, he opened the video. He confirmed he didn't recognize this person, though he was strikingly good-looking.

He watched for almost a minute, and was about to close it again when the comments suddenly filled with "incoming, brace yourself."

And then the man in the video started complimenting him, with feeling and flair.

He turned off the barrage of comments and looked closely at this man, and unexpectedly found himself genuinely amused by two of his lines.

A heavenly being come down to earth?

The most magnificent man alive?

A kindred spirit, he thought.

A moment later, another message came from Yang Meng: The "Actor" show's production team just called again. Better pay, double the fee! You up for it, boss?

Lin Xun sent a message to the enthusiastic contact who'd shared the video: Add him to the required viewing for real men collection.

chapters.title: Gifted a Trending Topic
chapters.content:
The production team moved quickly. They published the official announcement and released Jiang Qing's promo poster, confirming him as the first judge.

Shu Tong logged into Jiang Qing's account as usual to follow and repost the production team's page.

In the past, he'd paid no attention to building a public presence. No calculated controversies, no manufactured persona, just focused work; low-profile to the point of near-invisibility.

He'd occasionally take an endorsement here and there, and did interviews and variety appearances strictly when required for promotional cycles. Outside of that, he was essentially impossible to find.

Which made his current standing a rather awkward one.

In terms of seniority, he qualified as an industry veteran, but without the years and gravitas of the truly seasoned old guard.

In terms of age, he was younger than some newcomers, yet lacked anything close to their traffic or trending presence.

He logged into his private account, which went by the handle "boy with the little topknot." It was a mess of random daily life posts and shamelessly self-admiring photos.

He didn't like posting pictures publicly, but behind closed doors he was a walking, emotionless selfie machine.

Every single self-portrait was set to visible only to himself. A face that handsome absolutely warranted hoarding.

He opened the comment section under the production team's Weibo post. Ugh. An eyesore.

[Production team, are you serious right now? Dragging in a bunch of actors to make money off fans is one thing, but who exactly is this judge supposed to be? Jiang Qing. One question: is he worthy?]

[You don't need a brain to see what the production team is up to. This isn't a judge. This is obviously just a chaos agent they're throwing in.]

[I get the logic, but why did Jiang Qing specifically call out our Lin? Lin said he's not doing this show. Stop using his name.]

[Lin just finished his last drama, and now he's already getting dragged into someone else's mess. I have words.]

[Breaking news to those just joining us: Jiang Qing just publicly complimented a newcomer?????]

[Am I the only one who found that interview slightly odd? Was it scripted? Did they tell him to hype a new talent? Because I remember someone leaked that Lin Xun has serious backing.]

[Lin is 100% riding on real skill. The original male lead dropped out last minute; if Lin hadn't stepped in to save that drama, it never would have blown up the way it did.]

[Honestly? If Jiang Qing's on it, the variety show content is going to be fire. Bully king of the entertainment industry going full chaos mode, I'm here for it.]

[This show has to be cursed. Production team, do NOT invite our brother. Stay away from the toxic waste, protect your wellbeing.]

After suffering through the comment section, he decided to go look at his own fan forum as a palate cleanser. He navigated to his official account and, full of anticipation, opened the replies.

[Qingqing please don't do this show. They're just using you. Can't we stick to good films?]

[Qingqing sweetheart, don't be scared! Your aunties and big sisters are here for you always!]

[Oh my god, I could lick this poster for a hundred years. Jiang Qing, you've destroyed the mother-son relationship between us. From now on I just want to marry you.]

[Hard to put into words. Qingqing always used to say he'd never do variety shows or reality TV... I'm not blaming you, I just think things have been so hard for you, my heart aches.]

[Jiang Qing you disaster, leave the entertainment industry!!]

After that, the anti-fans had infiltrated the thread. His own fans tried to hold the line, but they were no match for the sheer nastiness of the trolls.

The thing was, he'd made enemies in too many places. The fans who'd stuck around through all of it without abandoning ship were almost exclusively the low-key, unbothered auntie-fans and older sister-fans, the kind who treated him like a son or a little brother.

He checked his follower count. Three million and change, and a fair chunk of those were ghost accounts. That was a pretty dismal showing.

Thinking of dismal things, he suddenly had a craving for hot pot. He ordered some delivered, and he was halfway through when Sang Yi showed up at the apartment.

Jiang Qing called her over to eat. Sang Yi cut straight to the point. "Tong-jie says to pack some things. You're moving to Yishui Bay tonight, and you need to swing by the company tomorrow."

"Okay, I'll go after I finish eating."

His current place was a villa on the western outskirts, where he usually stayed during quiet stretches with no scheduled work. Peaceful, good for puttering about and playing with Lego. But impractical when things got busy.

Yishui Bay was a residential compound in the city center, close to the company, great location, absurdly expensive per square meter, luckily he'd bought in early.

"Moving" was really a generous word for it; there was nothing to bring. The other place had everything already, so they went over empty-handed.

The neighborhood was surrounded by tall buildings on all sides, busy and buzzing, though inside the compound, elderly residents moved at a leisurely pace along the walkways. The homeowners were uniformly wealthy, their net worth likely rivaling or exceeding his own.

Stacked up against his fellow residents, he was just an unremarkable small-time actor.

He reached the 28th floor, pressed his thumb to the keypad, and the door swung open automatically.

He hadn't stayed here in a while, but the apartment was still spotless. Shu Tong had people come clean regularly, as if she'd always been waiting for the day he'd be too busy not to come back.

The next morning, Sang Yi came in with breakfast and ran through the day's schedule. "Company at ten."

Jiang Qing took a bite of his sandwich. "And then?"

"That's it."

"..." Really bleak. He ate his way through two sandwiches before he felt the faintest glimmer of warmth.

It was about ten minutes to the company by car. The two of them stepped into the parking garage elevator, and just as the doors were about to close, someone came sprinting toward them from outside.

He held the button. The newcomer stepped in and nodded at him.

As the doors slid shut, the other person turned around. He was a young man with a clean, pretty face.

About twenty, his hair was permed into loose waves that flopped softly across his head. His bangs were a touch long, but underneath them was a pair of clear, round eyes that immediately drew attention.

The young man glanced at Jiang Qing, then looked away. A moment later he snuck another look. He pressed his lips together, opened his mouth as if to say something, stopped himself, drew a breath, half-parted his lips again, and then the elevator chimed and more people poured in.

The young man immediately went silent and kept his eyes rigidly forward.

The doors opened and closed several more times. On the twelfth floor, the young man stepped out first and was practically jogging by the time he disappeared from view.

Jiang Qing stepped out with Sang Yi, perfectly casual. He murmured, "Who was that just now?"

Sang Yi snapped her fingers. "No idea."

"His name is Gao Yuanqiao." Back at the office, Shu Tong held up a promo photo. In it, the boy smiled brilliantly, showing two little canine teeth; it was the same young man from the elevator.

Shu Tong tapped the photo. "He's a new artist the company recently signed. He's going to be on 'I Am an Actor,' and the arrangement is for you to look after him. That's the real reason you were able to land this variety gig. You're the company's best available option: you meet the production team's requirements, and if things go sideways, you make a convenient person to throw overboard."

So he was going in as a stepping stone. That was quite a price to pay.

Jiang Qing studied the photo and couldn't help asking, "Does he have a backer?"

Shu Tong gave a slight nod but didn't name anyone, pivoting to say, "The company wants to expand. Not just film and television anymore. They've signed quite a few people in the past six months: actors, trainees, singers. The talent management division has been ramping up too, scouting everywhere. You need to start feeling some urgency."

She paused. "Oh, right. There's also one prize acquisition they haven't been able to lock down. Everyone's been pushing hard for it."

"Who?"

Shu Tong lowered her voice. "Lin Xun."

He was mildly surprised. "He said no?"

By any measure, the company was one of the top entertainment firms in the industry. The managers were sharp, and a signing deal came with substantial resources.

Shu Tong said, "That's right. Not that I mind being spared the trouble of running into that brick wall. It is strange, though; he's had such a smooth path since debut, and he's never had a management company behind him. It's curious."

Jiang Qing turned something over in his mind and smiled faintly. "He probably doesn't need the company's backing."

"You mean he has something even bigger behind him?"

The two of them exchanged a knowing look.

Beside them, Sang Yi was scrolling her phone and suddenly cut in. "Oh, Lin Xun is trending. You too, Qing-ge."

Jiang Qing's face lit up. "Tong-jie, did you buy me a trending spot?"

"I don't have that kind of money." Shu Tong took out her own phone, already irritated. The top trending item read: #LinXunRespondsToJiangQing.

Jiang Qing swiped the phone from her and tapped through to a two-minute video.

In it, Lin Xun was wearing a grey baseball cap. He'd been cornered by a reporter while out and, unable to dodge in time, had been pressured into a short exchange.

Reporter: "Jiang Qing mentioned you in a recent variety show interview. Have you seen that clip?"

Lin Xun inclined his head. His sharp-featured face looked even more arresting in the shadow cast by his cap's brim; his lashes shifted slightly, and those deep brown eyes carried a faint trace of irritation. "I've seen it. Sorry, I have something to take care of right now. Another time."

The reporter followed him undeterred. "You saw it, right? What do you think of Jiang Qing?"

"He's fine." Lin Xun paused mid-step. "At the very least, he doesn't go around stopping people for no reason."

"Would you join 'I Am an Actor'?" The reporter, ignoring everything else, pressed the one question they'd come to ask.

"Guess."

"I can't."

"Not very sharp, are you." Lin Xun gave a faint smile, and then he was out of frame.

The camera shook for a moment, clearly showing the reporter giving chase. No luck.

Lin Xun flagged down a passing car. "To Buerden, please."

Then immediately dialed a number on his phone. "They found my temporary place. I'm going to stay at a hotel for a few days. How's the apartment search going?"

"Still looking. Not much that ticks all your boxes. I'll come find you when I'm done here."

The video was generating significantly more heat than the interview clip from the day before. The comments were flooded.

[Disgusting paparazzi. How is this different from stalking? Someone please deal with this.]

[Please respect Lin's privacy. He has no management company, but that's not a reason to hound and harass him.]

[Called it! Jiang Qing has officially latched onto Lin now?! Fuming.]

Jiang Qing watched for nearly a full minute before a single comment appeared that mirrored his own thoughts: [What does any of this have to do with Jiang Qing? How is this a response?]

He handed the phone back to Shu Tong and said, exasperated, "Every piece of random nonsense has to drag my name into it. These tabloid accounts are infuriating."

Shu Tong thought it over. "Lin Xun clearly had no intention of giving an interview, and he certainly wouldn't have pushed a video like that onto the trending charts himself. So who did?"

It wasn't paranoia. Trending topics came up all the time, and sometimes a fandom was powerful enough to push something through organically, but more often than not there was money behind it, or someone orchestrating things from the shadows.

A vague clip like this one, tying Lin Xun and Jiang Qing together, with the online reaction from just days ago still fresh in everyone's minds...

Both of them arrived at the same answer at the same time. "The production team."

"And this is exactly why I hate being on these shows." Jiang Qing sighed.

Shu Tong said, "Apparently Lin Xun had already been approached by the team before, and hadn't agreed. After your interview, they sent several more invitations his way. They're probing him on one end and using the two of you for buzz on the other."

Jiang Qing accepted the situation with resignation. There was nothing to do but swallow this kind of mute loss. The higher the show's profile climbed, the more everyone involved benefited.

Since the production team had bought the trending spot, they'd handle the fallout on their end. No need to get involved.

Shu Tong's phone rang again. She answered it with a brightening expression. "It's Director Yu's assistant! Lucky I kept that connection warm. Comes through when it counts."

When the call ended, she said, "Director Yu is staying at Buerden Hotel right now, running auditions for a new project."

Jiang Qing stood up, grabbed Sang Yi by the arm, and headed for the door. "Let's go. Time to get to work."

chapters.title: A Friend Conjured from Thin Air
chapters.content:
The car pulled up at the grand hotel entrance. A valet attentively pulled the door open, accepted the keys, and drove the car away.

"Wait here for me. I'll be right back down." Jiang Qing gestured toward a European-style sofa tucked in the corner, then, out of habit, fished two pieces of candy from his pocket. "I'll be back before you finish these."

"Okay." Sang Yi took the candy.

Director Yu was staying in a presidential suite somewhere on the top floor. The top floor had its own dedicated elevator, and the security was airtight.

At the elevator entrance stood a dedicated registration desk. When Jiang Qing stated he was there to see Director Yu, he was promptly turned away.

"Mr. Yu has given instructions. No visitors during the audition period."

Jiang Qing agonized briefly over whether to just book a room. But a room here could easily run six figures; it wasn't worth it.

He tried to sweet-talk the registration attendant with a bit of charm, then, when that went nowhere, resorted to his final weapon. He slid off his sunglasses and smiled with the radiance of a man accustomed to turning heads. "Hi there. It's me. Jiang Qing."

The attendant nodded politely. "Hello. I'm not a fan."

"...Right. Got it." Jiang Qing quietly put his sunglasses back on and shifted his gaze toward the descending numbers on the display panel beside him.

Ding.

The elevator reached the ground floor. The moment the person inside stepped out, he pushed past them to get in.

The attendant, faster than he looked, immediately hauled him back out, showing absolutely no mercy.

"Hey, hey, easy." Jiang Qing put on a show of protest, smoothed out his rumpled collar, and glanced toward the yellow tinted mirror beside the elevator. He went still.

The person who had just stepped out hadn't left. He'd turned back and was watching Jiang Qing with mild curiosity.

He was in casual clothes: a blue gradient hoodie with the hood up, sunglasses over his eyes.

Jiang Qing turned and, without a moment's hesitation, grabbed the man by the arm. He tilted his chin up slightly, let his sunglasses slide down a fraction to perch on the bridge of his nose, and with two clear, guileless eyes showing above them, smiled with complete innocence.

The man in the hoodie blinked. His gaze moved across Jiang Qing's face.

Jiang Qing, warmly: "Hey, buddy. It's been so long since I... oh! There you are!"

Without waiting for a reaction, he turned back to the attendant. "Besides Director Yu, I'm also here to see this friend of mine."

The attendant looked at the other guest carefully. "Is that so?"

Jiang Qing tilted his head and gave him a quick, sidelong wink. He lowered his voice. "Help me out here, and I'll make it worth your while."

The man's eyes shifted slightly. He nodded. "Yes. He's a friend. I was expecting him. Come on."

Rescued by this unlikely good Samaritan, Jiang Qing stepped back into the elevator. As the doors closed, he exhaled with relief. "Thank you. Let me get your contact information. I'll be in touch."

"Sure." The man reached into his pocket and produced a pen.

Why anyone would carry a pen in their pocket was anyone's guess.

Jiang Qing watched with vague astonishment as the man leaned in, took his hand, and wrote his contact details on the back of it.

"No paper on me. This will have to do."

They were standing very close. Jiang Qing could smell something clean and faintly sweet, like someone who'd just come out of the bath.

He glanced up and noticed the hair beneath the hood: brown, slightly wavy, well-shaped. The features under the sunglasses were defined and deep-set, the skin fair. The man was half a head taller than him.

Something about all of this reminded him of someone, he thought.

"There. That's how to reach me." The man finished and straightened.

Well. Even the voice sounded like the person he was thinking of.

Old rival. Bastard Lin Xun.

He cursed internally, then snapped to attention. He leaned in and peered at the man's face, proceeding with caution. "Are you...?"

The elevator doors opened simultaneously. The man's lips curved upward. He took off his sunglasses, revealing a pair of beautiful, deep brown eyes. "A friend who doesn't recognize me in under a minute?"

Jiang Qing's knees went a little soft.

He put his hand against the wall to steady himself, eyes darting to the back of his hand and the contact information written there.

An... email address???

Jiang Qing felt nothing but question marks.

The eyes behind the dark lenses blinked again, studying Jiang Qing's face.

Bright eyes, fair skin, peachy features. Better looking in person than in the interview clip. The expressions were too lively, too unguarded; nothing like the cool, controlled persona he projected on camera.

In under one minute, he had watched this person's face cycle through startled, annoyed, guarded, and then relieved, one after the other. He found himself wondering if this was what it meant to be a Best Actor caliber performer.

This one chance encounter had somehow been played as a tearful, passionate reunion between long-separated lovers.

Jiang Qing got his expression under control, looked at Lin Xun, who was holding the elevator door open with one arm, stepped out, and said pleasantly, "Hi. I'm Jiang Qing. It's very, very, very nice to meet you. Don't ask me why I'm emphasizing that; it's just for emphasis."

Lin Xun smiled. He extended his right hand. "Hi. I'm Lin Xun."

Jiang Qing gave it a quick shake, then looked around in both directions.

"Who are you here to see?" Lin Xun asked.

"Ah, an old friend. Go ahead and get to whatever you need to do. Thanks again for today."

"Shouldn't you get your friend to come meet you?"

Jiang Qing's eyes slid sideways. He scratched the back of his head awkwardly.

Just then, about fifty meters away, a door opened. Two people walked out. One of them said, "Thank you, Director Yu."

"I'll head off now. Bye." He said his goodbyes and walked toward that door, arriving at it completely composed, then turned to the man inside. "Director Yu. It's been a while."

Everyone looked up at once, and he kept his gaze steadily on Director Yu.

Director Yu looked at him for a moment. His expression was neutral. "What are you doing here?"

"I had something to tell you. Are you done with auditions?"

"Jiang Qing." Another man's voice, accompanied by an easy smile.

He glanced over. One of the men who'd just come out was looking at him; presumably someone who'd just finished auditioning. He inclined his head in return. "Hello..."

Terrible. No idea who this was.

He did, however, recognize the manager beside the man. It was Zhang Lingquan, who'd been going head to head with Shu Tong for years.

Zhang Lingquan stepped in smoothly. "This is Wang Mingzhi. You'll be at the same company from now on; take care of each other."

Jiang Qing nodded. "Of course."

Director Yu cut across both of them. "If you two have anything to discuss, take it outside. I need to rest."

"Rest well, Director Yu." Wang Mingzhi said his polite farewell, and glanced briefly at Jiang Qing as he turned to leave.

Zhang Lingquan quietly tugged his arm and steered him forward.

A moment later, Wang Mingzhi looked back. He saw Jiang Qing bracing his hand against the doorframe and calling out softly, "Director Yu."

After half a minute of silence, Director Yu let Jiang Qing in.

Wang Mingzhi's expression tightened, his brows drawing together. He was well aware of the history between Jiang Qing and Director Yu; the two of them had been working together for over a decade.

He murmured, "The role isn't going to get taken from me, is it?"

Zhang Lingquan reassured him. "Don't worry. Director Yu has standards; he's not going to forgive and forget that quickly. Jiang Qing is wasting his time. The only person embarrassing himself here is him."

The two of them got into the elevator, talking as they walked. A stranger in a blue hoodie was already inside, head down, scrolling his phone.

Wang Mingzhi dropped his voice again. "What do you think Jiang Qing went to Director Yu for?"

"Probably to apologize, then angle for a role."

"Will Director Yu give him one?"

"Relax. The second male lead is yours. The first male lead has been locked in for ages, a veteran of his caliber isn't getting replaced. And even if Director Yu does throw something Jiang Qing's way, it'll be a third-billed role at best. Director Yu probably wants to knock that arrogance out of him anyway."

Wang Mingzhi relaxed, then let out a quiet laugh. "I was starting to think he was some unstoppable force. Turns out he's all posturing. Calling Director Yu 'Brother Yu' just now... so desperate and pathetic. I almost burst out laughing."

Zhang Lingquan smiled too. "Don't ever pick up habits like that. Protect your image. Think of yourself as the antithesis: understated, gracious, a true gentleman."

"Right."

The elevator opened. The two of them stepped out first.

Lin Xun looked up. He watched the man's easy, swaggering gait and the satisfied look on his face, then gave a small shrug. You two might have some interesting misconceptions about what gentlemen are like.

He had just stepped into the lobby when he came face to face with a familiar figure.

"Look at that, you came all the way down to meet me." Yang Meng was dressed in a suit, a few centimeters shorter than him, and came forward to sling an arm over his shoulder.

Lin Xun thought: all I wanted was to go out for a decent lunch. Was that too much to ask.

The registration attendant's expression had shifted entirely, like someone who'd taken up a permanent station in the lobby to receive guests.

Upstairs, Yang Meng made another attempt to drape himself over Lin Xun's shoulder.

Lin Xun stopped walking, turned his head, and looked at him in silence.

Yang Meng instantly backed down.

A pointed clearing of the throat came from somewhere nearby.

Both of them looked up. Jiang Qing was standing a few steps ahead, eyes shifting left and right with an air of studied innocence. "Ah, would you mind letting me through?"

Yang Meng barely moved to the side before he caught the barely perceptible curve at the corner of Lin Xun's mouth. Puzzled, he thought: have these two met without telling me?

And then it clicked. After showing Lin Xun that "required viewing" clip, Lin Xun had asked for some information on Jiang Qing.

He immediately turned to Jiang Qing. "Jiang Qing, hey, I'm Yang Meng. I'm a huge fan of yours..."

For some reason, he noticed Jiang Qing suddenly look at him very warily. Even Lin Xun gave him a second glance.

He rushed to add: "...of your work. I grew up watching your work."

Jiang Qing relaxed, then quietly felt a little put out. They were roughly the same age; why did that make him sound ancient?

Yang Meng he knew. Most people in the industry knew Yang Meng: a well-known entertainment investor, young and wealthy, the kind of person quite a few people were eager to get close to.

And Yang Meng was Lin Xun's backer.

At some gathering with investors, someone had asked a slightly drunk Yang Meng whether he and Lin Xun had a special relationship and had been working to launch Lin Xun's career. Yang Meng had confirmed it in front of everyone.

"Did things wrap up so quickly?" Lin Xun cut through his thoughts.

"Ah? Yes, done." He took an unobtrusive sidelong glance.

Come to think of it, Lin Xun had always been his biggest rival, yet the two of them had never actually crossed paths in any meaningful way. They'd occasionally attended the same events and ceremonies, but always seated far apart, and afterward... afterward he'd lost all opportunity to attend events at all. Ha.

And among all the fan bases in the industry, Lin Xun's lavender fans had the most formidable combat power. They paved their idol's path with flowers and paved Jiang Qing's with something considerably less pleasant.

"Have you eaten? Want to join us?" Lin Xun asked.

Jiang Qing blinked. Yang Meng blinked. Both of them stared.

"I'm all right, my friend is waiting for me downstairs." Jiang Qing declined pleasantly. For one thing, he didn't know the man well enough. For another, he had no desire to be a third wheel.

Besides, these two had the money and the taste to book presidential suites. Presumably they were there to... practice their English together.

Lin Xun was entirely unaware of the elaborate scenario being constructed in Jiang Qing's mind. He smiled. "Is there really a friend, or did you conjure them from thin air?"

Jiang Qing was faintly embarrassed. "A real friend. My assistant."

Lin Xun stepped aside to let him pass, still smiling. "Then go. Don't keep the young lady waiting."

"Yeah, okay." Jiang Qing walked briskly to the elevator, and seeing both men still turned toward him, gave a wave. "Thanks again for today."

Yang Meng automatically waved back. When the doors slid shut, he asked, "How do you two know each other?"

"We just ran into each other just now. He's interesting. Are his resources really that bad right now?"

"Bad? That's an understatement. Basically no one is willing to cast him at this point. He pissed off Director Yu most recently, and before that some A-lister, and before that... how does a person keep doing this without learning a single lesson."

Lin Xun nodded thoughtfully, went inside and poured Yang Meng a glass of water, then said, almost as an aside, "That deal the 'Actor' team offered. What were the conditions again?"

"Pretty solid. Plus the fee hike, they promised to guarantee you a finals spot." Yang Meng took a sip of water, then paused and looked at him, suspicious. "You're not actually considering it, are you?"

"Something wrong with that?"

"What do you mean what's wrong, do you need the money?" Yang Meng said, exasperated. "It's obviously a ploy to use you and Jiang Qing for publicity. You're fine with that?"

Lin Xun gave a noncommittal shrug.

"And besides, I'm fairly sure Jiang Qing would roast you into a fine powder."

Lin Xun's expression eased into something like a smile. "You saw him compliment me, didn't you?"

Yang Meng faltered. "That was just for the cameras. And besides, didn't you say the entertainment industry was boring?"

Lin Xun slid his hand into his hoodie pocket and felt the pen there. His mind went back to the image of writing on that pale hand, and how, just when he'd almost finished, he'd glanced up and found those attentive, searching eyes looking straight at him. The lashes were quite something; he'd nearly written a character wrong.

"Can't I find something interesting now?"

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Inner Circle
chapters.content:
Jiang Qing took Sang Yi out to eat. Midway through, Shu Tong sent a WeChat asking how things had gone. He typed back: [All good, Director Yu's not angry with me anymore.]

A chicken drumstick appeared in his bowl. He put away his phone and looked up.

Sang Yi said, without expression, "No phones at the table."

"Yes ma'am!" He ate it happily, then sighed. "Yiyi, you've grown up so fast."

Sang Yi gave him a look. Said nothing.

"Now that you've grown up, you have your own savings. Why don't you pick up the tab today?"

"..." Sang Yi clutched her wallet and hurriedly told the server to stop bringing out the remaining dishes.

"What's that on your hand?" Sang Yi pointed at his hand.

Jiang Qing followed her gaze. He rubbed at it with his fingers. It didn't come off.

"Nothing. Just something a rude, inconsiderate nuisance did."

Back home, Jiang Qing checked the time and said, "You have Muay Thai this week, right? Go on. I'll be staying in for the next few days. Call me if anything comes up."

"Okay."

That evening, Shu Tong stopped by after work and brought food, telling him to keep it light for now.

Jiang Qing opened the container: a tender, fragrant chicken soup, garlic shrimp with broccoli and chicken breast, and a small box of fruit salad.

Shu Tong had to get home to her child, so she got straight to the work matter she hadn't finished earlier.

"The drama I mentioned is a xianxia idol show, adapted from a popular novel with a large original fan base. Budget is over a hundred million, the production team is strong, and the female lead is Mu Ning, one of the biggest trending actresses right now."

Sounded decent. He asked, "The male lead isn't me, is it."

"No, it's Wang Mingzhi. He started as a singer, well-rounded in singing and dancing, good-looking, built up a strong fan base. He's transitioning to acting now, so the production chose him; the company's also been pushing for it behind the scenes."

"...I actually ran into him today." Jiang Qing said. "Are you sure, his looks are all that?"

"..." Shu Tong recognized the symptoms of his narcissism flaring up, and couldn't resist trying a different tactic. "If you worked at building your fan connection the way he does, you'd have blown up long ago."

"That's a non-starter. The more I spoil my fans, the more they treat me like their kid."

Shu Tong laughed. "The market is different now. No matter how much it bothers you, you need to dial it back. Especially with these newcomers; they blow up fast. Who knows who's standing on top next."

"What goes up fast comes down fast." Jiang Qing took a sip of soup. "Better to be like this soup: slow fire, low heat, long simmer. That's where the real flavor comes from."

"How's the flavor of being washed up treating you, then?" Shu Tong punctured his moment.

"..." Jiang Qing had no response to that and pivoted aggressively. "Anyway, back to the drama. The company invested, didn't they?"

"Quite a bit. Aren't you going to ask about your role?"

Jiang Qing could guess without much effort that it was something well below third billing.

"It's a villain." Shu Tong said.

"Oh? That's interesting. What kind of villain?"

Shu Tong let out a short laugh. "Corrupt and unscrupulous, evil without exception: betrays his master, assaults the second female lead, massacres innocents. A complete and total monster. And don't hope for some tragic backstory to make him sympathetic; in the original novel, this character exists purely so the leads have someone to humiliate and take revenge on..."

"Ugh, pass."

He'd played villains before. But a character this purely reprehensible was hard to feel anything for. That said, in a drama running sixty or seventy episodes, these kinds of roles were indispensable for drawing out the plot.

"The variety show is to push Gao Yuanqiao. What's the drama for?" he asked.

He didn't believe for a second that the company was doing him any favors.

Shu Tong saw he'd already put it together, so she dropped the roundabout approach. "The company put in the majority of the investment, so the cast is mostly their own new talent. They're trying to build a star-making vehicle."

In short: use him to generate heat and carry the newcomers.

If it succeeded, the credit would be spread across the whole cast. If it failed, he'd be the one taking the fall.

Playing a role like that, once the press releases went out, every bit of criticism would land on him.

"This is a grandmaster being dragged into a beginner's bracket. The grandmaster declines with dignity." He said.

Shu Tong went quiet. When she saw he wasn't budging, she said, "You already have something in mind, don't you. Your contract is up at the end of the year. Six months left."

Jiang Qing nodded. He'd been thinking about this since the moment he was reborn.

Three years ago, when the old leadership had retired or left and the new management pivoted hard toward market trends, renaming the company from a film and television company to an entertainment company, he should have seen the warning signs.

This wasn't the same company anymore. It wasn't the place that had valued substance and run on real human bonds. In this new entertainment market, whoever could entertain and generate profit was the company's darling.

In his previous life, he'd been too loyal, held on too long out of sentiment, and signed a cheap renewal deal. After that, things only got worse.

Going by the company's recent behavior, they clearly intended to wring every last drop of value from him in these final months.

"Tong-jie, this drama is the company's project. I'm not going to be in it. If I am, leaving later is going to be one endless argument, and I'll just end up stuck on a sinking ship."

Shu Tong's eyes brightened. "You're planning to leave?"

"Yeah. Will you come with me? I've got no popularity, no resources, a pile of unresolved problems..." He trailed off with a small, plaintive expression.

"Oh, spare me the dramatics; look how happy you are." Shu Tong rolled her eyes. "Honestly, I was more worried you'd want to stay. It's been nearly twenty years."

"It has. But the people we cared about are all gone. There's nothing to hold on to."

They sat with that for a moment, and then Shu Tong asked, "What's next? New agency, or your own studio?"

His own studio meant no more working under someone else's constraints. But it also meant far more pressure.

"That's the plan, just not yet. My market standing right now is what it is; even if I open tomorrow, I can't guarantee I'll grow it into anything, and I'll burn through everything I have before I can even afford to keep you and Yiyi on salary. I've got six months. I need to fix my reputation first."

"How?"

"By letting this company work for me, of course." The corner of his mouth lifted. "You want to bleed me dry? That's going to cost you."

After dinner, he opened Weibo and continued his ongoing study of rainbow flattery. His own fan forum required two pages of scrolling before he found it, and there wasn't much to see: the odd post here and there with a film screenshot, sparsely populated. A ghost town.

In the process, he noticed a newcomer's fan forum: Wang Mingzhi was already in eighth place?

No wonder the company had paid so much to sign him.

He hadn't noticed until now. He'd apparently had his attention fixed on Lin Xun at twenty-second the whole time.

He clicked into Lin Xun's fan forum. The pinned post at the top was a recruitment notice for forum moderators.

Something clicked.

If he could infiltrate the heart of enemy territory, wouldn't that be the highest level of anti-fan management? He could unite the lavender fans from within and get them to leave a certain handsome young fellow named Jiang Qing alone.

He liked this plan very much.

He quickly set up a side account, joined the forum, and applied for a moderator position.

He had badly underestimated the rigors of the fan club's selection process.

The moderator informed him that applicants were required to pass a review before gaining access to the main fan group. The review criteria included: reaching level ten in the fan topic, proof of exclusive fan activity on the Weibo account, voting, charting, and anti-fan data records...

And more.

He privately messaged the moderator: "Hi! I'm not very active on social media, but I have an autograph from him. Would that work?"

Moderator: "Babe, you're a fake fan, aren't you? Our brother doesn't give out autographs easily~~"

?

Jiang Qing quickly took a photo of his hand, the writing still faintly visible, and sent it. "He just signed this for me today, it's a bit smudged."

Moderator: "Too blurry, and the handwriting doesn't match. I'm going to have to remove you."

[You have been removed from the group by the admin.]

Jiang Qing: "..."

Total fake fan. Unbelievable.

He was so close. He couldn't stop now. Without stopping to think too hard, he emailed Lin Xun.

Subject: Help needed

Body: Hello Lin Xun, this is Jiang Qing. The situation is as follows: I need one signed piece of paper from you. I promise to repay you handsomely.

Send.

A few minutes later, a new email arrived.

Lin Xun: How will you repay me? [Handwritten signature, photo attached]

The response time alone gave him the strange impression that Lin Xun lived inside his inbox.

The signature was in some elaborate script; impossible to read. But a barrage of compliments was obviously the right call here.

As for the repayment... he would be giving Lin Xun a premium-grade fan, obviously. Heh heh heh.

Jiang Qing masked the relevant details in the photo with practiced sneakiness and sent it to the moderator.

The dream was gorgeous. Reality was a compound fracture.

Even with the handwritten signature, the moderator remained unconvinced; forgeries could be faked, especially from photos. Nothing spoke louder than hard data.

Did he or did he not post rainbow flattery on Weibo for his idol? Did he not do his voting, his charting, his anti-trolling data runs? Did he not log into the fan forum to scream about his brother with the rest of the sisters?

Without evidence of all this, he was a fake fan. Plain and simple.

The impartial and principled moderator had spoken.

Jiang Qing had to admit: she had a point.

No ironclad data. But he had the gift of persuasion. He thought for a moment, swallowed his dignity, and typed: "I'm so sorry, I'm just a primary school student, my parents control my phone, I had to uninstall Weibo and everything QAQ"

Moderator: "Aww, I'm sorry sweetie, the moderator requirements are quite strict. Come back when you're older."

...Brutal.

Then another message from the moderator, probably meant as a consolation to this supposed "little student":

"Sweetie, let me add you to the regular fan group. You can hang out there and chat with the other girls~"

"Thank you so much!!"

He had successfully infiltrated the regular fan group. But the moderator had announced his "primary school student" identity, and a wave of "big sisters" immediately sent messages his way.

"What grade are you in?"

"Have you finished your homework?"

"Do you have a little boyfriend yet?"

Jiang Qing: ...

He could not break character. Gritting his teeth, he typed back: "//W// I'm in fourth grade, homework's all done! A boy-boyfriend... not yet (hiding face shyly)"

AAAHHHH. That was not him. He must have been possessed by the spirit of the little student. That was the only explanation.

He closed his phone and shook off the goosebumps before heading to the shower and then to bed.

Right before turning off the lamp, his eyes landed on the back of his hand. The writing had been washed completely clean.

Yet somehow it had printed itself indelibly into his memory.

Damn it. His talent for memorizing lines was not supposed to be used for this.

chapters.title: Your Heart Is So Filthy!
chapters.content:
The next day, he received some good news.

"Someone reached out to offer you an endorsement deal," Shu Tong said over the phone.

"Really! What product?"

There was half a minute of silence on the other end before Shu Tong said unhurriedly, "Sanitary pads."

"......"

"A major European and American brand."

"............"

"There's another endorsement too."

Jiang Qing said mechanically, "I don't want to ask anymore."

"Shampoo."

"That I can do!" He came back to life!

"It's a major domestic brand. That kind of budget endorsement can't be boycotted by the other side."

He followed up, "After all, everyone needs to wash their hair. How is anyone still coming to me for endorsements right now? What did the advertiser see in me? My face, or my figure......"

"Your hair," Shu Tong said. "The advertiser said that among long-haired celebrities, you're the most handsome, and you have a lot of it."

"......Fair enough."

"Oh right, the roster for the other two mentors has also been released. Remember to check it out."

Shu Tong hung up and went to negotiate the terms of the collaboration with the advertiser's side. The contract only had six months left, but they could sign a short-term one.

Jiang Qing opened his phone and saw the related Weibo push notifications for "I Am an Actor." He tapped on one out of curiosity and was so startled he nearly kowtowed in the direction of the production team.

The second mentor was Teacher Wen Jiaxin, forty-six years old, originally a stage actress with extensive theatrical experience. Over a decade ago, she had appeared in two nationally beloved television dramas, leaving a deep impression on audiences. She kept a low profile, dedicating herself entirely to stage work, rarely attending events, let alone variety shows.

Jiang Qing had worked with her in one production before, where he had a guest role as the early love interest of her character's daughter, only appearing for an episode or two before exiting. They didn't have many scenes together, but he liked this teacher very much.

The third mentor was Su Hongru, a director and actor both, an inspirational icon in the entertainment industry.

Having been born with neither good looks nor a privileged background, he had clawed his way through the industry for twenty years before finally turning his fortunes around, becoming a box office legend whose every production was a masterpiece.

In recent years Su Hongru was no longer content with just acting, and had begun directing, occasionally making cameo appearances in the films of close friends.

Though Jiang Qing had been in the industry for nearly twenty years himself, he had never once collaborated with Su Hongru.

This was practically stargazing up close! He suddenly didn't feel like cursing out the production team anymore. They had a little conscience after all.

He decided to slip out and treat himself to a big secret meal, one last indulgence before the show started filming.

He had just finished getting ready to head out when his phone suddenly rang. Director Yu was inviting him to dinner.

He returned to Bourdain once more, where Director Yu's assistant waited downstairs to escort him to the hotel restaurant.

The restaurant was filled with the intertwining sounds of lilting music, the hushed murmur of diners' conversations, and the soft clinking of cutlery.

Director Yu was seated by a floor-to-ceiling window in the corner, and waved at him when he walked in.

Director Yu's full name was Yu Haoge. Though there was a generation's difference between them, Jiang Qing always called him Hao-ge in private.

"Hao-ge."

"Sit down. I figured you hadn't eaten yet, so I already ordered for you." Yu Haoge smiled, the wrinkles at the corners of his eyes immediately appearing. "I'm heading back this afternoon. The film starts shooting next month."

"That's great, wishing you a smooth shoot." He naturally began cutting the steak in front of him. "How long do you expect filming to take this time?"

"About half a year, I estimate. We'll be shooting on location out in the northwest." Director Yu kept his eyes down and continued eating. "Ah Qing, I spent last night thinking it over, and honestly, what you said last time was right. Remember how good our collaboration on 'Boundless' was? That production took nearly a year, the whole crew going back and forth between the northwestern desert and the Middle East......"

Jiang Qing smiled without a sound, bit into a piece of beef, and winked at him. "But you're not going to change your mind, are you."

"No." Yu Haoge spoke with feeling. "I'm not willing to stop here. I want to surpass everyone else. The market shifts too fast, and if you stand still, things will get difficult for everyone."

"Mm, I was being too idealistic." Jiang Qing shrugged. "I support you."

Yu Haoge was stunned. He had anticipated everything from the other man, a proper tongue-lashing, a plate slammed down on the table, a dramatic exit. The last thing he had expected to hear, out loud, was the word "support." Years of accumulated feeling suddenly surged up all at once, and he pulled Jiang Qing into reminiscing about old times.

Lunch ended. The two of them set down their utensils and walked out together.

Yu Haoge hesitated for a moment, then said quietly, "The roles are almost finalized. If you wanted to......"

"Is that so? Who's been cast?"

"You haven't been online? The production team posted about it half an hour ago."

"Come on, I was rushing over to see you." As he said this, he opened his phone and took a look. The male lead hadn't changed, only this second male lead......

"You replaced someone? It's not Wang Mingzhi anymore?"

"What do you mean replaced, he was only ever auditioning. He wasn't a good fit." Yu Haoge said. All the way to the main entrance, he still hadn't heard Jiang Qing say anything, so he took the initiative to ask, "The second male lead role, are you interested? I think you're a better fit than the current choice."

There were quite a few people coming and going at the entrance. Jiang Qing quickly stepped into the elevator and said quietly, "Forget it. With my reputation right now, even if I take the role it'll only drag your name through the mud. Let me get my footing first and then come find you."

Yu Haoge said nothing more, and clapped him on the shoulder. "Alright, I'll be waiting for you."

The two of them stepped into the elevator. A man standing a few steps away from them suddenly pulled out his phone, moved to the side, and made a call.

"I saw Director Yu, but I didn't get to see the person above. And he was actually having lunch with Jiang Qing! He even said he wanted to give him the second male lead role!"

"What?! That bastard......" Wang Mingzhi let out an irritated shout. "Did Jiang Qing agree?"

"I didn't catch the rest, but Director Yu patted him on the shoulder in a very friendly way, and the two of them were laughing and talking as they went upstairs."

A cold glint flickered in Wang Mingzhi's eyes. "Understood."

He hung up and slammed his fist down on the table.

How long had he been preparing for that audition! A full three days!

He rounded on Zhang Liquan. "Wasn't it agreed that you'd pick me? How did it end up switching to Yu Minghan halfway through?!"

Zhang Liquan frowned deeply. "Yu Minghan paid his way in."

"......"

Wang Mingzhi couldn't swallow this injustice. He stared at the floor for a long time before finally lifting his head with a vicious grin. "Get in touch with Yu Minghan. Tell him Jiang Qing might stir up trouble, and get them to go at each other's throats. There's still a month before filming starts. The production team can afford to reconsider."

Zhang Liquan's eyelids twitched. He gave him a long, searching look, and in the end nodded and agreed.

Jiang Qing had walked Yu Haoge to the door of his room, said his goodbyes, and was about to leave when he ran right into Lin Xun, who had just stepped out of the elevator.

The two of them both froze, sizing each other up with meaningful looks.
