This was the second time in a row that Jiang Qing had bumped into him, and it felt uncanny. But he couldn't quite read what Lin Xun's expression was supposed to mean.

"What are you looking at?" He raised his chin in a show of bravado.

Lin Xun glanced briefly at Director Yu's door, then asked, "The two of you finished that... quickly, didn't you?"

Jiang Qing: ???

Lin Xun curved his index finger and rubbed his nose, his gaze drifting off to the side. "Ahem. I just came back from the restaurant, and I saw you two."

Jiang Qing, baffled, asked, "And so?"

"You two are pretty close? Did you get the role?"

Jiang Qing's face went blank. He thought about it for a long time before it suddenly clicked, and he smacked Lin Xun on the shoulder. "What the hell, your mind is filthy!"

Lin Xun: "......"

Not that he could really be blamed. Jiang Qing had been taking subtle jabs at him in interviews not long ago, and then just days later had shown up at the hotel. Now he had walked right into the two of them looking awfully chummy. Words like "want" and "role" had drifted in fragments to his ears, startling him so badly that he hadn't dared to share the elevator with them and had deliberately come up a step later.

This sort of thing wasn't uncommon at all. Even Yang Meng had kept a few little companions on the side.

But judging by Jiang Qing's reaction, it was most likely that he had wrongly accused him.

Lin Xun said honestly, "I'm sorry, I misread the situation."

Jiang Qing: "......"

Ten thousand choice curses got stuck in his throat.

"Would you like to come in for a glass of water?" Lin Xun offered. "It's not a good place to talk out here."

"Who said I wanted to talk to you."

"Oh? So I'm no longer the celestial being in your eyes? I'm not your helpful friend anymore?"

"......"

The two of them went inside. Jiang Qing did a quick sweep of the room, noted it had the same layout and decor as Director Yu's room, and didn't look further.

Lin Xun poured him a glass of water and asked, "So did Director Yu offer you a role?"

"He wanted to, but I didn't take it." He accepted the water and took a small sip.

Wait. Why was he confessing so readily?

Lin Xun asked, puzzled, "Why did you turn it down? Weren't you there last time to audition for him?"

"Of course not."

Ahh! Why did he come clean again.

He decided to keep his mouth shut.

In truth, not just Lin Xun, even Shu Tong had assumed he had gone to lobby Director Yu for a role. Just a moment ago, when Shu Tong found out he hadn't been cast in the new film, she had even sent him a long message to console him.

The truth was, last time, he had simply gone to apologize to Yu Haoge.

The director of Jiang Qing's very first production, "Old Friends," was Director Guo Mingsheng. In every sense of the word, it was the film that had influenced him most deeply.

Guo Mingsheng was the most renowned director of the late twentieth century, with fans scrambling for tickets and actors flocking to him in droves. Many of today's most celebrated veterans in the industry had appeared in his films at one point or another.

However, the crown jewel of Guo Mingsheng's legacy in film history remained "Old Friends," a work heavy and profound in its subject matter, with characters whose fates left audiences with a lingering ache in the chest. It still held a steady place in the top three on lists of all-time classic films to this day.

Regrettably, immediately after the film left theatres, he had announced his retirement from the industry and retreated abroad, never to return.

All of this was nearly twenty years ago now, but the moments Guo Mingsheng had teased him, coaxed him, and guided him on set remained vividly etched in his memory. The two of them still kept in touch.

Though Guo Mingsheng had retired early, he did have one final disciple, and that was Yu Haoge.

The young Yu Haoge had few works and an unimpressive track record at the time, but he was full of fire and ambition, determined to surpass his own mentor.

So Guo Mingsheng had passed on the actors he had worked well with to him, including the young Jiang Qing.

Their collaboration started off quite well, but with the passage of time, much of it had faded, weighed down by the complications of that connection to Guo Mingsheng.

And if the two of them had a real falling out, the old man Guo would surely be disappointed in him as the younger one, once word got back to him.

As the saying goes, even when business falls through, the goodwill remains. Even if they couldn't collaborate, he couldn't afford to let the personal bond between them erode.

Fortunately, Yu Haoge also valued this feeling. It was just that any collaboration between the two of them was probably off the table for the foreseeable future.

He had a vague recollection of Yu Minghan, the one who had been cast. A rising artist still in development, but absolutely not someone whose ability would ever satisfy Yu Haoge's standards.

As for why the casting had switched to Yu Minghan midway, the various reasons weren't hard to guess. So he had declined to wade into that murky water, especially since there were more important matters at hand.

"Your phone is ringing." Lin Xun noticed him drifting off in someone else's room, which was rather unusual, and spoke up to bring him back.

"Hmm?" Jiang Qing snapped out of it and answered the call, his expression steady.

Whatever was said on the other end, Lin Xun had just stood up to give him some privacy when he saw Jiang Qing hang up, then start pounding the throw pillow on the sofa.

Lin Xun said blankly, "What happened?"

"The endorsement is gone too. One afternoon was all it took, and my magnificent hair has suddenly lost its appeal?!"

Lin Xun rapidly processed the news that within this brief span of time, Jiang Qing had lost both a film role and an endorsement deal, then summarized, "You're really having a rough time."

Thwack.

The throw pillow sailed through the air and landed on his waist, soft and harmless.

He smiled faintly. "Would you like me to help you?"

"Sure." Jiang Qing stuck out his hand. "Help me pick that up."

Lin Xun: emmm......

chapters.title: Perhaps
chapters.content:
Lin Xun picked up the pillow, gave it a pat, and had just set it back down when he saw Jiang Qing reach for it. He lifted it out of reach again and asked, "You came looking for my autograph last night. What was it for?"

Jiang Qing faltered and told a quick little lie: "I have a fri... friend, he, he, he, he's a fan of yours."

"They? Is it one person or a whole group?"

"Don't worry about the details." Jiang Qing said sheepishly. "The point is, someone en... entrusted me to get a signed photo from you."

Lin Xun sat down and said, "Why didn't they just come ask me directly?"

"Because... because you don't like signing autographs, do you!" Jiang Qing thought of what the moderator had said and immediately changed the subject. "Right, how come you still don't have a manager?"

In his past life, all he knew was that Lin Xun would eventually have an exceptionally capable manager, but at this stage he wasn't sure, and hadn't paid attention.

"Are you showing concern for me, or probing for information?" Lin Xun looked at him openly and without any pretense.

"Just pure curiosity. You must have a lot of activities right now, and quite a few fans too. Without a team managing things behind the scenes, it's easy for things to spiral out of control."

Though it was a bit strange. From what he'd observed in the fan group last night, that group of fans was actually quite cohesive. Was it precisely because Lin Xun had no team that they felt the need to keep the fandom's internal affairs in better order?

"There's someone handling it, just not a management team." Lin Xun said.

"Alright."

He had figured as much. What fans didn't need some kind of management.

Jiang Qing glanced at him, then looked again, and finally locked his gaze squarely on his face.

Lin Xun turned his face almost imperceptibly to give him a clearer view from every angle, and asked with full confidence, "Good-looking, isn't it?"

"Could you introduce me to your team?" Jiang Qing bypassed his idiotic question entirely.

Lin Xun's expression stiffened. His inner desires going unmet, he flatly refused. "Not lending them out."

Jiang Qing studied his expression for a moment, then shifted a little to the side and focused his full attention on his face. "My god, is this level of divine, di-divine beauty even legal? I truly want to know what it's like to live with a face like yours. This is what a real ma... manga heartthrob looks like! If I may ask, Your Hi... Highness the Prince, could you possibly be the legendary A, A, A, AA... ahem, A-grade charm machine?"

Lin Xun's lashes gave the faintest flutter. The corner of his mouth curved up into the lightest of arcs, and he gave a soft cough. "The team belongs to Yang Meng's people. He has plenty of talent like that, you could go ask him."

Jiang Qing dropped the fake smile. "......"

Give me back my flattery!

Lin Xun offered helpfully, "He doesn't just have talent, he has resources too."

Jiang Qing froze. He hadn't expected that this shameless person would say something so shameless to someone as pure as the snow on the Tianshan mountains.

He feigned composure. "So...... what exactly are you suggesting?"

"Why not go try your luck with him?"

Jiang Qing: !!!

Try what? His luck with his backside?

His gaze involuntarily drifted toward Lin Xun's rear end.

Lin Xun suddenly felt a chill run down his spine. Without any obvious movement, he shifted the throw pillow to cover his backside and said with a somewhat awkward smile, "What are you looking at?"

Jiang Qing turned his head away, eyes front, and said in a righteous tone, "I would never go to him. In the interest of the help you've given me a few times, let me give you a word of advice: stop always looking for shortcuts. Watch out or you'll capsize in the gutter. You should know, after the storm comes the rainbow, and we must rise up like roses through the wind and rain, unyielding and glorious......"

Lin Xun clapped like a seal.

Jiang Qing stopped his impassioned speech there. He had said his piece. Whether it was heeded was the other person's business.

"If there's nothing else, I'll be heading back."

Lin Xun thought for a moment, then said, "When I came up just now, I happened to overhear someone on the phone. They mentioned you and Director Yu, something about a role."

Jiang Qing looked at him in surprise. After a brief moment of consideration, he had a pretty good guess as to which side it had come from.

He asked, puzzled, "Why are you telling me this?" Aren't we supposed to be rivals?

"Can I not tell you? Then I take it back."

"......" Jiang Qing paused. "Are you actually trying to tip me off about the endorsement?"

Lin Xun shrugged.

Jiang Qing sat back down and reasoned through it. "If Wang Mingzhi was able to get an audition slot with Hao-ge, that means the project side has already started tilting in a certain direction. There's no reason for him to go after a small endorsement of mine."

Lin Xun smiled. "I only mentioned it in passing. I never said who did it."

Jiang Qing pressed his lips together, stood up, and took his leave. "I won't keep you from your rest. I'll treat you to a meal some time."

"I'll hold you to that."

"I was just being polite."

Lin Xun followed behind to see him out. "I don't do polite. Your generous reward still hasn't arrived in my account, so there will come a day when you come back."

Damn, what a snake.

Jiang Qing walked out the door, gave him a look of exasperation, glanced left and right, made a face at him, and was gone.

"Nyah nyah nyah."

Lin Xun stood where he was. It was two full minutes before he went back into the room and leaned against the door, turning that little face over carefully in his mind, and laughed out loud.

The one who ended up with the shampoo endorsement was a newcomer named Tang Huan. According to Shu Tong, the advertiser had suddenly noticed that Tang Huan's hair was longer than his, in better condition, more voluminous, and cheaper to hire, and so at the moment of signing the contract had decided on the spot to switch.

"Tong-jie, I really want to curse someone out." He said over the phone.

Shu Tong said warily, "Find somewhere with no one around before you do."

Jiang Qing walked from the living room to the bedroom, locked the door, and with phone in hand let it all out. "What the HELL! These bald freaks are saying whose hair is in poor condition and lacking volume?! Come compare if you dare, my individual strands of hair could wrap around the earth three times and swallow all their bald patches whole! I'm so angry I'm so angry I'm so angry......"

Shu Tong: "......That was entirely unnecessary."

Jiang Qing was outraged. "This is an affront to my dignity! If they won't sign me, fine, I wouldn't want to actually go bald from using their shampoo anyway."

Having let it all out, he felt refreshed all over, like even his skin was glowing.

He finally got back on track. "And who exactly is this Tang Huan, crawling out of what rock?"

"Apparently a newcomer from Dongying Entertainment. The company's only been around four or five years, but it's been growing well."

Dongying Entertainment? That name rings a bell.

He exited the call screen and opened a browser to search. Sure enough, he had just looked up Yu Minghan's company earlier, and that was Dongying Entertainment too.

Anyone and everyone could just come and snatch his endorsements now?

A man of pride cannot be humiliated. He would never use this shampoo brand for as long as he lived!

......How utterly bleak, how utterly bleak. Speaking of bleak, it made him want hotpot again.

"Absolutely not!" Shu Tong said sharply. "The show starts filming next week. You need to be in peak condition, and for the next few days I will have Yi-yi monitor your meals very strictly. Don't even think about hotpot or fried chicken."

"Wuwuwu, you really are a wicked stepmother."

"I have your embarrassing history in my hands, and if you don't behave I'll leak it."

"May your conscience be eaten by a dog!"

True to her word, for the next several days Shu Tong took shifts with Sang Yi to supervise his meals, standing guard over every bite of food with the vigilance of a hawk. Not a single extra scrap of meat slipped through, otherwise Sang Yi's freshly learned Muay Thai would have found its ideal target.

On top of that there was a daily fitness regimen, and whenever there was nothing else going on, he had to spar with Sang Yi on basic moves and kicks.

The saying goes that behind every successful man is a successful woman. In his case, behind this man who was whittling himself down were two women of unbending righteousness, impervious to beauty, their hearts as iron and their resolve as stone.

The night before filming, he took a deliberate look in the bathroom mirror after his shower. Not a trace of excess flesh remained on his abdomen. Those abs really were...... exquisite.

He couldn't help touching the lines, once again marveling at the wonders of creation.

How was he...... this...... good-looking!

The television station was right in the capital. Jiang Qing went to the company first thing in the morning, with Shu Tong leading him to the wardrobe and styling department to pick out an outfit.

He actually preferred wearing his own clothes, but the styling department had quite a few pieces that were brand collaborations. If the show blew up, the brands might notice and offer endorsements. Not a bad idea.

The stylist specially selected a dark navy blue suit for him, with clean-cut tailoring and well-defined lines, paired with a butterfly bow tie in a matching color palette.

On the table was a row of accessories laid out, and his eyes were immediately drawn to a box of brooches.

A little ice cream cone, a little bamboo leaf, a little hat......

So cute.

"Can I wear one of these?" He pointed at the brooch box.

"Of course." The stylist said, and then, hearing someone call from the doorway, turned and said, "Pick whichever one you like."

Seeing how busy she was, Jiang Qing just picked out his favorite, a little panda, and held it in his hand. "We'll head out then."

Back at the office, he had Sang Yi help him pin it on.

"So cute." Sang Yi couldn't help saying.

Jiang Qing lifted his chin. "Take a look at who picked it."

At eleven in the morning, the three of them quickly finished lunch and hurried over to the television station, where a staff member led them to the mentors' green room.

His room was the one closest to the hallway, with his name on the door. He had barely sat down when the makeup artist came in.

The makeup artist was a girl in her twenties, the most talkative member of the makeup team, though at the moment she was quiet as a mouse, steadily doing her work.

Shortly after, another staff member came in to walk them through the filming schedule.

Official recording started at three in the afternoon. The recording would run quite long, as after the first round of performances, the winning contestants would also each select a mentor to compete against in a PK round.

There were also a few unspoken rules mixed in, such as not putting all three votes toward the same contestant, not being the first to vote every single time......

Just thinking about getting to perform, Jiang Qing rubbed his hands together eagerly. "I'm kind of ex-cited."

Shu Tong held him back and smiled politely at the staff members. Once the preparation work wrapped up, it was already two in the afternoon.

With only the three of them left in the room, Shu Tong did a careful sweep to confirm there were no cameras installed. To be safe, she still chose to communicate over WeChat.

Shu Tong: "Gao Yuanqiao is competing today."

Jiang Qing: "Who's Gao Yuanqiao?"

"Scroll off. Let him advance, or you might get temporarily replaced."

"Got it. Who are the other contestants?"

Shu Tong: "The production team hasn't disclosed that, but Gao Yuanqiao's manager only knows who his opponent is."

"Ah." He turned his phone over and over, feeling like things weren't quite this simple.

He opened the door and called a staff member inside, and said with a smile, "Hello, Lin Xun sent me a message asking me to come by for a chat. Could you bring me to his room?"

The staff member was momentarily taken aback, then politely declined. "He's still in the middle of preparations, I'm afraid he won't have time."

Well then, the invitation was real!

How could the production team possibly pass up such a perfect opportunity to stir things up?

After sending the staff member away, he actually felt reassured.

If both Gao Yuanqiao and Lin Xun were here, there was no way he would get kicked out at any rate.

His path to a comeback...... seemed to find a glimmer of possibility in these two people.

At ten minutes to three, the staff member pushed open the door. "Recording is about to begin."

Jiang Qing stood up, straightened his lapels, fastened his suit button, and stepped onto the road ahead.

"Here we go."

chapters.title: Variety Show Recording
chapters.content:
In the corridor leading to the stage, he ran into the other two mentors.

Wen Jiaxin played old women and grandmother-type characters in stage plays and on television, but in person she looked considerably younger, carried no airs whatsoever, and was very warm.

Su Hongru was even more fun, witty and humorous, with over twenty years in the industry and a reputation for getting along with everyone. His ability spoke for itself as well.

The three of them exchanged greetings and got acquainted backstage while the host opened the show onstage and read through the introduction.

Going by both age and years in the industry, Jiang Qing was the youngest of the three, and therefore the first to take the stage.

When the host finished reciting a long list of his accolades and honors, a scattered, sparse round of applause rose from the audience.

He climbed the steps, and two paces forward was the glittering stage under the lights.

Under the bright lights, the tall figure in a suit moved with each step, those long legs cutting a lean, straight line.

His slightly long hair was parted to one side, revealing a clear, smooth forehead. A pair of beautiful eyes swept around the room with an expressive brightness, and he nodded a greeting to all sides before walking to his mentor's seat under the disinterested gaze of the audience.

The moment he sat down, he heard a female audience member seated just behind him exclaim in a hushed voice, "Wow! Jiang Qing is so handsome in person!"

Jiang Qing blinked, a hint of amusement lingering in his eyes, as the camera swiftly captured his profile.

The other two mentors took their seats in turn. Su Hongru sat in the middle, with Jiang Qing to his left.

The host was the same girl who had interviewed Jiang Qing before, a new host by the name of Du Yuening, trained by the station.

Du Yuening carried herself with ease and poise on stage, with not a trace of the screaming fan that she really was.

After finishing the opening remarks, she interacted briefly with the three mentors without trying to cause trouble or manufacture talking points, then introduced the ten public judges and the competition rules, and the event officially kicked off.

Good, no excessive interview-style questions. Jiang Qing quietly breathed a sigh of relief, then shifted his attention to the stage.

According to the rules, contestants would be paired into groups of two to perform together a scene from a classic film or television drama. They had arrived at the station the day before recording to rehearse, and what was about to be seen was the result of that practice.

The curtain opened. The first pair of contestants was Gao Yuanqiao and a young, trending actor. The selected scene was from a crime thriller.

The young actor played a police officer, frantically searching through a dilapidated rental apartment, his expression urgent.

On one side of the stage, Gao Yuanqiao made his entrance.

Jiang Qing had looked up Gao Yuanqiao's background beforehand. A college senior, a junior from the same school as him, who had had a minor supporting role in an online drama earlier in the year, then signed with a company. In addition to this variety show slot, there were film and television opportunities lined up for him afterward.

Jiang Qing propped one hand under his chin and narrowed his eyes, observing the performance carefully.

Gao Yuanqiao wore a white tank top stained with grease, his skin bronzed under the stage makeup, and slouched his way to his own room. Finding it in complete disarray, he yelled, "Bro! What are you doing!"

The police officer shot him a glare, hauled him inside and quickly locked the door, pressed a gun to his forehead, and lowered his voice. "Did you kill someone?"

Gao Yuanqiao stared straight at the gun to his forehead, his knees went soft, and his hands reached out uncertainly to touch the hand holding the weapon. He said in a trembling voice, "Bro, what are you even talking about? I don't understand... you're scaring me, put it down."

The young actor's eyes burned with fury as he closed in again.

The two of them spent three minutes suspecting and threatening each other back and forth.

Jiang Qing felt himself deflating. Every time a scene called for genuine immersion, this young actor would just bug his eyes out.

Such fiercely bugged-out eyes. Like a husky doing an impression of an Alaskan malamute. Quite entertaining, actually.

The two onstage reached the crucial moment in their lines. Just as it seemed the younger brother was cornered and had been begging for mercy the second before, he suddenly went quiet. An eerie little smile crept across his lips, and his voice became utterly flat. "My dear brother, stop pretending. There are no bullets in that gun."

The police officer's eyes widened in shock.

The younger brother reached up and grabbed the gun from his forehead, then strolled away and twirled it leisurely.

The police officer, in deep anguish and barely containing himself, launched into a passionate lecture on socialist core values.

The younger brother paid no attention, walking on his own toward the electrical socket in the corner of the wall, and pried off the cover with force.

It turned out to be a disguised socket. He pulled out a small box from inside and tipped it, and a few bullets clattered to the floor one by one.

The police officer stepped back. "Where did you get all this? Come back with me and turn yourself in!"

The younger brother loaded the bullets in at a leisurely pace, and when he straightened up, pressed the gun to his temple, mirroring the scene from when the police officer had first walked in, roles reversed.

Jiang Qing watched them in quiet silence.

All the way until a cold gunshot rang out, and the person crumpled on the ground pled with him in agony to turn himself in, unleashing a long stretch of emotional dialogue.

Yet the younger brother remained cold and detached, carefully caressing the gun, and when the other drew his last breath, he smiled like a child. "Thank you, big brother. I really like this toy."

A round of applause broke out from the audience. The two performers onstage immediately stood up and bowed to everyone.

The camera swept past the three mentors, and they made their appropriate sounds of appreciation.

Next came the mentors' comments. Following the order of seats, the host began with Teacher Wen Jiaxin.

Teacher Wen Jiaxin was gentle in her manner. "I think you were both wonderful. You pulled us right into the story in an instant, the physical acting, the dialogue, and the facial expressions were all solid. However, you're both short on stage experience. When the police officer fell to the floor just now, the audience should have been able to see that, not just the camera. But I still genuinely admired your performances."

Teacher Su Hongru was entertaining. "The two of you have great plasticity, and your character portrayals were solid. Especially the small character Gao Yuanqiao was playing. May I ask, did he end up biting the dust?"

Gao Yuanqiao grinned shyly. "He did, he did."

Finally it was Jiang Qing's turn, and everyone held their breath.

The poised and dignified host stood below the stage, gripping her microphone, rapidly searching her mind for emergency contingencies.

If Jiang Qing switched into insult mode, and she could successfully rescue the situation, her career would soar to the next level!

Even the two mentors beside him were sitting back with the look of people settling in for a show. Even the low-key Wen Jiaxin had heard plenty of Jiang Qing's "glorious exploits."

The director signaled the camera operators to follow along, the lens zooming in, aiming for a full 360 degrees without a single blind spot!

The camera first swept the hushed audience before quickly cutting to the front of Jiang Qing.

Just as Jiang Qing was about to speak, a girl in the audience suddenly called out, "Jiang Qing, no insulting people!"

Jiang Qing was taken aback, and glanced back.

The camera swung that way, and the girl immediately covered her face.

Jiang Qing couldn't hold it together, and laughed.

Seeing him laugh, the audience burst into laughter too, and one after another voices rang out telling him "no insulting," until somewhere among them an opposing voice cried out, "Do it! Go all out!"

He brought the microphone a little closer and cleared his throat.

Everyone went instantly quiet, with an effect comparable to the school's head disciplinarian about to speak.

"Your performance......" Jiang Qing paused, thought for a moment, then said to everyone, "......made me think of a song."

The entire room was baffled: ???

Jiang Qing, with complete seriousness, recited the lyrics with the pronouns slightly altered. "My friends, I want to tell you with pride, oh — you are truly not bad, you are really really really quite good!"

As long as it's lyrics, even the most ridiculous things come out without a stammer!

The room fell silent for half a minute before erupting in laughter.

"HAHAHAHA oh my god! How did he manage to say those lyrics with a completely straight face?! Is this not just reading from a script?!"

"Singer turned reader?!"

"I'm questioning whether my eyes and ears are conspiring to deceive me!"

"HAHAHA I can't, that song is kind of catchy, it's already on loop in my head!"

"What the — is that really it? You gave us that?!"

"It's a shame we can't take photos or videos. I want to post this on my Moments and Weibo so badly!"

"Look at the host and the mentors' faces, absolutely dumbfounded, eyes full of disbelief, completely floored!"

Teacher Wen Jiaxin, whose knowledge of current trends was limited, asked in genuine confusion, "Is that a song? What song is that?"

Su Hongru, a man of fashion, even started doing the hand gesture. "It goes something like this, right? I am really really very good?"

Du Yuening quickly took over. "Mister Su, you got the gesture wrong. It's like this." And with that, she led everyone on and off stage to do the "you're really not bad" gesture together toward Gao Yuanqiao and the young actor.

The atmosphere instantly warmed up.

Jiang Qing looked at the two of them and added, "The younger one has good looks. His police officer was cool, and he's charming. As for Gao Yuanqiao......"

Gao Yuanqiao immediately widened his eyes, looking at him with eager anticipation.

"Gao Yuanqiao has excellent plasticity and a solid foundation in dialogue delivery. The contrast between the character and his real-life persona is quite large, but if he can make the audience stay in the scene without breaking immersion, that's already half the battle won."

The other two mentors nodded in agreement.

The young actor was moved to tears. "Thank you everyone! Thank you Teacher Su, Teacher Wen, and Teacher Jiang for your recognition. I'm really so ex-cited. My experience is still nowhere near enough. I came here with a mindset of learning, and no matter the outcome, I'm very happy."

Gao Yuanqiao, catching up a beat late, nodded vigorously. "Same, same. Plus one."

Jiang Qing: ......

Is this kid under the impression that going through the back door means he doesn't need to use his brain?

The young actor then expressed his admiration for each mentor in turn. When it was Jiang Qing's turn, he said, "Teacher Jiang, you are truly the idol of us young actors. I grew up watching your work, and you are genuinely outstanding!"

Here we go again...... not exactly moved to joy.

He was clearly a full year younger than the young actor.

Gao Yuanqiao, as clueless as ever, chimed in. "Same, same."

Jiang Qing: ......

He had reason to suspect his company had deliberately paired him, the reigning verbal champion, with this inarticulate bronze-tier sidekick.

Gao Yuanqiao, remembering his manager's repeated instructions to talk more and grab more screen time, added, "I also grew up watching Teacher Jiang's work."

Again? Already?

Jiang Qing coughed twice. "Stop, or I'll dock your points."

"HAHAHAHAHAHA!" The audience laughter grew louder and louder. "Teacher Jiang, we all grew up watching your work!"

Jiang Qing pointed at the audience. "Director, cut their microphones."

"HAHAHA!"

"You lot are such a difficult audience." He said, at a loss for words.

"HAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"

"......"

For the voting segment, the two contestants received a similar number of audience votes, so the decision fell to the three mentors, each holding fifty votes.

Getting in first, he went straight ahead and voted for Gao Yuanqiao.

Even without going through the back door, Gao Yuanqiao would have beaten the husky. If he were properly honed and willing to put in the work, he had the potential to achieve great things.

What a pity, though, that he had taken the back door. Once you've had a taste of shortcuts, can you still keep your feet on the hard road?

Teacher Wen Jiaxin very graciously voted for the young actor instead, passing the difficult choice and the deciding vote to Su Hongru.

Su Hongru deliberated at length, praised both of them once more, then chose Gao Yuanqiao.

The young actor walked offstage in tears. The host offered some words of encouragement to Gao Yuanqiao, who had stayed, and then asked him to select a mentor for the PK round.

Everyone waited for Gao Yuanqiao's choice.

Jiang Qing relaxed his posture and leaned back, arms crossed over his chest.

If a contestant won their PK against a mentor, they could advance directly to the finals. If they lost, they would proceed to the semi-finals instead.

Gao Yuanqiao's gaze swept around, and without a moment's suspense he said straight out, "I choose Teacher Su Hongru."

Jiang Qing was mildly surprised.

"I really like Teacher Su Hongru's work, but I know my abilities aren't there yet. This might be the only chance I ever have to collaborate with him." Gao Yuanqiao said honestly.

Jiang Qing's lips curved slightly, and he led the applause. "Brave."

Charging straight at the biggest name in the room, Su Hongru, right out of the gate. Truly a young calf with no fear of tigers.

He also quietly breathed a sigh of relief. No need to wrestle with conflicting feelings after this.

The second pair was a male and female duo, both seasoned middle-aged actors of considerable strength. Their presence finally gave this program a taste of what it was actually supposed to be.

And this time, Jiang Qing served up genuine praise: "The performance of our two predecessors was magnificent, rich with feeling, emotionally full, controlled to perfection, and with a depth of diction that showed the fundamental quality a true actor should possess. I am sincerely in awe!"

The audience: We've actually gotten kind of used to the rainbow flattery......

The deciding vote among the three mentors rotated, and this round it was Wen Jiaxin who voted for the female actress, while the female actress also chose Teacher Wen Jiaxin in return.

The recording ran long. After this pair finished, there was a short break.

He stood up and went to the restroom, which was reserved for the performers and was relatively quiet at this hour. After finishing up, he walked to the sink and carefully scrubbed his hands with soap.

From outside came a steady, rhythmic sound of footsteps, even and unhurried, weaving together with the sound of running water.

He turned off the faucet. The footsteps had stopped at the doorway. He turned to look, and paused.

Lin Xun was leaning against the doorframe, smiling. "What a coincidence."

"Not really. I knew you were here for the show." He shook his hands dry, pulled out a paper towel to wipe them, and tossed it in the bin.

Lin Xun looked down with a quiet smile, the tip of his shoe nudging the floor. "Teacher Jiang, teach me a thing or two."

"What?"

Lin Xun walked forward and stopped beside him, looking into the mirror. "I'm playing your role. How do I become more like you?"

Jiang Qing was mildly surprised. Thinking it over, this was exactly the sort of thing the production team would cook up.

He raised his eyes to the mirror, a slight furrow in his brow, and said in a low, steady voice, "You're performing the role, and the performance should fit the character. I am nothing more than one interpreter of that character, not a template for you to imitate."

"That's a good point." Lin Xun smiled. "My acting coach told me to watch your works at home, and now my head is full of you."

"......"

Jiang Qing brought his index and middle fingers together and, turning his body sideways, pressed them to Lin Xun's forehead, just as Gao Yuanqiao had done onstage moments ago, but with a far shallower, quieter look in his eyes, carrying an inexplicable undercurrent of dread, like a real and ice-cold gun pressed to a forehead.

"Perform well. Don't ruin my work."

Lin Xun blinked. "Yes, sir."

chapters.title: Moonlight Before the Bed
chapters.content:
Jiang Qing returned to his seat and fell into conversation with the two teachers beside him about the four contestants who had just performed. Speaking privately, all three of them were more or less of the same opinion.

Su Hongru seemed pleased. "Xiao Jiang, you've got quite a good eye. Not bad."

"I'm really just going on instinct." Jiang Qing smiled. "You two are the ones I truly admire. I'd love to exchange some ideas with you both if the chance ever comes."

Su Hongru said cheerfully, "Ha, you're young, but your experience is nothing to scoff at. I've watched several of your productions."

"Is that so?" Jiang Qing felt a little flattered. "So which one did you like most, Teacher Su?"

"If it's my favorite, it would still have to be 'Old Friends.'"

"Ha, you sly one, that's not even one I led in! I'm barely on screen for five minutes."

"But those last few minutes were something else. A six-year-old child making an entire audience cry, that's raw talent!" Su Hongru was smiling even as he said it. "When I watched 'Old Friends,' I was hiding in a rented room and crying in secret. Ah, that was a truly great film."

"Old Friends" had won countless awards and taken home the Golden Leaf Award overseas. There was practically no one who said it wasn't worth watching.

Jiang Qing was a little moved by what he'd said, and changed the subject. "And is there anything you liked where I was the lead?"

"Yes, 'Boundless' too."

"Ha ha ha ha, Teacher, you really are sly."

Su Hongru, hearing him say that, felt not the least bit offended. If anything, he felt a little closer to him, like to a younger brother. Since making it big, very few people had dared to tease him to his face.

Su Hongru asked with a grin, "Tell me, how am I sly?"

"Everything you mentioned has won awards. Even without actually watching it, you could still name them." Jiang Qing said without missing a beat. "I'm different. I genuinely love your work. That early film of yours, 'The Last One,' with the eunuch Zhao, now that was truly immersive. I practiced it at home for a long time and couldn't ever get that quality out of it."

"Ha ha ha ha, you rascal! Out of all my tall, handsome, dashing roles, you pick the eunuch?!"

The two of them kept at it, trading quips and teasing each other until the on-site director announced that recording was resuming, and they finally wrapped up their conversation with reluctance.

Du Yuening introduced the next two contestants taking the stage, and though she worked to conceal it, the excitement slipped through in her voice. "Coming up to perform are Xu Jiacheng and Lin Xun, and the classic film scene they will be recreating together is from....... 'Boundless!'"

Su Hongru turned his head to meet Jiang Qing's eyes, and the two of them smiled at the same moment.

The applause that had started from the contestant introductions was already building, and when "Boundless" was announced, the cheering nearly blew the roof off.

Many audience members had been following the drama since the official announcement, and the prospect of any interaction between Jiang Qing and Lin Xun had been deliciously exciting. And now not only was Lin Xun performing a scene from Jiang Qing's drama, he was also playing Jiang Qing's character!

How thrilling! How wonderful!

Jiang Qing clearly felt that the camera operators, who had been roaming freely just moments ago, were now clustering around both his sides. He composed his expression and turned his attention to the stage.

"Boundless" was the film that had earned him the Golden Ram Award seven years ago, making him the youngest Best Actor winner at the time. Unfortunately, within days a Best Actor winner from the rival Golden Duck Award had been caught up in a drug scandal, and the news had blanketed everything, completely drowning out his winning moment.

"Boundless" followed the story of a wealthy second-generation young man who refused to be managed, fell out with his family not long after starting university, and in a fit of rage went off to the Middle East.

After a few days of baking in the sun and wandering around with nothing to see, he decided there was nothing interesting there and started thinking about going home. But just as he was about to leave, war broke out in the area he was in.

Smoke and dust swirled in every direction. He came face to face with death for the first time, and fear coiled in his chest. Just when he thought he'd never make it home, he stumbled upon a group of people.

They were spread out in an orderly formation, wearing white coats, racing against time to search for the wounded.

The female lead was one of them, a doctor who had graduated not long ago. Seeing that he was uninjured, she told him to help carry a stretcher, on which lay a badly injured patient covered in blood.

Through the hail of bullets, he and the doctors made it safely back to the treatment center.

It was only then that he understood. These were Doctors Without Borders, and among them were four doctors of Chinese nationality, including the female lead, who were therefore warm and friendly toward him.

With the airport temporarily out of reach, one of the older doctors told him to stay there and wait for the chaos to die down before heading home.

Every day he sat in that hospital, watching and listening. Outside, gunfire and shells. Inside, the cries of pain from the wounded. And weaving between all of it were those white coats, racing out to the battlefield each day to find patients, pulling them back to the hospital with urgent hands.

One day, the female lead was very late to return. Not knowing where the courage came from, he rushed out.

He searched for a long time before he found her at the doorway of a crumbling building.

She was holding a child of about ten in her arms. The child's head was covered in blood, and had already stopped breathing.

She gently patted the child's back, and with a soft smile murmured a lullaby in a hushed voice. Smiling and smiling, until the tears came.

He looked up at the sky, his eyes reddening. He brought the dazed and hollow woman back with him, and the next day saw her setting out again in high spirits.

He wanted to stop her. He couldn't.

She had said a word that was both terrifying and true. Accustomed to it.

But she had to steel herself, because out there were so many, many people still bleeding.

He joined the treatment unit. During the day he went out to carry stretchers, and at night he learned from the doctors how to bandage wounds and administer emergency aid. He was reckless, but his English was good, so communication was no problem, and he even cracked the occasional off-color joke to cheer up the patients, and the atmosphere in the wards began to improve.

When Jiang Qing had seen Lin Xun's outfit earlier, and the undercut hairstyle, he had already guessed the film. And with two people performing together, it had to be the emotional scene near the ending.

In truth, the film wasn't heavy on romance. The greater part of it was the story of war and the doctor-patient relationship. But for the box office, this scene had ultimately been added in.

The curtain opened, and the set and props for the scene were already in place.

Blazing sun. Desert. Smoke. Dust.

Lin Xun and Xu Jiacheng walked onstage together, speaking casually about something funny that had happened in the ward, while their eyes scanned their surroundings, not missing a single person who might be in need.

After walking a short while, Lin Xun suddenly stopped mid-step. His gaze drifted, and he asked with an uncertainty that felt unmoored, "If I go back home, will I be able to see you again?"

In this brief time together, he had already fallen in love with this young and strong girl. She was more real than all the daughters of wealthy families his father had arranged for him, and she moved his heart in ways those women never had.

God only knew when he had first learned to feel something ache inside him.

His scene partner, Xu Jiacheng, had debuted at sixteen and had spent her entire career in supporting roles. Audiences knew who she was, but that was about as far as it went.

Still, she was only twenty-two now, and the girlish heart she portrayed came across as completely natural.

Her face flushed, and she turned away. When she turned back, she wore an expression of studied indifference. "Next time you come, I'll take you to the best restaurant in the area."

Lin Xun touched the brass button on his denim jacket, pressed his lips together, then scratched vigorously at the back of his head, ruffling his hair into a mess. In a muffled voice he said, "How long are you planning to stay here?"

As he spoke, he quietly reached for her hand. And when he caught it, he bounced lightly in place.

Jiang Qing narrowed his eyes slightly. That movement was Lin Xun's own addition.

His version had been to step directly in front of the female lead, overbearing and a little reckless, pushing her to leave with him.

But this small improvisational gesture from Lin Xun quietly conveyed the male lead's state of mind when faced with love: nervous, careful, hopeful, like a child secretly clutching a piece of candy.

"I don't know." Xu Jiacheng's face was lightly flushed, her hand stiff, her eyes wandering, until they stopped at something in one direction.

A woman was lying there. Running closer, they saw she was a pregnant woman, bleeding from her leg, clutching her stomach in obvious pain.

Without a word between them, with a natural synchrony, the two of them hoisted the woman onto his back. Lin Xun bent forward and walked for about ten steps before a sudden cry of pain came from behind. He turned, and his face went ashen. He stood frozen in place.

A stray bullet from nowhere had struck Xu Jiacheng in the lower leg. Blood soaked through her jeans, staining even her white coat.

He went to her, careful and frantic at once, and was about to set the woman down when he heard her say, "Don't worry about me. Get to the hospital now. Her water has broken, she needs to deliver immediately."

Lin Xun's face went rigid, and his hands began to tremble. He struggled for words, voice breaking. "But you......"

Xu Jiacheng pressed a hand to her leg, cold sweat beading on her face. With steady calm she tore off her sleeve and used it to tie a bandage. "Go. I'll hide in that building over there. Come back for me quickly, and be careful."

The two of them were silent for half a minute. Lin Xun's eyes went red, jaw locked tight. The pregnant woman on his back groaned weakly, and he immediately steadied the person he carried.

"I love you." Lin Xun spoke suddenly, as calm as though the flustered young man from moments ago had never existed.

Xu Jiacheng's hands paused. She looked up. Her face was dirty, but her smile was extraordinarily bright. "Do you really love me? Do you know what I want?"

"I know." Lin Xun said heavily, and a smile slowly opened at the corner of his mouth. "So I have to go now. Wait for me."

With that, he turned and walked away with the woman on his back. In that brief instant, a single hot tear slid from the corner of his eye and fell across his cheek.

A grand and sorrowful score rose up, and quite a few audience members already had reddened eyes.

Lin Xun moved forward with heavy steps, unable to fall, unable to run.

"Stop please, stop, she's just a doctor! Please, please......" He murmured, his voice gradually rising, laced with a barely contained sob, pleading with whoever was shooting to spare the innocent woman, to spare all the innocent people.

Another gunshot rang out from somewhere behind him, and all sound cut off at once.

The stage lights went dark. Then came a raw, torn cry from Lin Xun, until his voice cracked and broke.

In the darkness, the cry of a newborn baby.

The audience: "Wuwuwu......"

The lights came back up, matching exactly the cinematographic effect used in the film.

The film had cut to black at that moment, leaving audiences with endless reflection, on the subject of war, on the cause of Doctors Without Borders. At the same time it had stoked curiosity: did the female lead survive? What became of the male lead?

Jiang Qing had been sitting in the cinema at the time, and when that moment ended, the whole audience had erupted in disbelief, turning to one another, unable to fathom that this was really how it ended.

Of course it wasn't. When the baby's cry rang out, the screen lit up again. The closing credits began to scroll upward, but the scene kept playing.

A pair of slender, lean legs came into frame. The female lead stood at the window of the delivery ward, watching the babies inside. Then she made her way, limping, toward an office.

"The sister's baby is so cute."

"Is that so? Let's have one too."

Jiang Qing turned away from his computer, his hair cut short and clean, his features fresh and clear, a quiet maturity layered over a youthful face.

He wore a well-fitted white coat, looking at her with a teasing smile. Then he stood, helped her to a seat, pulled a sheet of paper from the drawer, and set it on the table before her.

"Shall we?"

The two of them looked at it for a moment, exchanged a knowing smile.

The final shot rested on the paper on the desk.

— Doctors Without Borders Application Form.

"Jiang Qing, as the lead actor, what do you make of this performance?" The host's voice pulled him back from his thoughts.

He looked straight at Lin Xun and said, "Lin Xun, you really didn't disappoint me."

The rainbow praise he had blown earlier was finally not blind flattery after all!

The audience, pulled out of the sorrowful mood they'd been in just moments ago, broke into applause.

Lin Xun smiled brightly. "Thank you for the recognition, Teacher Jiang."

"You have a lot of potential, and I think very highly of you. Xu Jiacheng also gave a good performance. Keep it up."

"Is that all?" The host pressed.

Jiang Qing knew she wanted him to say more. Two or three lines of commentary had no dramatic edge at all, and the production team clearly hadn't put in all this effort to let things end so quietly.

He thought for a moment, then smiled politely and said, "Lin Xun, what an extraordinarily wonde... wonderful treasure you are! Stunning looks paired with in... incomparable ability, this performance simply must be preserved and cherished in all our hearts! Right now I have but one wish, to compose a verse in your honor."

Lin Xun's gaze was calm and unhurried, watching the person beneath the stage lights, now deep and still, now vivid and bright. His eyes carried a smile, and he said with a serene composure, "Please."

"Moonlight before the bed so clear, Lin Xun has no equal here.

I lift my gaze toward the moon so bright, and every maiden's heart takes flight."

The audience: !!!

Absolute madman.

The director was laughing. This episode was going to go viral.

The audience was laughing. Jiang Qing had clearly lost his mind.

The host Du Yuening smiled and asked Lin Xun what he thought of Jiang Qing's praise and poem.

Lin Xun: What beautiful Chinese.

He considered for a moment. "You're right."

Jiang Qing: ......

Smiling on the surface. Cursing internally.

You really are the shameless one here.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.content:
When the time came for the final vote to decide the winner, the deciding round came to Jiang Qing.

He looked helplessly at the other two teachers. "This is too hard to decide. Can you help me out?"

"No." Su Hongru said cheerfully.

"Hmph, heartless."

He turned back, his gaze shifting back and forth between Lin Xun and Xu Jiacheng.

In truth, the answer had been clear from the start, but for the sake of the show he had to make a performance of deliberating for a while.

Although Xu Jiacheng had performed without any obvious mistakes, she had lacked a certain commanding presence. The part near the end where they encountered the pregnant woman was the most glaring, where the female lead's toughness hadn't come through, and she'd come across more like a young girl who had simply been hurt.

Lin Xun, on the other hand, had kept his expression continuously shifting throughout the transitions between scenes, giving the audience a window into the psychological changes of his character as they unfolded.

Taking everything into account, along with what the production team was going for, he pressed the selection button.

"Lin Xun, congratulations!" Du Yuening announced the result happily.

Worthy of her beloved Lin Xun!

Somewhere in the audience sat a cluster of Lin Xun's fans, who upon hearing the news let out a breath of relief they'd been holding, and broke into their chant, "Lin Xun, Lin Xun, one of a kind!"

Next came Lin Xun's choice of mentor. The other two had already been selected.

Jiang Qing said, "Come on then, the time has come for your most difficult decision."

Lin Xun smiled faintly. "Then I'll choose Teacher Jiang Qing. Actually, the reason I came here was because of Teacher Jiang."

Jiang Qing: "How so?"

"I wanted to hear Teacher Jiang praise me in person. And it really does feel refreshing."

Jiang Qing: ...... This person needs his head examined.

In the hearts of the Lavender fans, however, Lin Xun's image grew a few sizes taller in that instant!

Of all the people Jiang Qing had publicly criticized, who had ever dared to go straight up to Jiang Qing's face, perform his own work in front of him, and come away with actual praise?

Only their Lin Xun!

The director was deeply gratified. Inviting Jiang Qing had been the best decision he had ever made!

The upper half of the recording wrapped up, and there was a thirty-minute dinner break before the lower half began at five-thirty, covering the mentor-versus-contestant PK rounds.

Jiang Qing returned to the green room to find the bento boxes already waiting. Three people, six dishes, one soup.

He snapped his chopsticks apart, then paused, and said, "Go get Lin Xun and bring his food here too. He's by himself and won't be able to finish it all."

Sang Yi headed out at once, and ten minutes later came back carrying a bag of bento boxes, with Lin Xun following behind her.

Lin Xun walked in with easy composure, took the only empty seat at the table, and said to the room without missing a beat, "Hello, everyone."

Shu Tong smiled and nodded. "Hello. I'm Shu Tong, Jiang Qing's manager. And this is his assistant, Sang Yi."

Jiang Qing was already swiftly opening Lin Xun's bento boxes. They all needed to eat fast.

He chewed a few bites, then asked across the table, "What do you think of your own performance?"

"Pretty good."

"......"

Jiang Qing kept eating, and seeing how completely relaxed the other person was, couldn't stop himself from asking, "Have you looked at our scene for the PK round?"

"As it happens, I've seen this film. I don't actually watch that many."

"Then how did you end up in the entertainment industry."

Lin Xun answered without a trace of self-consciousness. "Didn't you say I descended from the immortal realm? I suppose I landed right in the entertainment industry, and before I knew it the hearts of all the young ladies were in an uproar."

Right, there's no having a conversation with this person.

How is he even more shameless than me?

Sang Yi slid her chair back a bit to get further away from these two unhinged people.

Shu Tong, finding Lin Xun surprisingly approachable, probed gently, "Why haven't you signed with a management company? I'm just curious. No other agenda, and feel free not to answer."

Lin Xun started to organize his thoughts.

Jiang Qing answered for him, "Why else. He banged his head on the ground when he descended from the immortal realm, scrambled his brains."

Shu Tong: "......"

Sang Yi buried her face in her bowl. "Pfft."

Lin Xun: "You know too much."

The bickering aside, both of them finished eating at top speed and started the second round of recording.

Scripts in hand, they went into the rehearsal room. All four corners had cameras set up, and two more camera operators were inside with handheld rigs.

Lin Xun's earlier performance onstage had been the tear-jerking scene, but now they had to perform a slapstick absurdist comedy, which was actually harder in some ways.

The other two pairs were each still doing scenes with high emotional tension and strong dramatic conflict, while their scene had been chosen by the audience.

A large screen had displayed four options, and the audience, in the spirit of watching the fun unfold, had enthusiastically voted for this particular film on their behalf.

Jiang Qing personally didn't mind, but as far as competition went, comedy was never going to be as memorable as something emotionally heavy and thematically weighty.

Lin Xun, however, minded even less than he did. Whatever the audience chose, he would go with.

"Which role do you want to play, or do you have any thoughts on this scene?" Jiang Qing asked.

Lin Xun said, "No preference. You choose first."

Jiang Qing scratched his head. Wouldn't most contestants proactively go for the role that gave them a stronger shot at winning?

He considered for a moment. "Then you'll play Bai Wuchang."

It was an interesting character, and a crowd favorite.

The scene they were performing was from "A Fine World," a classic 90s absurdist comedy film from Hong Kong, packed with big names.

The story followed Bai Wuchang, who after spending tens of millions of years in the underworld suddenly felt the place was a little stifling, and went around asking people where there might be somewhere fun to go.

A crowd of wandering souls told him there was a paradise in this world, a place called the human realm.

Bai Wuchang was thoroughly bewildered. "I've been to that place. There's nothing fun about it. It's pitch black."

"You can go during the day and have a look! Just make sure you're not discovered!"

Long story short, after a series of disguises and a prolonged chase through the underworld, Bai Wuchang finally made it to the human realm.

But his appearance terrified the ordinary folk. His clothing was bizarre, a long white robe with long black hair, his complexion so pale it looked otherworldly, and his whole demeanor just entirely dejected.

At this point, a man dressed in black appeared, a hero who would not stand by and do nothing. He lopped off the long tongue hanging out of Bai Wuchang's mouth.

Bai Wuchang: QAQ

The man in black then took him to get a new outfit, making him look just like everyone else. The only drawback was that he was far too pale.

So pale that people kept mistaking him for a pretty young lady, and kept trying to drag him off to be their bride, a village tyrant's wife, a wealthy elder's wife, a general's wife, the empress......

Bai Wuchang decided the human realm was absolutely not delightful!

He wanted to go to heaven! He hadn't been there yet!

But the man in black said heaven was out of reach, unless he performed one good deed each day.

So Bai Wuchang came up with the idea of helping out the village tyrant, the wealthy elder, the general, and the emperor, by taking turns serving as their wife for one day each. Wasn't that a good deed a day?

And so he went......

On the very first night he was rescued from the tyrant's stronghold by the man in black, and the two of them sat on top of a mountain contemplating life and engaging in a deep philosophical exchange on the meaning of human existence.

The scene Jiang Qing and Lin Xun were to perform was exactly that one: exaggerated physicality, wild expressions, a flood of rapid-fire and absurdist dialogue.

"You go ahead and run through your lines. I'll go take a look at the filming location."

He walked over to the set and said hello to the director, climbed up onto the artificial mountain to find the right spot, then moved around to a few different positions, working with the director to adjust the placement of the cameras.

Performance on a stage and this kind of scene filming called for very different things. He needed to make sure every detail and expression would be captured on camera.

Once the positions were set, he went over the shot list with the director, offered a few of his own ideas, then handed the floor over to them.

He went back to the rehearsal room to find Lin Xun sitting quietly in his seat, looking over the script.

"How's it going?"

"More or less done."

"Done? Already?!" He couldn't believe it.

Lin Xun smiled modestly. "I tend to pick things up very quickly."

Jiang Qing: "Is that so? Then let's see you pick up a gymnastics routine. Something simple, just a Thomas flair into a handstand with a 180-degree turn, come down, then a Thomas with a 90-degree turn, come up into a handstand, and land in a straddle support. Go ahead."

Lin Xun: "......"

He conceded defeat. Back to running his lines it was.

chapters.title: Top-Grade Finest Flattery
chapters.content:
Jiang Qing knew this film's dialogue by heart. It had grown up with their generation, and he had watched it more times than he could count.

The two of them started running through the lines. Two passes in, and Jiang Qing had to admit he was genuinely impressed.

Not a single word off!

He gave credit where it was due, with full enthusiasm. "You're so good, so good."

"High praise, considering you only watched one or two run-throughs yourself."

"Then I'm pretty great too."

Jiang Qing stood up, called in the performance coach, and had them observe and give guidance on the physical and action elements.

They started doing formal run-throughs. The first time they just walked through the blocking and said the lines out loud.

Pretty easy, Lin Xun thought.

He was quickly disabused of that notion.

Jiang Qing's demands rose with every single pass. The first run only required that the positions be right and the lines come out. The next had to include rich, full emotion. The one after that allowed for no errors even in the smallest physical details, while at the same time showing no visible sign of performing.

Jiang Qing didn't scold anyone, only said "again" and "again" and "again," which built up its own particular kind of pressure.

Lin Xun's relaxed attitude gradually shifted to something heavier, and he could only accompany him through the scene again and again.

Two hours later, Jiang Qing finally let him rest.

Both of them simply sat down on the floor. Lin Xun pulled out a tissue and wiped the sweat from his forehead, then held out a few more sheets.

Jiang Qing's cheeks were faintly flushed from the exertion, and his lips were moist and vivid after a drink of water. The hair at the edges of his face was damp, his style well past disheveled.

Lin Xun stepped out and borrowed a fresh hair tie from the makeup team, then handed it to him.

Jiang Qing bit down on the hair tie, and with practiced ease swept the hair back from his face. The refined delicacy of his features was laid completely bare.

Lin Xun asked out of curiosity, "Doesn't long hair get in the way?"

"It does."

"Then why do you keep it?"

Jiang Qing pinched the hair tie and twisted it up in a flash, and said, "For work. It makes styling easier."

Lin Xun understood. Every role was different, so was the look, and having long hair made it much easier to style accordingly.

"Do you really love acting?"

"Of course. Don't you?" Jiang Qing turned the question back to him.

Lin Xun found himself momentarily unable to answer.

In that moment, he reflected deeply once again on his own attitude. Someone like Jiang Qing, who had every strand of his hair prepared and ready for the sake of acting, was the one who could truly claim to be passionate about it.

He only saw it as something to do with his time. It had been out of sheer boredom that he had agreed to Yang Meng's earlier request and taken a role in a drama, and honestly, he had barely watched it himself.

When it came to acting, he felt nothing in particular. In truth, he couldn't really say he liked much of anything.

When would he ever find something he loved the way Jiang Qing loved acting?

Jiang Qing noticed his hesitation and clapped him on the shoulder. "Enjoy it. You'll find the joy in it. Especially when you can experience another person's entire life, doesn't that feel new and surprising?"

"New and surprising?"

"Yes, you were playing Bai Wuchang this whole time. Don't you think he's kind of lovable?"

"Lovable, sure. But he's also genuinely a little dense."

For some reason that landed right on Jiang Qing's funny bone, and he started laughing, that distant look in his eyes softening and dissolving, replaced by amusement he couldn't keep in.

He laughed for a while, then noticed he was the only one, which was a bit awkward.

He immediately composed himself and assumed the proper air of a mentor. "In truth, you haven't really gotten into character at all. You've only been performing. You're probably still sitting there thinking, this Bai Wuchang is really a bit of an idiot."

Lin Xun: "...... How did you hear my inner thoughts?"

"Ha ha ha." Jiang Qing's funny bone was struck again.

After a good while he finally said, "Don't apply normal, rational thinking to him. If you go by real-world logic, his very existence wouldn't be possible. Try to imagine someone who has spent tens of millions of years in the underworld. He never saw a dinosaur, never saw an airplane or a ship or a train, and never had a phone he could shake to find people nearby. His life is pitiable in the extreme...... So when he arrives in the human realm, whatever reaction he has wouldn't be surprising at all."

"What a rough deal." Lin Xun said with genuine pity, but in his mind a blurry white figure was beginning to take shape.

"Use the break to think a bit more about his chain of reactions...... and you'll roughly start to understand what kind of person he is. Then the performance will feel much more natural."

In the rehearsals that followed, Jiang Qing could clearly feel Lin Xun changing. Certain movements were no longer stiff and awkward.

He let his attention drift for a moment too long, and the next instant, his wrist was seized in a firm grip.

The next thing he knew, he was flat on his back on the floor with a thud, both hands above his head, pinned down by a pair of large hands.

He looked up at the person looming over him, jaw set taut, chiseled angles sharp, but something guileless and searching flickering in his eyes. "Confess. Who exactly are you?"

Jiang Qing blinked.

Getting no response, Lin Xun dropped his gaze to look at him, eyes meeting eyes, and his throat moved involuntarily.

"That's the angle! Right there!" Jiang Qing said with delight.

Lin Xun: ?

"Come down a little more. Drop your head a little lower."

"...... Teacher Jiang," Lin Xun said, whole body tensing, "isn't this going a bit far?"

"What do you mean far! Hurry up. There's a fixed camera mounted on the artificial mountain, and the closer we are, the more clearly our expressions will read on it."

Lin Xun lowered himself slightly, holding the awkward position without daring to move, genuinely afraid that if he dropped his head even a fraction he might accidentally close the distance in an entirely different way. He said with utmost sincerity, "Teacher Jiang dedicates a great deal to his art."

"Not as much as you. You've already given your body to art."

Jiang Qing said meaningfully, looking downward, though unfortunately the angle didn't allow for a view of the rear.

Lin Xun followed the direction of his gaze and went rigid for a moment, his expression flickering.

He immediately released his hands and stood up, turning his back to Jiang Qing and saying with an awkward little laugh, "Teacher Jiang, shall we continue?"

Jiang Qing now had a perfectly unobstructed view.

Wow. No wonder Yang Meng was willing to pour so many resources into this. Truly top-grade finest quality.

"Let's continue." He said.

There were forty minutes left. They went to the makeup room to get into costume.

The makeup artist handed them one outfit each. One black, one white.

Three layers in total. Jiang Qing finished changing and sat down with the makeup artist to discuss the look.

After a while, Lin Xun still hadn't come out. Jiang Qing went to the changing room door and said, "How much longer? Pick up the pace."

"I can't quite figure out how to put this on. Could you help?"

Before he could reply, Lin Xun had already pulled the door open. The white T-shirt was on, with a loose, flowing white outer robe draped over it.

Before Jiang Qing even got a word out, Lin Xun said first, "You look...... quite good in that."

It was just a simple black outfit, a length of cloth tied at the waist cinching in a slender figure, the frame tall and lean. His face was clean without a trace of artifice, all his hair pulled back at the nape of his neck, with a few soft, curling wisps of hair falling at his temples.

The only thing breaking the beauty of the picture was the pink hair clip perched on top of his head.

Lin Xun found himself looking a moment too long, and then something pressed firmly against his chest.

Jiang Qing withdrew his hand, stepped inside and closed the door, and said with irritation, "Hurry up and get dressed. Who do you think you are, standing there like the village idiot gawking at the entrance?"

Lin Xun bit back a smile and cleared his throat. "Take a look, is this knot tied right?"

As he spoke, he tugged at the thin lace cord on the inner robe, wound it around his waist, but couldn't seem to get it to tie with the other cord no matter how he tried.

A pair of hands reached forward, took hold of his cord and started over, fingers nimble and quick, finishing in no time.

Jiang Qing looked up, switched on his condescending mode. "Hopeless. Can't even do this."

Lin Xun looked at the smug face and willingly played along. "You're right, I'm just terrible."

And then he watched the corner of Jiang Qing's eye curve up just a little further.

This person was far too easy to please. Lin Xun couldn't help adding one more line. "Not nearly as clever as that quick little brain of yours."

The words had barely landed before even the corner of Jiang Qing's mouth, which he'd been holding carefully still, slowly and quietly turned upward.

Lin Xun: ...... Cute.

chapters.title: You're Being Indecent
chapters.content:
Jiang Qing handed him the remaining two pieces of clothing one by one, mouth going the entire time. "Just do it the same way I just showed you. I demonstrated it in person. If you still can't figure it out after that, take the decoration hanging on your neck and throw it away. Useless."

Lin Xun listened to his stream of commentary and pulled on the final layer, then reached back and felt around. "Feels like something odd got in here."

Jiang Qing glanced over. There was a faint bulge at the back. He reached in directly through the collar at the back.

Lin Xun's body went rigid for just a moment. "You're being indecent."

"......"

Jiang Qing fished out a belt cord that had somehow gotten caught and tossed it onto him. "I could be wielding a blade or a sword or kneading mud, and I still wouldn't be making any kind of move on you."

"Why not?" Lin Xun felt genuinely deflated.

Jiang Qing had just opened his mouth when he suddenly realized he'd put his foot in it again. He met the other person's eyes and said with a stiff smile, "Because. I'm. Not. Worthy.

If Yang Meng beat him to death for it, now that would really be dying for nothing.

He took out his phone and checked the time. "Hurry up, we don't have much time left."

"Alright." Lin Xun fastened his belt cord in two or three quick motions and pulled the door open. "Let's go, Jiang Qing."

Jiang Qing paused slightly, and looked at Lin Xun standing by the door.

The strong light from outside came pouring in. Half of Lin Xun's body was in shadow, and his already fair complexion, caught in the backlighting, looked even paler.

White robes. A tall, considerable frame. He really did carry a faint suggestion of Bai Wuchang about him.

Only the hairstyle was far too contemporary.

"Come on, come on." Jiang Qing was a little impatient to see him in full costume and character, and grabbed Lin Xun by the arm to go running off to the makeup room.

Lin Xun dropped his gaze, watching the hand. Then he looked up again at the hair clip on top of Jiang Qing's head. He nearly laughed out loud.

At that moment, from somewhere around the corner to the right, a person came bursting out and came sprinting toward them. He was clearly about to crash right into Jiang Qing.

Lin Xun gripped his arm hard and stepped aside with a sharp pull, shielding him against himself.

Jiang Qing got a fright, and looked at the person who had come running. It was Gao Yuanqiao.

"Why are you running?"

Gao Yuanqiao bent over trying to catch his breath, and immediately bowed to apologize. "I'm sorry, forgive me. Teacher Su told me to run a couple laps to work up a sweat."

Jiang Qing thought of the role Gao Yuanqiao was playing, an athlete, and said, "Then keep running. Don't just run, keep something in your mind while you do. Think about your purpose. And watch where you're going."

"Yes, yes, I'm sorry." Gao Yuanqiao wiped his face with his sleeve, looked up at the two of them for a moment, and paused. "Senior Jiang, you two......"

Jiang Qing followed his line of sight and turned his head. Lin Xun's hand was still firmly holding onto his arm, and he himself was, by any measure, fully enclosed within Lin Xun's grasp.

The position was decidedly peculiar.

He was just about to pry that hand loose when Lin Xun let go naturally, and said, "We almost had an accident there."

Gao Yuanqiao apologized again, profusely. "Sorry, I'm really sorry."

Jiang Qing: ......

What a timid little apology machine.

After sending Gao Yuanqiao on his way, he brought Lin Xun quickly back to the makeup room, where the two of them sat in a row waiting for their turn.

The makeup artist walked over and smiled. "Jiang Qing, you've pushed my clip all out of place."

"Hm?" Jiang Qing touched his head and sure enough found a little pink clip sitting there.

When he had been talking with the makeup artist earlier about the look, she had clipped up some of his stray hairs to check the overall face shape.

He instinctively glanced sideways at Lin Xun, privately wondering whether his image as a tall, powerful, imposing man had been irreparably damaged.

For a male artist, the vibe had to be airtight!

Lin Xun caught his look and gave a quiet smile. "Very cute."

Jiang Qing: "......"

You're the cute one! Your whole family is cute!

So infuriating.

Using the break between makeup stages, Jiang Qing said, "Lin Xun, let's run lines."

Lin Xun decided he had been paired with a workaholic, and started right in from memory. "Why can't I be their wife? I can help them fulfill their wishes. I'm happy, they're happy, isn't that a good deed all around...... Look at those stars, how beautiful. The underworld has none of them...... My old friend, I'm getting hungry. You've gotten rid of all the chicken legs I smuggled from the banquet. Unforgivable......"

The instant he opened his mouth, Jiang Qing was right there with him. "Listen to me, you are a man, and so are they. Don't ask me such a stupid question!...... The stars may be beautiful, but they hang in the sky, and this is not the place that belongs to you...... Don't say another word to me about chicken legs! Now I'm hungry too......"

This was the most demanding segment of the scene. Both of them had to fire dialogue simultaneously at high speed, with lines that jumped all over the place, catching each other's words here and there, while the physical acting, facial expressions, and emotional layers all had to be spot on without looking like acting.

At the end, when Bai Wuchang could no longer win the argument with words, he extended two fingers and pressed them into both nostrils of the man in black, flipping him to the ground, and won the battle of words by pure cheating.

While speaking his lines, Jiang Qing kept his eyes on the mirror beside him, watching the other person's expressions as they changed.

The run-through ended. He said, "You have the lines down, but you're not quite cute enough yet. Bai Wuchang is an endearingly lovable person. It's not just about the expressions. You feel like a grown-up doing an impression of a small child. There's comedy there, but no cuteness."

Lin Xun asked with amusement, "Then how does one be cute?"

"...... Let me just demonstrate." Jiang Qing coughed once. He waited for Lin Xun to look toward his own reflection in the mirror, then loosened up his face, exhaled slowly.

The next second, he was staring straight ahead, eyes wide and genuinely guileless, his voice completely saturated with puzzlement at the very nature of the world. "Why can't I be their wife? I can help them fulfill their wishes! I'm happy, and they're happy too...... "

Lin Xun stared at him in astonishment. This devil had memorized even his own lines.

And yet, just by adding a handful of particles here and there, the person in the mirror came across as genuinely innocent, genuinely lovable, with just the faintest touch of a Cantonese lilt.

Honestly speaking, he had only agreed to this show because Jiang Qing seemed interesting, and because a new plan had just conveniently come together, so he had said yes to this so-called competition.

But in this moment, he suddenly felt that he had made the right call coming here.

Seeing him fall into thought, Jiang Qing assumed he was being hard on himself, and tilted his chin up. "You don't need to copy me either. The best approach is to go experience it yourself, feel the character's joys and sorrows. Believe in his existence. Trust that everything he does is real and necessary. That's what method acting is."

"Take Gao Yuanqiao, for contrast, he's an example of technical acting. He has a solid foundation, strong in all the basics, voice projection, stage presence, physical control. He can manage all the fine details across the whole emotional range. There's a reliable, polished format to it. But once he's locked himself inside that format, breaking out of it is hard. He lacks the kind of intuitive spark you have."

Lin Xun quietly filed this away.

They ran through the lines a few more times, and Jiang Qing made a curious discovery: Lin Xun's ability to absorb and apply was far better than he had expected. With every run-through he was making adjustments, and each time it was noticeably better than the last.

At this rate, Lin Xun had every bit of what it took to make it to the top.

But why, then, had Lin Xun's abilities in his past life been so oddly uneven?

When their hair and makeup was finished, the two of them looked each other over.

Jiang Qing: "Not bad."

Lin Xun: "Pretty good."

Both went quiet at once.

The makeup artist couldn't help herself. "What do you mean not bad, pretty good. You look incredible! Oh my goodness, can I take a photo? I am obsessed with these looks!"

The corner of Jiang Qing's mouth relaxed. The corners of Lin Xun's eyes curved.

The makeup artist fished out her phone, praising them the whole time. "You two are made for ancient costume! Gorgeous, I think I'm going to faint! Look at the camera, let me capture this beauty for posterity!"

Click.

She took over a dozen in a row and realized they had unconsciously shifted poses between shots!

These two...... surely they weren't...... this vain?

Someone knocked at the door from outside, telling them it was time. Jiang Qing adjusted the wig, turned and headed out. "Let's go, Xiao Bai."

"Hey, hold on, Xiao Lao Hei."

The makeup artist walked to the doorway and watched them go, phone in hand.
