He typed dismally to Shu Tong: "Tong-jie, I want to report them."

"There's nothing you can do about this."

"Then let the subject matter sort it out."

He sent a message to the subject matter: "Your fans have built a super topic. Aren't you going to do something about it?"

Lin Xun: "What super topic? Have they fallen for someone else behind my back?"

Jiang Qing: "Seeker Fan Club. Go see for yourself."

There was no reply from that end for a long time. He opened Weibo to check on things, and the moment he entered the main feed, saw the most popular post: nine photos of him and Lin Xun together.

And just now, Lin Xun had gone and liked it.

The Lavenders: SHOCKED FROM HEAD TO TOE!!

Jiang Qing: ???

Good grief.

chapters.title: The Race
chapters.content:
The Lavenders were completely thrown.

Okay, they were here minding their own business shipping this CP, and their idol comes and likes it. What does that mean?

Official endorsement? Dropping hints?

It was a little exciting, but by doing this, hadn't he taken away the whole process of getting to enjoy the slow burn? Was he just skipping the line and sending them straight to the wedding?

And besides, the super topic had just been created. The ranks hadn't even had time to swell yet. What was he doing showing up personally to hit like before the fanclub even got off the ground?

This kind of move had to be unprecedented for any CP fanbase.

They'd shipped plenty of pairs before, but this kind of behavior from the subject himself was a first.

For a moment, excitement and bafflement filled every CP fan's heart simultaneously.

Then a minute later, their idol actually posted in the super topic himself.

Lin Xun: [What is this place for?]

Everyone: ...

So the man had been out there on the internet and ended up in the wrong place. That was all.

Well then, since that's how it is, don't blame us for what comes next.

"This is where your fans gather, oppa! This is a place full of love and peace, where we shed tears for the beautiful friendship between you and Teacher Jiang!"

"This is a cultural square where countless talented writers, artists, photographers, videographers, and editors come together to explore the true nature and philosophy of love!"

"This is a harmonious and welcoming space, self-sustaining and full of warmth. Our one and only goal is to protect both you and Jiang Qing. As long as you two are well, we are content. May your bond endure forever!!!"

Lin Xun was quite moved. These fans were truly something special.

He'd always heard fan communities were difficult to manage. But these seemed perfectly organized, disciplined, and willing to look after Jiang Qing as well. They were practically a group of little angels.

He found himself wanting to share this discovery with Jiang Qing, which was a shame since Alipay was inconvenient for chatting.

He'd really need to get that WeChat after all. A phone number would be even better.

On the other side, Jiang Qing stared at this fool's post and fell into deep contemplation.

Perhaps Lin Xun was just genuinely not very bright.

Come to think of it, he had given only an email address as contact information. He probably used drift bottles to chat with people online for all anyone knew.

Jiang Qing ignored the post about praising his fans and replied directly: "Go cancel your like, delete the post, and have Yang Meng get someone to handle this properly. Don't give the marketing accounts any material to work with."

Two days later, Jiang Qing was still in the middle of a dream when Sang Yi called.

"Light-ge, the racing club is having a friendly match this afternoon! You promised to take me."

When did he promise that?

He thought about it. Probably before the rebirth.

"The match is this afternoon and you're calling now?"

"I was afraid you'd forget."

Jiang Qing hung up and went back to sleep.

Watching racing was one of his few genuine hobbies. He sometimes even suspected that all those years of watching had eventually made him want to show off on a mountain road, which had cost him his life. Even so, he still wanted to go.

After lunch, Sang Yi came to pick him up.

He was a lifetime member of the club, with one of the best viewing seats, just twelve spots, leather sofas, drinks and refreshments provided.

Dozens of race cars were lined up on the track, drivers suited up and waving to the audience. As far as the eye could see, it was a zone of pure masculine energy.

Completely uninteresting to Jiang Qing, and even more irrelevant to Sang Yi.

Such a young woman, no interest in men, but identical interests to most men.

Jiang Qing felt compelled to ask with some concern: "Yi-yi, maybe... you like women?"

"Hm??" The noise outside was loud, and Sang Yi leaned in with one ear turned toward him, but her eyes never left the track. She did a full sweep and grabbed Jiang Qing's arm. "Look, Liu Yang is over there!"

Liu Yang was a well-known professional driver who had won plenty of awards. Both of them admired him. His technique was skilled and his control precise, with a signature flourish in the final sprint that everyone loved to watch.

In the past, Jiang Qing would have yelled "Lay it on thicker" at a moment like this. But now, watching the cars tensed up and ready to go, he silently thought: please be safe.

The starting gun cracked. The brilliantly painted cars launched forward in a pack, drifting and sliding, tires shrieking against the asphalt, the roar of high-powered engines tangled with the whistle of turbos, and the crowd outside was completely electrified.

The whole venue erupted. Sang Yi was beside herself. "It's a friendly match, so there aren't many pros here. Probably Liu Yang again."

Jiang Qing nodded.

"I wouldn't be so sure." A voice from behind cut in. They both turned.

The man behind them wore a fitted suit, hair swept back, his bearing and presence entirely at odds with the boisterous crowd.

He smiled at them. "Jiang Qing. What a coincidence."

"Mm." Jiang Qing was mildly surprised to run into Yang Meng here of all places, but more than that he was curious about what had just been said. "Why do you say that? Is there a dark horse this time?"

Yang Meng nodded and even threw in a wink.

That alarmed him enough that he immediately turned back around. This little man and his winking.

Just then, the crowd erupted. He fixed his eyes on the track. Car number three had just pulled off a beautiful drifting overtake around a bend and was heading straight for Liu Yang's number eight.

Sang Yi latched onto Jiang Qing's arm in excitement. "Who is number three!"

Everyone wanted to know, but this was a friendly match. Not all names had been registered. Whoever wanted to give their name did, whoever didn't didn't. After checking the list twice, they couldn't find a match. There was one person missing from the list.

Then came the final sprint. Number three caught up to number eight.

The crowd went wild. Liu Yang had dominated this club's races for two years. People came to watch him show off, nothing more. No one had expected to see someone actually threatening his position.

"Go number three! Pass Liu Yang!"

"I swear if number three wins I'm buying a lottery ticket today!"

"Liu Yang is pulling out his signature move!"

On the track, the two cars ran side by side. Number eight surged, cut at an angle, and used his rear end to block the other car's path, then swiftly shifted direction to cut again.

It was a dangerous move. If the car behind failed to brake in time, it would run right into him. But Liu Yang had never lost control, because his speed was always fast enough to change course before the other car reached him. That was his "dragon's tail."

Then, in a moment when no one was quite expecting it, the car behind used the exact same technique.

From the audience's perspective, it was like watching a perfectly matched pair performing identical movements in sync. How fast did you have to be to keep up with Liu Yang's rhythm?

The roar of the crowd practically lifted the roof.

Approaching the finish line, Liu Yang gritted his teeth, the engine screamed, and his car punched through the line.

His hair under the helmet was soaked. He'd barely exhaled in relief when something struck him as wrong.

He spun around. Car number three had stopped in the area just before the finish line.

The entire venue went silent in shock.

What on earth was that?

Yang Meng had been mid-applause. He lowered his hands and laughed. "Typical. Still can't let go."

Jiang Qing turned and asked, "You know him?"

At that, Sang Yi was staring at Yang Meng too, her beautiful eyes wide with admiration and curiosity, completely unfiltered.

Yang Meng paused, looked at Sang Yi. "And you are?"

Jiang Qing narrowed his eyes.

Yang Meng quickly looked away. "Come on, I'll take you to meet him."

Liu Yang climbed out to collect his trophy, eyes never leaving the tall figure of number three's back. He asked a staff member, "Who is that?"

"Ah, he asked us not to reveal his name or get him on camera. Said he didn't want his family to find out he was here and get an earful."

Liu Yang: To hell with getting an earful, I want to give him one right now.

In the back room.

Yang Meng and Jiang Qing sat across from each other, but Yang Meng kept glancing over at Sang Yi. "So this is your assistant I've been hearing about?"

More striking in person than he'd expected.

Jiang Qing gave a nod. "Sang Yi, call him uncle."

Yang Meng sputtered. "There's really no need, I'm barely thir-"

"Uncle." Sang Yi always listened to Jiang Qing.

Yang Meng: "..." Fine. Whatever.

Voices drifted in from outside, followed by steady footsteps approaching the door. The door swung open to reveal a man with broad shoulders, a lean waist, and long legs, one hand holding his helmet loosely, backlit by the light outside, a shadow falling across his face. He was looking back over his shoulder, still talking to a staff member.

Jiang Qing's mind went blank, and a single face surfaced rapidly in his thoughts.

A moment later, the man turned and looked into the room.

Jiang Qing: "."

How old are you exactly?

Lin Xun's steps faltered slightly. "Jiang Qing?"

Every last bit of Jiang Qing's charged enthusiasm evaporated on the spot. He thought of his own crash, then of this man's effortless ease out on the track, and felt sour enough to fizz. He stared blankly and said: "Hey."

"How did you end up here?" Lin Xun came and sat down beside him, a faint sheen of sweat at his temples, hair damp at the ends, the heat of the sun outside still clinging to him.

Burning, Jiang Qing thought.

chapters.title: Friends
chapters.content:
Without making it obvious, Jiang Qing shifted a little to the side and asked, "What brings you to racing?"

"Bored. Yang Meng dragged me along." Lin Xun said.

Yang Meng, who had been invisible this whole time, finally felt acknowledged. He offered helpfully: "Right. Lin Xun is an incredible driver. That's actually how we met."

"Oh~" Jiang Qing nodded, his tone laden with implication.

No wonder. With skills like that. He was almost tempted to hire the man to drive him around every day. Suddenly he found himself wondering, idly, what Lin Xun's going rate might be.

Lin Xun set his helmet on the table and stood. "I'll go change."

After he left, Jiang Qing finally let the reality of Lin Xun being car number three properly settle.

Sang Yi, however, hadn't moved on at all. Her eyes were fixed on the door to the changing room, and if Jiang Qing hadn't known Sang Yi's temperament so well, he'd have started to wonder about her.

Yang Meng was, in fact, thinking exactly that.

He looked at Sang Yi with a complicated expression, thinking to himself that Lin Xun really was a hazard to innocent people. Such a pure-hearted girl was already developing inappropriate ideas.

"Since you all know each other, let's head back." Jiang Qing glanced at Sang Yi.

Sang Yi didn't budge. "He's so impressive. Can I get an autograph?"

Oh, was someone about to lose first place in someone's heart.

He said, "I think he doesn't really like signing autographs."

Sang Yi looked at him with pleading eyes.

He sighed, and the moment Lin Xun came out of the changing room, the first thing out of Jiang Qing's mouth was: "Sign something for her, friend."

Lin Xun dried the last of the sweat off with a towel draped over his shoulder, puzzled. "Again? You're not selling these, are you?"

Jiang Qing's eyes drifted evasively. He hadn't sold them, technically, but he hadn't done anything particularly respectable with them either. He pointed to Sang Yi. "She's the one who wanted it."

Sang Yi nodded vigorously, eyes lit up. "May I?"

Yang Meng jumped in: "He really doesn't like sign-"

"Sure."

Yang Meng: "."

Lin Xun rummaged through Yang Meng's bag for a pen and paper, then casually sketched a cute little red panda, and signed his name on its belly.

"Thank you! Why did you draw a panda?" Sang Yi asked.

"Just felt like it. And as a precaution, better not to sign directly on a blank sheet of paper. My apologies."

Jiang Qing raised an eyebrow. Someone who hadn't been in the industry long, yet already had that kind of presence about him.

It was a detail many people overlooked. Ill-intentioned individuals sometimes used the guise of wanting an autograph to get someone's signature on a blank page, which could later be used for fraud or forged contracts.

He thought of the signed email from before, and couldn't help asking, "Why didn't you draw anything on that one?"

"I was tired. Couldn't be bothered."

An airtight reason.

With the autograph secured, Jiang Qing was about to leave with Sang Yi when Lin Xun suddenly stepped in front of him. "Add me on WeChat."

"Why?"

"For next time you want an autograph." Lin Xun said.

"..."

They had run into each other enough times now. It would be awkward to refuse, so Jiang Qing opened his QR code.

A flicker of amusement crossed Lin Xun's eyes. He scanned it quickly. Then, after a moment, he looked at the screen with mild confusion.

A payment page?

Jiang Qing watched him out of the corner of his eye, then couldn't hold back a faint smile.

Yang Meng leaned over to look, getting to witness Lin Xun being caught off guard for once, and laughed out loud.

In the end, the two of them successfully added each other. Lin Xun looked at Jiang Qing's WeChat name.

QYY.

What did it stand for?

He asked directly. Jiang Qing looked perfectly innocent. "Your grandpa Qing," he said pleasantly.

Lin Xun: "...Noted."

He immediately changed his own display name from "Lin" to "LBB," then sent Yang Meng a message.

LBB: Check out my new name.

Yang Meng, who was standing right there, took out his phone, looked at it, rolled his eyes, and asked the obvious question: "What does that stand for?? Your baby?????"

Ridiculous.

Lin Xun: "Your Lin Baba."

Yang Meng: ............

You're really going all in on this.

Yang Meng fumed and changed his own display name to "YZZ," intending to declare himself Yang's ancestor, but Lin Xun got there first.

"Yang Family Idiot. Charmed."

Yang Meng was incensed. He sat down and turned his back to indicate he was very upset.

Jiang Qing didn't entirely understand the dynamic between these two, but quietly admired anyone who could keep a grip on their backer. At the same time, a small, private "pffft" went off in his head.

"We're heading out. Goodbye." Jiang Qing took his assistant and walked toward the exit.

Sang Yi took a few steps and then turned back to ask Lin Xun, "Will you come race again in the future?"

Lin Xun paused. "Hard to say. Depends on time and mood."

Sang Yi nodded with visible disappointment. "Alright. Light-ge really likes car number three. I was hoping we'd get to see you race again."

Jiang Qing's eyes went wide. "When did I say I liked number three?"

Sang Yi: "You did. You even pinched my arm, you were so into it."

Jiang Qing was pained by that, and turned quickly to explain, but catching Lin Xun's expression of complete and unconditional belief, he gave up.

Lin Xun looked down, shoulders moving slightly, then looked up with a smile. "Next time. If I come to race, I'll let you know."

"Yes! Thank you, we love watching you!" Sang Yi said cheerfully, already being pulled along by Jiang Qing.

Just as they reached the door, Jiang Qing stopped. He turned to look at Lin Xun, paused, and said: "Be safe."

Lin Xun tilted his head just slightly, a faint smile in his reply. "I will."

He watched the two of them leave, then turned, only to find Yang Meng's gaze boring into him.

"What are you looking at me like that for? Freak."

Yang Meng was speechless for a long moment before he finally managed to squeeze something out: "You are something else. A known double-standard."

"I'm not. Don't make things up."

"Don't you famously hate signing autographs? I see right through you..."

Lin Xun's hand stilled. "What?"

Yang Meng slapped the table and demanded with righteous indignation: "Did you or did you not just have eyes for the assistant?!"

Lin Xun gave him one withering look. "I'm going home to shower."

"Smells terrible." Yang Meng said dramatically.

Lin Xun stopped. He turned with a genuinely troubled frown. "How bad? Would someone nearby smell it?"

Yang Meng slowly narrowed his eyes. "Interesting. Are you worried the assistant might have caught a whiff?"

Lin Xun threw the towel over his head and walked off. Then something else came to mind. "That apartment in Yishui Bay is available."

"When are you moving in?"

"Not much to move. Probably within the next few days."

Yang Meng took the towel off his head and followed him out the back exit, turning the question over in his mind before landing on the most important one: "There are several properties. Why Yishui Bay specifically?"

Lin Xun touched the area on his chest where the panda brooch would have been, found nothing there, and smiled quietly. "Fate?"

Yang Meng: "Oh, please."

When Jiang Qing got back to the complex, he noticed a moving truck parked downstairs. Workers from a moving company were carrying things in and out in a steady stream.

He went up to the twenty-eighth floor, puzzled, and when the elevator doors opened, found the hallway stacked with large boxes while movers moved in and out of the unit next door.

The building was one elevator to two units. His neighbors were an elderly couple whose children and grandchildren had all settled abroad. When they crossed paths, they'd exchange greetings and sometimes share food.

"Wang-shu, are you moving?" He raised his voice.

Old Wang smiled from the doorway. "We are! The two of us old folks are heading abroad! The kids missed us, they did! Ha ha ha!"

"That's wonderful, the family can finally be together." Jiang Qing listened to the unbroken stream of laughter and knew exactly how happy the man was. He pointed to the boxes in the hallway. "Need any help?"

"No, no, the movers have plenty of hands. Little Jiang, who knows when we'll see each other again." Old Wang said wistfully, giving him a pat on the shoulder.

"You can watch plenty of TV. I'll be right there on your screen."

"Ha, that's true! Oh, and by the way, we found a buyer for the apartment. A young man, very good-looking! Good temperament too. Take care of him when the time comes, maybe you two will become good friends!"

Jiang Qing smiled. "Don't worry. I don't really get along with people my own age."

"Oh, this kid..."

"Little Jiang! You came at just the right time!" Old Wang's wife appeared at the doorway with a beaming smile. "We have so many potted plants we can't take with us. Old Wang picked them out himself, and some of them have even won prizes! Do you want them?"

"I'd love some. I've been eyeing them for a while." Jiang Qing smiled and followed her into the balcony.

The balcony was spacious. Aside from a washing machine and two rocking chairs, it was filled with potted plants of all shapes and sizes.

He carried several pots over to his own balcony. After a few trips, his arms were soft, and he leaned against the railing to rest and chat with Old Wang. There was still a large portion of plants left untouched. Old Wang gave him the door code and told him to hurry and take them before the new tenant moved in.

"I take it you won't be coming back this time?"

"We won't be back. We're too old to keep traveling back and forth." Old Wang waved his hand and looked at Jiang Qing sideways. "Little Jiang, how old are you now? How come you still haven't found someone? Never seen you bring anyone home in all these years."

Jiang Qing said with a laugh, "Would I let you see even if I had? And I'm only two years older than your grandson."

"Ha! My grandson already has a son of his own!"

"Wow, Little Wang's impressive." Jiang Qing rubbed his nose.

Old Wang burst out laughing.

After everything was packed, Old Wang said goodbye to him several times over. They didn't usually talk this much, but now that the moment had really come, he was treating Jiang Qing like his own grandson.

"Little Jiang, take care of yourself. Work hard, and get yourself a son one of these days!"

"Take care."

Jiang Qing smiled and saw him and his wife to the car. Back on the twenty-eighth floor, he looked at the empty apartment next door, sighed, and closed his own door.

Back in his room, he had the nagging feeling he'd forgotten something, but couldn't put a finger on it. He let it go.

Dongying Entertainment office.

A man with shoulder-length hair sat at a wide desk, looking forlornly at the two people across from him. "Minghan, maybe we should just let this go? That endorsement was never really mine to begin with..."

"Let it go? Tang Huan, you're my boy, I said I'd get it for you and I will." Yu Minghan gave him a pointed look, then turned to the other person. "That guy, what's his name, Gao Yuanqiao? Ruihua Entertainment is really pulling out all the stops for him."

The manager beside him adjusted his glasses. "I don't think it's that simple. Who exactly told you that Jiang Qing was after the male secondary lead?"

The reminder brought Yu Minghan back to something he'd been turning over lately. "Someone claiming to be a crew member said it. Said they personally saw Jiang Qing go visit Director Yu, the two of them talking and laughing, and Director Yu asking him if he wanted the part."

"But Director Yu hasn't said a word about recasting even now. The credits have already been announced publicly. If he were replacing someone, it would have happened already. Do you have contact information for this person?"

"I do." Yu Minghan opened WeChat. The last call had gone unanswered, and the person had just added him on WeChat instead. He pulled up the profile and showed it to his manager.

The manager had been in the business for over a decade and kept a sharp memory for the details of the industry. He studied the profile carefully, then the recognition landed. "That's Wang Mingzhi's assistant. He appeared on camera when Wang Mingzhi signed his contract."

Yu Minghan's eyes narrowed, his phoenix eyes cutting with sudden sharpness.

Wang Mingzhi, who had also auditioned for the secondary lead...

So that's how it was. Someone had set their sights on him.

"Do you have Jiang Qing's contact information?" he asked.

"What are you planning to do?"

"Find an ally, obviously." Yu Minghan smiled.

He could easily take Wang Mingzhi down through other channels, but since Wang Mingzhi liked to play dirty from behind the scenes, he'd return the favor. And send a favor to Jiang Qing while he was at it.

Jiang Qing was at the styling department in the company, getting ready for an afternoon recording. After the red panda brooch incident, he had sworn off bringing anything extra onto set.

Once he was dressed, he stepped out to use the restroom. He'd just pulled up his zipper when his phone rang. He put in his Bluetooth earpiece, took the call, and washed his hands.

"Hello, is this Jiang Qing? I'm Yu Minghan." The other party introduced himself.

He paused, then eventually placed the name. The secondary lead in Director Yu's new project. Odd. "Hello. What can I do for you?"

"I heard from someone that you wanted Director Yu's secondary lead role. Is that true?"

"No."

"Alright, I believe you."

Jiang Qing: "..." Your trust comes pretty cheaply.

"Want to guess who told me?" Yu Minghan said playfully.

No reply from the other end. The sound of water stopped, and after a brief pause, a faint laugh came through. "Speak of the devil. What timing."

Yu Minghan: ?

And then, right on cue, he heard Wang Mingzhi's voice on the other end, unpleasant and flat: "Mm."

And then... the unmistakable sound of someone urinating.

He stared blankly. "Man, are you watching him pee?!"

"He's not as impressive as me." Jiang Qing said.

Yu Minghan's jaw dropped.

Wang Mingzhi, unaware that a phone call was happening, heard those words and had a catastrophic loss of aim. Through gritted teeth: "Jiang Qing, what did you just say!"

"It takes real courage to face the harshness of life." Jiang Qing looked at him with genuine encouragement, his tone warm and sincere, as though he truly meant to comfort him.

"Oh for, you're a real piece of work." Wang Mingzhi said with cold contempt. "No wonder you have no friends, with that poisonous mouth and rotten heart of yours. You're pathetic."

Jiang Qing gave a mild smile, dropped one line as he walked away. "Small birds must compensate with big courage."

"I will end you!" It took Wang Mingzhi a few seconds to work out the insult. He started cursing Jiang Qing's entire family tree going back thirty-six generations.

Yu Minghan, on the other end, was laughing so hard his stomach was practically seizing up. "Incredible, my dude. I'm sending you a yacht right now. Who said you don't have friends? Count me in as one..."

"I'm sorry." Jiang Qing cut him off. "If you have something to say, say it. Otherwise I'm hanging up. I'm not dating, not hooking up, not making friends, not drinking."

Click.

Yu Minghan stared at his dark screen. In the stunned silence of his manager and Tang Huan, he slammed the phone on the table and declared with feeling: "I am making friends with you whether you like it or not."

chapters.title: Where Do You Live?
chapters.content:
Wang Mingzhi finished in the restroom, wandered around the company for a while, and didn't find Jiang Qing anywhere. Still seething, he drifted to a corner, pushed open the fire escape door, climbed one floor, and sat at the stairwell landing to smoke.

He was exhaling a long breath and quietly cursing when the door below let out a soft creak and opened.

Probably another smoker. He blew a smoke ring.

But no lighter clicked. Instead came the sound of two pairs of slightly unsteady footsteps, followed by the unmistakable sound of water and a low sound that grazed his nerves.

Well, this was interesting.

He craned his neck out of curiosity and peered down. He could only see two heads of hair.

Two men. Now that was interesting.

Hold on. One of them looked awfully familiar.

He looked harder. One man was being held by the other, and as he turned his face slightly toward this side, his features came into view.

Gao Yuanqiao.

Zhang Lingquan had always told him not to go near Gao Yuanqiao, and he'd gathered there was someone backing him, but as for who exactly...

That thought made him look more carefully at the other man, and when that face finally came into focus, he quietly sat back.

Hell. The young master of Ruihua.

No wonder the resources were so good. He had that kind of backing.

He had glimpsed the young master once when he signed his contract, a man in his early thirties, good-looking, rumored to have several lovers. He hadn't expected Gao Yuanqiao to be one of them.

He lost track of how much time passed, almost starting to wonder if they were still breathing down there. Finally, the two separated and filed out one after the other.

Wang Mingzhi waited a while before making his way back to Zhang Lingquan's office. She was going over his upcoming schedule.

"The new drama the company invested in doesn't start filming for another two months. I think those two months are better spent on a variety or reality show."

He asked, "Is Gao Yuanqiao in the new drama?"

"Yes, he's the third male lead."

Though it was a supporting role, the character was popular, pure and kind with a tragic ending, and was the character book fans felt most for. Whoever played him was bound to break through.

He nodded thoughtfully. "What variety show?"

"'I Am an Actor.' You've seen the ratings and the buzz. Go on it, you won't regret it." Zhang Lingquan said.

Wang Mingzhi just thought of running into Jiang Qing on that show, and his expression soured. But from what the first episode showed, Jiang Qing was putting out nothing but lavish compliments...

"Let me watch a bit more." If Jiang Qing kept up the rainbow praise, he'd go on.

Zhang Lingquan frowned slightly. "Don't wait too long. People are already lining up for this. You might miss your window."

"The second episode airs in three days. I'll give my answer after I watch it."

Third recording session.

Now that the first episode had aired, the audience knew what to expect from Jiang Qing, and the applause started the moment he walked out.

Jiang Qing himself was in an equally good mood. The guests this time were genuinely talented, which made it no effort at all to lay on the praise.

Since his unexpected pivot to playing the good-natured one, the production team had discussed with the other two mentors and assigned Su Hongru the role of the straight critic.

Every time Jiang Qing finished laying on the warmth, Su Hongru would follow with a splash of cold water, and Teacher Wen would finish by soothing the contestants' feelings.

Jiang Qing: "Honestly, if I only go by your deceptively stunning looks, it would be hard for me to imagine that you are this strong. Remaining in supporting roles this whole time is a real loss for the audience. I hope to see you on the big screen in the future!"

Su Hongru: "But your range is narrow. Try branching out into different types of roles."

Teacher Wen summarized: "You're beautiful!"

Jiang Qing: "I love your drama! The moment you appeared, my entire attention was yours. That magnetic pull is nothing short of stunning! And your live performance is flawless. I cannot find a single fault, and if there is one, it must be that your talent makes me envious!"

Su Hongru: "But be mindful of chemistry with your co-stars. Don't get lost in your own performance. Acting is a team effort."

Teacher Wen summarized: "You're wonderful!"

Jiang Qing: "I was completely pulled into the world of this piece. Thank you for such a vivid performance. You made it feel like being there, and showed us what a true moment of theater looks like!"

Su Hongru: "Getting into character is good, but getting out of character is equally important. Always keep the real world separate from the script."

Teacher Wen summarized: "What a drama queen!"

A brief silence fell over the room.

Jiang Qing stepped in to smooth it over: "Teacher Wen, the phrase drama queen has been taken over by internet culture. It's not really a compliment the way it used to be."

Teacher Wen, who clearly hadn't been keeping up with online culture for some time, looked genuinely baffled. "Oh?"

One look at that expression and it was obvious she had no idea. He pointed to himself and redirected: "Teacher Wen, do you think I'm a drama queen?"

"Yes, you are the greatest drama queen I have ever met! I adore you! The future is yours!" Teacher Wen said with sincerity.

The whole room burst into laughter, and even the contestant who had been called a drama queen suddenly felt at peace.

So when Teacher Wen said drama queen, she meant a real, authentic dramatic actor. That actually made sense, even if it still sounded a bit strange.

The recording grew smoother with each session, and the three mentors developed a better and better rhythm with each other.

Jiang Qing was selected by a middle-aged actress whose screen presence had been honed over years of craft. The two of them played neighbors, trading surface pleasantries while underneath they circled and probed and calculated. Sparring with someone of that caliber was genuinely satisfying. He couldn't remember the last time he'd enjoyed himself this much. He only started to feel the tiredness when the recording wrapped.

He got home close to one in the morning, removed his makeup, showered, and only then remembered that tonight was the second episode's broadcast. It had already aired.

But sleep was pulling hard at his eyelids. He couldn't be bothered to sit up and watch, and besides, if Shu Tong hadn't called about anything, it was probably fine. He collapsed into bed.

The next morning, he was woken by sunlight. He groped around on the nightstand until he found the remote and pressed the button. The curtains drew shut automatically.

He rolled over. But there was something on his mind, and sleep wouldn't come back.

He reached over with one hand and grabbed his phone. Squinting at the screen, he found it blurry and confusing.

Wait, was he going nearsighted?

He rubbed his eyes. Once his head cleared a little more, his vision sharpened considerably, and he relaxed. He opened last night's episode.

The first episode had ended on the cliffhanger of his and Lin Xun's performance. The second episode opened right away with the footage from their collaboration.

The moment the main content started, the comments flooded in.

[First!]

[Finally! My legs are asleep from sitting here waiting!]

[The shot of Jiang Qing and Lin Xun together is stunning!]

["The World at Its Finest" is a childhood memory for me! Honestly, this is a hard piece to perform. Get it wrong and it comes out painful to watch.]

[Just this look alone and I'm already gone! The black and white pairing!]

[Haha Lin Xun is so tall but he's eating a chicken drumstick like it's the most adorable thing. Zero brain cells. Precious.]

[My whole impression of Lin Xun was from his domineering CEO role, didn't expect him to handle something this grounded and sweet. I'm a convert.]

[His acting has improved so much! The CEO role was honestly only good for the visuals, no idea how it got popular. But now the performance feels genuinely natural!]

[The person ahead saying what?! You're saying only the face was good? What about the body? What about those hands? Every strand of Lin Xun's hair is good-looking!]

[He's the kind of person where even his tears are pearls and his flattery is limited edition perfume, alright?]

[Jiang Qing directed this well. You could tell from the first episode how invested he was. He's a bit softhearted under the harshness, just needs to work on that.]

[True. Jiang Qing didn't overshadow. Most newcomers would struggle to hold their own opposite him, so that's actually a point in his favor.]

[They're so well matched!]

[The line delivery is great here! So much chemistry!]

[Lin Xun just grabbed him! Go! Get him face to face!]

[Content warning!]

[Lin Xun was sneaking looks at Jiang Qing onstage! Those eyes! I'm dying repeatedly!]

[We slaughter gods and vanquish Buddhas, and the Seeker Fan Club shall see its ship sail into harbor!!!]

[Sisters! Where is the base camp? I'm on my way!]

[Seeker Fan Club, all sisters welcome!]

[CP fans out! Stop tagging this!]

[I'm a regular viewer with no stake in this, and even I'm like... kiss him already!]

[Not my beloved Qing. Finding the joy of fandom all over again. (Wait, why did I say again?)]

[Too short! This left me completely unsatisfied! That's it? Let me rewind and watch again.]

...

The video continued. Jiang Qing kicked off his blanket, took his phone into the bathroom, propped it on the stone ledge beside the mirror, and watched while he brushed his teeth and washed his face.

The second portion of the broadcast was from the most recent recording. It didn't generate quite as much buzz as the first episode, but the contestants got a lot of attention.

He finished changing, sat down for breakfast, and the episode was winding up as he ate, ending on a cliffhanger featuring Su Hongru.

Half an hour later, he put away the dishes, leaned against the kitchen counter, and opened Weibo. Another million or so new followers, a good portion of them with Lin Xun as their avatar, clearly the CP crowd.

The performance clips had been spreading steadily online, especially the one with him and Lin Xun, along with two segments featuring Su Hongru and the contestants.

The second episode's genuinely skilled performers pushed the show's critical reception straight up. The Douban score had climbed from 7.6 to 8.1.

He browsed over to Lin Xun's Weibo page. Good grief, his following was growing faster than anyone's. He was already in the tens of millions.

Quite a few new followers were sporting Jiang Qing as their avatar, which could only mean one thing.

Then a new message notification popped up. WeChat.

LBB: Good morning [sun emoji]

Given that this man was probably someone who communicated via email and drift bottles, Jiang Qing decided to forgive him for the pointless message. He typed back: [cleaver emoji]

Then he went to update Lin Xun's contact name. His finger hovered for a moment, indecisive, before slowly tapping out a few characters: Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!

With an exclamation mark. Non-negotiable.

He was nothing if not steadfast.

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: Question for you.

QYY: ?

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: Where do you live?

QYY: In the hearts of young women everywhere.

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: [social social]

No further messages came from the other side, so Jiang Qing didn't press him about what he'd actually meant to ask. He checked his bank balance, which was fine, better than it had been right after the rebirth, at least.

The show's fee had also come through, the first third of the payment. The rest would arrive once filming was complete. A not-insignificant sum.

Summer break had started. He wondered how the kids in Wutong Village were doing.

He called Shu Tong, set aside a portion of funds, and asked her and Sang Yi to handle the donation arrangements.

"Yi-yi hasn't been back to Wutong in a while either. This is a good chance for her to see the younger kids. Let her stay a few extra days. Pass along my greetings to Principal Sang, I won't be going this time."

Shu Tong said, "Got it. I'll head back as soon as I'm done. Oh, by the way, I heard Wang Mingzhi is going to join 'I Am an Actor.'"

He was genuinely touched. "He's traveling a long way just to hand me his head. The thought is what counts."

He had been supporting the Wutong orphanage for nearly six years, and had always left the logistics to Shu Tong. She kept close tabs on it and kept the finances transparent, giving him a thorough report whenever she returned.

He rarely visited Wutong Village in person. For one thing, it was far, tucked into a small town in the south.

For another, the place was something like a hometown. His grandfather's old house was near the orphanage. But with no one left there, going only ever brought grief.

That afternoon, he finally climbed into the driver's seat. Since the rebirth, he'd always relied on Sang Yi or taxis or his own feet, but with her away for the next few days, he'd have to drive himself.

Besides, after watching Lin Xun's racing, his hands had been itching a bit.

He kept the car at a steady speed and drove out to the suburbs. The streets were empty and wide, so he opened the convertible top and let the wind in, and the tension in his chest gradually eased.

Just then, a motorbike came up alongside him, the rider calling out cheerfully: "Look at you, all flash, convertible sports car, and you're slower than me!"

Jiang Qing laughed back: "Thirty miles an hour, and my heart is free as ever."

He headed out to the villa in the western outskirts for the evening, sorted some things, had dinner nearby, and meandered back to Yishui Bay as the city lights came on.

He settled into the sofa for a while, restless from boredom, and eventually got up to tidy the apartment.

Passing the balcony, his gaze caught the few pots sitting along the railing, and it suddenly came back to him. Old Wang's prize-winning plants were still in the unit next door.

He hadn't been gone many days. There was probably no one in there yet. He had to get them before it was too late.

Old Wang had mentioned the concern about him forgetting and specifically recited the door code. New tenants would change it anyway. He typed it in.

Click. The door opened.

A sliver of light was coming from inside.

Had someone left the lights on when they left?

He pushed the door open and stepped in. Standing in the entryway, he noticed a tea cup on the coffee table and a few scattered objects. Probably things Old Wang had left behind.

He walked over, gathered what was on the table, then found a plastic bag in the drawer and crouched beside the coffee table to sort through things.

He picked up a European-patterned cup and turned it over to look at it. It was quite pretty. A shame to throw it out. It might make a nice decorative piece.

At that moment, a soft click came from somewhere not far away, resonating through the quiet apartment with unusual clarity.

His whole body stiffened. He looked toward the sound, and the bathroom door on his left swung open.

A tall, broad-shouldered man stepped into view, bare from the waist up, lean, with a towel wrapped around his hips, the lines of his torso and abdomen unmistakably defined.

His hair was wet, a single drop of water tracing the column of his throat, catching at his Adam's apple, then continuing its descent with the next swallow.

Both of them froze.

Jiang the Statue: "You, you, you, how are you here?!"

Lin the Statue: "What's going on?"

They spoke at the same time, both equally confounded.

A moment later, Lin Xun walked toward him, one hand pushing his soaking hair straight back from his face, the striking precision of his features coming almost uncomfortably close.

Jiang Qing, misreading the advance as hostile, felt his hand go weak. The cup slipped from his grip and shattered on the floor.

Lin Xun stopped in front of him. His gaze moved over Jiang Qing's face for a moment. Then he crouched down and pinched Jiang Qing's jaw, tilting his face upward.

Jiang Qing pulled back as much as the grip allowed, which wasn't much at all. His eyes were wide open, clear and ignited with indignation. "What are you doing! I'll call the police!"

His cheeks were lightly pinched into a small round shape, his mouth opening and closing, very much like a furious and entirely adorable rabbit.

Lin Xun's lips curved. He spoke with the tone of someone both interrogating and mildly aggrieved: "I just moved in, and here you are showing up at my door in the middle of the night of your own accord..."

His voice carried an ambiguous note. The light from the chandelier stretched both their shadows long across the floor...

He paused for a moment, then pointed to the shattered fragments on the ground, and said with a mild smile: "Just to smash my high-priced auction cup?"

chapters.title: Three Chapters in One
chapters.content:
Lin Xun's head was full of questions. Why are you here? How did you get in? Do you have any idea what could happen, walking into a man's home unannounced in the middle of the night? Are you here to tempt me...

But looking at the other person's expression, which was even more bewildered than his own, he chose the most inconsequential question instead.

Jiang Qing stared at him wide-eyed. Only once Lin Xun let go did he manage to ask faintly: "The cup. How much was it?"

Lin Xun held up his hand. "This many."

Jiang Qing's legs gave out. He dropped to the floor, sat there, and carefully picked up the fragments, trying to fit them back together like a puzzle, muttering under his breath: "It was an accident. I'm so broke... Let me try to piece it back together first."

Lin Xun closed his hand around Jiang Qing's wrist to stop him from moving. "Don't cut yourself."

"This hand is useless now. It betrayed me. Do you want it? You can have it."

Jiang Qing looked at him pitifully, hoping to be let off the hook, but Lin Xun wasn't moved. He swept the shards into the trash and said, "We'll find another way for you to make it up to me."

Jiang Qing: "..."

I was just making a polite gesture! You could at least be polite back!

Wasn't the proper response here something like: it's just a small sum, don't worry about it, as long as you make me happy? That's how every CEO character in every drama handled this kind of thing!

It was all fiction. Every last bit of it. And these fans calling him President Lin. The man was tight as a drum.

Lin Xun collected the remaining shards, came back, and stood above him, looking down for a moment. Then he extended his hand. "Are you planning to spend the night with the floor?"

Jiang Qing looked at those hands, capable and lean. His gaze drifted to the enviable physique, and he felt deeply, personally insulted.

He said nothing and got up on his own.

Lin Xun smiled silently, then composed his expression and asked bluntly: "How did you get in?"

"I typed in the passcode." Jiang Qing mumbled, then looked at him carefully. "Wait, don't tell me you're the new tenant?"

Lin Xun raised an eyebrow. "Yes. You as well?"

Jiang Qing rubbed his face, marveling once again at this inexplicable twist of fate. "I live next door. The previous neighbor asked me to move his plants over. I only just remembered to come back and finish. It didn't occur to me you hadn't changed the code."

While he was explaining, Lin Xun had somehow produced two cups with the same European pattern, poured hot water into both, and offered one to Jiang Qing.

"I see. That was my oversight. I didn't expect him to share the code with anyone."

Jiang Qing took a sip of the warm water without thinking. The tension he'd been holding onto gradually loosened, and he settled onto the nearby sofa, legs crossed, narrowing his eyes slightly. "The cup. You weren't just saying that to mess with me, were you? Was it actually worth that much?"

"You're welcome to check."

That was said so openly and without hesitation that refusing to look it up would make him the fool.

"Auction house, date, and time?"

He pulled out his phone, typed in what Lin Xun told him, and when the page loaded, he counted the digits twice. His hand nearly sent the cup he was holding the way of the first one.

This man's idea of drinking from a cup. Obscene.

He asked faintly: "You buy things this expensive. Does Yang Meng know?"

Lin Xun didn't understand why the topic kept circling back to Yang Meng, but answered honestly: "He knows. Some of it he even gave me." Meaning he made me pay for it.

He didn't say the last part out loud. Restraint was, as ever, his policy. Though much good it seemed to do him, since even without the detail, the other person was already staring at him with an expression of pure, uncomprehending shock.

He cleared his throat. "It's really nothing, compared to..."

Jiang Qing was even more astonished.

He had clearly underestimated Yang Meng. This wasn't someone keeping a pretty dependent. This was someone bankrolling a golden idol.

One willing to spend, one willing to indulge. Truly made for each other.

He looked Lin Xun up and down, trying to work out what was so special about him to justify this level of investment.

His gaze landed on Lin Xun's face. Features this precise and this faultless could, without exaggeration, bring people to their knees.

Then the body. He shed a single private tear of envy.

Tonight, once again, he was a lemon.

Lin Xun noticed the conflicted expression on his face. "What are you thinking about?"

"This water is a bit sour." Jiang Qing gave an awkward smile, set the cup down, and stood. "I should go. You can keep the plants."

"I'll walk you out."

"You can't go out dressed like that."

"I didn't say I was going out."

"...Oh."

Lin Xun stood and followed him. Two steps along, the person in front suddenly turned back. Lin Xun stopped just in time.

"What is it? Reluctant to leave after all?"

Jiang Qing pursed his lips. "That cup, let me transfer the money over when I get back. Give me a card number."

"No need." Lin Xun said.

"Really?!" Jiang Qing looked at him with eyes that had gone a little luminous, thinking of how much that one cup could fund an entire year of Wutong's expenses, and his chest ached just thinking about it.

Just as he was beginning to revise his opinion of Lin Xun, he heard: "I already said we'd settle it another way. I just moved here and I'm not familiar with the area. You can take me around for a bit over the next few days."

Jiang Qing pressed his lips together. His time was precious too. Trading meals and movies and evening walks for a broken cup was an absolute bargain for Lin Xun.

"Fine."

Lin Xun raised an eyebrow. "That's not very enthusiastic. Maybe I should just take the money."

"Not fine at all! Showing you around is the greatest, greatest, greatest joy of my life!" Jiang Qing flashed all eight of his front teeth.

That string of "greatest"s landed well enough that Lin Xun was visibly satisfied. "Wonderful. I'll call on you whenever I like."

"Sure." Jiang Qing turned away, out of view, and rolled his eyes with feeling.

At the door, he raised his wrist to reach for the handle, and a hand reached past him from behind and gripped it first, nearly encircling him entirely in the process.

Jiang Qing went rigid for a moment. "I've got it."

"No trouble. First night in the new place, thank you for coming, Teacher Jiang." Lin Xun smiled pleasantly and opened the door. "Good night."

Jiang Qing opened his mouth, managed an "mm," and went back to his own apartment.

He waited until he heard Jiang Qing's door close, then shut his own, leaned against it, and smiled quietly to himself.

Who would have thought. He'd expected running into each other around the complex to already be a stroke of luck. He hadn't expected to end up as neighbors.

He thought again of the panda brooch and his cousin's ridiculous claim.

Could it really be fate?

Destined to be neighbors?

The next morning, Jiang Qing was still deep in a pleasant dream when the doorbell began to ring, rapid and insistent, one after another.

"Who is it!" he called, muffled, but of course no one outside could hear. Only the ringing answered him.

He threw back the covers, every inch of him radiating cold displeasure, and stalked downstairs to open the door.

Damn Lin Xun.

He squinted. "Did I steal your money or your wife? What gives you the right to do this to me?"

"It's almost ten." Lin Xun was dressed casually. He glanced at his watch. "Early to bed and early to rise makes for a good child."

"Go away." He grabbed the door handle to close it, and a foot slid into the gap with calm, precise accuracy.

Lin Xun didn't seem bothered in the least. He held up the bag in his hand. "Breakfast. Fresh and hot. Want some?"

Jiang Qing rubbed his eyes. The morning irritation began to dissolve. He reached out. "Yes, thanks."

Lin Xun raised the bag slightly out of reach, smiling. "Reciprocity. Won't you invite me in?"

"I could just treat you to breakfast another time."

"No. You broke into my apartment. The least you can do is allow my friendly morning visit." Lin Xun pressed his advantage while Jiang Qing's mind was still slow from sleep. "For the sake of building a harmonious and friendly neighborhood relationship, every one of us has to do our part. You come over, I come over, together we uphold the spirit of community civility."

Jiang Qing, half-awake and not entirely in possession of his critical faculties, let him in. Something felt slightly off, but he couldn't quite pin it.

Ah. This person was better suited to being the Lavish Praise Ambassador than he was.

Lin Xun followed him inside and quietly looked Jiang Qing over from behind. Silk pajamas to mid-calf, bare feet against the floor, head tilted back as he walked, hair falling loosely against his cheek. There was something effortlessly beautiful about it.

"I'll go wash up. Sit for a minute." Jiang Qing led him to the dining table, pulled out a chair, and then felt he was being too generous and nearly pushed it back in.

"Alright." Lin Xun had already sat down, tilting his head back just slightly in Jiang Qing's direction, the corners of his eyes catching what seemed like the warmth of the morning outside. "Go put on some shoes first."

Jiang Qing looked down at his bare feet. His toes curled once. He went to find his shoes, then glanced back at the figure by the floor-to-ceiling window.

Lin Xun was leaning back in the chair, looking around at the apartment, and caught his eye without quite meaning to.

Something stirred. Jiang Qing walked quickly into the bathroom, brushed his teeth, and looked at himself in the mirror.

This stupid Lin Xun, looking this good at this hour of the morning.

In matters of appearance, he could not afford to lose.

He took out the most expensive face wash on the shelf, worked it in thoroughly, and checked his chin in the mirror. No stubble breaking through yet. Good.

He patted his hair into place with a few passes and a bit of styling spray, put together something quick but sharp. Then went to the wardrobe and made his selection carefully, eventually putting on a custom-made set.

Lin Xun had been looking around the living room. The décor was minimal and clean, and the space was open enough that it could be taken in at a glance given the smaller floor plan.

He hadn't expected someone so lively to have such an understated home.

The breakfast had cooled considerably by the time the footsteps came down the stairs.

He turned back, and in spite of himself, paused for a moment.

In less time than it seemed possible, Jiang Qing had put himself together entirely, and even his hair carried a certain studied effortlessness about it.

As he passed by, a faint clean citrus scent drifted over, a welcome counterpoint to the heat of summer.

The behavior was genuinely baffling...

According to one unreliable but enthusiastic source known as a certain Yang, his past companions had varied personalities but shared one curious trait: all of them would rise early to dress and present themselves, hoping to catch a word of praise the moment he opened his eyes.

He swallowed once, and after Jiang Qing sat down, studied him for a moment before offering: "You look very good."

As expected: Jiang Qing blinked once, then tipped his chin up with unmistakable pride, eyes curving warm for just a second before he looked away and turned his attention to the food. The corner of his mouth stayed stubbornly lifted.

Lin Xun was struck into something approaching silence. He kept his face still, but inwardly a wave had moved through him.

He had been surrounded by people who loved him his whole life. He had always maintained a comfortable distance, a kind of indifference to it all. He had never been able to picture sharing his life with any one person, and after a certain point, he'd stopped expecting to find someone who would feel different from the rest.

He'd always thought of himself as someone who ran out of interest quickly. Most things bored him once he'd mastered them. People too, once he felt he understood them well enough.

But Jiang Qing seemed to be different. He kept pulling Lin Xun's attention without trying. It was as though you could never quite determine what he was, which made Lin Xun want to keep finding out.

Right now, he thought, maybe he was starting to understand.

Could Jiang Qing actually...like him?

What was he supposed to do with that?

"You're not eating?" Jiang Qing opened the bag and found both Eastern and Western options inside. Noticing that Lin Xun had spaced out, he asked.

"Hm?" Lin Xun came back to himself. "I already ate. This is for you."

Jiang Qing blinked. "You got it just for me?"

"Yes. For the spirit of community."

Jiang Qing, right in front of him, gave the most theatrical eye roll imaginable.

Lin Xun laughed quietly to himself. Yes, exactly. Sly and cute, then playfully difficult, quietly calculating. This person knew exactly how to catch someone's attention without appearing to try.

Jiang Qing ate breakfast under the weight of Lin Xun's complicated gaze, feeling very pleased with himself, and privately certain that his extraordinary appearance was simply too much for the man to handle.

Ha. You didn't know how good your grandpa Qing looked until he made the effort.

In this mood, he agreed without thinking to take Lin Xun around the neighborhood, as had been requested.

Before leaving, he ran back to the wardrobe and came out with a pair of the newest sunglasses he'd recently bought, pushed them on with practiced swagger, snapped his fingers, and said: "Let's go."

The corner of Lin Xun's mouth refused to cooperate and curved up.

Fine, he thought. He'd observe for now. See what moves this person made. Lin Xun, in the early stages of an unfamiliar self-directed romance, nodded to himself.

The complex was well maintained. Even in the city center, the greenery was carefully tended, and the trees lining the paths cast enough shade to soften the summer heat.

All the recreational facilities were well equipped. Gym, casual bar, every kind of sports club.

Past the main gate and a few dozen meters down was an imported supermarket, flanked by shopping malls and office buildings on either side.

The two of them walked along, trading the occasional remark.

Both were tall with long strides, and even with sunglasses, it was difficult to conceal the effect they had. This area had no shortage of attractive people, and the complex itself housed several entertainers, but the two of them together on the street still drew more than a few eyes.

A group of young women nearby were nudging each other. The boldest among them came toward them, cheeks flushed.

Lin Xun caught the movement and noticed that Jiang Qing had suddenly picked up his pace, leaving the woman nothing but an unattainable retreating figure.

The woman hesitated, then shifted her attention to Lin Xun.

The next moment, the second handsome man went running off after the first.

The woman: "..."

The small detour passed without further comment. Lin Xun checked the time. They'd covered most of the area, so he offered to treat Jiang Qing to lunch.

Jiang Qing accepted without ceremony and chose the revolving restaurant on the top floor.

Various dishes were laid out across the buffet area. Jiang Qing carried his plate back to his seat and noticed that Lin Xun's plate was all Western food. "You prefer Western?"

Lin Xun nodded. "I'm used to it."

"I see... Let me get a few more things." A thoughtful glint crossed Jiang Qing's eyes. He got up and came back with several Sichuan dishes, placed them on the table with a mischievous smile. "I'm more of a Chinese food person. Want to try some?"

Lin Xun met those expectant eyes and knew full well this was deliberate. But he couldn't resist trying, and picked up a few pieces of kung pao chicken.

The tingle of the spice hit all at once, awakening his taste buds. It wasn't overwhelming, but for someone who never ate spicy food, it was still quite a risk.

He exhaled repeatedly, drank a long sip of plain water, and still said, "It's good."

Jiang Qing had assumed he was putting on a show, but it was becoming clear that Lin Xun genuinely couldn't handle spice. He quickly refilled the water, and once Lin Xun looked better, said with more gruffness than he intended, "If you can't eat it, don't. I'm not making you."

Lin Xun waved it off. "It's fine. Good to try new things. This particular new thing is clearly beyond my spice tolerance."

Jiang Qing laughed despite himself, and pushed all the Sichuan dishes back to his own side. Then, without a word, slid the Western plate that Lin Xun had been eating from toward him, as an offering.

Lin Xun watched the small gesture. The heat in his throat moved to somewhere around his chest, a faint, unfamiliar warmth.

"It's hot." Jiang Qing said, out of nowhere.

"Hm?" Lin Xun looked at him, something deep flickering in his expression. "Hot where?"

"The weather." Jiang Qing gestured toward the windows. "The sun's intense. I forgot to put on sunscreen."

The first step in preserving good looks, and he had missed it.

Lin Xun lowered his head. The corner of his mouth lifted almost imperceptibly.

This inexplicable warmth really must be the weather's fault.

The sun blazed outside. After lunch, they headed home.

At the door, Lin Xun stopped him. "Thank you for the company today. I'll return the favor one of these days."

"Didn't you just treat me to lunch?"

"That was today. Next time I'll cook."

Jiang Qing raised an eyebrow. "You cook?"

"Yes. It's a rare opportunity. First come, first served." Lin Xun smiled, pushing his door open. "Let me get through the next few days of work first, then I'll let you know."

"Alright." Free food was free food.

He reflected once more that Yang Meng had truly excellent taste.

Shu Tong, once she'd wrapped things up at the Wutong orphanage, came straight back and left Sang Yi there for a few extra days.

When she found out Lin Xun had moved in next door, she made up an excuse and went to introduce herself, but no one answered at his apartment. She came back and got down to business with Jiang Qing.

"The director of 'I Am an Actor' reached out. The recent episodes have been doing well in ratings, but the buzz is starting to dip. He wants you to stir up some conflict and tension."

Jiang Qing indicated that he understood.

The production had brought him on precisely because of his reputation for being harsh. His lavish praise had caused a spike in interest for novelty's sake, but if it kept going, it would grow stale. They wanted something different, and since Teacher Wen and Su Hongru were harder to work with on this front, the target fell on him again.

"Do we have a contestant list for next episode?"

"The only name we know so far is Wang Mingzhi."

"Poor man." He said with genuine sympathy.

Shu Tong gave a helpless sigh and rubbed her forehead. She glanced at the calendar, weighed it for a moment, then said: "You remember what's tomorrow, right?"

"No." Jiang Qing didn't even pause to think about it.

"You say you don't remember, but I haven't even told you yet... When was the last time you went home? Go see your father, at least. It's his birthday."

She knew Jiang Qing had a difficult relationship with his father. Since she had taken over managing him, he had never once brought up going home voluntarily. He'd said his family disapproved of him being in the entertainment industry, and every visit ended in a fight. Eventually he'd moved out and made his own way. It had been like that ever since.

By all rights, a child actor was usually the most difficult to manage, especially during the rebellious adolescent years. But Jiang Qing never dated, never stirred up trouble, never created rumors for her to deal with. He was the easiest client she'd ever had.

That said, he wasn't without his sharp edges. He had just channeled all of them in one direction, toward his father, and that stubbornness had never softened even now.

She had been looking for an opening to mend things between them.

Jiang Qing spun his phone without interest. "What's the point of going? There are plenty of people lining up to celebrate his birthday. He doesn't need me there."

"Can you do it as a favor to me? I don't want people saying I let you skip your own father's birthday." Shu Tong let her voice go soft, the particular tone she used when she really needed something. Jiang Qing was almost always unable to refuse it. "Besides, Xiao Bao has a parent-teacher conference tomorrow, and I haven't been able to make it to one in years."

Jiang Qing's eyes dropped. He nodded. "Go. I'll handle tomorrow."

After Shu Tong left, he lay down for the rest of the afternoon, got up for dinner at some point, and went back to bed.

Around ten at night, someone rang his doorbell. He didn't answer. He didn't want to see anyone.

His phone lit up in the dark. A new message.

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: Asleep? I brought some food. Want any?

He typed two words: Asleep.

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: Rest well then. I'm making a big dinner tomorrow, inviting a few friends. Come join us.

He didn't reply, and pulled the covers over his head.

The consequence was waking up before six the next morning.

He dragged himself out of bed, washed up, and went to the wardrobe.

Jiang Huai was a businessman. He dressed sharply every day, like someone who took himself seriously. He had never stopped resenting Jiang Qing for being an entertainer, as though it were some great stain on the Jiang name.

Jiang Qing selected his outfit with deliberate care. He'd bought this one from an online shop, a cheap purchase, a loose street-style white T-shirt covered in English text that was, to put it plainly, profane, though most people wouldn't notice unless they looked closely.

The trousers were distressed jeans, the ripped and ragged kind most likely to make any middle-aged person visibly pained.

He worked his hair with a curling iron into something flashy and spiraled, then drove to the family home in this particular ensemble.

The Jiang family home was in the eastern outskirts, surrounded by hills and a stream, quietly elegant.

He drove a sports car at a tortoise's pace, which earned him a string of honks and choice words from other drivers.

The wrought-iron gate at the entrance was still faithfully open to both sides. The household staff, busy in the garden, all stopped what they were doing to look at him.

He parked beside the fountain, shut the door with force, leaned against the car and put on his sunglasses. Under a roomful of complicated looks, he walked into the opulent European-style villa.

The housekeeper, Auntie Yu, was directing the staff. She saw him come in and said politely, "Young master, you're here."

He gave a flat, "mm," and looked up at the closed door on the second-floor landing. "Still in bed?"

"Yes, Mr. Jiang had a late engagement last night. He had a few drinks."

Auntie Yu added carefully: "More than a few. He couldn't walk straight."

Jiang Qing looked at her steadily.

Auntie Yu lowered her eyes and said nothing more.

She had been with the Jiang family for eighteen years. She could count on one hand how many times she'd seen the young master in person. He had never once smiled, and the size of his temper was enough to frighten anyone, the kind that left things in pieces. All the staff were afraid of him and didn't much care for him either.

Every year on the day of Mr. Jiang's birthday, they were all on high alert. No one knew what disruption this young master might cause.

Especially today, given what was upstairs.

She glanced anxiously toward the second floor.

Jiang Qing followed her gaze, seemed to draw his own conclusions, and his expression went entirely flat, eyes going cold. He went up the stairs without another word, every step carrying a contained edge.

"Young master, go slowly, the Master is still sleeping..." Auntie Yu followed at a half-jog, her voice rising slightly, as though trying to give someone upstairs a warning.

Jiang Qing's suspicion was becoming more certain with each step. As he reached the second floor, one of the doors opened.

A woman with long hair stepped out, wearing one of Jiang Huai's shirts, her legs pale and bare beneath its hem. She looked toward the staircase with a startled expression. "Auntie..."

Auntie Yu, standing behind Jiang Qing, answered quietly.

The woman turned her head, noticed Jiang Qing's presence, and went still, fingers clenching around the shirt hem. Her voice carried a faint edge of panic: "A-Qing..."

"A-Qing?" Jiang Qing gave a cold laugh. He walked toward her, step by step, eyes like a blade being drawn slowly. "You call me that?"

The woman's looks were unremarkable, the kind that would not draw a second glance in the entertainment world.

But Jiang Qing's gaze was drawn to a single detail. She had a beauty mark. A well-placed teardrop mark.

"You think you can call me that?"

"I... listen to me, it wasn't intentional, Mr. Jiang had too much to drink last night..." The woman's face was red, and she stumbled through her explanation, only to be cut off.

"And took advantage of the situation?" Jiang Qing's lips curved slightly, his eyes showing nothing like a smile. "That excuse has been worn out. Every woman who climbs into his bed says the same thing."

The woman's eyes dropped with embarrassment.

Jiang Qing tilted her chin up, not a trace of gentleness in it, and examined her face. "Secretary Mu?"

The woman nodded, powerless to pull away, and murmured, "If the Master knew you were here, he would certainly be glad."

Jiang Qing released her chin, smiled without warmth. "Glad? Call him out."

"He's still sleeping. I was going to head home, he probably doesn't even know it was me..." Secretary Mu said softly, managing a wry smile, "We could act as though none of this happened."

"Pathetic and stupid." Jiang Qing held her gaze, each word distinct and measured. "Do you not know who lives in this house?"

His voice dropped sharply—

chapters.title: QAQ
chapters.content:
Six dishes and a soup were laid out on the table, still steaming, the fragrance already stirring Jiang Qing's appetite.

He followed the smell to the table and sat down. The centerpiece was a large plate of baked Australian lobster with cheese, the color vivid, the meat fragrant.

"This is good." He tasted a couple bites and was fully satisfied.

Lin Xun said: "No papaya with snow jelly, but the lobster should do for now."

He watched Jiang Qing scrunch his nose in a way that said he was enjoying it very much, and quietly added more to his bowl.

Yang Meng took issue with this: "I thought I was invited here to eat. Not to watch you serve someone else."

Jiang Qing paused and explained: "We don't have that kind of relationship. You two are the ones who belong together."

Yang Meng stared at him, baffled. The words themselves weren't wrong, strictly speaking, but something about the way they landed felt distinctly strange.

Lin Xun agreed pleasantly: "I love you both equally."

Classic line out of a terrible drama.

Jiang Qing: "I don't deserve such generosity."

"Hey, where's the wine?" Yang Meng looked over the table and found not a single bottle. "You have good wine and you're hoarding it? What kind of host are you?"

Lin Xun opened a can of soda and set it in front of him: "Dream on. You're driving home tonight, so behave."

Jiang Qing: "I'm not driving, though..."

"Yours is on the stove." Lin Xun said.

Jiang Qing turned to look at the ginger broth simmering in the pot: QAQ

A housewarming dinner with only a neighbor and a backer in attendance, which was honestly rather pitiful when he thought about it.

Thoughtful as he was, Jiang Qing decided to shrink into the background and focus on eating, leaving the two of them in peace.

Before long, Yang Meng brought up business, and the two began discussing the company's operations and a new investment proposal.

Ruien Investment had been operating for nearly ten years. Headquarters were abroad, and after Yang Meng graduated he had come back to China with capital and established a domestic branch.

Their investments spanned several sectors, but over the past five or six years, Yang Meng had apparently discovered the film and television industry's profitability. Returns were high and came quickly, and through that sector he had made substantial gains and become a well-known name in the industry.

What Jiang Qing hadn't expected was for Yang Meng to discuss company matters so freely in front of Lin Xun without any apparent concern about confidentiality.

He glanced at Lin Xun, who was listening with genuine attention.

A suspicion began to form. Were these two actually in a real and serious relationship?

Thinking about it, Lin Xun was accomplished across the board. There was no reason for him to play any kind of supporting role. He could easily be the primary partner.

The mood at the table was pleasant when Yang Meng's phone rang. After a brief exchange, he ended the call.

"Who calls at this hour for business?"

Lin Xun: "Who was it?"

"A director. Says he has a project worth investing in. He's been after me for the past month and a half." Yang Meng said without much interest, and took a sip of soda. "I've looked at the proposal. It's a science fiction film. The budget would have to be massive to make the effects work. But it's a scrappy team with a shoestring operation. Most likely it would fall apart, and it's not worth the risk."

"Which project?" Jiang Qing sat up with sudden interest.

"Something called 'New Homeland,' I think."

Jiang Qing's hand froze. He looked up sharply, eyes lighting up. "'New Homeland'? Are you sure?!"

"Yes. Why?"

Jiang Qing leaned forward with some intensity: "That film is going to do extraordinary box office numbers. Trust me on this. Invest in it. You won't lose a cent, and it'll earn you credibility on top of everything else."

Yang Meng looked at those eyes, which were distinctly radiating a greenish light, and found it somewhat difficult to take entirely on faith.

"I'm serious!" Jiang Qing couldn't exactly explain that he'd come back from the future, but "New Homeland" was, in three years' time, the most acclaimed science fiction film in the country, both critically adored and commercially dominant, redefining what audiences thought domestic science fiction could do.

And the road to get there had been extraordinarily difficult. The director had mortgaged several properties just to keep going, and the whole team had spent three or four years building something exceptional, cutting scenes along the way.

If Yang Meng put in the funding now, it might be possible to bring everything forward and deliver something even more complete.

This was the hope of someone who cared deeply about film.

"Yang Meng, speaking as a professional, I'm genuinely recommending you invest now while you can. Film history will remember you for this." Jiang Qing said plainly. "And if you're not interested, give me the contact. I'll invest myself."

The table went quiet for a moment. Yang Meng had never once encountered an actor who campaigned this hard to get him to invest in a project they weren't even attached to. He was both curious and genuinely intrigued.

Lin Xun watched Jiang Qing steadily. When a topic genuinely captured his interest, the whole of him came alive, nothing like the subdued person who had walked through the door earlier this evening.

He tapped a finger on the edge of the table, then turned to Yang Meng: "Go meet with the director. Get the documentation ready. Let me know if anything comes up."

Yang Meng's expression went through several phases, and in the end he got up and headed to the office.

The door clicked shut.

Jiang Qing looked at Lin Xun with confusion. "He listens to you that much?"

Lin Xun gave neither a confirmation nor a denial. He got up, went to the kitchen to turn off the burner, ladled out the ginger broth, and set a cup in front of Jiang Qing. "Let it cool a little before you drink."

Jiang Qing looked at the broth, warmth rising from the surface, and said quietly: "Thank you."

"Don't mention it." Lin Xun smiled, and ruffled Jiang Qing's head on his way past. "Your head is quite soft."

"..." Jiang Qing touched his own hair and shot him a look.

After dinner, with the ginger broth warming him from the inside, Jiang Qing felt settled and comfortable again.

As a precaution, Lin Xun mixed him a packet of herbal powder as well, and waited until he'd finished it before letting him go.

Jiang Qing stopped at the door, looked back once: "Dinner was good. Um..."

"No more thank yous needed."

"Oh. Then good night."

Lin Xun said quietly: "Good night."

Jiang Qing lay awake for two hours, sleep refusing to come.

He switched on the lamp, sat up bent slightly forward, and rummaged through the nightstand drawer until he found a small pill bottle.

He checked the expiry date, shook one out, and swallowed it dry. He fell asleep before long.

In the morning, Shu Tong called over a dozen times and got no answer. She drove to Yishui Bay herself.

In the hallway, she ran into Lin Xun on his way out, exchanged a brief hello, and asked: "Did you see Jiang Qing this morning?"

"No. Is something wrong?"

"He's not picking up. He went back to the Jiang family home yesterday and I don't know if something happened." Shu Tong explained, already pressing the doorbell as she spoke.

Lin Xun said: "He was caught in the rain yesterday. He might be sick, or still sleeping."

That was enough. Shu Tong punched in the door code and went straight in.

Lin Xun: "..."

"Jiang Qing! Jiang Qing!" Shu Tong called out a couple times, confirmed he was still sleeping somewhere, and hurried upstairs.

Lin Xun was worried enough to follow. This was his first time on the second floor, but there was no time to look around. He went straight behind Shu Tong to the bedroom.

The bed was empty and disheveled.

"I shouldn't have let him go back there." Shu Tong was already blaming herself, going from door to door to look.

Wardrobe, nothing. Study, nothing. Home theater, nothing.

She stopped in front of a small door in the corner, eyes gone slightly red. She gripped the door handle and said quietly to Lin Xun: "Are you his friend?"

Lin Xun, though surprised by the question, answered immediately: "Yes."

"If he's still in the apartment, he'll be in here." She kept her voice low. "If there's ever a time when I can't get here in time, I hope you'll help."

"Alright."

Shu Tong opened the door. They stood in the doorway.

One wall was lined with a tall shelf filled with model cars. The rest of the room was covered with Lego sets, some completed, some half-assembled, placed and stacked without much order, a thoroughly childlike space.

In the middle of the floor, Jiang Qing was sleeping. The morning light came through the window, touching the edge of his face.

His expression was quiet. He was curled into himself, arms wrapped around his knees, the tucked-in posture of an infant.

A psychology professor had once told Lin Xun that this kind of sleeping position indicated a lack of a sense of security.

Shu Tong went in gently and touched Jiang Qing's shoulder, her voice the same way she might wake a child: "Jiang Qing. Jiang Qing. Time to get up. It's almost noon."

Jiang Qing stirred, slowly opened his eyes, raised a hand to shield his face from the light, and blinked at her in mild confusion: "Tong-jie, when did you get here?"

Shu Tong swallowed whatever she was feeling, and restored her usual manner at once, reaching over to pull his ear: "I called you for ages and you didn't answer. Now you're giving me attitude? And why are you sleeping on the floor again? You have a recording at the station today, do you have any concept of being a professional?!"

"Ow, I know, I know!" Jiang Qing sat up, caught a glimpse of someone else in the doorway, and his eyes went wide. "Why is he here? Trespassing?!"

Lin Xun smiled: "I came to ask what you wanted for breakfast."

Jiang Qing said nothing, just got up with a residual foul mood and went to wash up without another word.

Shu Tong exhaled, then stood beside Lin Xun and said quietly: "Sorry you had to see this. If you're his friend, I only have one small request."

"What is it?"

"You don't have to open your heart to him. But please don't stab him in the back."
