After Jiang Qing finished washing up and getting dressed, he came downstairs to find Lin Xun already gone.

"Where did he go?"

"A friend called. Something came up."

"Ah."

He went to the station that afternoon for the next recording. He took his place on the mentors' panel looking composed as ever and greeted the audience with his usual warmth.

But the moment filming actually started, every viewer who had been expecting lavish praise looked up in confusion.

Was Jiang Qing... back?

A performance had just finished, and Jiang Qing delivered his critique: "This is not a difficult scene. How did the two of you manage to turn a performance from Dream of the Red Chamber into something out of a haunted cave? The female lead's quality of seductive without vulgarity, alluring without cheapness, was completely absent. Don't try so hard to stand out. There's always a price to overplaying."

The expressions on the two actresses onstage went through more changes than a set of traditional painted masks.

Su Hongru quickly adapted to the shift, going back to playing the encouraging voice. One critic, one cheerleader, and Teacher Wen finishing with wisdom. The director nodded with great satisfaction, already feeling the ratings climb toward him.

The final group was Wang Mingzhi paired with a middle-aged actress.

Wang Mingzhi was backstage, entirely unaware of what had just happened out front, and feeling fully confident. His opponent was an obscure actress, the scene gave him the dominant role, and the audience had been stacked with his own team's arranged fans.

Jiang Qing hated him. Fine. He would make Jiang Qing acknowledge him in front of every camera present.

Even if Jiang Qing didn't mean it, hadn't he still swallowed his pride and kept blowing smoke for the whole show? This was no different.

Wang Mingzhi walked out onto the stage with his head high, performed for about ten minutes opposite his unassuming scene partner, then stood in the spotlight.

Teacher Wen and Su Hongru finished their assessments. The cordial Jiang Qing finally raised the microphone.

"Wang Mingzhi."

"Yes." Wang Mingzhi lifted his chin with pride. As long as Jiang Qing said a few words in his favor, his path into acting would be considered validated.

He'd debuted as a singer and faced no shortage of mockery for crossing over into acting. But wasn't this what everybody did now? Why was he the only one who had to put up with constant criticism?

To receive personal acknowledgment from a Best Actor winner was to open every door going forward. Even Gao Yuanqiao, that nobody, was being called a rising star of acting everywhere he went just because of a little exposure.

Jiang Qing had no idea about the elaborate internal drama unfolding on the other side of the stage, and simply asked: "In your own opinion, how did you do?"

"I don't think I reached the level I was aiming for. I performed better in rehearsal. There's still room to improve." Wang Mingzhi made the necessary show of humility, while also giving himself a graceful out.

"I see. You do have a certain self-awareness, then." Jiang Qing said, perfectly neutral.

Wang Mingzhi blinked, his eyelid flickering once. He smiled: "In what areas do you think I fell short, Teacher Jiang?"

Jiang Qing said, slowly and distinctly: "Every area."

"What were you performing? Do you actually know? This was supposed to be a delicate, devastating love story. You turned it into a weepy mother-son drama. Look at how you regarded your scene partner. Was there even a trace of romantic feeling?"

Wang Mingzhi thought privately: Who could summon romantic feeling for a face like hers.

Jiang Qing continued: "Your crying scene was truly extraordinary."

Finally, one compliment. Wang Mingzhi braced himself for a classic bait-and-switch, adopting an expression of attentive receptiveness. Jiang Qing's next sentence was: "Extraordinary in the sense that I have never in my time on this stage witnessed anyone capable of turning their tears into nasal bubbles."

Wang Mingzhi's face turned every color of the spectrum. In his mind, he was destroying Jiang Qing in every way imaginable. On his face, he maintained the expression of someone receiving valuable feedback.

Su Hongru, unable to hold it together any longer, lowered his head behind his hand and subtly gave Jiang Qing a thumbs up. He failed to notice the camera catching every bit of it.

He genuinely admired how unafraid Jiang Qing was. There were a considerable number of Wang Mingzhi's fans seated in the back rows.

Seeing Wang Mingzhi's carefully arranged expression of attentive humility, Jiang Qing continued generously: "I had assumed that vocal delivery would be your strongest point, given your background as a singer. How is it that you can't manage even the basic rhythm and emphasis of a line?"

"My expression guidance instructor is exceptional. I've recently had the privilege of working with that teacher firsthand, and I know exactly how good that instruction is. Even newcomers like Gao Yuanqiao and Lin Xun were transformed by it. If you had applied even a fraction of genuine effort and attention, you would not be presenting what we just saw."

"Voice, body, words, presence. Not one of the four reaches my standard. If you have any free time, I would suggest spending some of it on the fundamentals. This stage is called I Am an Actor. Do you have the nerve to stand here and say out loud that you are an actor?"

Wang Mingzhi's expression hardened. He met Jiang Qing's gaze with a sharpness in his own eyes, then let his lips curl slowly upward: "In that case, I'd like to challenge Teacher Jiang directly. Please give me the opportunity."

The room erupted.

The director and producers were briefly stunned, then immediately went into emergency deliberation. By the rules of the current round, the winner was the actress. This hadn't been accounted for.

The director was about to go smooth things over with Jiang Qing when the sound of Jiang Qing's voice already carried through the microphone, calm and self-assured, with a particular kind of quiet energy underneath it.

"Why not."

Wang Mingzhi's fans: "He won't fall! We'll always be here for you!!!"

A rare handful of Jiang Qing's fans were also present, calling out: "Wang Mingzhi, don't cry!!!"

What these fans didn't realize was that their Jiang Qing had never once brought out his real ability on this stage.

Su Hongru, who had been happy to sit back and watch until now, finally had something to sink his teeth into. He proposed: "Given that the original competition format and schedule are already set, we can't exactly have everyone sit here for three hours waiting for Jiang Qing to work with both contestants in full. That's too much time. Here's a modest suggestion, since we're doing something fun anyway. Why not make it even more interesting."

The host asked: "What do you have in mind?"

"What if we played a chain improv game? Everyone here, audience and staff, can each contribute a line or two of dialogue, and we'll piece it into a brand new script. Whatever direction they take it is up to them."

The audience, on hearing this, immediately and enthusiastically agreed.

It was a genuinely exciting prospect. No one knew what outlandish or absurd situations might appear in the middle. No one knew the ending. There was no source material to reference. It was pure performance, entirely improvised.

Jiang Qing looked at Su Hongru: "You've got a real talent for chaos. I like it. Let's do it."

The director thought this was a brilliant idea and started making preparations.

Everyone was buzzing with enthusiasm, practically rubbing their hands together in excitement. Everyone, that is, except Wang Mingzhi, who stood on stage with the expression of someone who had just stepped into a pit.

A pit he had dug himself.

Author's note: Wang Mingzhi: He travels a long way just to hand me his head. The thought is what counts.

Don't worry, the backer mystery will be cleared up very soon~

chapters.title: Crisis and Opportunity
chapters.content:
Recording entered its second phase. Jiang Qing went to prepare the new scene with the actress while the production team handed out paper to the audience and crew for writing the new script.

Waiting in the dressing room, Wang Mingzhi felt as though he were sitting on death row. Everyone around him was pouring fuel on the fire, and the one who had put him on the rack was himself.

He rubbed his head anxiously, slumped down and buried his face in his knees, silently cursing Jiang Qing.

If it weren't for this insufferable person, he would never have said something that rash in public.

Zhang Lingquan pushed the door open, her brow knotted so tight it could have tied itself into a bow, and said with displeasure: "Why did you provoke Jiang Qing directly? He doesn't respond to pressure, he responds to reason!"

"I just couldn't stand looking at his superior, self-satisfied face. Acting like being a mentor was some kind of distinction." Wang Mingzhi exhaled slowly and leaned back against the sofa. "My original plan was to stir something up. The production team would pick up on the tension and try to smooth things over by having him put on a good show and let me win. Wouldn't that be a better angle?"

"The plan had its merits." Zhang Lingquan said without warmth. "Unfortunately, Su Hongru walked in out of nowhere and made the whole scheme irrelevant. The improv script has enough on its own to carry the ratings. Your spark wasn't needed."

"So what now? Will Jiang Qing go easy on me?"

"Almost certainly not." Zhang Lingquan had been around long enough to know Jiang Qing's temperament reasonably well. "The thing he cannot tolerate is someone trying to cut corners right in front of him, especially when it comes to performing. There was a newcomer once at a dinner who said acting was just about winging it. Jiang Qing tore into that person in front of everyone, and they ended up leaving the industry."

Wang Mingzhi scoffed: "If that's all it took, retiring was the right call."

He closed his eyes, and whatever he was chewing over showed nothing on his face.

Zhang Lingquan was beginning to regret taking on such an impulsive artist.

Then Wang Mingzhi opened his eyes, and something glinted in them with a quiet edge. "Do you have the young master's contact?"

"I can reach him. But you two haven't been introduced. What do you want with him?"

"To give Jiang Qing something to think about." Wang Mingzhi smiled with no warmth in it.

In the rehearsal room, Jiang Qing noticed a problem with the actress. She lacked confidence.

She was at ease playing the kind of quiet, ordinary characters she'd been doing for years, but whenever a role called for boldness or presence, she visibly deflated.

Rather than jumping straight into running scenes, Jiang Qing dug up old footage of her work and had her sit and watch it with him.

Every time a genuinely strong moment came up, he would mention it without making a ceremony of it, and offer a natural word of recognition.

Perhaps because Jiang Qing had been so harsh onstage earlier, the actress had been a little wary of him. But now, hearing him acknowledge her directly, she couldn't help but feel something taking hold.

Maybe it was true, what he'd said. She wasn't young, and she'd never had the good fortune to be in anyone's frame for a lead role, just an endless procession of supporting parts no one remembered. But Jiang Qing was right. Everyone is the lead of their own frame.

As he felt her mood shift, he began working on scenes with her, going over details patiently, one pass at a time.

Liu Huimin felt her eyes begin to well up as they went. Nearly a decade of thankless supporting roles, never once earning the attention of a director or the eye contact of a leading actor, just growing wild on her own and hoping for the best.

And now this young man, a decade her junior, was looking her in the eye and telling her she was thirty-five, not dead. The best time was right now.

Jiang Qing assumed she'd gone too deep into the character and passed her a few tissues. "Sis Huimin, that was strong, but this shot doesn't call for tears."

"Yes, yes, I know." Liu Huimin wiped her eyes and smiled. "You can just call me by my full name."

"Is 'sis' getting to you? Liu Huimin, madam."

Liu Huimin laughed, something stirring warmly in her chest.

This was the enthusiasm she remembered in young actors. It was so different from the cold dismissal she'd received during yesterday's rehearsal. She found herself far preferring this direct, blunt Jiang Qing.

Whatever happened, she intended to go out there and give it everything. She couldn't let the younger generation down.

The rehearsal found its rhythm after that. When filming ended, Jiang Qing relaxed with a genuine smile. "Sis Huimin really is something."

"Not at all. It was you. Thank you. If you ever need anything, say the word." Liu Huimin smiled back. "Even if I'm not much use."

"Don't say that. If you were no use, who was I just acting with?"

He walked back to the waiting room with her. "Keep at it, Sis Huimin."

"I will!" Liu Huimin nodded, then fell a step behind and watched him.

Even in a narrow, crowded hallway, Jiang Qing walking into the light was still the one who caught the eye.

He glanced back at her with a mild smile. "If the day ever comes when people stop caring about my work, then my life has really lost its point."

He had been chasing the camera since childhood, but the distance between where he was and where the best had been was something he still hadn't fully closed.

He said goodbye to Liu Huimin and headed to the waiting room for water.

Shu Tong was off to the side on a call, her expression darkening. By the time she ended the call, her hand was shaking. She nearly threw the phone.

"What happened?" Jiang Qing picked it up. "Good build quality."

"Wang Mingzhi is absolutely insufferable!" She said through her teeth. "I don't know who he went to, but someone from above just called. They want you to lose the upcoming round to him. In exchange, you'd get the male lead in a major production. Otherwise, expect to see nothing coming your way, including the variety show Manager Chen promised."

"I never expected much from Manager Chen's variety show to begin with." Jiang Qing stretched. "The contract has about four months left, right?"

"Yes."

"Give me Manager Chen's number."

Three minutes later, Manager Chen's voice came through: "Jiang Qing, Shu Tong's filled you in, right? Look, Wang Mingzhi's request isn't unreasonable. You take the loss, everyone benefits, the show is happy, and your own buzz goes up. Then I arrange something for you, a good reality show, maybe get you some new fans..."

"I'm not a person, but you're a genuine dog." Jiang Qing cut in flatly. "That kind of solution only someone who'd eaten garbage could produce. I won't agree."

"Don't refuse a toast and force me to offer the harsher alternative. Leadership cares about this." Manager Chen dropped his voice. "I've known you long enough to say this: some people are not worth provoking."

"Oh. And I've known you long enough to tell you, I'm one of those people."

"Jiang Qing!" Manager Chen's voice went tight. He took a breath, and pulled out the last card he had. "Do you even want to renew your contract?"

"No."

"..."

"Let's move on this while there's momentum. I'll come into the company tomorrow and we can discuss terminating the contract. Have everything ready to go through the process. I don't want any delay." While Manager Chen was still silent, Jiang Qing added, almost conversationally: "I've been around long enough to have seen some things. Some of those things, if the wrong bottle of liquor loosened my tongue at the wrong moment, might just come out on camera. You wouldn't want that kind of complication, would you?"

Manager Chen's voice went sharp: "I really did underestimate you."

"You overestimated me. Did you actually think I was still holding out hope for renewing? Genuinely thought I was some naive little kid?" Jiang Qing said.

Manager Chen thought of several things to say, and decided none of them were worth the effort.

Shu Tong took the phone back and handled the rest with Manager Chen herself: "I think he's made himself clear. If you've both had enough of this arrangement, ending it early makes sense for everyone. If he decides to make things difficult, no one benefits. And you don't want that kind of noise right now with the company's plans on the horizon, do you?"

Manager Chen cursed under his breath and ended the call.

Shu Tong asked: "You're confident they'll agree to terminate early?"

"The contract's almost up anyway. And once Wang Mingzhi loses tonight, they won't want me around the company any longer than necessary."

"I still don't understand how Wang Mingzhi managed to get someone that senior to intervene personally."

"Who knows." Jiang Qing rolled his wrists. "Whoever's backing him doesn't change anything. Hit him hard enough in front of everyone and that's all there is to it."

The second half of recording began. His phone buzzed twice, and he glanced down quickly to see a WeChat notification from a new neighbor.

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: Are you at the station? I have something to take care of nearby. Let's go back together after.

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: How much longer?

He typed back a quick response and ignored it after that.

QYY: As long as eternity.

Lin Xun stared at the message, pressed one hand loosely over his mouth, but couldn't hide the smile.

Yang Meng suddenly kicked his foot under the table, chin tilted toward the director sitting across from them. "What do you think?"

The three of them were seated at the revolving restaurant near the TV station, talking business over dinner.

The director hadn't understood why Yang Meng had brought Lin Xun along, and the connection clearly ran deeper than surface level. He was privately wondering whether this was some kind of arrangement to have Lin Xun attached to the project.

He was still quietly working out the implications of funding tied to casting when Lin Xun asked, unprompted: "If you stay unable to secure investment, would you consider switching to a commercial project?"

The director shook his head: "My last two films were commercial work, done for the box office. The results were mediocre and I wasn't happy making them. Maybe that's just not my kind of filmmaking. I want to try once more with a subject I care about. Even if it fails, I'll have no regrets. I'm not switching."

Lin Xun considered this with a quiet nod, something in his expression lifting slightly. "Have you cast the lead yet?"

There it was. The director sighed internally. This was probably what it had all been leading up to. In principle, he didn't want anyone's hand in the casting process, but if funding never came through, the whole crew would be worn down long before anything was made.

He admitted honestly: "Still looking. We're going to schools and drama programs to find young talent."

"Why students specifically?"

"They're unguarded. Energetic. They follow direction." He paused, then added the most important reason with the same honesty: "And they're affordable."

Yang Meng glanced at Lin Xun and said: "If Ruien were to invest, the standard expectations around casting would naturally apply. Using an unknown carries too much risk. You've looked into our previous investments."

"Of course, of course." The director nodded repeatedly, then exhaled into his cup. "The trouble is, any established actor with both the name and the skill is out of our price range. We've approached several and all of them were either unavailable or uninterested in the material. We can't get anyone."

If they could have, this scrappy team would not have spent so long failing to attract funding.

The table went quiet for a moment, broken only by the director's ongoing sighs.

Lin Xun put down his phone. "What do you think of Jiang Qing?"

The director's head snapped up. He stared, thrown entirely off balance, not understanding why Jiang Qing was being brought up. Had Lin Xun been the one being considered for investment all along?

"Jiang Qing would be perfect. In terms of age and ability, everything fits what we need. But he's a Best Actor winner. Our budget is too low to even approach mid-tier actors, let alone someone of his level."

Lin Xun's expression was mild and unhurried. "Jiang Qing is the one who told Ruien to invest in your project. He said it would be one of the best films of the next several years."

The director could not believe those words had come from Jiang Qing's mouth. But Lin Xun had no reason to invent such a thing.

He felt something come loose in his chest, the blood in his veins reversing direction. He clasped his hands under the table and held on to keep them from shaking visibly.

"He really said that? I wouldn't dare make a claim like that about my own work. Why would he say that? Has he seen the script?"

"I'm not sure about that. He also said if we didn't invest, he'd come in himself."

The director was struck speechless, then thoroughly overwhelmed. Someone had seen his work and believed in it this much, was willing to put their own money in?

He wanted to have a long conversation with this kindred spirit.

"But I'm not inclined to let him have that pleasure." Lin Xun followed it immediately with a cold splash.

The director went still, no longer sure what to make of any of this.

Lin Xun tapped the table quietly. "Ruien will fund it. A hundred million up front. If more is needed in later stages, applications can be made."

The director's eyes went wide. His mood had been climbing and falling all evening.

Even now, he found himself wondering if this young actor had drunk something suspicious, or if he had simply been playing a domineering CEO for too long.

Lin Xun, without waiting for a response, continued: "We'll be your sole investor. You won't need to solicit anyone else. I have no interest in a situation where multiple parties are pulling the project in different directions or inserting their own people. So don't go looking for additional funding. Go back and focus on getting your team ready."

Never mind the inherent risk of a single investor arrangement for either side. The fact that these words were coming from Lin Xun already stretched credulity past its limit.

The director looked desperately at Yang Meng, the one who was supposed to be in charge. Only to discover that Yang Meng had been quietly focused on his food since Lin Xun started speaking.

Yang Meng caught the look, smiled back, and said by way of introduction: "Director Han, just go with what he says. Otherwise you'll get nothing. Ruien Investment has been operating under the name Lin. I'm just the salaried help, been at it for ten years now. Lin Xun founded the company in his first year of university. I know it's a lot to take in, but trust me on this one."

Director Han spent a long time processing this, then looked at Lin Xun, who had his head down playing with his phone, and swallowed. "So the investment is settled?"

"Yes, provided you're willing to take us as your only investor."

Director Han barely remembered how he made it home that evening. A single dinner had not only secured over a hundred million in funding, but effectively locked in the lead actor.

After the director left, Yang Meng asked: "You really want Jiang Qing in this? Why not take it yourself?"

"He's better suited to it than I am. The director said it himself. Besides," Lin Xun smiled and lifted his phone, "this is the bait on my hook."

"Hook for who?"

Lin Xun waved the phone slightly. "Jiang Qing."

Yang Meng: So you're fishing, not looking for a groom?

He glanced down at the chat window and caught one line from Jiang Qing: something about "as long as eternity."

And then Lin Xun's reply, which was a certain kind of thing.

LBB: I'll wait as long as it takes.

LBB: [heart] [heart] [heart]

LBB: Wait for me. I have a project worth over a hundred million I'd like to discuss with you.

Yang Meng: "..."

He felt compelled to point something out to this supposedly high-IQ individual. "Friend. You may not be aware. 'A project worth over a hundred million I'd like to discuss with you' is a pickup line. You might get hit."

Lin Xun: ???

chapters.title: The Improv Script Round
chapters.content:
Jiang Qing had no time for his phone. He was fully focused on the stage as the recorded VCRs for all three groups finished playing. None of the contestants had managed to beat a mentor.

Liu Huimin delivered her thanks to Jiang Qing with grace and warmth before bowing out after a close fight.

It was past ten at night, but the audience was still fully charged, and the energy had only built to its peak. Because coming up next, the youngest Best Actor winner and the most popular idol in the country were about to perform a script that every person in this room had had a hand in writing.

One for the record books. The kind of thing you'd want inscribed on a headstone.

The director had organized and printed the script, and mentors and audience alike read through their copies.

Jiang Qing and Wang Mingzhi went backstage to get into costume, with only this short window to learn their lines.

Jiang Qing sat at a makeup mirror, looked at the freshly minted script, and laughed.

Wang Mingzhi sat nearby, struggling to maintain a pleasant expression: "Go easy on me out there, Teacher Jiang."

"Sure." Jiang Qing said, and went back to reading.

The script's first line: Once upon a time, in a mountain there lived a great dragon.

Second line: An ugly dragon with a fondness for women's clothing.

Third line: He kidnapped a young man and brought him to the mountain. The dragon bellowed: who are you?!

Fourth line: The young man said: My name is Shangguan Milande Kundera Mingxi Xuan Fengxue Wuying Qianye Shang Ao, but you can call me Xiao Er.

...

"Which role do you want?" Jiang Qing asked, still smiling.

Wang Mingzhi hadn't gotten far into the script yet. He'd barely finished the opening. He decided to play the young man.

Yes, the lines were ridiculous, but if he recited them without stumbling, that alone would demonstrate his command of delivery.

Besides, this dragon was a cross-dressing ugly creature, hardly compatible with his image. He had no intention of presenting himself as hideous in any public setting.

Once they'd divided the roles, the makeup team set to work.

Half an hour later, Wang Mingzhi stood and looked in the mirror. He'd been styled as a simple, guileless young man. He looked decent. The knot in him loosened a little.

As long as he could ignore the lotus leaf shorts he was wearing on the bottom half, the character who had apparently transformed into a little gourd child by the end.

He turned to look at Jiang Qing's costume. Some consolation, finally.

Jiang Qing had something painted across his face, a full spectrum of color, like a rainbow had broken directly onto his skin.

His outfit was essentially a plastic bag given structure. Once he stood, the makeup team pumped it full of air, and very slowly, a dinosaur shape inflated from the front up, producing a completed dinosaur suit of outstanding ugliness.

Wang Mingzhi pressed his mouth together to contain the laughter going off in his head. What kind of catastrophic costume was this?

Then he quickly flipped to the end of the script and read the conclusion, which he had missed earlier while half-watching what the makeup team was doing to Jiang Qing.

He immediately wanted to switch roles. Was there any chance of that now?

There were only ten minutes left, and he had to commit the lines to memory.

He managed it just as the staff came to collect them. He looked at Jiang Qing. "How are you doing on the script, Teacher Jiang?"

"Well enough."

Good. He'd absorbed about half of it, which was a reasonable performance for the time he'd had. Jiang Qing was probably in a similar position.

The two of them ran through their blocking once, and then it was time.

The stage lights dimmed. A single beam illuminated stage left, where a strangely shaped, unfortunately-proportioned dragon appeared before the audience.

Audience: Hahahahahaha!

Another beam hit stage right for the entrance of the storm-prince hero.

Wang Mingzhi already felt the secondhand embarrassment creeping in. He had to recite a preposterous introduction and then mime drawing a nonexistent sword in challenge to a dragon.

He was just bracing himself to hurry through this absurd spectacle when Jiang Qing began to move. He came bounding across the stage in the inflated dinosaur suit, which made a rushing sound with every step. Everything about the image was comedy. The audience hadn't stopped laughing once.

But Jiang Qing moved through it all without a trace of self-consciousness. He came to a stop in front of Wang Mingzhi, face painted in every color, eyes completely clear and guileless, voice slightly altered: "Are you really Xiao Er? You wouldn't dare answer to that name if I called you by it, would you?"

He had even changed his voice. An actual small dragon.

Wang Mingzhi found himself unexpectedly off-footed. This was the person he despised most. And this was the character he was meant to kill. But he was caught by those eyes.

Everything that followed came as a further surprise. He had watched Jiang Qing's previous performances carefully before agreeing to appear on this show.

Honestly, looking at them now, none of it had seemed exceptional. At most a degree better than the other performers, nothing more.

But standing here now, opposite this formidable and slightly frightening opponent, he finally understood how absurd that impression had been.

How difficult was it to be consistently one degree better than everyone else? How fine was that margin to calibrate?

Jiang Qing must have been holding back the entire time, carrying everyone else instead of overshadowing them.

And even with material this nonsensical, Jiang Qing had found the depth in it. The comedy was held up by something underneath, something almost earnest. The wide-eyed innocence turned cunning turned wide-eyed again, and a completely ridiculous dragon somehow became a living thing.

Wang Mingzhi felt the pressure in a way he hadn't in a very long time. More than a few of his movements came out wrong, and he began making up lines on the fly.

Jiang Qing picked up every single one of them, fast and clean. He wove them in, pulled new threads from them, handed Wang Mingzhi a hook to grab when there was nothing left.

And every time Wang Mingzhi fumbled, Jiang Qing wrapped the scene back around itself and kept it moving, seamless.

The audience had long since forgotten the script. They were simply calling out in delight.

This was ability. Actual, unconditional ability. A scene made up on the spot, with no preparation, and it still held more than most carefully rehearsed performances.

By comparison, Wang Mingzhi was a puppet. Face moving through gestures that didn't mean anything, delivering lines that landed in the air and stayed there.

Not to say the scene wasn't what it was meant to be, a comedy. But Jiang Qing had made it a real comedy. Wang Mingzhi was performing a joke.

Contrast was everything.

Shu Tong, watching from the audience, let the corner of her mouth move.

She'd managed this person long enough to know his ability down to the bone. Sometimes you had to hold back, but sometimes you had to let the world remember who it was dealing with.

He loved the camera. He was greater than the camera.

And some people lived. And some people were already finished. Wang Mingzhi, in this moment, was the second kind.

He could already see the flood of commentary that would follow this episode's air date.

Then Jiang Qing caught his wrist and swept his leg out, sending him to the ground, one foot pressed lightly to his stomach, smiling with a beauty that was genuinely unsettling: "My dear Xiao Er. Will you marry me."

Wang Mingzhi managed a look of appropriate horror and vocally refused.

Jiang Qing had him tied to a column and proceeded to describe in tender detail the domestic joys that awaited them, while drifting toward the corner of the stage.

There was a basin of water there. He washed his face clean, stepped out of the inflated dragon suit, and stood in plain white.

Back to the audience, he reached into the front of his outfit and adjusted what he'd placed inside it while the audience couldn't see, commenting on the audience's deeply questionable creative instincts in a murmur.

"Xiao Er, fear not your beloved's strange appearance. The truth is, I am a woman. Beneath this terrible disguise, I am nothing more than a humble creature of the softer kind~" He pitched his voice lighter, reduced the theatrical flair.

When he turned around, a fair and delicately featured face met the audience.

He took small, neat steps, inclined his head with a slight smile, and as he moved toward Wang Mingzhi, pulled free the band in his hair. A fall of dark hair cascaded down, drawing audible gasps from the women in the audience.

Stunning.

Wang Mingzhi watched him approach. This was a man who stood at nearly a hundred and eighty centimeters, but the way he walked was somehow entirely at odds with that. The movement was light and deliberate. The waist carried a quality that was both exact and effortless.

The face had been wiped clean. Nothing on it but the skin. The contrast with everything else created something strange and genuine.

In that moment, he actually looked like a character who had walked out of the story.

Jiang Qing reached him and touched the side of his face.

Wang Mingzhi's whole body locked up. He looked at Jiang Qing and for a moment forgot to breathe.

Those eyes were genuinely beautiful. Peach-shaped, with the corners lifting slightly at the ends.

They were looking at him now, warm and completely present, and for a second Wang Mingzhi forgot who he was looking at.

His gaze dipped, landing on the mouth. Fresh, just washed, the shadow of a single water drop still at the corner of the lip.

Then he heard this vision of loveliness open those lips and say, in a voice like running water: "Shangguan Milande Kundera Mingxi Xuan Fengxue Wuying Qianye Shang Ao."

Wang Mingzhi: "..." The spell evaporated entirely.

Audience: HAHAHAHAHA!

That was whoever wrote that name. They deserved a bonus.

Jiang Qing, his voice soft enough to drip, said: "In truth, I should confess. I am a princess."

Wang Mingzhi: "No. You are not!"

Damn. That was his actual opinion coming out.

Audience: You weren't supposed to say that!

"If I am not, does that make you one?" Jiang Qing redirected him gently and continued with his own lines. "I am from the neighboring planet Meow. We are people of the Meow. You may use my name. I am called Yalishanda Yingxue Jian You Dai F Siyu Yao Le Tao Xian Aier Shu Fen Er."

"I was cursed by a witch. I need a young man to break my curse."

Wang Mingzhi rose to the occasion with dignity: "How do we break it? Let's hear it."

Jiang Qing said, with all the allure he could summon: "If someone can speak my full name without stopping, I can leave this forsaken place."

Wang Mingzhi: "..."

Audience: BRAVO!!!

The stage lights came up in full. Jiang Qing exhaled, let everything fall from his expression, and reached over to untie Wang Mingzhi with complete neutrality.

Wang Mingzhi looked at him for a moment. Said nothing.

The two bowed to the audience. Jiang Qing then, with the casual manner of someone returning borrowed goods, retrieved two red apples from inside his costume and handed them to a staff member.

Wang Mingzhi: "..." Unwatchable.

Su Hongru laughed hard enough to hit the desk and proceeded to deliver Jiang Qing an enthusiastic review, entirely omitting the fact that there was another person on the stage who had also technically performed.

Teacher Wen said a polite word or two for Wang Mingzhi, then spent the remaining three minutes on Jiang Qing.

After recording wrapped, the hour was late, and Jiang Qing didn't linger at the station. He walked with Shu Tong toward the parking level.

"Is Xiao Bao still up?"

"He said he was waiting for me. What he means is he wanted to watch more TV." Shu Tong said with mild exasperation.

Jiang Qing checked his phone, and paused when he saw Lin Xun's chat window.

This impossible pig, was something off with him tonight?

He thought about it for a moment, then typed a message.

QYY: Done. Did you go home?

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: Not yet. I'm in the parking level waiting for you.

Jiang Qing turned to Shu Tong. "You don't need to drive me. Lin Xun's downstairs. I'll go with him. Get some rest, good night."

Shu Tong blinked: "Why is he here?"

"He said he wanted to talk to me about... I honestly don't know."

In the parking level, Shu Tong got into her car, triple-confirmed that she wasn't needed, and left. This was the TV station's territory, nothing was going to happen here.

Jiang Qing started looking for Lin Xun's car.

A horn sounded from across the dim lot, and two headlights came on.

He walked over steadily. Behind him, the elevator chimed as the doors slid open, and someone called out.

He turned. It was Wang Mingzhi. He said, mildly: "Something you need?"

Wang Mingzhi's expression was displeased from the moment he looked at Jiang Qing, especially at how unbothered Jiang Qing seemed, how little he seemed to register Wang Mingzhi's presence at all. He said, cold: "Why won't you do what you're told."

Jiang Qing had thoughts, most of which he set aside, choosing one that mattered: "Who exactly did you get involved?"

Wang Mingzhi didn't answer. He came forward until he was directly in front of Jiang Qing, eyes pressing down, looking for some crack in the composure, some flicker of retreat or unease.

There wasn't one.

"Not answering? Fine." Jiang Qing turned to leave. His arm was grabbed and pulled back hard, nearly driving his head into Wang Mingzhi's. His nose caught a sharp whiff of cologne.

That was the cologne Jiang Huai used most often.

He frowned. "Are you unwell?"

"Listen to me, Jiang Qing. I'm willing to overlook what you pulled earlier."

"No need. You're out of your mind." Jiang Qing pushed the hand off him, smoothed his rumpled sleeve, glanced back with something cold in his eyes. "Touch me again and I won't be polite about it."

Wang Mingzhi's fingers tensed. Before the next move could form, Jiang Qing had already turned and walked away.

A tall figure came toward him from the opposite direction, wearing a cap, face not easy to make out in the dim light.

A moment later, Jiang Qing stopped. He said something to the man that was too quiet to hear, and the man looked up briefly at Wang Mingzhi.

Those eyes. Deep-set, the low light concealing their color, but with something moving beneath the surface, quiet and deliberate.

Wang Mingzhi stood where he was and, unaccountably, felt something uncertain move through him. When he looked again, the man had settled his expression into something composed and pleasant, said something to Jiang Qing, and the two of them walked away.

Lin Xun.

Wang Mingzhi had not known these two were this close, and he hadn't understood what that expression had meant. Who was this newcomer to be making looks like that?

He watched a beat longer, his gaze dropping to Jiang Qing's back, and then to the waist.

That fitted shirt and trousers. The waist shown through, defined.

For no reason he could identify, something came to mind from the stage. A particular kind of movement.

Beep beep.

A horn snapped him back.

Zhang Lingquan had brought the car around, window down: "What are you staring at?"

Wang Mingzhi pulled the door open and got in. Eyes shut: "Did anyone from above reach out to Jiang Qing? Because he's not scared of anything."

"They did. He wouldn't listen." Zhang Lingquan started the car with a small scoff. "Rumor has it he's pushing to terminate his contract early."

"Terminate?" Wang Mingzhi opened his eyes. "He's leaving Ruihua? Ruihua is the biggest name in the industry."

"Too many people, too few good parts. Don't follow his lead. You've been at the company long enough, and you don't want to end up making enemies on both sides with nothing to show for it."

Wang Mingzhi slumped back against the headrest, one corner of his mouth lifting. "I won't. Get in touch with the young master. I want to meet with him in person."

"He'll come looking for you anyway. You had the nerve to threaten the boss's favorite asset. Bold of you."

The car slipped out of the lot, and across the way, Jiang Qing got into the passenger seat and buckled in. He'd barely settled before Lin Xun asked: "This late tonight?"

"Did you wait long?"

"Not long. I'd just finished my own business."

Lin Xun steered out onto the main road. The neon signs outside were still burning bright. A few people walked along the sidewalk, unhurried.

Lin Xun was thinking about how to bring up the film and the studio. He'd been organizing his words for some time, and glanced to the side, only to find Jiang Qing with his eyes shut, head tilted slightly toward the window, fast asleep.

Tired, probably.

He pressed the accelerator a little harder, staying just at the edge of the speed limit, and they reached Yishui Bay in no time.

He parked, switched on the reading light, and reached over to wake Jiang Qing, but his hand stopped halfway.

The car had been running the air conditioning. Jiang Qing had folded one arm loosely across himself, eyes closed, breathing quiet, clean and still.

The warm amber glow of the reading light fell on that unguarded face, and every feature seemed more precisely cut than usual. A few strands of hair had fallen forward toward his lips, casting the faintest shadow.

Lin Xun stared without meaning to. His hand moved again, fingers extending slightly, wanting to brush those strands back.

He was almost there when Jiang Qing's lashes moved. His eyes opened, and he looked at Lin Xun, steady and unblinking.

Silence.

Lin Xun met those eyes. His throat moved. He opened his mouth, thinking to explain himself, when he heard Jiang Qing say, flatly: "Were you about to do something to me?"

Lin Xun: "..."

He pulled his hand back. He thought, privately, about who exactly was tempting whom.

Here, in another man's car, late at night, falling asleep with complete and total trust, and looking this good doing it. That was deliberately catching someone's attention.

He'd seen that move in more variations than he could count. It had never worked on him before.

It wasn't going to work now. He was immune.

Jiang Qing, unaware of the mountain range Lin Xun's thoughts had just crossed, rubbed his eyes, unclipped the seatbelt, and walked ahead.

Lin Xun sat in the car watching him from behind, and gave a quiet, brief laugh. So you know how to play it slow, make someone reach first?

At the apartment doors, Jiang Qing yawned, then turned abruptly: "That WeChat message, you said something about a project worth over a hundred million?"

Lin Xun looked at him, eyes soft with the tail end of that long yawn, the tiredness in them still clouding the edges.

He thought something he did not say, and instead spoke: "Yes. I want you to..."

Jiang Qing woke up immediately.

Author's note: Jiang Qing: I have something to say and I'm not sure I should say it.

chapters.title: The Conversation
chapters.content:
The hallway was so quiet it could have caught the sound of a pin dropping. A moment later, the clear snap of knuckles cracking.

Jiang Qing flexed his hand, turned to face Lin Xun, eyes sharp, teeth on edge: "What did you just say?"

Lin Xun's expression was calm and pleasant: "I'd like you to join my studio."

Jiang Qing stood there blankly for a moment, slow to register it. "What studio?"

Lin Xun glanced at his watch. It was very late. "It's a lot to explain right now. Get some rest first, we'll talk tomorrow."

Jiang Qing gave him a half-suspicious look, feeling fairly certain this was a stalling tactic. "You'd better have something real to say. Otherwise..."

He let his gaze drift downward, landing somewhere below Lin Xun's waist.

Lin Xun felt a chill run up his spine. He couldn't make out what was behind that look in the dim light, but he was fairly certain the intention was intense.

He got himself inside in a hurry, pressed his back against the door, and let out a slow, deliberate breath. He tugged at his collar, fanning the warmth away.

This Jiang Qing was getting harder and harder to read.

He peeled off his jacket and went toward the bathroom, setting the water temperature a degree cooler than usual.

The next morning, the first light was barely visible on the horizon. Elsewhere, a different kind of vitality was making its presence known.

Lin Xun glanced down. He let out an almost imperceptible sigh.

This was not an unusual occurrence, but it had a particular kind of energy about it today.

He went for a run in the complex gardens, then stopped to pick up several types of breakfast before heading back to entice Jiang Qing with food.

But the door stayed unanswered through ten, fifteen rings of the bell. In ordinary circumstances, that was when the grumpy version of Jiang Qing would have flung the door open for his morning routine of hostile remarks.

There was something very appealing about a person whose irritability dissolved so easily, who could be entirely soothed with a single bag of food.

Jiang Qing was sitting in the office with a steamed bun.

Sang Yi had caught an early flight back and gone straight to a nearby breakfast stall to pick up his favorites.

"Light-ge, Principal Sang mentioned wanting to expand the facility. A music room and an art room."

Jiang Qing looked at what was left of the bun in his hand and passed it back to her. "Is this why you bought the buns?"

"Of course not." Sang Yi froze, eyes going a little evasive. "I would come all the way just to bring you buns any day. That's not what I... The principal brought it up briefly. He didn't feel right asking directly. He told me not to say anything, but there are kids with real talent..."

She scratched her ear, looking miserable, and met his eyes: "I'm sorry. I shouldn't have... Eat your buns, they're getting cold."

Jiang Qing took them back.

He finished the bun in a few bites and wiped his mouth. "You don't need to talk yourself into knots about it. If the principal wants to build something, he should just submit a proper request. What does he think he's doing, sending messages through you? Have I ever turned down a legitimate request in all the time I've known him?"

Sang Yi looked at him with quiet gratitude and said quietly: "He's been ill. He didn't want to reach out directly because he was afraid you'd think he was using it as leverage."

Jiang Qing paused. "Is it serious?"

"He just got out of the hospital."

"Mm... I should go visit when I have time." He caught the flicker of emotion in Sang Yi's eyes and smiled a little. "After the contract wraps. Once things settle down, we'll go back together."

"Yes!" Sang Yi broke into a genuine smile.

The office door opened from outside. Shu Tong came in with a stack of documents, and the sound of the two of them talking and laughing brightened her mood before she'd even said anything.

"The young master came into the company. He's in a meeting with the head of the artist department. It's probably about you."

"Welcome, I'm sure."

He thought back over what he remembered. His interactions with this person were nearly nonexistent. All he knew was a name: Bai Bangnan. Returned from abroad, showing signs of taking over Ruihua Entertainment.

Half an hour later, Shu Tong got the message. She picked up the documents, and both of them headed to the conference room.

At the head of the table sat a lean, sharp-faced young man, dressed impeccably. In the world of second-generation heirs, he would count as someone with actual ability.

To Jiang Qing, he was simply another wealthy heir in a well-fitted suit.

The man had his legs crossed and his manner unhurried, and let his gaze land on Jiang Qing for a moment before moving on.

The head of the artist department was seated to the right. Shu Tong took the seat across from them. Jiang Qing sat quietly beside her.

The two sides exchanged brief civilities and went straight to the point.

The department head raised the matter of early termination and laid out several reasons why it shouldn't happen.

Shu Tong produced a documented record of every resource and project over the past year and a half, then pulled out the contract, highlighting the clause that guaranteed a minimum of one film and one endorsement per year.

The department head responded that Jiang Qing had been at the peak of his marketability when he signed, but that the current landscape had shifted, and the company had to make clear-eyed decisions accordingly. Resources had to go where they were most effective.

Jiang Qing laughed inwardly at that.

Redirect every resource to the newcomer, use his name to pave the newcomer's path, and then on top of that ask him to throw a competition in a televised show to let the newcomer win. And this was being called effective allocation?

How effective.

"Skip to the end," he said. "Will you agree to terminate or not?"

The department head exchanged a glance with Bai Bangnan, then argued: "The contract hasn't expired. There's no need to rush. Manager Chen found a variety show for you. Spend the last few months constructively, and then when the time comes, we all part on good terms."

"What variety show?" He looked at the department head without particular urgency, one hand resting on the table, fingers tapping lightly.

"I... don't have those details on hand. Manager Chen is personally keeping an eye on it."

The department head had been dealing with Shu Tong for three years and had very little direct contact with Jiang Qing himself. But the last few minutes had adjusted his assessment. However young, this was someone who had been operating in this industry for years. There was nothing naive about him.

With the recent boost from the variety show, Jiang Qing's profile was up again, and even with only a few months left on the contract, he was still technically under the company's umbrella and subject to its decisions.

The department head had thought of that. Jiang Qing had clearly thought of it too.

Jiang Qing set aside the diplomatic approach: "I want to terminate now. Otherwise we take it to legal, and then we'll see which holds out longer, me as a fading name with nothing to lose, or a company that has plans on the horizon."

The department head went still.

So that was it. The company was preparing to go public, and there couldn't be any complications at this stage.

Risking a lawsuit over an artist whose contract was nearly up anyway, one who could generate noise and bad press at any moment, was not a calculation worth making.

The department head looked to Bai Bangnan.

Bai Bangnan let out a short laugh. His gaze found Jiang Qing with a sharpness in it. "A mutual equity clause. Five years of full autonomy, in exchange for which you'd agree to bring in a baseline of returns for the company at agreed-upon intervals..."

"I decline." Jiang Qing cut him off before the sentence finished. If he was going to have that kind of freedom, he might as well go independent. No point.

An equity clause sounded attractive, but it was still a leash. If he was going to carry the risk, he wanted to carry it entirely on his own terms.

Bai Bangnan regarded him in silence for a long moment, then turned to the department head: "Draw up the paperwork for termination. Ruihua doesn't hold onto people who don't want to be here."

Jiang Qing rose with a mild smile, no desire to drag it out further. He nodded: "Thank you. And congratulations in advance on the listing."

Bai Bangnan watched him and Shu Tong leave. At the door, Jiang Qing said something to Shu Tong, and they were talking and laughing again.

A clean profile. A good smile that went directly to the chest.

A shame he preferred the uncomplicated type. Jiang Qing, whatever else he was, was clearly not that.

Something else came to mind. He said: "Get Wang Mingzhi. Tell him to come see me."

Someone who threatened him in a parking lot in the middle of the night was not a category of person you encountered often.

Fifteen minutes later, Wang Mingzhi came in. He was wearing a plain white T-shirt, none of the dramatic styling from the recording. He looked young. Seventeen, eighteen.

Bai Bangnan's expression registered something approving. He indicated the seat beside him and shifted his own chair slightly left, looking at him directly: "You've got nerve. Anything you want to say?"

Wang Mingzhi glanced at the department head.

Bai Bangnan followed the look: "You can get back to work. Move quickly on the Jiang Qing matter, and keep it quiet. My father doesn't need to know about it."

"Yes. I'll see to it immediately." The department head gathered his documents, gave Wang Mingzhi one unreadable glance as he passed, sighed almost inaudibly at something, and left.

Once the door closed, Wang Mingzhi surfaced from what had just been said, and tested the air: "Jiang Qing is really terminating?"

"Isn't that what you wanted?" Bai Bangnan said with a quiet laugh.

"Yes..." Wang Mingzhi's fingers contracted slightly. He'd wanted this. But now that the moment had arrived, something hollow moved through him.

Bai Bangnan said: "Tell me. How did you find out about me and Gao Yuanqiao?"

Wang Mingzhi steadied himself, met the appraising look, and then, as though throwing everything on the table, reached over and took the other man's hand: "Because I was jealous of Gao Yuanqiao."

Bai Bangnan looked down at the overlapping hands. Then he looked up at Wang Mingzhi's face, clear-featured and vivid.

A brief, quiet laugh.

On the other side of the building, Shu Tong had been handling the contract details with the department head all morning. She'd barely made it back to the office before her takeout went cold. She ate quickly, three or four fast bites, then looked up at the two of them sitting there waiting.

A short silence, and then Shu Tong's entirely composed face allowed itself one small crack. A smile. "Done. Termination is official as of next week. The compensation from 'I Am an Actor' will still be processed per the original contract terms. Everything else has been cleanly divided. My own resignation was accepted at the same time. Sang Yi was never under the company directly, she's been paid through your private account, so there's nothing to untangle there."

Sang Yi put down her chopsticks and did an enthusiastic seal clap. "We get to go home."

Jiang Qing knocked the top of her head lightly and said with mock severity: "Your brother is about to be unemployed. And you're sitting there grinning."

Sang Yi covered her head and laughed. "Light-ge is finally free."

Whether it was real freedom was another question. For all he knew, the next step would land him straight into a different kind of trap.

The next move had to be chosen carefully.

After lunch, he checked the time and started for home.

He pulled open the door and found Gao Yuanqiao hovering outside it, shifty and uncertain.

"Something you need?"

Gao Yuanqiao's shoulders went up, and he turned. He pressed his lips together and murmured: "Shixiong. I have something I need to tell you."

Too many ears in the company. Jiang Qing took him to a private members' club nearby, the kind with a cocktail bar, billiards, a card room, all the trappings, and a quiet corner booth.

Jiang Qing ordered an Americano. Gao Yuanqiao was hugging a glass of milk, and Jiang Qing noticed: "Not a coffee person?"

Gao Yuanqiao nodded, then shook his head. "I like coffee. But I have anxiety, and it keeps me up."

Jiang Qing was opening his mouth to respond when his phone interrupted. He looked at the call from "Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!" and frowned slightly. "What's going on?"

The Pig said there was something important to discuss.

He was about to brush it off, but then Lin Xun mentioned "New Homeland." He paused. "I have something to take care of right now. I'll reach out when I'm done."

He hung up and met Gao Yuanqiao's curious look. "A pig's call. In life, you end up dealing with all kinds."

Gao Yuanqiao pulled hard on his milk straw, suddenly wondering which category he fell into in Jiang Qing's head.

He looked away, turned it over a few times, and then mustered his courage: "Shixiong. The person trying to cause you trouble is Wang Mingzhi."

Jiang Qing: "..."

That was it?

He'd sacrificed a perfectly good nap to come sit here in the afternoon and watch this kid drink milk over that?

...

Wait.

"Why do you say that?" He kept his voice entirely ignorant, which worked well enough on Gao Yuanqiao.

Gao Yuanqiao seemed to be working through something significant. It took him a while before he said quietly: "I accidentally heard a phone call."

Jiang Qing stopped. He looked at the boy, worked out the general shape of things, and felt his tone cool without meaning to: "What's your relationship with Bai Bangnan?"

Slurp.

Gao Yuanqiao drank his milk and didn't look up, flushing hard enough to want to sink through the floor.

Jiang Qing, putting it together, asked carefully: "You're not actually... in a relationship with him, are you?"

Gao Yuanqiao stopped. He looked up. His eyes were bright.

Jiang Qing thought: this kid is in serious trouble.

"Is it actually just dating?"

"He loves me and I love him." Gao Yuanqiao nodded, quietly and firmly. He snuck a glance at Jiang Qing's expression.

It was the first time he'd told anyone about this. In principle, something like this was safest kept entirely private.

But this was Jiang Qing. His idol. With the fan's particular lens applied, you always assumed your idol was different from everyone else.

But... the idol's face looked a little off.

He ducked his head in sudden regret, already bracing for the consequences of saying too much, then felt a new unease settle in.

What if his idol reacted the same way his manager had? What if he looked down on him, or threatened to expose him?

The atmosphere pulled tight. For a moment the only sound was a coffee spoon.

Then Jiang Qing drank a quiet sip and said, with a mild smile: "Love? You're really using that word?"

Gao Yuanqiao, confused, nodded.

"Rare." Jiang Qing said, something unreadable passing through his eyes and gone before it could be named, replaced with a measured kind of care. "You're young. Don't put too much weight on that word."

Especially when the person in question was Bai Bangnan. A resource-rich heir who had a habit of cycling through companions. In this morning's meeting alone, the intent in his gaze had been unmistakable.

And Gao Yuanqiao was clearly the kind of person who had just stumbled headfirst into love for the first time, fearless simply because he didn't know enough yet.

He said: "Focus on your work. Sometimes what you know is only what someone else chose to let you know. Don't be deceived by what looks true on the surface."

Gao Yuanqiao let out a breath that sounded like relief and smiled. "Understood. Thank you, Shixiong."

At that moment, the phone on the table lit up. Gao Yuanqiao picked it up and looked at the screen. An unknown number. He opened it.

A photo.

A man. Bare from the waist up. A towel barely staying in place at the hips. The most familiar person he knew.

Outside, the sun was blazing. Inside, Gao Yuanqiao felt like he'd fallen into ice water.

Jiang Qing finished his coffee, noticed that the other boy's hands were white around the phone, his face drained, nothing at all like the sweet, oblivious kid from moments ago. Without quite meaning to, he asked: "Is something wrong?"

Gao Yuanqiao's fingers shook slightly. He arranged something that looked like a smile on his face, and it looked worse than crying. "Shixiong. I just remembered I have somewhere to be. I'll head out."

He stood, and the motion was too large for the space. The milk glass was knocked off the table and broke, milk spreading from the edge of the table into the carpet.

He didn't stop for it. His footsteps were uneven as he went toward the door.

Jiang Qing was on his feet, a little uneasy. He'd barely taken two steps when his phone started up again.

He looked at the door, then at the phone. Going after Gao Yuanqiao would be overstepping if the boy had something private to sort through. He picked up the call, gave an address, then asked a staff member to come clean up.

Half an hour later, Lin Xun came through the door. He caught the smell of the room and said, mildly surprised: "You found a place this nice, just to secretly drink milk?"

"Pfft." Jiang Qing nearly choked on his coffee.

He pressed a napkin to his mouth, kept his eyes down, and said: "If you came just to say that, you can go. Don't disturb the atmosphere of this very fine room and its dairy fragrance."

Lin Xun sat down across from him with an expression of quiet amusement, looked around, and said idly: "No cameras around. You don't bother praising me anymore?"

"Get to the point."

"I want to open a studio. I'd like you to be part of it." Lin Xun said, direct and steady, eyes on Jiang Qing without wavering.

Jiang Qing drank from his new cup with complete composure, and smiled pleasantly: "You really do keep surprising people. Always one new idea. Quite something, coming from a man who must have descended directly from the heavens. Even the grandiosity of your ambitions has a certain otherworldly delicacy."

Lin Xun thought with considerable feeling: No. I don't want this kind of compliment.

chapters.title: The Misunderstanding Resolved
chapters.content:
Jiang Qing, naturally, didn't believe a word of it. Opening a studio was not a small thing, but it wasn't impossible either. The industry was full of them these days, every artist with any name at all dreaming of independence. But the ones that actually grew into something real were few.

Most of them burned through whatever personal visibility the artist had left, running a shell company that propped up no one. Eventually the music stopped.

Even for someone with a recognizable name, it was a gamble. As for Lin Xun, with whatever capital Yang Meng might be providing, and the fanbase he'd built, but very few credits to his name, still being called a pretty face with no depth by critics and general viewers alike. If he opened a studio, it would almost certainly be a vehicle to push himself. Where would the space be for anyone else?

And if it were to operate under an existing entertainment company, that raised its own issues. Lin Xun didn't even have a proper management team to speak of. How would such a structure even work?

None of this lined up with how Jiang Qing had been thinking about his next move. He had in mind a genuinely independent studio, one that signed artists, not just a vanity structure. But the timing and conditions had to be exactly right. His reputation among critics was complicated. Resources and funding alone were not enough. Everything had to be airtight before he could make that move.

Lin Xun said: "I'm serious."

"You're not planning to incorporate an empty shell?" Jiang Qing said, not unkindly.

Some people set up studios in name only, trading on their own recognition until someone with capital offered to buy them out, and then cashed in. It was a known strategy.

Lin Xun raised an eyebrow. "You don't trust me?"

"You barely deserve... I mean, then walk me through the actual plan. I don't agree to vague invitations."

He picked up his coffee and settled back, prepared to listen to something that would not persuade him.

"This is the plan I drafted based on my analysis of the structure and operations of domestic film and talent companies. This is the short-term development plan for the next five years, and the ten-year roadmap. And this is the artist contract framework..." Lin Xun had come prepared. He set down one document after another.

Jiang Qing stared at the stack, then at Lin Xun, then back at the stack. "You're actually serious?"

"Of course." Lin Xun blinked at him.

Jiang Qing: "..."

That reduced credibility by fifty percent.

He was going to look through this himself and see whether any of it held up.

He flipped one open at random, glanced at two lines, then looked back at Lin Xun, who nodded. Jiang Qing turned his full attention to it.

For the next hour or so, the only sound in the room was the turning of pages. His coffee went cold without him registering it. He reached for the cup out of habit, and felt a hand close around his wrist.

Lin Xun took the cup. "Cold. I'll have them refresh it."

He nodded without looking up.

Lin Xun, watching him like that, felt something quiet and warm move through his eyes.

While the server refreshed the coffee, Lin Xun got a message from Yang Meng asking how things were going.

He looked over at Jiang Qing.

The afternoon sun was coming through the window at an angle, carrying the last heat of summer, warming what the air conditioning left cool. All the light that remained landed on the person by the window.

A clean white shirt. An intent expression. The smell of dark coffee. This scene had the quality of something remembered, something from a dream he couldn't quite place.

He picked up his phone and, without thinking, took a photo of the moment, capturing the light and the stillness of it.

He was about to send it to Yang Meng to show him the current situation, but his finger stopped.

He'd just taken it without any real intention. And now he found he didn't feel like sharing it.

He typed instead: "Still in the conversation. May be a little difficult. Get my background materials ready."

Yang Meng, who knew him well, understood immediately and replied: "On it! I'll make sure he has full confidence and complete trust, and becomes your person heart and soul!"

Lin Xun read the last line. Something pulled at the corner of his mouth unexpectedly.

Becomes my... person?

Strange. The moment that thought surfaced, his pulse skipped once.

He had seen more striking people. More beautiful, better built, more privileged in background. More objectively impressive than Jiang Qing in every measurable respect. And yet very few had made him want to keep paying attention, made him feel like there was always something more to discover.

Right now, he thought...

Maybe he'd found it.

Could Jiang Qing, by some possibility, also...like him?

If so, what was the appropriate response?

"You're not eating?" Jiang Qing looked up, rubbed his eyes, and found Lin Xun staring vaguely forward. He asked.

"Hm?" Lin Xun came back. "I already ate. The food's for you."

Jiang Qing blinked. "All of this is just for me?"

"Yes. For community relations."

Jiang Qing rolled his eyes at him with extreme conviction and in full view.

Lin Xun smiled to himself. Yes, exactly. Quick and charming one moment, stubborn and difficult the next, quietly scheming all the while. This person knew, without appearing to try, exactly how to keep someone's attention.

Jiang Qing finished a full breakfast under Lin Xun's complicated gaze, felt very satisfied with himself, and privately concluded that his extraordinary appearance was simply too overwhelming for the man to properly handle.

Ha. You had no idea how good your grandpa Qing looked when he made the effort.

In this elevated mood, he agreed without thinking to Lin Xun's request to be taken around the area, as he'd been asked before.

On the way out, he ran back to the wardrobe and produced a pair of newly purchased sunglasses, the latest model, put them on with practiced ease, snapped his fingers, and declared: "Let's go."

The corner of Lin Xun's mouth lifted and refused to come back down.

Fine, he decided. He'd watch and wait. See what moves were made. Lin Xun, entering what felt very much like the beginning of a new personal project, nodded to himself.

The complex was well-maintained. Even in the center of the city, the greenery was proper greenery, the shade along the paths genuinely blocking out the summer heat.

Every facility was in good shape. Gym, casual bar, all the usual sports and recreation options.

Past the main gate and a short walk ahead was an imported supermarket, with shopping malls and office buildings on either side.

They walked, exchanging the occasional comment.

Both of them were tall with long strides, and even behind sunglasses, their effect on the surrounding air was undeniable. This area had its share of attractive people, and the complex housed more than a few entertainers, but two of them side by side on the street still drew more attention than either alone.

A group of young women on the side of the road were nudging each other. The bravest among them, cheeks flushed, started toward them.

Lin Xun caught the motion and noticed that Jiang Qing had suddenly accelerated, leaving the approaching woman nothing but a retreating back that made it clear he was not interested.

The woman hesitated, then redirected toward Lin Xun.

Then that handsome man also went chasing after the first one.

The woman: "..."

The small episode passed. Lin Xun checked the time. They'd covered most of the surrounding area, and he offered to buy lunch.

Jiang Qing accepted without ceremony and picked the revolving restaurant on the top floor.

Dishes of all kinds were laid out around the buffet. Jiang Qing carried his plate back and noticed Lin Xun's selection was entirely Western. "You prefer Western food?"

Lin Xun nodded. "I'm accustomed to it."

"I see... Let me go get a few more things." Something moved across Jiang Qing's eyes. He stood up and came back with several Sichuan dishes, set them down with a mischievous smile. "I'm more of a Chinese food person myself. Want to try?"

Lin Xun saw through the intention completely. But he couldn't resist trying, and picked up a few pieces of kung pao chicken.

The heat of the spice activated his senses immediately. Not unbearable, but for someone who had genuinely never built up a tolerance, it was still a small adventure.

He exhaled carefully, drank a long sip of water, and still managed to say: "It's good."

Jiang Qing had assumed it was a performance, but it was becoming clear that Lin Xun actually could not eat spicy food. He quickly poured more water, and once Lin Xun's color returned to normal, said gruffly: "Don't eat it if you can't. No one made you."

Lin Xun waved a hand. "I'm alright. Good to try things. And this particular thing is clearly outside my range."

Jiang Qing laughed in spite of himself, and pushed all the Sichuan food to his own side. Then, without comment, slid the Western plate Lin Xun had been eating from across the table, as an offering.

Lin Xun took in the small movement. The warmth in his throat relocated to somewhere around his heart, an unfamiliar and faintly unsettling heat.

"It's warm out," Jiang Qing said, out of nothing in particular.

"Hm?" Lin Xun looked at him with something quiet and attentive in his expression. "Where?"

"The weather." Jiang Qing gestured toward the windows. "The sun is intense. I forgot my sunscreen."

First rule of maintaining one's appearance, and he'd missed it.

Lin Xun lowered his head, one corner of his mouth curving by a fraction.

This inexplicable heat was definitely the weather's fault.

The sun outside continued to blaze. After lunch, they went home.

At the door, Lin Xun stopped him. "Thank you for the company today. I'll return the favor soon."

"Didn't you just take me to lunch?"

"That was today. Next time I'll cook."

Jiang Qing raised an eyebrow. "You cook?"

"Yes. A rare chance. First come, first served." Lin Xun smiled as he pushed his door open. "Let me get through the next few busy days first, then I'll let you know."

"Alright." Free food was free food.

He reflected again on Yang Meng's genuinely excellent judgment.

Shu Tong wrapped up at the Wutong orphanage and came straight back, leaving Sang Yi to stay a few extra days.

When she found out Lin Xun had moved in next door, she invented a reason to go introduce herself, but no one answered. She came back and got down to business with Jiang Qing.

"The director of 'I Am an Actor' was in touch. Recent episodes have been performing well, but the buzz is dipping. He wants you to create some conflict."

Jiang Qing signaled that he understood.

The production had specifically brought him on for the sharp edge of his reputation. The flattery had generated novelty-driven interest, but sustained exposure to the same dynamic would eventually bore an audience. They wanted something new, and since Teacher Wen and Su Hongru were harder to involve in that kind of shift, he was the obvious choice again.

"Is there a contestant list for the next episode?"

"The only confirmed name so far is Wang Mingzhi."

"He's really something, that one." Jiang Qing said with genuine appreciation.

Shu Tong gave a weary sigh and rubbed her forehead. She glanced at the calendar, weighed it, then said: "You remember what day it is tomorrow, don't you?"

"No." No hesitation.

"You say you don't remember, but I haven't even said what day... When did you last go home? Go see your father. It's his birthday."

She knew Jiang Qing's relationship with his father was bad. Since she'd taken over his management, he had never once brought up visiting voluntarily. He'd cited disagreements over being in the entertainment industry, fights every time he went back, and eventually he'd simply moved out and not returned. That dynamic had held ever since.

By all accounts, a child actor was the hardest to manage, especially through adolescence. But Jiang Qing had never dated, never caused incidents, never generated rumors for her to chase. He was the easiest client she'd ever had.

That said, he was far from without edges. They had all been concentrated and directed at one person, and that particular stubbornness had not softened across all the years since.

She had been watching for an opening to help bridge things.

Jiang Qing spun his phone without much feeling. "Why bother going? There are plenty of people queuing up to celebrate him. I'm not needed."

"Can you do it as a favor to me? I don't want to hear people say I let you skip your own father's birthday." Shu Tong let her voice go soft, the one that rarely failed. "And Xiao Bao has a parent-teacher conference tomorrow. I haven't been able to go to one in years."

Jiang Qing's eyes dropped. He nodded quietly. "Go. I'll take care of tomorrow."

After Shu Tong left, he lay down for most of the afternoon, got up for dinner, and went back to bed.

Around ten at night, someone rang the bell. He didn't answer. He didn't want to see anyone.

His phone lit up in the dark.

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: Asleep? I brought food, want some?

He typed two words: Asleep.

Stinky Smug Stupid Pig!: Rest well then. I'm making a big dinner tomorrow and inviting a few people. Come join us.

No reply. He pulled the covers over his head.

The consequence was waking up before six the next morning.

He dragged himself up, washed, and went to the wardrobe.

Jiang Huai was a businessman. Always sharply dressed, projecting seriousness. He had resented Jiang Qing's choice to be in entertainment from the beginning, as though it were some lasting embarrassment to the Jiang name.

Jiang Qing selected with deliberate care. He'd bought this online, cheap, a loose streetwear white tee covered in English text that could only be described as coarse, though at a glance most people wouldn't read closely enough to register it.

The trousers were distressed and torn in all the ways most likely to make any respectable middle-aged person's eye twitch.

He styled his hair with a curling iron into something conspicuous and deliberately spiraling, then drove to the family home wearing all of this.

The Jiang house was in the eastern outskirts, surrounded by hills and a stream, quietly refined.

He drove a sports car at a tortoise's pace, earning himself a string of honks and colorful remarks from other drivers.

The iron gates at the entrance were faithfully parted on both sides. The domestic staff, working in the garden, all paused to look at him.

He parked beside the fountain, shut the door hard, leaned against the car, and put on his sunglasses. Under the weight of several complicated expressions, he walked into the opulent European-style villa.

The housekeeper, Auntie Yu, was giving instructions to the staff. When she saw him enter, she said with polite composure: "Young master, you're back."

He gave a flat "mm" and looked up at the closed door on the second-floor landing. "Still in bed?"

"Yes. Mr. Jiang had a late engagement last night. He had a few drinks."

Auntie Yu added: "More than a few. He was not in any condition to walk."

Jiang Qing looked at her steadily.

Auntie Yu dropped her gaze.

She had been with the family for eighteen years and could count the times she'd seen this young master on her fingers. She had never once seen him smile. The size of his temper was the kind that left things in pieces, and all the staff kept their distance. Every year on this particular day, the whole household braced itself. No one knew what he would do.

Especially today.

She cast a worried glance toward the second floor.

Jiang Qing followed her gaze, drew his own conclusions, and his expression went entirely flat, eyes cooling quickly. He went upstairs without another word, every step controlled and deliberate.

"Young master, go slowly, Mr. Jiang is still resting..." Auntie Yu followed behind at a half-run, her voice rising in a way that suggested she was trying to reach someone's ears upstairs.

Jiang Qing's certainty was building. He reached the top of the stairs and one of the doors opened.

A woman with long hair stepped out. She was wearing one of Jiang Huai's shirts, legs bare beneath the hem, and she looked toward the staircase with visible alarm. "Auntie..."

Auntie Yu answered quietly from behind Jiang Qing.

The woman turned her head, saw Jiang Qing, and went very still. Her fingers closed around the shirt hem. Her voice carried a faint tremor: "A-Qing..."

"A-Qing?" Jiang Qing gave a flat laugh. He moved toward her one step at a time, his gaze doing exactly what a drawn blade does. "You think you can call me that?"

She was not remarkable-looking. In the entertainment world she would have gone unremarked.

But Jiang Qing's attention caught on one thing. A beauty mark. A well-placed teardrop at the corner of the eye.

"You have the right to address me like that?"

"I... listen, it wasn't intentional, Mr. Jiang had too much to drink last night..." The woman's face was red, and her explanation faltered before she'd even finished it.

Jiang Qing cut her off. "And you took advantage of that?" His lips curved slightly, without warmth. "That excuse has been thoroughly worn out. Every woman who ends up in his bed says the same thing."

The woman's eyes dropped.

Jiang Qing tilted her chin up with two fingers, no gentleness in the gesture, and looked at her face. "Secretary Mu?"

She nodded, unable to move away, and murmured: "If Mr. Jiang knew you were here, I'm certain he would be very glad."

Jiang Qing released her chin. "Glad? Tell him to come out."

"He's still asleep. I was about to leave. He probably doesn't even know who I am yet..." Secretary Mu managed a wry, uncomfortable smile. "We could act as though none of this happened."

"Pathetic, and stupid." Jiang Qing held her gaze, each word measured. "Do you not know who lives in this house?"

His voice cut off sharply—
