chapters.title: Hot Pot and Drama
chapters.content:
Jiang Qing couldn't cook, but he had agreed to it in a moment of impulse.

Of course, quick-witted as he was, he immediately thought of hot pot, a one-stop solution, meat and vegetables together, perfect in every way.

Since Lin Xun didn't eat spicy food, he prepared a beef hot pot.

The ingredients at home were pitifully scarce, so he set up the pot in Lin Xun's kitchen.

Lin Xun asked, "What about the broth base? Are you making that by hand too?"

"I'll order the broth base by hand," Jiang Qing said cleverly, picking up his phone. The moment he opened the delivery app, Lin Xun snatched it away.

"I'll teach you."

Jiang Qing said, "That doesn't seem right, it's too much trouble."

"It's fine."

"No, I mean my hands might not be very convenient."

Lin Xun looked at him quietly.

After a long moment, Jiang Qing caved. "Fine, fine, fine, let's do it!"

Once all the ingredients were prepared, Jiang Qing stood in front of the pot like he was facing a great enemy and asked, "How do I start?"

A full minute passed without any response.

He turned to look, and there was Lin Xun, leisurely pulling up a webpage and searching for a beef hot pot recipe.

"......Jiang Qing gritted his teeth. "Don't think I won't stew you into red-braised Lin Xun."

"Good things take time," Lin Xun said with a faint smile. "Pour the oil, add the ginger slices, star anise..."

The oil sizzled and crackled. Jiang Qing retreated half a meter back, tossing in the ginger slices and star anise from a distance, waving the spatula from afar, looking for all the world like he was performing some kind of ritual.

Suddenly, a large hand covered his, warmth spreading across the back of his hand, not much cooler than the oil in the pan.

"How are you supposed to cook from way over there?" Lin Xun said, his expression unchanged. He applied pressure with his hand and drew Jiang Qing closer, guiding his hand to stir-fry the contents of the pan.

The aroma immediately began to fill the air. Lin Xun's other hand dropped in the sliced beef.

Jiang Qing tried to pull away a couple of times, but the other man only held on tighter. He said blankly, "You never said anything about hands-on teaching."

Lin Xun said, "Desperate times call for desperate measures. I'd rather not watch my own kitchen go up in flames. Pay attention."

"Oh." Jiang Qing was persuaded. Come to think of it, Lin Xun had already cleared up the whole gay thing, so there was nothing to be awkward about anymore.

After water was added to the pot, Lin Xun finally released his hand and smiled with perfect composure. "Simple enough, right?"

"Seems manageable."

Jiang Qing leaned in with some curiosity to watch what was happening in the pot.

He didn't notice Lin Xun move his hand behind his back and close it gently, his palm burning with heat.

Once the broth base was ready, they moved to the living room. The table was laid out with fresh slices of marbled beef, various cuts of tripe and brisket, beef tendon, hanging dragon, beef balls, and fresh vegetables.

Steam curled above the pot, and just looking at it was enough to work up an appetite.

Jiang Qing placed the meat slices into the strainer ladle, dipped them three times, then placed the cooked pieces into Lin Xun's bowl before happily starting on his own.

Halfway through the meal, with his stomach only half full, he slowed down.

Through the rising steam and haze between them, he glanced at Lin Xun across the table, a stomach full of questions and no idea where to start.

Just then, Lin Xun looked up. The steam had turned his lips an even deeper shade of red. "What do you want to know?"

Jiang Qing was momentarily caught off guard, then decided to just ask directly. "Is Ruian Investment really your company? Where did you get the capital?"

"It is. The assignment at school was about how to run a company. I figured practicing was better than just discussing it, so I tried my hand at it."

Jiang Qing was speechless. What kind of prodigy does something like that?

"Don't worry about the capital. I made quite a bit from competition prizes, project fees, stocks, and mutual funds. Oh, and my allowance from growing up."

"Did you make a lot from stocks?"

"A lot. I got lucky and caught a bull market, then got too lazy to keep managing it and cashed out. Who knew the market would tank after that? Just lucky, I guess." Lin Xun smiled like luck was all it had been.

Jiang Qing's eyes shifted. "And was the allowance a lot?"

"A lot. My family has many relatives but very few children, and I'm the oldest." Lin Xun smiled. "I also have a few younger female cousins. Very sweet girls."

After saying so, he noticed Jiang Qing give a flat "oh" and poke at his bowl without responding.

It suddenly came back to him, that rainy night when Jiang Qing had returned home drenched to the bone. Reading between the lines of what Shu Tong had shared, it seemed like Jiang Qing didn't have the best relationship with his family.

Lin Xun quietly cursed himself and redirected with a smile. "They love good-looking guys. If they ever meet you, they'll definitely adore you."

"Is that so?" Jiang Qing smiled a little.

"Of course." Lin Xun looked into his bright eyes and added, "No one could dislike you."

Jiang Qing smiled and bit down on his chopsticks, thinking to himself: rainbow flattery really does pack a punch, it's genuinely pleasant to hear.

He returned the favor. "You're pretty handsome yourself."

"Pretty?"

Jiang Qing was at a loss. Why does he always push for more?

He added, "Very! Extremely! The kind of handsome that overflows!"

Lin Xun's eyes curved into a smile as he placed a beef ball in his bowl. "If you have nice things to say, say more of them."

"......"

Jiang Qing bit into the beef ball. Savory juice burst out, wrapped around the springy meat. He chewed for a moment, then circled back to the real topic. "What was the idea behind opening the studio?"

"Because of you."

Jiang Qing's hand stopped. His lips parted slightly, and for a moment he didn't know whether to keep eating or say something. Then he turned his head and coughed twice. "Almost choked!"

Lin Xun propped his chin in one hand and laughed for a good while before finally saying, "I mean it, it really is because of you. I admire how seriously and selectively you approach your work. I believe you can make me a lot of money. And at the same time, I want to help you. Someone who puts in as much heart as you do shouldn't be held back by outside noise."

Jiang Qing stared at him, unsure what to say.

To call him a businessman felt off, given how simple and almost laughable his reasons for helping were. To call him a philanthropist didn't quite fit either, since he still intended to use Jiang Qing to make money.

"There are so many people in the entertainment industry......" Jiang Qing muttered.

"But you're the only one I like." Lin Xun cut him off.

Jiang Qing shot him a look. If he didn't already know Lin Xun wasn't gay, he'd almost think the man had spent the entire evening finding roundabout ways to flirt with him.

"What do you like about me?"

"Everything. Your looks, your figure, your personality, your work......" Lin Xun rattled off a long list of qualities, then added, "Mm... and the way you've decorated your apartment. I like that too."

Jiang Qing was stunned.

You like that too?

The toilet paper is imported and the washboard is a family heirloom. Do you like those as well?

He grumbled internally, almost starting to wonder if Lin Xun was confessing in some roundabout way. He even began to ask himself, was he really that outstanding?

Yes, he was.

He proudly popped another ball into his mouth and asked, "Where's the company located?"

"Right above Ruian. We just leased the space, and the paperwork is still being processed. No rush, take your time thinking it over."

"What if I never agree?"

"Then I won't open it. I'll open an esports club instead."

Jiang Qing nearly choked on the ball again.

Good lord. The domineering CEO Lin Xun played on screen was nothing compared to the real thing.

"So you're saying you absolutely have to sign me?"

"Yes."

Jiang Qing felt a little giddy, and smiled with a satisfied air. "I'm very grateful that you think so highly of me, but this isn't something that can be settled over one meal."

"Then three meals?" Lin Xun asked. "Plus five cups of milk tea?"

Jiang Qing was speechless.

Sir, slow down, I can't keep up with the way your mind works.

After dinner, Lin Xun cleared the table and stood at the sink getting ready to wash the dishes. "There's fruit in the fridge. Want some?"

"Sure." Jiang Qing pulled out a box of strawberries and set them on the edge of the sink.

Lin Xun casually opened the box, washed each strawberry and arranged them in a bowl, pushed it in front of Jiang Qing, then went back to washing the dishes.

Jiang Qing ate a few, finding the gesture oddly thoughtful.

He was the guest and he was acting like quite the pampered lord. Out of goodwill, he picked up a strawberry and held it up to Lin Xun's lips. "A reward for you."

"Thank you." With both hands occupied, Lin Xun leaned forward and bit into it, accidentally grazing Jiang Qing's fingers. He pressed down the stir of feeling that rose in him.

The sweetness spread through his mouth at once, slipping somewhere into the vicinity of his heart.

He tilted his head and murmured, "Another one."

"Fine, fine," Jiang Qing passed another over, but warned, "Don't touch my hand again."

A moment later, Jiang Qing was furious. "Lin Xun! I said don't touch, so you bite instead?!"

Lin Xun's shoulders trembled lightly. He took the few punches that followed without flinching, barely feeling them, like a cat scratching at him.

That evening, the latest episode of "I Am an Actor" was airing. Jiang Qing grabbed drinks while Lin Xun washed more fruit, and they settled onto the sofa together to watch.

Once they were set up, Lin Xun opened his laptop to handle some work matters.

He glanced up at the screen every so often and noticed that Jiang Qing wasn't exactly showering anyone with praise. He was picking things apart.

[Jiang Qing's seal has been broken! He's roasting people now!]

[His commentary is so satisfying!]

[Isn't he being a bit too harsh? At least leave the poor girl some dignity, I feel so bad, she's about to cry.]

[Jiang Qing is like ten years younger than her, he has zero respect for his seniors.]

[No shade, no hype, but I think he has a point. The reason so many terrible films pile up is because people are too lenient with actors.]

[Jiang Qing's styling keeps getting better and better, give the makeup artist a raise.]

......

Halfway through the episode, Jiang Qing took a sip of water and suddenly said, "Let's make a bet."

"On what?" Lin Xun turned to look at him.

Jiang Qing lifted his chin slightly, a flash of cunning and smugness in his eyes, and spoke slowly. "I bet that by the end of this, you'll be completely hooked on me."

Lin Xun's throat tightened. His fingers slipped, and he accidentally pressed a key on the keyboard before composing himself and asking casually, "And the stakes?"

"Hmm......" Jiang Qing looked around and picked up a bottle of cold beer nearby. "This. Whoever loses has to finish it."

"Deal."

Lin Xun wrapped up the last of his work and turned his full attention to the television, just in time for the final contestant to take the stage.

The moment Wang Mingzhi stepped out, the comment section exploded. His fans swarmed in and flooded it with praise, but his performance was noticeably less impactful than the two groups before him.

Then Jiang Qing started in on him again.

[Tearing into a traffic star with his bare hands, Jiang Qing, you're something else!]

[Oh god, run! The enemy fans are coming to attack Jiang Qing!]

[Jiang Qing, I'm begging you to have some kindness. The entertainment industry isn't your house and the stage isn't your ruler, both senior judges haven't said a word, so what are you going on about?!]

[I love my brother's acting, so what! He's a newcomer, he can't compare to someone who's been in the industry for twenty years. Who are you to attack him like that?!]

[My brother is so brave for going on this show, I respect his courage. Keep flying, brother, we'll always be here for you!]

[Su Hongru is trying not to laugh! Hahaha Jiang Qing's antics must have gotten to him!]

[Su Hongru's inner monologue: how is this kid saying everything I was thinking.]

[Wang Mingzhi should probably go back and train some more. Also, the fact that Jiang Qing hasn't been punched yet is genuinely a miracle.]

Lin Xun said wryly, "You're sure a scene like this is going to make me fall for you?"

Jiang Qing stared at the ceiling, embarrassed.

Just then, a line from Wang Mingzhi on screen cut through their exchange and sent the comment section into a frenzy.

"Teacher Jiang, I challenge you."

[Ahhh! A casual viewer just became a fan from that line alone! So cool!]

[Go, Wang Mingzhi!]

[You're the best, brother, go for it!]

[Am I the only one who thinks he's playing with fire?]

[This is exciting, enough talking, let's go!]

What followed was the backstage mentor battle round. The edited segment of Jiang Qing and Liu Huimin wasn't long, mostly showing the part where he had her watch playback footage to rebuild her confidence.

[Why is Jiang Qing still not rehearsing? He's just watching videos. Isn't it obvious he doesn't want to coach anyone?]

[Who's this woman? I don't recognize her.]

[Is he underestimating his competition? How could anything good come out of this?]

One minute later, a voiceover played with Liu Huimin's personal interview. "The greatest thing I got from being on this show was getting to know Jiang Qing. He helped me adjust my mindset, had me watch my own edited footage to rebuild my confidence, and taught me without holding anything back. Honestly, at my age, I thought my creative passion was long gone, but working with him made me feel like I'd found it again."

[Do the people who were talking trash feel any sting now?]

[Were you all getting too full of yourselves, or did you think us Jiang fans had gone soft? We were just trying to quietly enjoy his show, and you had to stir everything up. When we old fans were stanning, you lot were still playing in the mud.]

[Exactly, sis. We need to reorganize ourselves. Old-school fans aren't easy to mess with either.]

[Not hyping, not hating, but the pairing of Liu Huimin and Jiang Qing genuinely worked better than the one with Wang Mingzhi.]

[Wait, didn't this actress star in a really acclaimed arthouse film? I almost didn't recognize her.]

[A truly good actor isn't just someone who performs well themselves. Being able to bring out the best in others around you, now that's what real talent looks like.]

[Are we finally getting to the exciting part?!]

[Ahhhhh I'm so jealous of the live audience! I can't wait to see the improv script!]

[Dying to know what kind of scene they're going to be given!]

Lin Xun's attention was fully captured. Watching the person who had just finished one scene immediately go prepare for the next, he said, "No wonder it ran so late last time."

Jiang Qing nodded. "If it hadn't gotten so late, the recording probably could've gone even longer, given us at least a little more time to prepare."

At that moment, a burst of enthusiastic applause from the video interrupted their conversation.

[Hahaha oh my god, that outfit, let me laugh for a second first!]

[These lines are genuinely ridiculous. Wang Mingzhi almost broke character just introducing himself, hahaha, I'm losing it, next please.]

[How is Jiang Qing not breaking character? Why can he keep a straight face through this? Isn't this basically a parody?]

[Jiang Qing: time to show them what I'm really made of.]

[Wang Mingzhi can't keep up, it's getting awkward. He was so fired up earlier and now look.]

[He really did walk into that fire, he can't even hold up against one of Jiang Qing's looks.]

[Calling it now, someone's about to say: do you know how hard my brother works!]

[Haters get out! Do you know how hard my brother works! He's not trained like Jiang Qing, he's been in the industry forever! Don't mock him!]

[Hahaha I'm going to die, the prediction was spot on.]

[Go back to singing, this is a stage for actors.]

Lin Xun was genuinely surprised. He had never seen Jiang Qing like this.

Every movement carried its own shift of expression, and the enunciation and rhythm of every line were flawless.

It seemed that back when they had worked together, Jiang Qing hadn't been using anything close to his full ability.

Just how much more did this person have to offer?

As the performance reached its final stretch, Jiang Qing bound his scene partner, then stripped off the dinosaur costume. The audience let out a wave of stunned gasps.

[What the heck, what kind of ridiculous plot twist is this?]

[He was playing a woman? And without any makeup or costume to support it?!]

[Awei is DEAD!! Those eyes! That posture! He's disturbingly convincing as a woman!]

[So this is what real skill looks like. No wardrobe, no makeup, playing the opposite gender without a single awkward moment. He just completely blew every female actor on the show out of the water. I am in awe.]

[Excuse me, I think something just awakened in me. That hip movement is devastating.]

[Jiang Qing, are you looking for a boyfriend?]

[Hey buddy, stop trying to compete with us!]

[Haha relax everyone, whoever can recite his full name gets to take him home!]

[I don't deserve him. Goodbye. One last thing before I go: Jiang Qing is incredible!]

[I can't do it, I'm out. So long. Jiang Qing is incredible!]

Lin Xun tuned out the increasingly unhinged comments and kept his eyes fixed on the screen. He could even make out Wang Mingzhi's stunned expression, clearly not having anticipated this side of Jiang Qing either.

Every glance and smile pulled at something. Every step felt like it was landing directly on a person's chest.

"Pretty good, right?" Jiang Qing shook his leg and looked at Lin Xun with a satisfied smile.

Lin Xun turned to him, and the two of them smiled at each other.

Jiang Qing browsed Weibo for a while. His clip with Wang Mingzhi was being reposted everywhere, the topic tagged with the word "trending," and short video platforms were picking it up rapidly.

Wang Mingzhi already had no shortage of antifans. Someone had stirred the pot, and a flood of hate comments was targeting him across every platform, turning public opinion against him. In the same breath, his detractors were propping Jiang Qing up to the skies.

Shu Tong had seen it coming. She scrambled to contact familiar marketing accounts to push the narrative back down, then went to the fan group to make an announcement: no riding this wave of praise, or they'd be treated as antifans.

Watching Wang Mingzhi get dragged for his awkward performance, Wang Mingzhi quickly posted a self-deprecating Weibo.

@WangMingzhi: Teacher Jiang, you really are something. I lost fair and square. Next time we meet, I'll definitely be able to say your full name correctly. [fist raised]

Jiang Qing had no interest in going at him publicly, and his account was basically always in Shu Tong's hands anyway.

Shu Tong was smart. She waited until Wang Mingzhi's self-deprecating post had been upvoted to the trending list by his own fans before dropping a single comment: Sure. [grinning]

Then suddenly, a topic popped up online about Jiang Qing and Wang Mingzhi being warm colleagues, things like "co-stars in an absurd skit" and "brotherly Weibo likes and comments," as if people had uncovered something significant from such a simple exchange.

At that point, the veteran Jiang fans who had been quiet finally made their move.

They compiled every standout moment from Jiang Qing's appearances on the show, no spin, no exaggeration, just straightforward clips posted to Weibo.

So Jiang Qing's acting was pulled back into public discussion again. Every actor he had worked with got a round of scrutiny too, from rising traffic stars to background players who had never made headlines, and the conclusion people kept landing on was that Wang Mingzhi was still the weakest link.

Wang Mingzhi's fans couldn't argue on the basis of acting, so they put out singing videos of him and buried him in compliments, which only made more casual viewers recoil.

Wang Mingzhi was seething. He ordered his team to get the trending topics taken down and found someone to take the heat off him.

Before long, a story about a minor celebrity smoking in public shot up the trending list.

......

Jiang Qing watched all of it unfold online and shook his head. "These days, you never know when an artist is going to blow up or crash and burn completely. Signing talent is more and more like gambling. You know what I mean?"

Lin Xun nodded, his mouth curving up as he said with total certainty, "But you're different from them. You're worth investing in. You won't let me down, will you?"

Jiang Qing held his gaze for a long moment, then said, "Please. I haven't said yes yet. I'm going home to sleep."

"Good night." Lin Xun got up and walked him to the door.

Jiang Qing had his back to him and gave a casual wave.

After seeing him out, Lin Xun returned to the sofa to tidy up. His eye caught something out of the corner of his vision. He set down what was in his hands, then reached for the cold beer sitting on the table.

The image of a certain someone, shameless and recklessly beautiful, surfaced in his mind. Those eyes, which seemed to hold back so much, their corners carrying emotions that couldn't quite be named.

He curved his lips into a small smile. His sharp, clean features softened for a moment, and he pulled the tab, drinking it all in one go.

chapters.title: Sweetness
chapters.content:
"I Am an Actor" had completed six episodes, and the show was approaching the grouped semi-finals. Contestants who had won in the first round would return to the stage for fresh matchups; the winners would then choose a mentor to join their team, followed by a mentor team battle.

Over the past two days, Lin Xun had been dropping by under the guise of "asking for advice," getting Jiang Qing to give him lessons.

Jiang Qing was deeply skeptical, strongly suspecting it was just a cover for getting closer to him and nudging him toward signing the contract.

"Didn't you say filming was fun?"

"It is, so if I want it to be even more fun, I should take it seriously." Lin Xun arrived with breakfast in hand and strolled through the door with an unhurried smile. "Teacher Jiang, if I win this time, I'll grant you one request, anything you want."

"For real?" Jiang Qing closed the door. The two of them sat down at the dining table for breakfast. He flashed a sly smile. "Alright, I'll hold you to that."

After eating, Jiang Qing took him up to the second-floor screening room.

Three of the four walls were lined with shelves holding posters, discs, and books related to film. The fourth wall had a projection screen mounted on it. In the center of the room sat a semicircular sectional sofa, with a small round table in front holding a projector and a few bottles of drinks underneath.

While Jiang Qing powered up the equipment, Lin Xun made a slow circuit of the room, taking in the posters on the walls, some new, some old.

They were arranged by year, the best works of each era displayed side by side. Under the varied play of light and shadow, faces of all kinds unfolded across one remarkable story after another.

He stopped in the middle of the poster wall and tilted his head back slightly, gazing up at a woman whose features were exquisite and precise, beyond easy description.

She had a youthful, lively quality and, at the same time, the worn-in lines of someone who had lived. The two things should have been at odds, and yet they coexisted on a single face without contradiction.

The warm, dim light seemed to split that beautiful face right down the middle.

One half, the dream of a girl in her prime. The other half, the marks left by years slipping away.

He recognized this woman. She had been the most beloved actress on the mainland in the late twentieth century: Ye Wu. The object of countless men's admiration. He remembered his father mentioning her once or twice.

The bottom of the poster read two large characters: "Old Flame."

Below that, in much smaller type, were the names of the rest of the cast.

He ran his finger along them one by one, then said, puzzled, "Why aren't you on here?"

Jiang Qing had finished setting up the equipment and glanced over. "I wasn't a lead. The poster's only so big; there's no room for every single person."

"Fair enough." Lin Xun nodded and asked with some curiosity, "What did it feel like the very first time you acted?"

Jiang Qing went still for a moment. He walked over and stood beside Lin Xun, looking at the poster on the wall. There was a light in his eyes, and the corner of his mouth lifted softly. "Awe. I was completely in awe."

"The set was chaotic, lights, cameras, props everywhere, but the moment the director called action, every single person went quiet and waited on the actors. Every frame, every image, every passing second was being captured, to bring an audience into a strange and dazzling world."

"The seniors could endure so much. I still remember Ye Wu, Mom... sorry, we were all kids on set back then and got into the habit of calling her that; we still do. She was just as much at home in a dance hall as she was rolling in the dirt. She'd wrap at five or six in the morning and, worried we kids might be hungry, she'd take us all out to get baozi. We'd sit on the steps of the set and watch the sun come up while she talked about her dreams in the industry."

"She said she wanted something that would last forever."

Jiang Qing's voice drifted a little at that. "We were too young then to really understand what she meant... but the forever she was looking for did come, just not in the way any of us expected."

Lin Xun exhaled quietly. He knew this story.

"Old Flame" had made waves when it opened, drawing fervent attention and discussion. But the night before the Golden Leaf Awards ceremony, Ye Wu took her own life.

Some said she had slipped too deep into her role and developed depression. Others said she had already been ill. Nothing was ever officially confirmed.

What was certain was that Ye Wu, so young and alone, had indeed become something permanent on screen. Even now, fans still gathered at her grave on the anniversary of her death.

Something stirred in him, and Lin Xun turned abruptly to look at Jiang Qing. "You love the screen this much, you're not also chasing some kind of eternity, are you?"

Jiang Qing pulled at the corner of his mouth. "No. I've been turning this over for a long time, trying to figure out what kind of eternity actually counts as real. Look at all the people who've spent their whole lives acting, only to find in their later years that they can't recapture their former glory, and the goodwill they'd built up collapses. If Ye Wu, Mom, had lived, would she have ended up in that same place?"

The market was uncontrollable; there was no guarantee every project would reach the heights of "Old Flame."

If she had made too many mediocre films, if audiences had grown tired of her, then she would no longer have been the Ye Wu that everyone held in their hearts.

Looking at it that way, was dying for her art actually a kind of good ending?

Lin Xun picked up a bottle of the drinks and twisted the cap off, handing it over. "No. You've got it wrong."

"Where am I wrong?"

"You told me before, we're only playing characters, inhabiting them. So why not just let the characters be eternal? Why does it have to touch the actor themselves? You just wore a character's mask; once you take it off, you're still you. Jiang Qing. Personally, I'd take a living, breathing person in the present over any preserved memory." Lin Xun's voice was steady and low.

Jiang Qing's fingers curled slightly. His gaze went briefly unfocused, and a faint mist gathered at the edges of his eyes. He blinked hard to hold back whatever was rising up, then turned his head and smiled. "Right. Nothing beats being alive."

Perhaps that exchange had touched something in him, because the lesson that followed was unusually focused.

And Lin Xun started to regret agreeing to it.

When this guy got serious, he was genuinely terrifying.

He stood in front of the mirror running through facial expressions on repeat, laughing one second and crying the next, and occasionally getting swatted, which was more demanding than either of his parents had ever been.

Jiang Qing said seriously, "Relying purely on instinct isn't enough. You can't always count on the right feeling showing up at the right moment. You have to learn how to use technique. When the two work together, that's how you minimize mistakes."

"Teacher Jiang, how does this smile look?" Lin Xun nodded along while pulling out a grin.

"Too sleazy. Again."

"Then what should it look like?"

Jiang Qing decided to make things difficult. "Give me a smile that's three parts cold detachment, four parts mockery, five parts nearsightedness, and eighty-seven parts disdain."

"You're really going out of your way to torment me," said Lin the Tormented. "Also, your math is off. That only adds up to ninety-nine."

Jiang the Terrible at Math responded without blinking, "I left one part out so you wouldn't get arrogant."

Lin Xun was at a loss for words.

The day Lin Xun went to the television station to rehearse, he cut his morning run short by half, then stopped at a newly opened breakfast stall and bought a bag of steamed buns and soy milk.

The doorbell rang, as usual, five times. Quick footsteps sounded inside, drawing closer, and a shout rang out right as the door swung open.

"What are you, summoning spirits?!"

"Summoning you." Lin Xun's expression didn't shift. He ruffled the sleep-wild ends of Jiang Qing's hair, caught his wrist, pressed the breakfast into his hands, and smiled. "Wake up. Don't drop it. Eat properly. Good boy, I'm heading to the station."

Jiang Qing stood there in a daze until the figure had disappeared around the corner of the hallway, then slowly closed the door and stayed rooted to the spot.

Something felt off.

The two of them had gotten a little too close. Breakfast every day, dinner next door every evening, and he'd almost forgotten this person had once been his rival.

Was it just a way of getting close, winning him over, so he'd sign the contract without a fuss?

That had to be it. Ever since Lin Xun had cleared up the whole gay thing, Jiang Qing had lowered his guard considerably.

Honestly, Lin Xun wasn't a bad friend to have.

By the time Lin Xun arrived at the television station and was being walked through the building, his phone buzzed once. He glanced at it.

The corners of his eyes went warm with a smile.

The staff turned around and noticed his expression. "You're in a good mood today?"

"Very." Lin Xun smiled and looked back down at his phone.

QYY: Go rehearse properly. Don't embarrass your neighbor. [nose-picking emoji]

He tapped on the sender's name, thought for a moment, then changed the contact name to: Little Firecracker Neighbor.

On the day of the official recording, the sidewalk outside the TV station was surrounded by fans gathered in clusters, some holding up banners.

From a distance, one enormous purple banner stood out above the rest: Lin Xun, Lin Xun, Best in the Universe!

The car came to a smooth stop. Under the eager gaze of the Lavender fans craning their necks, the door slowly opened.

A pair of long, straight legs stepped out, and then a face appeared that drew a collective stunned silence from the crowd.

Unfortunately for them, it wasn't their person. It was the rival: Jiang Qing.

The Lavender fans stared at each other in speechless silence, watching him climb out of the car with subdued composure.

It wasn't exactly their fan gathering. Was he getting out here on purpose?

Then, a sharp-eyed girl in the front row spotted another silhouette still inside the car, that unmistakable profile, the perfect proportions, the face that could bring down a civilization. Who else could it be but their Lin Zong?!

"Look, Lin Zong might be in the car!"

That set off a wave. Everyone surged forward with curiosity.

Sang Yi stepped out first and positioned herself in front of Jiang Qing, sweeping the crowd with a cool look that sent an invisible pressure through the air.

She and her peers were roughly the same age, but the reputation of Jiang Qing's assistant was well-known among them.

Beneath that calm, pretty exterior was someone who had taken down six full-grown men single-handedly without breaking a sweat. She was essentially a walking Barbie with a black belt.

Jiang Qing rubbed the tip of his nose and called out past Sang Yi, "That banner slogan, shouldn't you all be paying me a licensing fee?"

The Lavender fans went silent.

"Jiang Qing, we love you!" A cluster of fans nearby shouted in unison.

Jiang Qing looked over in pleasant surprise. Huh, those aren't Jiang fans.

Where are my million loyal subjects? Come pay your respects!

Since the show had been airing for a few episodes and the reception had been strong, fans had started organizing to come and show their support in person.

As an actor who had come up through craft rather than viral fame, Jiang Qing's fanbase was still a little green when it came to this sort of thing. Most of them were at home waiting to watch the episode.

Then again, he had never been especially fond of being at the center of everything.

The bigger the love given, the heavier the responsibility that came with it. He was well aware he wasn't nearly as perfect as his fans imagined him to be.

Given the time he could spend on fan engagement, it was better spent thinking about his craft.

So really, it wasn't without reason that his fanbase was smaller.

From the other cluster nearby came the shout, "We're Qiaomaifen! Thank you for looking out for Xiaoqiao!"

"Oh, you're the sweetest." Jiang Qing said sincerely, walking over to chat with them. "It's hot out, don't get heatstroke. Head home and rest soon."

On the other side, the Lavender fans exchanged awkward glances, watching him bond with the Qiaomaifen fans, at a loss for what to say.

They were murmuring among themselves in little clusters, but the attention of most of them was still fixed on the car.

Then the person inside closed the laptop, opened the door, and smiled at them from across the gap of one car's width. "Thank you for coming all this way."

"Ahhhhh, Xun-ge, go get it!!"

"Lin Zong looks so good today!"

"Lin Zong, work hard today too!"

Lin Xun smiled. "Thank you. Take care of yourselves. You don't need to come out like this next time."

"We want to! We'll always be here for you!"

"Why did Xun-ge come with Jiang Qing?"

Lin Xun glanced at Jiang Qing's retreating back and said, "Because we're friends."

"Really?"

"Is this just a PR thing?"

"Does Gege like him?"

"I do." Lin Xun said it naturally and openly, which somehow made it come across as perfectly innocent. "Don't you?"

The Lavender fans were quiet for a moment.

"If Xun-ge likes him, then so do I!"

"Same, same!"

"Yes!"

Time was running short, and a nearby staff member reminded them gently.

Shu Tong slipped over and steered Jiang Qing toward the entrance. Jiang Qing fished out a piece of candy and tossed it to Sang Yi. "Good work."

Lin Xun glanced over without a word and held out his hand. "No playing favorites."

Jiang Qing clicked his tongue twice, but he happened to have two more pieces, so he placed both in Lin Xun's palm.

The Lavender fans who had been watching this exchange fell into a collective hush, looking at each other.

So the two of them really were that close?

This didn't look like a performance.

This friendship came in candy flavor?

One self-identified "shipping fan" was on the verge of tears.

She had been shipping them since the moment they'd gotten into the same car, and now here were her two favorites handing out actual candy to each other in person, real candy!

She could not let herself be the only one witnessing this. She had to go tell the others.

She posted the photos she'd taken to the fan forum, and every hibernating fan came crawling out of the woodwork.

Backstage, in the makeup room.

Jiang Qing was getting his makeup done when Du Yuening walked in, smiling brightly, and sat down beside him. "Jiang Laosi, you look especially handsome today." Especially with those candy-sharing photos with Lin Zong!

After several rounds of recording together, Du Yuening had become thoroughly at ease around him and greeted him without any attempt to hide her fondness.

"Jiang Laosi, tonight's the team selection. Do you have any contestants in mind?"

"I do." Jiang Qing smiled slightly. "Liu Huimin, Gao Yuanqiao, Duan Jiaxu..."

Du Yuening listened as he rattled through a long list of names, and not a single one of them was Lin Xun. First she felt a small pang of disappointment, and then she understood. He was being careful not to show bias.

Hidden sweetness like this was also pretty sweet.

Noticing the little scheming look on her face, nothing at all like a proper, composed host, Jiang Qing remarked, "You know, as a host, you're less steady and composed than my own assistant."

The moment the words were out, Sang Yi, who had been quietly playing games in the corner, spoke up in a flat tone. "Trash support player. Keep it up and I'll unscrew your head and use it as ammo."

"......" Jiang Qing cleared his throat. "Pretend I didn't say that."

Du Yuening let out a delicate laugh, then completely lost control of it and burst into a full-on cackle.

The staff around them seemed long accustomed to her terrifying laugh and didn't react with anywhere near the shock that appeared on Jiang Qing's face.

During the competition, Jiang Qing noticed clear improvement in several contestants, Lin Xun among them, and Liu Huimin as well.

Gao Yuanqiao, however, was disappointing. He didn't seem to be in the right headspace, and his performance fell short of what he'd shown in the first round.

Jiang Qing exchanged a glance with Su Hongru, and they both read the same thing in each other's eyes: confusion mixed with quiet resignation.

Gao Yuanqiao's opponent, meanwhile, made more obvious mistakes, flubbing two lines, and the two of them delivered a stage that fell apart completely.

Jiang Qing didn't hold back in his critique of both performances, and seeing the two young contestants standing there dejected and deflated, he paused and said, "There is only one stage, and not everyone gets to stand on it. Since both of you are here for a second time, I hope you can at least respect the ground you're standing on, and the audience that came here with something to expect from you."

Gao Yuanqiao lowered his head. The female contestant began to cry softly.

Gao Yuanqiao won in the end. Before the female contestant left, she said a few words of apology, then added almost as an afterthought, "My grandfather passed away."

A hush fell over everyone in the room. More than a few audience members fixed pointed stares in Jiang Qing's direction.

Jiang Qing breathed in slowly. "I'm sorry to hear that. But I stand by my decision. On stage, managing your emotions is part of the work."

Murmurs started rippling through the audience, growing louder.

"That's cold."

"Seriously, her grandfather just died. Who wouldn't be affected?"

"The least he could do is say something kind. What kind of person has no friends? I'm not surprised."

"What's wrong with someone like that? Just because his own life is fine, he expects everyone else to be perfectly composed too?"

Jiang Qing looked down and said nothing more.

Su Hongru and Wen Jiaxin quickly stepped in and took over, comforting the contestant and sharing their own experiences of losing loved ones, gently steering the atmosphere somewhere else before the moment finally passed.

But the energy in the second half of the recording wasn't as lively. A lot of the audience was carrying some residual tension.

When the nine winning contestants began choosing their mentors, most of the shouts were for "Teacher Su" or "Teacher Wen." The occasional "Teacher Jiang" that broke through was quickly drowned out.

The contestants on stage could read the audience well enough to get a rough sense of where Jiang Qing stood in terms of popularity.

Compared to a mentor whose influence had faded and whose tongue had gotten him into trouble, Su Hongru and Teacher Wen seemed like the clearly better choices.

Su Hongru had been around long enough that his connections spoke for themselves; landing a film role through him wasn't out of the question. Wen Jiaxin was low-key, but she was a pillar of the spoken drama community.

The first four contestants in succession chose those two, and the audience applauded warmly.

Then it was Lin Xun's turn.

"Su Laoshi! Su Laoshi! Pick Su Laoshi!"

"Wen Laoshi would be great too!!"

Lin Xun nodded with a smile. "Thank you, everyone. I choose Teacher Jiang."

Du Yuening was thrilled on the inside but kept her expression professionally neutral. "And what's the reason for choosing Teacher Jiang?"

Lin Xun looked across at Jiang Qing, who had been quiet this whole time. His gaze was deep, unfathomable, a slow current turning somewhere beneath the surface, as if he were looking back at the image of someone asleep in a room full of toys.

Outside, the sun was bright. And yet that person had been so alone.

"Because we're friends." Lin Xun curved his lips.

The audience began whispering again. Du Yuening's smile deepened a little as she turned to Jiang Qing. "So, Teacher Jiang, will you accept Lin Xun?"

Jiang Qing looked directly at him.

A long beat passed. Then he nodded, slowly and deliberately.

Lin Xun's smile grew. People around them murmured and speculated, but he had understood it perfectly.

That nod wasn't only about accepting him as a student. It was an answer to the words "we're friends."

Gao Yuanqiao and Liu Huimin both chose Jiang Qing as well. Liu Huimin made no secret of her fondness for the younger man.

Gao Yuanqiao said, "Shifu has always been someone I look up to. I hope you can forgive my mistake just now. I really admire you. Please give me this chance."

Lin Xun's smile stiffened for just a fraction of a second. He glanced over at Gao Yuanqiao, calm on the surface.

Then Jiang Qing nodded again, and the corners of Lin Xun's mouth dropped completely.

He was displeased.

No.

Very displeased.

chapters.title: The Art of Changing Faces
chapters.content:
Recording wrapped.

Lin Xun seized the moment and went to hitch another ride.

The mood in the car was a little subdued. Shu Tong cleared her throat. "Don't let all of that get to you..."

"I'm fine." Jiang Qing cut her off and closed his eyes. "Wake me when we get there."

Shu Tong sighed helplessly. In the rearview mirror, her gaze met Lin Xun's. She gave him a rueful smile and shook her head.

The car pulled up outside the complex. Once the two women had headed off, Jiang Qing went back to the car.

He rummaged around for a moment and found a half-finished pack of cigarettes left from some previous time, lit one, and closed the car door before heading toward the building.

"Smoking alone?" Lin Xun asked.

"Do you smoke?" Jiang Qing looked at him, a little surprised, and pulled out the pack, holding out a cigarette.

Lin Xun took it, and his long, slim fingers brought it to his lips.

Jiang Qing reached for his lighter, but a shadow fell over him.

Lin Xun had leaned in slightly, borrowing a light from Jiang Qing's own cigarette.

Jiang Qing blinked, meeting his eyes. For a moment, his mind went completely blank and he couldn't think of a single thing to say.

The elevator doors happened to open at that exact moment. Lin Xun stepped out first and turned back with a smile. "Not coming?"

"Damn." Jiang Qing irritably scrubbed at his hair. "Can you not be so weird about everything?"

"What's weird about it? Friends borrow lights from each other all the time."

Jiang Qing exhaled a smoke ring in his direction. "Friends don't do it like that."

"Then how do they do it?"

Jiang Qing furrowed his brow, feeling like the question had somehow gotten even weirder, and deflected with a quip. "If you're really friends, you'd come at me swinging."

"...?"

Jiang Qing saw the genuine alarm on Lin Xun's face and broke into a laugh. "Idiot."

Moonlight fell through the corridor, weaving together with the hallway lights.

Lin Xun leaned in the doorway and watched him laugh, a little exaggerated, but the smile itself was lovely.

He went quiet for a moment, just listening.

It wasn't exactly the right time or place. Even so, something seemed to pluck at a string in his chest, the echo of it vibrating and refusing to settle, as if it might crack right through.

The two of them defaulted wordlessly to leaning against the hallway railing and smoking. Lin Xun barely touched his, letting it mostly burn down on its own.

Jiang Qing glanced over. "Doesn't taste good? Or have your standards gotten too high for domestic brands?"

Lin Xun shook his head with a smile. "I'm just not that into it."

"When did you learn?"

"I don't remember. I picked up too many things when I was younger, and by the time I thought about it, it was just something I could do." Lin Xun said. "What about you?"

"Second year of middle school." Jiang Qing remembered it clearly. "A director taught me. He showed me how to blow smoke rings, how to make my expression look more worn, more interesting. Does this look right?"

As he said it, he narrowed his eyes just slightly, let his gaze drift upward toward the moon, his face tilted in profile, looking quietly striking.

Unfortunately, Lin Xun seemed immune to it. "Not really. I still think you look better when you smile."

"You have no taste." Jiang Qing's mouth curved almost imperceptibly, and he watched the cigarette burning down. "Do you think I'm cold?"

So it had gotten to him, Lin Xun thought. He kept his expression even. "People's pain doesn't always speak the same language."

Jiang Qing gave a light, detached smile. "I really am pretty cold. My grandfather... I drove him to it."

Lin Xun said nothing, and tapped a small length of ash off the cigarette, watching it break apart in the night air.

"He was against me acting too. Said I was young and going down the wrong path, that the right thing was to study hard and take over the family business. We had a huge fight, and it triggered his heart condition."

"He never came around. Just slipped into a coma and was gone."

"He must have gone to complain to his daughter. But I'm not worried, he had more of a problem with her husband than with me, so if he's going to yell at anyone, it's him first."

Lin Xun listened to all of it without a word, piecing together what he could from the fragments.

Offering comfort was a skill, the same as knowing when to stop pouring someone a drink.

Too much, and it did harm. Too little, and it left a wound open.

At moments like this, Lin Xun generally chose to listen. Listening was the better medicine, and it was much harder to get wrong.

The cigarettes burned out. They said good night and went their separate ways.

When Lin Xun saw Jiang Qing the next day, he was back to being a handsome disaster with a serious case of morning moodiness.

After breakfast, Jiang Qing headed to the company. Today was the day to sign the termination agreement.

Nearly twenty years there. He couldn't say it meant absolutely nothing.

The old Ruihua had run on loyalty and a certain code of conduct. But the people who had built it had gradually stepped back, and the new Ruihua had grown into something with far more power and far more ambition.

The lobby downstairs was busy, people coming and going. Several newcomers crossed his path, still wearing the unpolished, half-eager look of people who had just started out, not quite sure what awaited them but full of anticipation.

Jiang Qing turned his gaze away and stepped into the elevator. When he reached the conference room, the manager was there along with lawyers from the legal team and a few assistants, already mid-conversation.

Things had come this far. There was no use in keeping up appearances.

The manager slid the financial summary and the contract across the table. Jiang Qing and Shu Tong went through everything carefully before Jiang Qing signed his name.

"You'll need to be careful out there on your own," the manager said with a pleasant smile. "Without a big organization behind you, I worry you'll stumble."

Jiang Qing smiled back. "Congratulations on getting rid of the dead weight."

The unspoken thought had been said out loud. The manager didn't seem the least bit embarrassed. Both of them knew perfectly well.

Out the door, Jiang Qing drew in a breath of fresh air and said to no one in particular, "Unemployed. Back to square one in one go. Not a cent to my name."

Shu Tong checked the time. "I haven't finished packing my things up yet, go home and rest. Go ahead."

"Do you have a lot? I could help."

"It's fine, Yi Yi is already boxing things up. The two of us can handle it. You go home and rest properly. Don't slack on your workouts. And absolutely no fried chicken. No one's going to want to buy you if you turn into a balloon."

Shu Tong kept talking as she walked back inside to the office.

Jiang Qing lingered for a moment, and then on impulse decided he wanted to see someone.

Just as he turned around, Gao Yuanqiao came jogging over with a face full of worry. "Shifu, you're really leaving Ruihua? Why would you do that?"

"I was just looking for you." Jiang Qing looked him over. "Want to go get some milk?"

Same place as before, but this time Gao Yuanqiao didn't order milk. He ordered a vodka.

"Are you out of your mind? Do you know how strong that is? Since you want something with a kick, let's go all the way." Without a second thought, Jiang Qing crossed off the vodka and ordered him the most intense thing available, an iced cola.

Gao Yuanqiao obediently drank a big sip, let out a carbonated burp, and stared at Jiang Qing with dark circles under his eyes that drained all the light from them. "Shifu, why did you suddenly leave? Isn't Ruihua good?"

"My contract was up. Just the normal process." Jiang Qing didn't want to get into it with a newcomer, especially one who might be staying at Ruihua for a long time. Better not to knock the wind out of him.

"Is it... because of Wang Mingzhi?" Gao Yuanqiao said in a low voice. Just bringing up the name made him reach for his cola again. "He's not a good person."

Jiang Qing neither confirmed nor denied it, and changed the subject. "What's going on with you? You haven't been yourself lately."

Gao Yuanqiao looked at him, kept looking, and then two tears slipped out. He wiped them away, and his mouth pulled into a miserable line. "I got dumped."

"You... got dumped?" Jiang Qing stared at him. "Kid, what you had, did that even count as a relationship?"

"Of course it did." Gao Yuanqiao reflexively pushed back, then started sinking into the memory. "He said I had a lot of potential. That he admired me. He said he liked me... and I liked him too. But now he's fallen for someone else."

"He didn't fall for someone else. He never had a heart to begin with." Jiang Qing looked at him with flat exasperation. If he told this poor kid that Bai Bangnan was stringing along several people at once and he was just one of them, would the kid actually jump off something?

"So what are you going to do?"

"I went to see him. He said he likes someone else now." Gao Yuanqiao buried his face on the table and started crying, all muffled and pitiful. "How could he do this? He was my first love. I even came out to my family for him and got kicked out, that bastard."

Jiang Qing drank his coffee without expression.

Ten-odd minutes later, Gao Yuanqiao lifted his head, face still wet, and asked in a small voice, "Why aren't you comforting me?"

"Men cry, it's not a crime." Jiang Qing said, unmoved. "You broke up. Next one will be better."

"I don't want a next one. I'm done with men. I don't think I'll ever love anyone again!"

Jiang Qing rubbed his forehead. "You're barely old enough to be saying things like that. Wipe your face, you look terrible."

Gao Yuanqiao sniffled and mopped his face with a napkin, and felt a little better for it.

He'd been keeping all of it to himself this whole time, without anyone to say any of it to.

"Shifu, you're really great."

"Hey, don't say things like that. I'm afraid you'll fall for me."

"I'm done falling for anyone."

"Good." Jiang Qing smiled. "Is acting not rewarding enough, is the whole world not big enough, that you'd degrade yourself for something so pathetic?"

"You're right!" Gao Yuanqiao clenched his fist, then wilted again a moment later. "But he was so good to me before. No one's ever been that good to me."

"So you got taken advantage of. The emptier someone is inside, the easier it is to be moved by the smallest kindness." Jiang Qing said.

Gao Yuanqiao slowly nodded, then seemed to think of something and looked up with sudden curiosity. "Shifu, have you never been in love?"

Jiang Qing looked at him. "That's none of your business. Focus on the semi-finals coming up. I need you back to where you were. Don't embarrass me."

Gao Yuanqiao puffed out his cheeks and nodded firmly. "Okay! I'm going to terminate my contract tomorrow."

"Ha." Jiang Qing picked up a napkin and dabbed the edge of his mouth. "Don't be impulsive. The penalty fee is steep. How many years did you sign for?"

"Ten." Gao Yuanqiao's voice dropped. "I don't want to see him anymore. Even if I have to leave the industry, I'm not staying at Ruihua. He gave me a lot of money. It should be enough to cover the penalty, I think."

"How much?"

"About this much. I haven't spent a single cent." Gao Yuanqiao held out his phone, showing the bank balance. The number made Jiang Qing's chest tighten a little.

Since the money wasn't going to be a problem, Jiang Qing said, "Just make sure you own every choice you make."

"Okay. Shifu... will I still get to see you after this?"

"We're recording the show soon. Win a few more rounds and you'll see me plenty."

Gao Yuanqiao pressed his lips together. "I'll try."

"It's not try. It's will." Jiang Qing said. "Work hard, and then step on everyone who ever treated you like you were nothing."

"Okay." Gao Yuanqiao raised his fist, then looked wistful again. "Shifu, you seem like someone with a lot of stories."

"Get out of here."

Gao Yuanqiao: QAQ

Over the next few days, Jiang Qing's three team members went to the television station to rehearse, and he stopped by now and then to supervise when he had time.

The performance piece had been selected in the previous recording session. It was a palace intrigue drama.

The four of them sat down together to divide up the roles. The only woman in the group, Liu Huimin, naturally took the role of Empress Xiao.

That left the Second Prince and the Third Prince. Jiang Qing asked Lin Xun and Gao Yuanqiao if they had any preference.

Neither of them had strong opinions, so Jiang Qing made the call based on their natural personalities and skill sets. He gave Gao Yuanqiao the role of the loose-cannon Second Prince and assigned Lin Xun the deeply calculating Third Prince.

Their acting instincts were complete opposites, and his hope was that putting them in these two roles would help balance each other out.

At that point, someone from the directing team mentioned that each mentor was allowed to invite a friend to join the performance. The other two groups had already made their selections. The condition was that the guest couldn't be too high-profile, to avoid upstaging the contestants.

All three of them looked at Jiang Qing.

Jiang Qing scratched his nose awkwardly. The directing team was clearly having a go at him. Everyone knew he had practically no friends in the industry.

"I'll just go up myself, then. There's still the deposed Crown Prince, right? That fits me perfectly, I'm pretty deposed."

The directing team had no objections. If he was willing to step in himself, all the better.

The Crown Prince didn't have many scenes. Jiang Qing started by helping the team get a feel for things. "Huimin-jie, you don't have much physical action, so the focus is in the eyes. Make sure you can shift between the cruelty at the beginning and the fear once everything unravels. Don't relax even when the camera isn't on you. The audience in the room can see you the whole time. And ease up the tension in your face a little, don't hold everything so rigid."

"Gao Yuanqiao, wake up and focus. That listlessness of yours, is that how you sleep-walk through life? Even if your character is a reckless playboy, you're still a prince. Don't bring street punk energy to it. Think about what it actually looks like to be a favored son."

"Lin Xun, look in the mirror and give me your most ruthless expression."

A moment later, Jiang Qing shoved Lin Xun's head lightly. "Ruthless. You know what ruthless means, right? Stop being so soft about it."

Lin Xun was suffering in silence. How was he supposed to look ruthless when he was staring at Jiang Qing's face?

Jiang Qing saw that Lin Xun had somehow ended up smiling during the exercise and immediately lost his patience. Keeping in mind that there were others around, he leaned in close and said through gritted teeth, "Are you doing this on purpose? Why won't you listen?"

The warmth of breath close to his ear sent a tingling sensation through Lin Xun. He leaned in a fraction more on purpose and said, laughing quietly, "I'm not doing it on purpose. You just look particularly good today, and I can't bring myself to be ruthless."

Jiang Qing went still for a second, shot Lin Xun a look, and his ears, without his realizing it, had gone red. He covered it by yelling, "Focus on rehearsing!"

Then he spun around to check on Gao Yuanqiao. Seeing the kid going way too big with his performance, Jiang Qing thought for a moment, then pulled him aside to a corner and murmured in his ear, "You can think about Bai Bangnan. The way that Crown Prince holds himself."

Gao Yuanqiao looked at him in surprise and turned. "You... you knew it was him?"

Jiang Qing patted his shoulder and nodded. "What was it about him that drew you in, apart from how he treated you? Was it that kind of carelessly elegant energy?"

Gao Yuanqiao didn't deny it. He looked at Jiang Qing's face and let his mind drift into a kind of empty focus.

Across the room, Lin Xun had been watching them the whole time, ever since they moved to the corner. Especially the part where they were whispering together, and now this lingering eye contact.

His gaze went abruptly cold, a don't-come-near-me energy radiating off him that cleared the space around him.

Jiang Qing looked over from across the room and raised his thumb, just starting to say something complimentary. Then those sharp, bristling eyes went suddenly soft, curving at the corners.

Jiang Qing was at a total loss. Are you really that susceptible to flattery? I haven't even said anything yet.

Even so, by the time of the final run-through, he found that Lin Xun's cold, darkened energy was actually quite effective.

The moment he locked eyes with Gao Yuanqiao in a scene, the intensity was unsettling enough that on the first pass, Gao Yuanqiao almost broke character and got a scolding from Jiang Qing before regrouping.

While he'd been dealing with Gao Yuanqiao, he caught Lin Xun out of the corner of his eye looking perfectly serene and innocent. The speed at which this man changed faces was something else entirely.

On the day of the official recording, the four of them were together in the makeup room getting ready. Liu Huimin was a little nervous. "What if I drag everyone down?"

"No, no, I'm the one who'll hold us back," Gao Yuanqiao jumped in firmly.

The two of them went back and forth being self-deprecating, each outdoing the other in tearing themselves down, it was genuinely painful to witness.

Jiang Qing couldn't take it and issued his own ultimate disclaimer. "My mouth keeps getting me into trouble. Being in my group means suffering for it."

"No no no, Shifu, you're the best!" Gao Yuanqiao immediately said. Liu Huimin nodded vigorously in agreement, and the flattery started coming in from all sides.

Jiang Qing smiled a little, turned his head, and found that Du Yuening had somehow slipped in again.

"Wow, Lin Xun, you look incredible today! Can I take a photo with you?"

"Of course." Lin Xun stood up and posed with her.

Du Yuening lingered shamelessly, and the moment Jiang Qing's makeup artist finally stepped back, she pounced. "Jiang Laosi, you should get in too, what a waste to not take some photos when you look this good today!"

"......Fine."

Du Yuening stood in front of them and held up her phone, snapping a group shot, then turned around immediately. "Come on, let me get a few of just the two of you."

"That's enough," Jiang Qing said awkwardly. Then something settled against his arm unexpectedly, and he turned to look at who it belonged to. "What are you doing? Is this a tiger's shoulder you can just lean on?"

Lin Xun raised an eyebrow. "You can put your arm around Gao Yuanqiao's shoulder. Why can't I put mine around yours?"

"What does one have to do with the other?"

"How does it not?"

"If there's a connection, it's the wrong bus connection. Let go of me."

Du Yuening watched them murmuring away at each other in obvious familiarity and could barely contain herself. Pure bonus content.

She couldn't help asking, "Jiang Laosi, you two seem so close. What are you talking about?"

Heads turned at the question. The surrounding crowd leaned in to watch.

Front row spectators settling in with popcorn.

Jiang Qing shifted his expression rapidly. "Ha, I was just, just complimenting him, saying his performance has been really..." The words stuck. He immediately added, "...not up to scratch."

The camera operator heard them and came rushing over to start filming.

Du Yuening's professional instincts kicked in and she switched to her broadcast smile in under a second. "Do you have confidence in your team tonight?"

"Yes."

"Who do you think will shine the most?"

"You."

Du Yuening blinked. "...?"

Jiang Qing, with a completely straight face, said, "You're not just an outstanding host. I believe your acting ability is also exceptional."

Du Yuening laughed. "Teacher Jiang flatters me."

"Mm, I was just being polite. Don't take it seriously."

Du Yuening was speechless.

A career-defining stumble. She had been rendered speechless.

Had she done something to offend Jiang Laosi?

She was dead. Devastated.

Beside them, Lin Xun's lips curved without warning.

Du Yuening: The way he's indulging him! Ahh, I'm alive again!

"Teacher Jiang, can you and the contestants do a little pose for us?" Du Yuening said.

Jiang Qing raised his fist, just about to hold it up, when Du Yuening cut in. "How about a heart instead?"

Jiang Qing thought: Young lady, is your brain exclusively occupied with content that needs to be censored?

The audience chimed in. "Yes, yes! A heart! We want a heart!"

Before the words had even fully landed, Lin Xun had already bent his right arm and held it out near his chest, waiting with a spring-sunshine smile for the matching half of the gesture.

The camera operator framed the shot. "Three, two..."

Jiang Qing extended his hand.

"One."

Click.

The shutter went off. The audience, for some reason, seemed like someone had hit their mute button. Everyone was staring at Jiang Qing and Lin Xun with puzzled looks, until someone finally started laughing, and then the whole room followed.

The makeup artists' hands trembled slightly where they stood.

Du Yuening laughed until she was doubled over, and went to look at the photo on the camera.

In the image, both of them were smiling with the same warm, sunny expression. The pose, however, was entirely mismatched.

Lin Xun had his palm open and extended. Jiang Qing had used only his thumb and index finger to form a perfectly complete heart all by himself.

Lin Xun hadn't gotten his matching half, and he found it funny too. He said in a low voice, "You seem very averse to any kind of contact with me."

Jiang Qing was speechless.

It's not you I'm worried about. It's Du Yuening fabricating another "love story" out of thin air!

chapters.title: Dragged Online
chapters.content:
The performance began.

Empress Xiao was a second wife whose maternal relatives held enormous influence at court. After scheming and poisoning the first Empress, she had set about removing the weak-willed Crown Prince, determined to place her own son, the Second Prince, on the throne.

But a Third Prince, born to an unremarkable palace maid and long ignored, had quietly built his own power base, owing his loyalties to the late Empress and the Crown Prince she had left behind.

On top of this, there was the faction of the Prime Minister, a three-way struggle carried out in the open and in the shadows alike.

The Emperor appeared to be kept in the dark and used by all sides. In truth, he had been orchestrating everything from the start.

The scene selected for today centered on the inner palace. Empress Xiao had discovered the Third Prince's ambitions. Under the pretense of a palace banquet, she had him brought before her so the two of them could probe each other.

The curtain rose on a backdrop of gilded halls in all their splendor.

Liu Huimin sat at the head of the room, lifted a cup, took a slow sip, and at the sound of light, hurried footsteps approaching from outside, her brow furrowed.

A figure stepped through the doors, and the teacup came crashing down onto the stone floor.

The newcomer startled. "Imperial Mother, who's upset you again? Just say the word and I'll go sort them out for you!"

Empress Xiao slapped the table and looked at him with the frustration of someone watching iron fail to become steel. "Always so reckless! Why did you show such poor judgment at the banquet just now? Can you not take a lesson from the Third Prince? You have no patience at all. How are you going to handle anything that matters?"

The Second Prince sauntered up, rubbing her shoulders and murmuring a few flattering words to soothe her.

A palace attendant entered to announce the Third Prince's arrival.

Mother and son exchanged a look. Empress Xiao's eyes shifted, a flash of cold viciousness crossing them. She leaned in to whisper something, and the Second Prince took his cue and slipped out through a side door.

The Third Prince entered with his expression unreadable, composed. Every movement carried a certain refinement. His eyes were deep, still, giving nothing away.

"This subject greets the Empress."

"No need for formalities. I heard you recently welcomed a son into your household. Wonderful news. I had you brought here only because I wished to offer a small gift." Empress Xiao lifted a jade pendant. "Bestowed by His Majesty himself. May it keep your son safe."

The Third Prince accepted it. "This subject thanks the Empress for her generosity."

Empress Xiao smiled faintly. "You don't look pleased. Are you not satisfied? Is there something else you want?"

The Third Prince raised his eyes. "I would like to see the Crown Prince."

Empress Xiao had moved into the Empress's palace and, by some means of persuasion upon the Emperor, had been entrusted with keeping watch over the deposed Crown Prince.

She put on a gentle, benevolent expression. "I knew you had a kind heart. That is why I had the Second Prince fetch him. Wait just a moment."

The Empress returned to her seat. The two of them sat in silence, each watching the other, their faces composed, everything expressed only through the eyes.

Then a shuffling noise came from outside.

The Second Prince swaggered in, dragging behind him a figure who looked haggard and disheveled.

The moment the Third Prince made out who it was, his whole body leaned forward as though he might rush across the room, and then he stopped himself with visible effort. His hands closed into fists beneath his sleeves. "Is this how the Empress treats the Crown Prince?"

The Second Prince scoffed. "Crown Prince? Does he deserve that title? He was caught in the act with one of Mother's lowly serving girls. If Mother hadn't covered for him, he'd have been the city's biggest laughingstock long ago."

The Third Prince ignored him entirely. He walked slowly toward the Crown Prince. The Crown Prince shrank back, eyes darting away, shaking his head again and again.

"Imperial Elder Brother. It's me. I believe you."

The Third Prince reached out to push the hair from the Crown Prince's face. The Crown Prince slapped his hand away.

The Crown Prince turned and tried to crawl toward the door. The Second Prince caught him by the hair and yanked. The pulling stretched the Crown Prince's face out of shape.

The gentle, mild expression in those eyes slowly reddened, whether from pain or something else, it was impossible to say.

The Third Prince drove a kick into the Second Prince. The Empress, watching the scene, raised her voice. "Guards!"

The false civility between all three of them shattered. The tension in the room turned knife-sharp.

While the three of them traded blows with their words, the Crown Prince had his head down, crawling slowly forward. He stopped, looking at the red pillar in front of him, red as his mother's blood.

The argument continued. Then, with a crack, the sound cut through everything.

The Crown Prince had walked into the pillar and crumpled to the ground.

"Imperial Elder Brother!" The color drained from the Third Prince's face. He crossed the room, gathered the Crown Prince in his arms, touched the blood at his temple, and bolted for the doors with him. "Help! Someone come! A physician! NOW!"

The Second Prince immediately looked to Empress Xiao in a panic. Empress Xiao's eye twitched. "Stop them."

"But..."

"He walked into it himself. What does that have to do with us?" Empress Xiao drew in a slow breath, her expression composed into something almost serene. "The physician arrived too late to save him."

The Second Prince understood her meaning and immediately sent someone to the imperial physician's quarters.

The Crown Prince was gone.

From that day forward, the Third Prince spent every effort opposing Empress Xiao and her faction, drawing the Prime Minister into his orbit, stripping away the power of her relatives, until finally Empress Xiao and the Second Prince were imprisoned in the dungeons.

The Third Prince, now Crown Prince himself, went to see them. Empress Xiao was no longer the imperious woman she had once been. A prisoner was a prisoner. The Second Prince, meanwhile, had fallen ill with a chill and was huddled in the corner, refusing to see anyone.

The Third Prince's gaze was cold and merciless. He smiled faintly. "Empress. Are you finding it comfortable here?"

Empress Xiao's face spasmed. She shot him a sharp look, then heard her son's racking cough. Her expression went through several shifts in rapid succession. Her hand reached out and gripped the hem of his robe, and she pleaded, "I beg you. Let us see a physician. I'll kneel to you. I'll kneel."

And she did, pressing her head to the ground.

"Who exactly are you kneeling to?" the Third Prince said with a cold laugh. "The first Empress treated you generously, and where was your mercy when she died in childbirth? The Crown Prince gave your son every advantage, and your worthless son turned around and framed him over an affair with a palace maid, then had the nerve to humiliate him while he was kept in the Empress's palace. The filth that you are deserves nothing but death."

"No, no, no!" Empress Xiao watched his retreating back and broke into sobs.

The performance ended. The audience erupted in applause, with scattered shouts of approval.

Liu Huimin took a moment to let herself come back. Gao Yuanqiao and Lin Xun both offered her tissues.

While the other two mentors added their praise, Jiang Qing let the makeup artists clean up the traces of blood on his face and fix his hair before settling back into his seat.

Du Yuening said, "Teacher Jiang, how do you think your team did?"

"Extremely well. I'm very satisfied with all of them." Jiang Qing said with genuine pride. "Gao Yuanqiao and Lin Xun may be newcomers, but don't underestimate what they can do. Your instincts are sharp. If every newcomer could do what you two did today, that would be a real gift to audiences. And Huimin-jie, you were extraordinary in this one. You really are the gold-standard supporting actress. Working with you is a genuine pleasure."

Su Hongru agreed. "Absolutely. Though Jiang Qing, you gave quite a performance yourself. Not a single line, and half the audience was in tears."

The audience agreed, some of them still wiping their eyes.

The three contestants each talked a little about what rehearsals had been like, and it was clear this was a cohesive, easy-going group.

Since this was the mentor team battle round, the unfortunate reality was that their opponents were Su Hongru's stacked lineup of proven talents. One of Jiang Qing's team would have to be eliminated, and the choice was his alone.

After a brief discussion with the other mentors, his gaze settled on Gao Yuanqiao, and he felt the reluctance of it.

Gao Yuanqiao, however, accepted it with visible relief and bowed.

Du Yuening asked Jiang Qing to say a few words of encouragement to his team.

Jiang Qing had never been good at those kinds of speeches. He thought for a moment. "Then I'll send you off with a little rap I wrote in my head while I was down there."

The audience: ???

You spent your downtime during a stage performance writing a rap?

Give us back our tears!

"I'm not exactly a trained rapper, so I'll just recite it for you."

The audience: ???

How many tricks do you have up your sleeve?!

Jiang Qing went:

"Who says

Lin Xun is the new face of being all looks, no substance?

Who says

Gao Yuanqiao can't come from behind and take it all?

Who says

Liu Huimin only gets to play the old lady?

The ones saying all that are the ones who don't know anything.

Hey, you walk your own road.

Don't be afraid, don't fold.

Put your hand up and be bold,

Speak up for yourself, go,

Life is a stage,

We speak only for ourselves."

The audience: WHERE ARE ALL OUR TRAINED MUSICIANS?!

Liu Huimin, who had just been crying over losing a teammate, burst into laughter and bent over holding her stomach.

Gao Yuanqiao lost it completely. "Thank you, Shifu! I love you!"

The audience: "Awww~~~"

Gao Yuanqiao said those words, and for some reason, felt a sudden chill run up his spine. He glanced sideways at Lin Xun, and nearly jumped.

That look was terrifying.

More terrifying than the Third Prince.

He whispered, "Are you still in character?"

Lin Xun looked away. "Hmph."

Du Yuening was a little displeased as well. As a member of the shipping faction, she felt as though a third party had just crashed the scene. She turned to Lin Xun. "Gao Yuanqiao is such a sweetheart. So, Lin Xun, is there anything you'd like to say to Teacher Jiang?"

Lin Xun said, out of nowhere, "I love you too."

The audience: "Awwwwwww~~~~~"

Du Yuening: AHHHHH, two steps removed from an altar! I am losing my mind up on this shipping wall, my tears are free-flowing!

Su Hongru suddenly said, "Jiang Qing, I love you too."

Du Yuening's smile fell flat. The whole venue erupted in laughter.

Their rose-tinted moment had been thoroughly demolished.

After the recording wrapped, Jiang Qing was in a good enough mood to agree immediately when Lin Xun tried to hitch a ride home again.

Once they were in the car, Jiang Qing noticed Shu Tong had been silent since before, staring at her phone with a darkened expression.

"What happened?" he asked.

Shu Tong pressed her fingers to her temple. "You're being dragged all over the internet."

Lin Xun sat up straight. "Over what?"

Shu Tong said, "Tonight's the broadcast date for last week's episode, and it's been blowing up online."

The only real flashpoint from that recording had been the news about the female contestant's grandfather. She was a second-tier actress with a quiet, hardworking image, and her fanbase was considerable, her general reputation warm.

The problem was that she had performed below her level because of her bereavement, and Jiang Qing had called it out plainly. Even after the truth came out, his manner had remained sharp. In the eyes of the audience and the internet, that read as heartless.

Jiang Qing had already seen this coming. He'd sensed during the recording that someone would try to make something of it. "Didn't we handle some pre-emptive damage control?"

That was exactly what was eating at Shu Tong. Her frown deepened. "We're unaffiliated now."

Marketing accounts always read the room before deciding where to point. Even ones she worked with regularly had taken those deals in part because of the muscle behind Ruihua.

Now that the contract was gone, all Ruihua had to do was make one phone call.

Across every platform, commenters were piling onto Jiang Qing for being cold and heartless, while also flooding the female contestant with messages of sympathy and support.

Within a short time, Jiang Qing had become the target everyone was aiming at.

Old pieces of gossip that had supposedly died down were being dug back up. On top of that, the news of his departure from Ruihua had started circulating.

A self-proclaimed fearless exposé account pulled everything together and posted a summary calling out what he described as Jiang Qing's five major offenses.

@EntertainmentInsiderGossip: This Jiang Qing character is obsessed with his own image. Twenty years in the industry and he acts like the elder statesman, coldly mocking every newcomer who crosses his path, apparently unaware that the wave behind him has long since pushed the one ahead onto the shore. Below I will outline several of the most inexcusable things this man has done. Feel free to add your own.

One: Low emotional intelligence, insufferable arrogance, zero regard for others. Most people didn't find out who Jiang Qing was through his work but through how viciously he runs his mouth. He's burned bridges with countless people. From what I know, at least five young newcomers have been driven out of the industry because of him. A few words from him and a person's career is finished.

Two: On-set tyrant. He throws his weight around, rewrites scripts at will, treats co-stars without basic courtesy, and routinely forces the whole crew to stay late without any regard for anyone else's physical limits.

Three: Completely devoid of human feeling. As the recent "I Am an Actor" incident makes clear, he has no emotional capacity whatsoever. His only concern is grabbing attention, and getting on the trending list is exactly what he wanted. The industry doesn't forgive people without connections. Twenty years in, can anyone name a single friend of his?

Four: Biting the hand that fed him. First he publicly criticized Director Yu Haoge, who gave him years of work. Now he's walked out on his agency early. According to a source inside Ruihua, he stopped coming to the company regularly long ago, was unhappy with the resources being offered to him, and pushed for the early termination himself.
