On top of that, he refused to use a company-assigned assistant, going out and finding his own young female assistant privately. Word is this assistant has already bought property in the capital within just a few years. One wonders what kind of arrangement would result in benefits like that.

Five: A crumbling image. He made a point of declaring publicly that he would never touch variety shows or reality television. Now he's standing on "I Am an Actor" of his own accord. Count how many trending topics have carried his name since this show began. Also, for someone whose whole brand is professionalism, where is the quality work? What has he put out lately?

In under half an hour, the post was climbing the trending charts. Someone with money and reach was clearly pushing it.

There were too many people he had crossed over the years, and it was nearly impossible to pinpoint who was behind this particular hit. It could have been any number of parties acting at once. Ruihua itself might even have had a hand in it.

Without friends in the industry, without institutional protection, no one stepped forward to say a word in his defense. Everyone watched the spectacle unfold.

The keyboard warriors showed up in their masses, each one radiating righteous indignation, charging in like heroes who had seen injustice and drawn their blades. They wouldn't be satisfied until they'd drawn blood. The self-appointed defenders of morality were united in a single mission: drive this heartless, ungrateful man out of the industry for good.

The mood in the car grew heavy. Even Sang Yi had gone quiet, and the car picked up speed until Jiang Qing snapped back to attention. "Slow down. There are four people in here."

Sang Yi pursed her lips. "Qing-ge, let me go at them."

"Go at who?"

"Whoever I can get to."

Jiang Qing laughed out loud, scolded her lightly, and the atmosphere gradually lifted.

Shu Tong had been reminded of something though. She turned around. "There's one thing that might turn this around fast. I don't know if you'll agree to it."

Jiang Qing was still laughing. "What is it?"

"Wutong Orphanage."

Plenty of celebrities had turned their public image around through charity work. Some used it to recover from a crisis.

More to the point, Jiang Qing had genuinely done good. The moment his years of supporting Wutong became public knowledge, all the accusations of cold-heartedness would fall apart on their own.

"No." Jiang Qing refused without hesitation.

Shu Tong sighed. "Fine. I had to ask."

Sang Yi gripped the steering wheel tighter. "Qing-ge, maybe consider it."

"I said no."

Sang Yi's knuckles went white. She said, barely above a whisper, "Thank you."

Once those children became a news story, they would never have another peaceful day.

Reporters and cameras would descend looking for angles. The kids would be exposed to something far worse than obscurity: the intrusive gaze and pitying stares of the outside world.

"Tong-jie, did you change my password? I can't get into my Weibo." Jiang Qing had been trying and failing.

"Yes, and it's staying that way. If you go online right now, you're handing them exactly what they want. Everyone's still fired up. One wrong move and they'll run with it for days. Stay low, I'll find something to redirect the news cycle."

She opened her contacts and called a few paparazzi contacts, fishing for anything fresh. Not much to work with. The most interesting thing anyone had was some unknown fifteen-minutes-of-fame type cheating on their partner.

She kept scrolling and then let out a sharp sound. "Lin Xun!"

Jiang Qing flinched. "He's sitting right behind you, relax."

Shu Tong turned around, pointed at her phone, and said with visible delight, "Lin Xun stood up for you."

Jiang Qing blinked and looked at Lin Xun, who had been quietly on his phone this whole time. "What did you do?"

Lin Xun put his phone away and looked over at him with a slight smile.

Outside, the scenery kept sliding past. Neon lights scattered and repeated, flashing briefly across the glass before disappearing, and now and then a beam of light caught the surface of Lin Xun's eyes and lit something there.

Jiang Qing went still for a moment. A suspicion was already forming. He opened his secondary account and scrolled through the front page, where Jiang fans were screaming Lin Xun's name.

"Ahhhhh I've been crying all night. I can't believe Lin Xun did this. He's so good."

"Same, my hands were shaking when I saw it. Qingqing finally gets a bit of momentum and they come for him like this. I want to cry so badly. Thank you, Lin Xun."

"Who said our Qingqing has no friends?!"

"Antifans, get wrecked!!"

"I am never calling Lin Xun a pretty face again. Lin Xun is the one and only man worthy of standing beside Jiang Qing!!"

"Lin Xun is amazing. The only people who show up for you in a moment like this are real ones!!"

The picture was becoming clearer by the second. He couldn't quite name what he felt, but he looked down and kept very still, not letting anything show on his face.

Maybe Lin Xun had only just entered the industry and didn't fully understand what speaking up at a time like this could mean. The safest thing anyone could do in a situation like this was stay out of it entirely. The moment you got involved, you risked being pulled into the same fire, and could end up facing the same kind of backlash.

He wanted Lin Xun to not have done this, to not have invited trouble on his own behalf. But when he opened Lin Xun's Weibo and saw the pinned post, his eyes, half-lowered a moment ago, caught a small flash of light they couldn't quite suppress.

@LinXun: Are you an adult? @EntertainmentInsiderGossip. If you are, you're responsible for what you say and do. Your statements constitute a serious violation of Jiang Qing's reputation and the reputation of his assistant. Under the law, defamatory content that reaches five thousand views or five hundred reposts meets the threshold for criminal defamation.

You are hereby required to issue a public apology to my friend @JiangQing and his assistant, to pin that apology permanently, and to delete your most recent post. If you fail to do so, our legal counsel @RuianInvestmentAttorneyLi will be in contact with you directly.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns
chapters.content:
[Ahhhh Lin Zong, do you even remember you have a Weibo? When was the last time you posted?! Your Weibo is begging you to come back!!]

[Gege comes out of hiding just to defend Jiang Qing? Socialist brotherhood, I ship it!]

[Xun-ge, you're so bold, I love you so much!]

[Oh my god, what a man. CEO energy fully activated. Feels like watching Lin Xun the domineering president take names again!]

[Waiting for that apology!!]

[We Jiang fans love you, Lin Xun! Thank you for having his back!]

[So they just casually slap people with legal threats now? Jiang Qing must have given you something good, because right now I'm seriously wondering if he went easy on you during the competition.]

[You two never even interacted on Weibo before, and now you suddenly show up to defend him? Riding the trending wave for clout, or were you paid?]

[Explain yourself. You go after this blogger with a legal threat out of nowhere and call it justice? That's cyberbullying!]

[Cyberbullying my foot. Did you see how they were cyberbullying Jiang Qing? Do celebrities just have to sit there and take it?! Keyboard warriors can crawl back under their rocks. Lin Zong is a real one, and I'm a fan for life!]

[By the way, why did Lin Xun tag the Ruian Investment attorney? Why not one of his own people?]

[Oh my, you're onto something. Isn't Ruian Investment Yang Meng's company?]

[Wait, what is actually going on here? What's the relationship between all three of them? Why hasn't Yang Meng said anything?]

[Yang Meng has been linked to all kinds of female celebrities. I guess this time it's a male celebrity's turn.]

Just as the internet was splitting itself apart over Lin Xun's post, Gao Yuanqiao dropped a new Weibo.

@GaoYuanqiao: Shifu is the best! @JiangQing

Not long after, Liu Huimin added hers.

Liu Huimin: You are actively destroying a genuinely talented and respectable actor @JiangQing. Let the rumors stop here.

Neither of them had massive followings, but the show had brought in a wave of new casual fans, and even a modest ripple was better than nothing.

Back at the complex, Shu Tong reminded Jiang Qing to get some rest before heading off to figure out a way to shift the conversation.

Online noise moved fast. Any given topic would be buried under something new before long.

But if this one wasn't dealt with properly, it would stick around as a piece of history, following Jiang Qing like a shadow.

Lin Xun spoke up at the right moment. "Tong-jie, let me handle this."

"You?" Shu Tong looked at him with mild surprise. "I appreciate what you did just now, speaking up for him online. But don't worry, we won't let you get pulled into it."

Lin Xun looked at Jiang Qing. "Didn't you tell her?"

"I got busy and forgot." Jiang Qing looked away. "I genuinely forgot."

Lin Xun was heartbroken. The man hadn't even thought about it.

He said, putting on a wounded tone, "You have no heart."

"......" Jiang Qing's head dropped slightly. His foot nudged the floor, and for once he actually felt a faint flicker of guilt.

Shu Tong looked between the two of them, confused. "What are you two dancing around? Out with it."

"It's like this......" Lin Xun would have explained everything, but it was late and a long story was better told short. "I'm opening a studio. I want to sign Jiang Qing."

There was certainty in his voice. He was not hedging.

Shu Tong's eyebrow climbed slowly until it tied itself into a knot. "That's a very abrupt pivot."

Jiang Qing laughed a little, then checked the time and started steering her toward the front entrance. "Okay, okay, head home with Yi Yi. I'll send you his information and you'll understand once you read it. Stop worrying about me, I'm fine. This isn't the first time I've been dragged."

Strictly speaking, the worst of it had come before he was reborn. That version had been dragged so thoroughly he'd started to believe he really was the villain. And the ones who'd gone hardest at him had been Lin Xun's fans, who had wanted to dig up his ancestors, to the point where even now, catching sight of a Lavender fan made something in him flinch.

But tonight, more than a few Lavender fans had stood up for him. The feeling that left him with was strange and complicated.

Of course they'd stood up for him because of Lin Xun's post.

The two of them got into the elevator. He forwarded part of the information Yang Meng had given him about Lin Xun to Shu Tong, then put his phone away and looked ahead at the reflection in the elevator doors. "Thanks."

"If you want to thank me, come make me money." Lin Xun said, seizing the moment.

"I'll take that under advisement."

Lin Xun smiled. "What are you worried about? My operation has the people, resources, and capital to back it up. And you'd be the only client. No one competing with you for anything. You'd be the undisputed headliner."

Jiang Qing didn't respond. Before all this, what he had wanted most was to start his own studio.

But tonight had made the risks of that very clear.

How many people in the industry would risk the fallout of signing with him as their artist?

Veteran supporting actress Liu Huimin? Newcomer Gao Yuanqiao?

They'd tried their best. But even if they signed, what kind of resources could he realistically offer them? Better ones than what they had now?

He let the thought go.

"Just give me a little more time. Three days. I'll give you a real answer in three days. I promise." He looked at Lin Xun with a flicker of genuine apology, his eyes wide and direct, his lashes shifting lightly like two small feathers drifting down to land somewhere they weren't supposed to.

"Don't look at me like that." Lin Xun's voice came out lower than intended.

Any longer and he was afraid he'd hand over the studio itself.

Jiang Qing blinked, genuinely uncertain.

"......" I said stop looking at me.

Lin Xun moved his gaze away. The moment the elevator opened, he stepped out at a brisk pace, opened his door, closed it, and didn't even leave time for a good night.

Jiang Qing stood there for a second, wondering if he'd accidentally wounded Lin Xun's apparently very delicate feelings again.

He went home, showered, was halfway through blow-drying his hair when his phone rang.

Shu Tong's voice jumped about three octaves. "What the hell?! Ruian Investment is Lin Xun's company?! This isn't some elaborate joke between the two of you, right?!"

Her image was gone, clearly.

Though compared to his own reaction when he'd found out, his own gracelessness didn't seem so extreme.

He smiled. "Would tricking you get us anywhere?"

"Oh my god, oh my god, babe come here, pinch me!" Shu Tong shouted somewhere in the background, and then a squeal, followed by the sounds of her husband getting swatted.

It took Shu Tong a long moment to collect herself. "Good thing, good thing, since you're friends with him, at least I pointed you in the right direction when I told him to get close to you."

Jiang Qing's smile froze. "You told him to get close to me?"

"Right, you have too few friends, so I asked him to spend more time with you, to get to know you a bit, so he'd see how great you actually are." Shu Tong kept talking to herself, then suddenly noticed the silence on the line. "Hello? Jiang Qing, are you still there?"

"Yes." Jiang Qing answered, and dropped down onto the sofa. His fingers absently caught the drawstring of his sleeping shirt and played with it while he stared at the ceiling.

So it had been out of pity.

Because he had no friends, someone had asked Lin Xun to look after him, to offer a little warmth.

He pulled one corner of his mouth up and laughed at himself.

The doorbell rang. Five times in a row, with the kind of boldness that only someone completely unbothered by consequences would attempt. Which left only one person in the building.

"Who is it? Visiting this late?" Shu Tong said on the other end.

"Give me a second." He left the phone on the table and went to open the door, looking at the person standing there without expression.

Lin Xun paused. "Your hair isn't dry yet. You'll catch a cold."

"Oh."

The tone was nothing like moments ago, and Lin Xun assumed the online mess must have finally gotten to him. He held up the bowl in his hand, a cluster of freshly washed grapes, and offered them with an easy smile. "Want some?"

"No!"

The door shut with a bang.

Lin Xun blinked, eyes going wide. He pressed his ear to the door to listen, then immediately straightened up at the sound of the lock.

A long, slim hand appeared through the gap in the door and snatched the bowl out of his hands.

"Good..."

Bang.

"...night." Lin Xun waved and turned to go home, thinking to himself that the little neighbor was in a mood again. Must be something to do with being a walking firecracker.

And yet thinking of that prickly, defensive posture just now, he found it quietly, inexplicably endearing.

Once you decide someone is endearing, everything they do becomes endearing.

Inside, Jiang Qing bit into a grape, and picked up the phone again.

"Why are you so grumpy?" Shu Tong said, resigned.

Jiang Qing chewed loudly on purpose. "What's wrong with being grumpy? I've always had a bad temper. If that's a problem, you don't have to be my friend."

"Honestly, I don't know what he sees in you. He puts up with so much." Shu Tong sighed, and then, "Oh right, when he and I came to your place that time, I gave him a heads up not to betray you. You know what he said?"

"......" Jiang Qing wasn't happy. "Why do you tell him everything? What betrayal? You make me sound completely pathetic. I'm doing fine."

"You're going to listen or not?"

Jiang Qing stretched his hand into the bowl, pinching a plump grape between his fingers without pulling it free. He turned it gently, his gaze fixed on it, and said with studied nonchalance, "What did he say? If it's anything unpleasant, I'm going over there right now to deal with him."

"He said other people betray you because they want something from you. He won't, because there's nothing here that he wants. The most he could want is sincerity, and a real friend."

Jiang Qing went still. When his attention came back, his fingers were already damp with grape juice. Shu Tong was still talking on the other end: "I didn't quite understand it at the time, but now it makes sense. He has everything already, so he genuinely doesn't need connections or leverage or status from you. An ally like that is worth having. Don't you think?"

He turned on the tap. Cool water ran over his fingertips, washing the juice away. After a long moment, he gave a quiet sound of agreement.

After hanging up, he passed through the living room and stood looking at the bowl of grapes for a while before moving quickly to the kitchen and opening the refrigerator.

More than twenty kinds of drinks lined the shelves. He moved things around looking, and no fruit.

Just a couple of grown men, and somehow the other one's fridge was like Doraemon's pocket, holding absolutely everything.

He kept searching, and then found two bottles of grape juice wedged into a corner. Good enough.

Return the grape with grape juice.

It was late. He didn't know if Lin Xun was asleep yet.

He stepped out to the balcony and saw the lights on next door.

Just as he turned to go find him, he heard movement from the balcony over there.

Lin Xun stepped out, phone pressed to his ear.

He turned and spotted Jiang Qing on the other balcony, looked surprised for a second, then smiled and waved back.

"When are you coming back? I miss you so much!" A bright, sweet female voice floated from the phone.

"In a while. I've been busy lately." Lin Xun strolled to the railing on the left side of his balcony, now facing Jiang Qing directly.

Jiang Qing held up the juice bottles and mouthed: want some?

Lin Xun extended his hand: okay.

Jiang Qing turned and went back inside.

"What are you smiling at? You're this happy without me around? I see how it is, out of sight, out of mind." The girl on the other end of the phone raised her voice.

Lin Xun was leaning over to look next door, and said, "Yeah, pretty happy. Oh, by the way, thank you for the brooch."

"What brooch?"

"Never mind. It's late here. Let's talk another time. Good night."

He ended the call, headed back to the living room, and the doorbell rang. Five times.

The little firecracker was holding a grudge, Lin Xun thought, amused.

He opened the door. Jiang Qing was standing there with three bottles of juice, transferring all of them into his arms.

He caught them as they came. "What's all this?"

"The juice you asked for. Three bottles."

"...?" Lin Xun blinked. "I thought I said okay?"

Jiang Qing stared at him, then said with a threatening edge, "No. You said three bottles."

"Fine, three bottles it is. Are these about to expire?"

"Can you not assume the worst about me? Do I look like the type to pawn off expired drinks on friends?"

"No, you're the type to drink them yourself."

"Painfully accurate." Jiang Qing was thrown for a moment.

Lin Xun smiled, then said with sudden sincerity, "You just said 'friends.'"

Jiang Qing's gaze drifted, surveying everything around him at random. After a beat, he looked back and nodded.

"That's a sad way to put it." Lin Xun said.

Jiang Qing: ???

Friends isn't enough for you? What more do you want?

"Weren't we already friends long before now?" Lin Xun looked at him.

"...Were... we?"

Lin Xun mirrored the exact decisive nod Jiang Qing had given, firm, unambiguous, leaving no room for argument. "Yes."

Jiang Qing let out a surprised laugh.

Lin Xun laughed along with him, and that smile was a little blinding.

Jiang Qing remembered that in his previous life, some of his own fans had seen Lin Xun's smile in person and defected entirely.

He laughed and laughed, and then he felt like crying.

There they were, like two idiots, standing in the hallway in the middle of the night laughing at nothing, not exactly exchanging mountain songs.

"It's getting late. Sleep."

"Yeah. Thanks for the juice."

"Don't mention it. I have more if you want."

He said it like a tycoon throwing money around.

Before bed, he sat back against the headboard, a sleeping pill in one hand and his phone in the other, thinking: if those self-appointed crusaders were still piling on, he would just knock himself out and sleep right through it.

He opened Weibo, still the secondary account. The main one was probably a disaster zone.

But the battle lines had clearly shifted.

[Hahaha this is SO satisfying. I am officially declaring Lin Xun my second favorite person.]

[That blogger is crying now hahaha, look at them go! Love to see it!]

[@EntertainmentInsiderGossip, hey, are you there? You look really good on your knees!]

[Qingqing still hasn't come online at all.]

[Believe in Qingqing! I don't believe a single word those accounts said!!]

[The blogger's apology is pinned! Go repost it everyone!]

Jiang Qing's eyebrow rose slightly. He clicked on the blogger's profile and found the freshly posted pinned apology.

@EntertainmentInsiderGossip: @JiangQing, I'm sorry. Without fully verifying the facts, I published statements about you and your assistant that were false and fabricated, seriously damaging your reputations. I extend my sincere apologies to both of you and hope you can forgive my error.

[Your account is done. :)]

[Get out! You're a murderer! If nobody had stopped you, you'd have been the one who destroyed Jiang Qing. You're not a hero, you were just a fool being used!]

[Keyboard warrior, also known as a small-time clown. Self-righteous one minute, on your knees the next. You used us like ammunition!]

[So everything was made up?]

[Of course. Sang Yi is a beloved assistant. For the record: they have a sibling relationship, nothing more.]

[This is exactly what women face in the workplace. It doesn't matter how hard you work. If you're young and attractive and making good money, people will say you got there on your looks. No logic, no fairness.]

The conversation had drifted from the apology into a broader thread about the unequal treatment of women in professional environments, striking a chord with a lot of people who had stumbled onto the thread.

The shift was clearly being steered. When he spotted a familiar large account picking up the thread, he knew Shu Tong was behind it.

Still, the fact that the apology had named both him and Sang Yi told him something. It told him why Lin Xun's original post had kept coming back to her.

The entertainment world ran on rumor and ambiguity. Marketing accounts knew exactly how to use that. They didn't need to prove anything because the audience rarely pushed back.

But Jiang Qing and Sang Yi's relationship was clean. That was a fact, and that fact gave them legal standing to go after anyone who said otherwise.

[The idea of Qingqing and Sang Yi having anything going on is genuinely the funniest thing I've heard all year. You're just mad that he has a capable, good-looking assistant and you don't. Bunch of miserable people online. Rest of you, Jiang Qing is amazing and always will be!]

[Jiang Qing, I'm sorry. I accidentally became a keyboard warrior. I'm going to go buy your movies right now to make up for it.]

[By the way, the blogger caving this fast, doesn't it have something to do with Lin Xun's post? Was the attorney actually in contact with them?]

[So what exactly is the connection between Ruian Investment and Lin Xun? Or between Yang Meng and Lin Xun?]

[Lin Xun's first project was financed by Ruian Investment! Oh my god, I think I just found something.]

[Stop right there. Are you starting another rumor? Attorney warning incoming!]

......

Jiang Qing sent Lin Xun a message. "What exactly did you do?"

That Insufferable Cocky Pig: Just had the legal team reach out. They had no leg to stand on, so of course they folded.

Jiang Qing had already said thank you so many times it felt tired. He thought maybe he'd bring over a few bottles of grape juice tomorrow instead. Lin Xun seemed to like that stuff.

The two of them kept up a lazy back-and-forth over text, and then a push notification surfaced at the top of his feed.

After Standing Up for Jiang Qing, Lin Xun Changed His Personal Certification. Netizens: Classic Move.

Jiang Qing stared at it, completely lost. What was this?

He tapped the notification. Under Lin Xun's profile, where the credited works used to be listed, it now said: Jiang Qing's friend.

[HAHAHA okay, someone says Jiang Qing has no friends, so he just slaps a label on his profile? Only you, Lin Xun.]

[I've said it too many times tonight but I have to say it again: Lin Xun, you are the best man in the world apart from Jiang Qing. You protect Jiang Qing, we protect you.]

[I've shipped so many pairings and none of them have ever felt this real.]

[Welcome to the fan shipping community, come join us!]

That one-of-a-kind certification brought the two fanbases together in one place, and with the general public's late-night disaster-tourism energy running high, the topic #LinXun—JiangQing'sFriend had climbed the trending list before long.

The smear campaign collapsed under the weight of the blogger's apology, replaced by a surge of attention and discussion. Both of their profiles stayed near the top of the trending charts throughout the night.

The production team, ever attuned to the moment, released a few behind-the-scenes clips, and footage of the two of them in easy, comfortable sync during rehearsals kicked off another wave of conversation. The whole night had been a rollercoaster.

Jiang Qing understood that Lin Xun wasn't worried about what changing a certification might cost him. He had come into the industry as a hobby, and as long as it was fun, that was enough.

Besides, it was just a profile description. It wasn't announcing a relationship.

What it did do was drive up their combined trending presence, and people started running with the joke.

It began with the fans. Certifications like "Lin Xun's girlfriend," "Lin Xun's wife," "Lin Xun's collarbone," "Lin Xun's individual hair strand," and "Jiang Qing's waist" started appearing everywhere.

Then it spread to the general public. Profile descriptions like "XX's girlfriend," "XX's boss," and "XX's litter box attendant" began popping up across the platform. It had quietly turned into its own little genre.

The feed was dizzying. Jiang Qing's eyes were starting to droop, and his phone buzzed once more.

That Insufferable Cocky Pig: Good night.

He yawned, pulled the blanket around him, and thought about logging today's share of energy but decided to let it go.

Then he opened his secondary account and changed his certification to: Lin Xun's friend.

Just one anonymous account buried in the crowd. No one would find this little secret.

Good night.

chapters.title: Negotiating the Contract
chapters.content:
Lin Xun had noticed recently that something about Jiang Qing had shifted; not dramatically, but in the small, overlooked details.

For example, in the mornings, the doorbell needed fewer rings than before, and Jiang Qing would open the door.

He'd still be wrapped up in morning grumpiness, but he seemed to be reining it in, and all that was left was a faintly reproachful look.

Then there was the fruit. Every time Lin Xun dropped some off, Jiang Qing would return within minutes with a few bottles of juice in matching flavors.

At some point Lin Xun had started to wonder if Jiang Qing was secretly a juice machine.

And sure enough, one day the bottles of store-bought juice were replaced by freshly pressed.

After a little investigation, Lin Xun discovered that Jiang Qing had gone out and bought a juicer, and was squeezing it fresh from the fruit Lin Xun had brought over. The fruit had come from Lin Xun, the juice was given back to Lin Xun. Full circle.

However he looked at it, the dynamic between them was harmonious.

Harmonious... neighbors. Which was starting to feel a little insufficient.

He couldn't quite pin down how exactly it was insufficient, only that the relationship between them ought to be something closer than neighbors, something warmer than friends.

If there were one more thing he could add to bind them together, he hoped it would be: a contract.

Sign the contract and Jiang Qing would be his. Five years, ten years, fifteen years, all of it spent side by side.

Money clearly wasn't going to sway Jiang Qing, and resources didn't seem to make much of a dent either.

That left only the last resort: beauty.

No one had ever escaped the reach of his face.

One afternoon, he invited Jiang Qing over to watch the newest episode of "I Am an Actor" together.

Jiang Qing accepted with pleasure and immediately carried the juicer over, already fairly at home heading straight for the fridge to look for fruit while the episode hadn't even started yet.

"What would you like? These oranges look nice, orange juice then? Does that sound good?"

Lin Xun frowned slightly, glanced down at his well-put-together outfit, touched his perfectly styled hair, and genuinely could not understand how he was apparently losing to a piece of fruit.

"Or do you not like orange juice?" Jiang Qing looked up and saw Lin Xun fidgeting, scratching here and shifting there. "Do you have lice?"

Lin Xun swallowed a mouthful of something unpleasant and switched strategies.

A moment later, he straightened his collar, settled onto the sofa with the ease of someone born to it. Long legs crossed, the composed and indulgent air of a CEO fully present, he said warmly, "Anything you make yourself, I'll like."

"Make you into a corpse," Jiang Qing replied. "Would you like that?"

"Too extreme. We can skip straight to the result."

"Which result?"

"We can drop the 'into a corpse' part."

Jiang Qing processed this. An orange sailed across the room and caught Lin Xun directly in the head.

Lin Xun rubbed the spot, picked up the flying orange. "Man, you have no idea what you're up against."

Jiang Qing: Old man on the subway staring at his phone.

In the end, Lin Xun sat on the sofa watching the episode with his hair mussed into something resembling a bird's nest, both hands dutifully wrapped around a cup of hot water with a few wolfberries thoughtfully dropped in by the little neighbor.

He turned to look at Jiang Qing, and the orange juice in his hand, and could not conceal his longing.

Jiang Qing felt the puppy-dog stare and tilted his head back for a long, deliberate sip, exhaling contentedly afterward.

The episode was well-produced; the pre-rehearsal footage had been padded out by over ten minutes compared to previous weeks.

When the camera cut to their group, Jiang Qing was in the middle of coaching all three of his contestants.

When he moved to the corner to talk with Gao Yuanqiao, the camera found Lin Xun, and caught his gaze suddenly sharpening into something pointed, directed toward the corner of the room.

Then, when Jiang Qing gave him a thumbs-up from across the room, those eyes went soft again.

[My girlfriend specifically made me watch this to study the "friendship" between Lin Xun and Jiang Qing. As a straight man I can confirm there is nothing here. These looks are completely normal. Babe, are you satisfied with that answer?]

[I keep telling myself it's just shipping, it's just fiction. And then the two of them insist on stuffing more sweetness down my throat with their bare hands.]

[Lin Xun: you promised to teach me for a lifetime, and a year short, a month short, a single hour short, none of that counts as a lifetime.]

[Jiang Qing is coaching. Stop projecting your fantasies onto this. I've been calming people down over this for hours now.]

[Isn't this just rehearsal? Jiang Qing literally asked for that expression, didn't he?]

Lin Xun looked at the footage and genuinely paused.

He remembered only being a little irritated at the time, and then glancing over at Jiang Qing. But apparently the emotion on his face had been a little more layered than that.

If Jiang Qing ever asked him what that expression meant, how would he answer?

He casually looked to the side. Jiang Qing wasn't even paying attention, scrolling through his phone.

"What are you looking at?"

Jiang Qing didn't look up. "Tong-jie said a few agencies reached out. She wants me to take a look at the materials."

Lin Xun's internal alarm immediately went off. He snatched the phone out of his hand. "No looking. You are only signing with my company."

"Give it back."

"No."

The moment he said it, Lin Xun sensed something dangerous in the air. He bolted.

Jiang Qing chased him through the apartment, cursing as he ran, then in one decisive move launched himself forward and landed squarely on Lin Xun's back, forearm locking around his neck.

"I'll count to three, two..."

"One," Lin Xun counted it out himself and gripped the phone tight, refusing to give ground. "Get off me. Let's talk this out."

"Phone first."

Lin Xun looked down, eyes shifting. "Get off me or don't blame me for what happens next."

"What do you mean by that, I..." The sentence shattered into laughter. "Haha, stop it, stop it, seriously stop, please!"

The tickling attack had barely started and already Jiang Qing had no strength left in his hands.

He reflexively kicked out a few times, but his feet were caught, and there was no getting free.

"Haha, you absolute menace, you wait until I haha, I beg you, please!"

Lin Xun stopped.

Jiang Qing seized the moment, threw his weight, and slid off Lin Xun's back, collapsing to the floor.

He lay there laughing until he couldn't breathe, then kicked Lin Xun twice in the shins out of principle.

Lin Xun stood there and took it without moving.

Once Jiang Qing had worn himself out and gone still, Lin Xun crouched down beside him. He looked at the slightly reddened corners of Jiang Qing's eyes, and laughed quietly. "Sign with me or not?"

"Ha. Not signing."

Lin Xun pressed a hand to his shoulder. "I should mention that I've studied boxing, sanda, taekwondo, shooting..."

Jiang Qing: visibly shaking.

After a long moment, he sat up abruptly and slapped the floor. "You can't do that! That's blatant coercion!"

Lin Xun sat down across from him, eyes bright with laughter. "Yes, and I'm absolutely going to have you."

"There are so many other artists out there. Any one of them would probably be better looking than me, which, actually, impossible, but the point stands, you have options."

"No, you're the one who sparked the idea of opening a studio. Without you, there's no point."

Jiang Qing had no words left. He took back his phone, returned to the sofa, wrapped his arms around himself, and said after a silence, "Three days. Give me three days and I'll have an answer for you."

"Deal."

"Also, is the office even finished? If you don't take me to see it in person, how am I supposed to know it's not just a shell?"

"Should be ready in the next day or two. I'll take you as soon as it is, first on the list. Is that acceptable?"

Jiang Qing was satisfied.

The two of them had lost track of the show in all the chaos, and it was now drawing toward its end. The footage of their group's performance was playing.

[Okay, this group's actually really strong? Two newcomers and an under-the-radar veteran, and they're all genuinely good?]

[Empress Xiao's eyes are something else. Oh my god, is this actually Liu Huimin?!]

[Lin Xun, Lin Xun! Ahhh! Cold and devastating!]

[The Crown Prince died and they know it. I cried and no one cares about me.]

[Jiang Qing had not a single line of dialogue and I cried buckets. What is this man doing to people?!]

[Lin Xun's eyes were red. So much restrained feeling. One clip and I was completely pulled in, I'm already gone.]

Meanwhile, Shu Tong had reached out to some new marketing accounts and circulated a piece on Jiang Qing's work ethic and dedication. His general reputation among casual viewers ticked up.

The female contestant who had stayed quiet since last week, ever since news about her grandfather came out, finally posted a Weibo after this episode aired. She said Jiang Qing was a genuinely serious and committed actor, and asked people not to attack him.

The move earned her a wave of goodwill. Plenty of people found her understated and gracious.

Jiang Qing asked Shu Tong why she'd spoken up now. Shu Tong replied: "Apparently Ruian Investment's team reached out to her. She didn't want to cross Ruian, so she figured doing them a favor was the better play."

Then Shu Tong sent a follow-up message: "If you do end up going with a company, Lin Xun's setup is genuinely a strong option. Based on what you sent me, his financial backing is solid, and I still haven't been able to trace his family connections at all. Anyone capable of keeping things that airtight comes from somewhere serious."

Jiang Qing immediately thought of himself. The press had never managed to dig up anything about his own family either.

"Actually..." Jiang Qing started to say, and looked at Lin Xun. "Can I ask, you're not actually a prince or something, are you?"

Lin Xun genuinely did not know how to answer, because the question had come out of nowhere, so far out of nowhere that he almost fired back: "And are you actually a princess from Planet Cat?"

He thought for a moment and said, "Yes."

Jiang Qing: !!

"A prince who walked out of an oil painting." Lin Xun smiled. "Those are your words."

Jiang Qing: ...you remember that?! I can barely keep track of every compliment I've ever thrown out!

"What else did you call me?" Lin Xun shamelessly pressed.

"A walking promotional poster, a man ripped from the pages of a comic, a miracle from the hands of God..." Jiang Qing's mouth was moving before his brain had fully engaged, and by the time he caught himself, Lin Xun had already hit record on his phone.

"Ah, so this is how much you like me. Thank you for your kind words. I'll do my very best to live up to them." Lin Xun put his phone away with amusement.

Jiang Qing stared at the ceiling with no words left.

The joy of sparring with people is one thing. The damage of sparring with a certain dog is quite another.

As he stepped out of Lin Xun's place, the night sky stretched deep above him, a full moon hanging bright and high. He couldn't help calling out, "Lin the Dog! It's a full moon tonight!"

Lin Xun materialized quietly in the doorway and looked at him with an unreadable expression. "What did you call me?" One minute you're calling me your prince, and the next?

Jiang Qing mentally bit his tongue. He pointed at the moon and turned around with a wide-eyed look, trying to charm his way out of it. "Look at that moon. Round and full."

"So what did you call me?" Lin Xun folded his arms and stepped closer. His tall frame settled over him in the narrow corridor, carrying a mild but definite air of someone who would not be letting this go.

Jiang Qing backed up a step, his lower back pressing against the railing, and blinked guiltily. "You know the Heavenly Hound? The one that's absolutely relentless in chasing the moon? Brave and unstoppable? That's you. Your whole being radiates the same brilliance as the moon, and you've inherited that spirit of never giving up until you reach what you're after."

Lin Xun looked at him without expression. "Keep going."

"The Heavenly Hound is devastatingly handsome. Even Chang'e herself, if she saw it, would... would feel her heart race and her soul stir." Jiang Qing was talking himself into a corner. He noticed Lin Xun slowly lowering his head and leaning closer, and instinctively pulled back a fraction, eyes fixed on Lin Xun's. He said each word deliberately: "In my heart, you are exactly that kind of dashing hound."

"Your face is red," Lin Xun said.

Jiang Qing instantly cupped his own face in both hands. He didn't feel any heat. He glared back. "Liar. I'm going to sleep!"

You dog!

He shoved past Lin Xun and yanked his door open, and Lin Xun's soft laughter followed him in. He slammed the door behind him with feeling.

When he happened to glance at the mirror while washing up, he saw it then: a faint flush across both cheeks.

He immediately turned the water cold. High temperature made the blood move faster, which could cause temporary redness of the face. That was all it was.

He thought back carefully, and maybe the blush had been real, but it was just because he'd been saying things he knew were lies, and he'd felt guilty. He'd even dragged Chang'e into it. Was Hou Yi or Wu Gang going to come find him?

The next day, Shu Tong had arranged a few things, some agencies to go see.

There were plenty of companies interested in signing him, but none of them came close to matching Ruihua's weight. Most were small operations where he'd essentially be fending for himself.

After Shu Tong had ruled out everyone without the credentials or the potential, only two companies remained.

The first meeting was in the morning. The representative was warm and effusive from the moment they sat down, showering him with praise that bordered on the surreal.

The negotiation went nowhere in the end.

The company's strength was in marketing. Virtually every artist on their roster had been through some kind of manufactured scandal, all of them riding the line between controversy and publicity.

The representative made it clear: if he signed, they would design the perfect public image and marketing approach specifically tailored to him.

The second meeting was at a five-star hotel. When they arrived, Jiang Qing asked, "Which company?"

"Dongying Entertainment."

"That sounds vaguely familiar."

"The agency that represents Tang Huan, the one who took your shampoo endorsement. The endorsement ended up going back to Ruihua later, which wasn't on us."

Jiang Qing remembered now. The endorsement had originally been taken by Yu Minghan, who had actually called him personally about it once.

Sang Yi pushed open the door to the private room. Inside were two men.

The one seated closer to the door was a middle-aged man in thick-framed glasses, Chao Lianchuan, who had come up through Ruihua before jumping ship to the newly established Dongying Entertainment, where he was now a top-tier manager.

"Long time no see, Shu Tong. Jiang Qing." Chao Lianchuan stood and buttoned his jacket, shaking hands with both of them in turn. "Please sit."

Shu Tong was his former colleague. After a few pleasantries, she glanced at the man across the table who had been staring at Jiang Qing from the moment he walked in. It was Yu Minghan.

He had an eye for trends: relaxed clothes, hair dyed an ash grey. Headphones hung around his neck, and he was sitting like the concept of posture had never been introduced to him, practically draped over the back of his chair.

The moment Jiang Qing had walked through the door, Yu Minghan had studied him without any attempt to hide it.

Jiang Qing behaved as though there was nothing to notice, and turned to catch up with Chao Lianchuan.

Shu Tong smiled and asked, "I thought this was about a signing. Why did you bring one of your artists along?"

Chao Lianchuan smiled smoothly. "Minghan isn't just a Dongying artist. He's also the son of the owner."

Yu Minghan propped up his chin with a pleased look, then aimed a direct look at Jiang Qing. "So? Feel like joining Dongying? I told you I wanted you as a friend. And when it comes to friends, I'm generous."

Jiang Qing frowned. "If your company's heir is this unreliable, what exactly are you selling me on?"

Yu Minghan's eyes went wide. He sat up straight, bewildered. "I'm being serious! I genuinely admire you. Come join us. Dongying's two powerhouses, and we'll take on the world together!"

Jiang Qing: ...

The two managers: ...

Chao Lianchuan cleared his throat with visible discomfort. "He's not usually like this. He's just expressing his enthusiasm and eagerness. He's genuinely been hoping to sit down with Jiang Qing for a while. He hadn't found the right moment until he heard that Jiang Qing had left his agency, and rushed over immediately."

Shu Tong remained unconvinced. Yu Minghan had made a grab for one of their endorsements before. If she'd known he was the young heir of Dongying, she would have turned down this meeting from the start.

Jiang Qing asked without ceremony, "What do you actually want?"

Yu Minghan grinned. "I just want to know, is Wang Mingzhi's bird actually that small?"

Shu Tong: ...?

She'd lost the thread completely.

She looked helplessly at Chao Lianchuan, who wore an expression even more agonized than hers. Years managing this young man had clearly left their mark. She could see new grey hairs from here.

She found herself thinking, with some genuine feeling, at least her own artist was well-behaved. Sensible. Mature.

She cleared her throat, attempting to steer things back. Then she heard her own sensible, mature artist answer, "Small."

Shu Tong: ...

She turned to her former colleague. "Quick, tell me, do I have many grey hairs?"

The two veteran managers silently offered each other a moment of mutual understanding and sorrow.

Yu Minghan slapped the table, delighted. "Seriously?! Hahaha, that fake-it-till-you-make-it attitude and he's packing nothing? What a joke!"

Jiang Qing started laughing too. Half a minute in, he suddenly remembered someone else was in the room.

He stood up, crossed to the corner under the puzzled gaze of everyone present, and held out a hand to Sang Yi, who had been playing handheld games this whole time. "Not suitable for minors. Go get us some ice cream."

Sang Yi pocketed the device and followed him toward the door. "What's unsuitable? Is a new game releasing?"

That was reassuring. Good old Sang Yi; completely tuned out the whole time, as absorbed in games as ever.

"What flavors does everyone want?" Sang Yi stopped at the door and turned, and then her sharp senses caught the sound of movement from the neighboring room.

She looked toward the sound. A well-dressed young man stepped out.

He stopped, looking mildly surprised but clearly pleased, and started walking toward them. Before he could say a word, the girl said politely, "Yang-shushu."

"......" Yang Meng's eye twitched.

Jiang Qing lowered his head, his shoulders shaking.

A moment later, footsteps followed from behind Yang Meng. Someone came out after him.

Sang Yi's eyes lit up when she saw who it was. "Xun-ge!"

Yang Meng: ...... I object. I'm at a complete loss.

Lin Xun saw it was them, and a smile broke across his face. "What a coincidence. What are you doing here?"

Jiang Qing hesitated. "We came for... a..."

"Qing-ge came to negotiate a signing." Sang Yi told him directly.

"!" Jiang Qing turned to look at the little sister he'd raised for years, his expression complicated.

"Signing?" Lin Xun's eyes narrowed slightly. He stepped around Yang Meng and came to stand in front of Jiang Qing, voice low. "Who are you signing with?"

In his head, Jiang Qing thought: none of your business.

But for some reason, looking at Lin Xun's interrogating gaze, he felt a flicker of something that came awfully close to the feeling of getting caught red-handed.

He shook it off and said with a stubborn air, "What's the problem? Even when you go buy groceries, you compare a few stalls first."

Lin Xun was about to say something, but from inside the room came the unmistakable voice of someone who had absolutely no sense of timing: "Jiang Qing! Get back in here! You still owe me the rest of the bird story!"

Jiang Qing: I'll show you a bird!

Yang Meng let out a barely contained laugh. "What kind of conversation is happening in there? Sounds exciting."

Lin Xun's expression flattened completely. He looked at Jiang Qing with no warmth at all. "I hope we're not disrupting the atmosphere."

"We're not!" Jiang Qing's head snapped up. His face had gone a suspicious shade of red from the embarrassment of it all. "We were talking about, about raising birds. It's a hobby, for older people. Starting early is better. You know how it is."

As he said it, he realized Lin Xun wasn't listening at all. He had looked right past him, into the room, and then pushed the door open and walked in.

Jiang Qing: ???

Strange. He had the distinct feeling he was about to witness a scene.

chapters.title: The Meeting
chapters.content:
Lin Xun walked into the room and immediately locked onto the young man seated across from him.

Ash-grey hair, effortlessly tousled. Vaguely familiar.

After a moment it came to him.

Yu Minghan. The face of a yogurt brand, one of the sponsors for "I Am an Actor," which meant his ad ran before every episode.

"Lin Xun?" Yu Minghan's eyebrow went up. The name wasn't unfamiliar to him.

Flows of attention ran both ways between anyone competing for the same spotlight, and Lin Xun was one of Yu Minghan's points of observation.

After watching for a while, though, he'd noticed this one wasn't cut from the same cloth as Wang Mingzhi. There was none of that hungry, calculating energy. If anything, he was almost Buddhist about the whole thing, low-key in his private life.

"Hello." Lin Xun smiled and extended his hand across the table. "I've heard a lot about you."

Yu Minghan blinked, leaned across the table to shake it, then said, confused, "Why are you here? Did you come to see me, or..."

As he was speaking, he noticed the people who had followed Lin Xun in, including the owner of Ruian Investment. Something clicked somewhere in the back of his mind, and he said with a carefully feigned smile, "Or did someone else arrange the meeting?"

Jiang Qing rubbed the side of his nose and said, "He was just passing through..."

"I came to see you." Lin Xun glanced briefly at Jiang Qing, then looked back at Yu Minghan.

Jiang Qing: Excuse me?

Yu Minghan's eyes went round. He pointed at himself. "Me?"

"Yes. I have a small business matter I'd like to discuss with you."

Chao Lianchuan, thoroughly lost, got to his feet. "If it's about a collaboration, that conversation would go through me."

"That's fine, it's nothing major." Lin Xun held Yu Minghan's gaze steadily, quietly running his eyes over the easy, devil-may-care posture, and something that had been tense inside him quietly relaxed.

Yu Minghan had never faced Lin Xun directly before, but the stunt Lin Xun had pulled a few days back, standing up for Jiang Qing and changing his personal certification, had lodged itself firmly in his mind.

Hadn't Jiang Qing said he didn't do friendships? And then turned around and did that love certification thing with someone? What was that about?

He wanted to see for himself what the deal was with this Lin Xun.

"What kind of business?" Yu Minghan asked.

Jiang Qing gestured for him to sit down and take his time, but Lin Xun didn't move. He said, "I was wondering: as the brand ambassador, do you get any kind of discount if I want to buy yogurt in bulk?"

Yu Minghan: ???

Jiang Qing: ...

The room: ............

Yu Minghan was fairly certain he'd misheard. He cleared his ear with one finger, stared in disbelief, and asked, "Did you just, while talking to me, ask if I could get you a discount on yogurt?"

"Yes. I urgently need a few cases of the brand you represent. As the ambassador, do you have any kind of deal you could offer?"

Yu Minghan stared with enormous eyes at Chao Lianchuan, who looked just as derailed, then at Yang Meng, and finally fixed Jiang Qing with the expression of a man who had given up trying to understand the world. His eyebrows were basically tied in a knot. "So this is the type you like?"

Jiang Qing: Could you please finish your sentence before implying things?!

Lin Xun's eyelid twitched almost imperceptibly. He looked at Jiang Qing. "Hmm? What does he mean? You like someone like me?"

"He means friends," Yu Minghan added helpfully. "Like, Jiang Qing likes having friends like you."

Lin Xun: "Oh."

"Jiang Qing, look at me! I can be that too!" Yu Minghan waved a hand in his direction.

Lin Xun: "Oh!"

"Leaving a sentence half-finished is genuinely dangerous for everyone in the room," Jiang Qing said flatly. He looked at Yu Minghan, then started maneuvering Lin Xun toward the door. "His brain isn't done developing. Don't take anything he says to heart. And you, we'll talk when we get home. Stop making things complicated in here."

Lin Xun didn't push back further, and pulled Yang Meng along to leave. A few steps out, he noticed Yang Meng wearing an expression of profound grievance.

"What's that look for?"

"I hate you." Yang Meng gritted out, then with a dramatic shake of his head. "Stay away from me. I don't deserve to be your friend. I only deserve to be your uncle."

Lin Xun looked at him calmly. "Do you actually dare to be my uncle?"

Yang Meng felt a chill run through him as a certain terrifying presence surfaced in his mind. He shook his head rapidly. "No, never mind. Can't afford that."

Today they were here to meet a client; the new studio had wrapped up its finishing work, and they had invited clients to dinner to mark the occasion. Running into Jiang Qing and the others here had been entirely unplanned.

Yang Meng asked, curious, "Do you think Jiang Qing will sign with them?"

"No."

"Why not?"

"Because Jiang Qing is loyal. After everything I've done for him, he'd have no reason not to sign with me."

Yang Meng rolled his eyes silently and scoffed. "Loyal? The whole internet says he's the most cutthroat, cold-hearted person in the industry."

They got into the car, and Lin Xun looked up at a certain floor of the hotel. A small smile crossed his face. "The colder he is on the surface, the more he feels things underneath. You just haven't seen it."

Otherwise he wouldn't bother returning a bowl of grapes or a handful of strawberries in kind.

Jiang Qing was someone who lacked security, who had few friends, who had been starved of family. Maybe because he'd entered society too young and seen the kinds of ugliness that most people never encountered, he had wrapped himself in something very tight and very hard.

But once you pried that shell open, what you found inside was a pearl, clean and rare.

So Lin Xun wasn't worried that Jiang Qing would impulsively sign with some other company on the spot. The man seemed to be waiting for something, a complete and total and unshakeable reason to trust someone and throw himself into a venture alongside them.

The so-called three days wasn't a brush-off. Most likely it was a window to see whether whatever remaining hesitation he had might finally dissolve, and whether he could walk into this with nothing left to second-guess.

Yang Meng suddenly asked, "By the way, aside from Jiang Qing, who else are you planning to sign?"

Lin Xun noticed the leading tone. "Do you have someone in mind?"

"What do you think of Mu Ning?" Yang Meng was in a good mood, humming under his breath while he drove. "One of the top six young actresses, good traffic, good reputation. Hard-working too, she basically lives on set all year. Looks great."

"Hard-working on set," Lin Xun said, "or hard-working making her way to your place?"

"Ahem." Yang Meng cut him off and laughed awkwardly. "Man, what can I say, I'm not practicing celibacy here. What two people do of their own accord is their own business."

"I never said anything about you. But I'm not agreeing to this." Lin Xun pulled up Mu Ning's information on his phone. "She's not positioned the same way as what I'm building. And on what basis would she even join? Your situation with her would invite trouble."

"I was just throwing it out there. I obviously know it's complicated. But she apparently heard you were opening a studio and wanted to come take a look."

"Why would she want to look at my studio?"

Yang Meng turned that over for a moment, puzzled. "Actually, good question. I haven't told her anything about your background. So why would she already know to look for leverage here?"

Lin Xun dropped his gaze and arrived at an unlikely conclusion. "She doesn't know who I am. But based on what Jiang Qing has said, there are people in the industry who assume the two of us have a certain arrangement. Maybe she thinks you're the one who's bankrolling this for me, and that's why she wants to come see."

"Oh my god," Yang Meng came to the same realization, "she might actually think it was me who set you up with all of this, and she wants to come have a look and possibly get in on it. I'll have to actually ask her about this next time."

"Are you two together?"

"No, no. The world is too beautiful a place to walk into a grave that early."

Lin Xun smiled a little, reminded him gently not to let things spiral out of control at home, and then after a pause added, "Also."

"What?"

"I'm not celibate."

"......"

Yang Meng turned the sarcasm all the way up. "Oh really? Does that make a difference? Were you not a virgin before I met you?"

Lin Xun shot him a cool look.

Back in the hotel private room.

Jiang Qing sat properly in his chair, making a point of not acknowledging Yu Minghan, who had slid his chair over to sit right next to him, while listening to Chao Lianchuan and Shu Tong talk business.

The two managers had, somewhere along the way, drifted into reminiscing about old times, then into a heated discussion about teenagers and their rebellious years.

"Forget those two oldies," Yu Minghan was saying, leaning toward him. "Come on, let's play a round. I'm Diamond tier, I'll carry you."

Jiang Qing took a discreet look at Yu Minghan's screen and said with the air of someone who had seen too much, "You're a grown adult and you're still in there playing with middle schoolers. Can't you find something more age-appropriate?"

Yu Minghan's hand paused. He fixed Jiang Qing with a slow, knowing look. "Oh? Adult games... what kind of games are we talking about?"

Jiang Qing pulled out his phone with confidence. "Speaking of which, people in our industry tend to live pretty messy lives. Which is exactly why we need to purify the soul."

"Right, right," Yu Minghan leaned in eagerly, eyes already glued to Jiang Qing's phone, somewhere between shock and excitement that Jiang Qing apparently had a hidden side. "Pure of soul, clean of heart, virtuous and noble. Come on, what is it, show me."

"Purify the soul, protect the environment, go green, donate to charity, starts with you and me." Jiang Qing opened Alipay, navigated to the Forest feature, and harvested the energy he'd been saving from Lin Xun's account before coolly tilting the screen toward him. "So? Are you in? No winners or losers here. Just conservation."

Yu Minghan: ...

Dear lord. When I said adult games, this was not even in the same galaxy as what I meant.

Yu Minghan stared into the middle distance with the hollow look of a man whose soul had briefly left his body. He looked at Jiang Qing with eyes that had seen too much. "Ha. Hahahaha."

The meeting, which had the energy of a PTA gathering, wrapped up in an atmosphere of complete harmony. Yu Minghan went cheerfully back to his car, waved at Jiang Qing, and was already staring at the new Forest contact Jiang Qing had added when something suddenly struck him.

He slapped himself on the forehead. "Lianchuan-ge, what did we even call him here for?! The signing! He never agreed!"

"Let it go. If he wanted to sign, he wouldn't have spent the whole meeting playing Forest games with you." Chao Lianchuan laughed, then glanced in the rearview mirror, seemed to stop himself, and then said anyway, "Speaking of which, Tang Huan has had his mind somewhere else lately. Do you have any idea what's going on with him?"

"How would I know? He's my friend, not my girlfriend."

"Right, because you're so protective of your friends. Fair enough." Chao Lianchuan said with a dry tone. "In all seriousness, it's getting to be a problem. The endorsement you helped pull for him got canceled, and even though it wasn't technically his fault, he's still been in a mood about it. And then he heard you wanted to make friends with Jiang Qing, which probably rubbed him the wrong way. He was asked to go to a booking last time and flat-out refused. Said something about how no matter how hard he tries, he'll never be as good-looking as the next guy."

"That's ridiculous." Yu Minghan said it with genuine irritation. He had only bothered with Tang Huan at all because back in school, Tang Huan had been the one quietly saving him seats, grabbing meals for him, actually paying attention to him.

He had studied computer science but graduated with zero interest in becoming a prematurely balding software developer, so he came home and prepared to take over the family business.

He happened to be good-looking enough for the industry, and the traffic wasn't bad.

Tang Huan was decent-looking too. Pale and delicate, the type that stood out in a room full of rougher types, the type that made people want to cause trouble.

Yu Minghan had given him a hand up, and Tang Huan had been a loyal little shadow ever since.

Soft and agreeable: that was the first impression Tang Huan had always given him. So it was a little unexpected that he'd apparently developed a bit of a temper.

Yu Minghan wasn't the kind of person to just absorb that. He said, "I'll talk to him. If you can take the heat, stay in the kitchen. If you can't, go back to making software."

Then he added, "Honestly, Jiang Qing's easier to deal with. Straight shooter, nothing to read between the lines."

Chao Lianchuan looked at him in the rearview mirror. "Are you sure you only want to be friends with him?"

"Obviously! I'm completely straight! Steel-rod straight!!"

"Then why have you never dated anyone?"

"Have you been to the computer science building? Count the women. The few there were, I..." Yu Minghan trailed off. "They weren't better looking than my mom. I'm done talking about this. You're ruining my game."

After dinner, Jiang Qing and Shu Tong and Sang Yi headed home.

Jiang Qing stepped off the elevator and instinctively moved toward the balcony to check next door. The light was on in Lin Xun's apartment, and he felt a quiet release of breath he hadn't realized he was holding.

Then felt annoyed at himself for it. A perfectly good negotiation, and Lin Xun had walked in and scrambled the whole thing.

"You're home?"

Lin Xun appeared on the balcony, making Jiang Qing jump. His hand jerked against a large cactus. He'd landed on a cluster of spines.

"Ss—"

He held his hand up under the light and squinted.

Lin Xun stepped closer, peering at it. "Are you okay?"

"Got spined."

"You're not careful at all. Come here, I'll get them out. I'm good at this."

"I can manage."

"Stop being proud about it. I've done this before, come on."

The spines were too fine and too small to pull out cleanly with his bare fingers, and he stopped arguing. He went straight next door.

They sat on the sofa. Lin Xun produced a needle from somewhere, took his hand, bent his head low, and fixed his eyes on Jiang Qing's long, pale fingers. He studied them for a moment before beginning to work carefully at the embedded spines.

Jiang Qing braced himself, but the pain he expected didn't come.

After a moment, he opened his eyes slowly. Lin Xun's lashes were cast downward, shifting lightly, and Jiang Qing thought of what the Lavender fans were always saying about wanting to ride a swing on those lashes.

From this angle, the sharp line of Lin Xun's brow softened into something almost unrecognizable. The corner of his eye was low, his expression unreadable. But something in the set of his brow created an illusion of something like gentleness.

Then Lin Xun looked up, directly at him.

Their eyes met. Words failed him.

After a beat, the corner of Lin Xun's eye curved slightly. "What are you thinking about?"

Jiang Qing blinked fast and reached for something to say, glancing down at his own hand. "Where did you get experience with this?"

Lin Xun smiled a little, tilted his head, and kept working with quiet care. "My younger sister. She's a few years old and spends all her time in the garden. She gets spiked constantly. No matter how many times I remind her, she never learns."

Jiang Qing pictured it without meaning to, and laughed before he could stop himself.

Lin Xun glanced at the laugh, drew in a slow breath, and steadied his fingers enough to guide the last spine out cleanly.

"Done. Try not to let it happen again. Being your spine-removal service is exhausting."

Jiang Qing felt over his fingertips, checked that nothing had been left behind, and said thank you.

Then silence settled in.

He could have gone straight home, but for reasons he couldn't entirely explain, he didn't want to yet.

He also couldn't come up with a reason to stay, so he sat on the sofa and looked at Lin Xun.

Then his phone broke the quiet.

It was Sang Yi calling, which was unusual. She almost never reached out to him in the evenings unless something urgent had come up.

"Qing-ge! Dean Sang collapsed again. I want to go back."

"Again?" Jiang Qing stood up and paced. "I'll come with you."

"Really?"

"Yeah. Book the tickets now. And don't tell Tong-jie. Xiao Bao's on summer break, she should spend the time with her kid."

"Okay!"

After he hung up, Lin Xun saw the tension in him. "This late, where are you going?"

"Wutong Village. It's a small town in the south."

He had only taken a couple of steps when Lin Xun caught his arm.

"I'm coming too."

"You're coming?" Jiang Qing looked at him, puzzled.

"Yes. I have a friend who lives there. Been meaning to visit."

Jiang Qing studied him for a long, skeptical moment, then called Sang Yi back. Under Lin Xun's perfectly steady and unreadable gaze, he said, "Yi Yi, book three tickets."

chapters.title: The Orphanage
chapters.content:
They didn't leave that night.

It was too late. Even if they made it to the provincial capital by plane, they'd still need to take a high-speed train to the town, and by the time they reached the orphanage, it would practically be dawn.

The children would all be asleep. Arriving at that hour would have been a disruption.

So Sang Yi booked tickets for eight o'clock the next morning.

She arrived early to pick up both of them, double breakfast in hand.

Lin Xun ate in the car and glanced sideways. Jiang Qing was sitting there with his head drooping, lethargically nibbling on a bun he'd barely touched.

"Did you finish?" Lin Xun asked, hesitant.

Jiang Qing slowly raised his face, eyes closed, and continued nibbling at the bun like a person sleepwalking.

"......" Did a single night of not sleeping do this much damage? Lin Xun frowned. "Did you not sleep?"

"Mm." Still eyes closed, still chewing. "Yu Minghan's fault. He snuck into my Forest at midnight and stole all my energy. So I set a seven o'clock alarm and robbed his blind while he wasn't looking."

Lin Xun filed that away as information he had not expected to receive.

Jiang Qing went limp against the headrest, ate his way through breakfast, and passed out.

Half an hour later the car pulled up at the airport. He came awake to find himself in Lin Xun's arms, startled, and sat bolt upright, glaring back at Lin Xun. "You ambushed me!"

Lin Xun looked completely innocent. "You toppled onto me all on your own. My leg's gone numb from you pressing on it."

"Sorry." Jiang Qing rubbed his face, gave Lin Xun an apologetic glance, and got out.

From the front seat, Sang Yi turned around with a puzzled look. "Xun-ge, didn't you pull Qing-ge in on purpose just now?"

Lin Xun put a finger to his lips and gave her his most winning smile.

Sang Yi, thoroughly unaffected, looked at him with a blank expression.

"I'll teach you to drive."

"Yes!" Sang Yi immediately lit up. "Xun-ge, you're so good."

He caught a bit of sleep on the plane and stepped off feeling considerably more alert, stretching as he went. After a few more connections, they arrived at Wutong Village just before noon.

Wutong Village was tucked between mountains and water, scenic and peaceful, though the inconvenient access had kept it from ever becoming a proper tourist destination.

The local economy was modest; the population was small, and most of the people still living in town were elderly residents and children.

The taxi driver was a local who could tell at a glance they weren't from around here, and went straight in for the tourist markup.

Lin Xun didn't particularly mind, but Jiang Qing fired back at the man in dialect. The driver backed down and drove off, embarrassed.

Fortunately, the next driver was perfectly fair and kept the meter running, though he more than made up for it in conversation: first a rundown of the big local news, then a detailed account of his second cousin's third aunt's son's altercation with the neighbor's dog.

He kept trying to get the cute girl in the passenger seat to chime in, but the cute girl was deep in her game and had no interest in talking to him.

He glanced hopefully in the rearview mirror, expecting the two sunglasses-wearing guys in the back to have some advice about dealing with aggressive dogs.

What he saw instead was the one with the brown hair pulling the one with the longer hair into his side.

He chuckled. "Are you two brothers? You really are close. My two boys fight every day. If they could get along half as well as you two, I'd die happy."

Lin Xun smiled politely. "He's asleep. Could you keep it down a little?" He didn't explain the relationship.

Jiang Qing wasn't actually asleep. His head was spinning from the winding roads of the old lanes, and he couldn't be bothered to keep watching out the window. So he'd leaned against Lin Xun and closed his eyes.

Lin Xun seemed to be worried he'd slide off and had an arm loosely around his shoulder the whole time, not moving.

Of course he'd heard Lin Xun's quiet murmur. With his eyes shut and the visual noise gone, his hearing had sharpened, and for just a moment, there was something in Lin Xun's voice that sounded almost like tenderness.

He let himself drift rather than overthink it, shifted to find a more comfortable angle, and looped an arm loosely around Lin Xun's waist. He felt the other man go rigid.

"Yi Yi," he said, muffled, "turn your game sounds down."

Sang Yi's fingers stilled. She turned to look at him with a bewildered expression, thinking: I've been in silent mode this whole time.

She looked to Lin Xun for guidance.

Lin Xun smiled slightly and shook his head, signaling that it was fine.

He looked back down at the sleeping face resting against him.

The car rocked gently through the streets, and finally came to a stop in front of a large gate.

Jiang Qing seemed to sense the stillness and opened his eyes, stepping out with practiced ease. He stood in front of the gate and looked up.

Wutong Orphanage, painted in red characters across the top. They had faded some, and the walls were starting to flake in places.

But the building inside looked clean and freshly kept, a two-story structure with four rooms on each floor. Two smaller buildings flanked it on either side, the whole thing resembling a compact little school.

Sang Yi paid the driver, then walked with Lin Xun to stand beside him.

Lin Xun asked, "What made you come back here?"

Jiang Qing smiled a little. "Home visit."

"Are you..." Lin Xun started to ask, and before he could finish, Jiang Qing had already guessed the direction of the question.

He walked ahead, not looking back. "Everyone's an orphan in the end, one way or another."

Lin Xun followed without fully understanding, and after a few steps, caught the sound of children reading aloud.

He was about to look in when Jiang Qing pulled him by the side toward a staircase and up to the second floor.

Moments later, the three of them were standing outside the door to a room labeled "Office."

Sang Yi saw the door was open and heard voices inside. She burst in and flung herself at one of the people sitting there. "Dean!"

The man she'd called Dean had white hair at the temples and a network of lines at the corners of his eyes and mouth. His face was warm. He looked at the girl who had appeared out of nowhere, laughing as he patted her back. "Yi Yi. What are you doing here again?"

He noticed the two following behind her, and his face brightened further. "Ah Qing! You came too!"

"Of course I came. What do you think you're doing, having some ailment and fainting every five minutes? What did the doctor say?" Jiang Qing came to stand beside him and look him over. "What's wrong with you now?"

"Nothing serious. The old thing acting up again, head pains." Dean Sang smiled a little sheepishly, then looked at the tall stranger. "And this is?"

"My friend. Lin Xun." Jiang Qing made the introduction, then gestured to Dean Sang for Lin Xun's benefit. "Dean Sang."

The two of them exchanged nods.

Dean Sang suddenly put on a serious face. "What are you all doing here? Did someone tattle on me?"

The woman who had been quietly sitting to one side, Li Dajie, broke into laughter. "You, Dean, really. You fall ill and you're surprised the children want to come check on you. I have nothing more to say. I'm going to start on dinner. Special meal tonight!"

Jiang Qing pulled up a stool across from Dean Sang and asked after him properly. The two hadn't seen each other in a while, so naturally they had catching up to do.

Sang Yi still had the car on her mind. Seeing Lin Xun looking around the office with obvious curiosity, she took it upon herself to guide him.

Unfortunately, her social skills were essentially nonexistent.

Lin Xun found himself standing in front of a table stacked with teaching materials as Sang Yi jabbed a finger at it. "Look."

Before he'd made any sense of it, she was already pointing at the wall. "Look."

Lin Xun looked up at a group photo mounted on the wall. Dean Sang sat in the center, surrounded by over twenty children. The tallest one stood at the back in the middle, fifteen or sixteen years old, expressionless and vaguely lost-looking. That was Sang Yi.

"Look!" Sang Yi had already led him out to the corridor and was now indicating the courtyard below. "Playground."

Lin Xun: ...

Ah. So it's a playground. From the way you're presenting this, I almost thought you'd built it yourself.

Sang Yi marched down the stairs and led him to the western building, pushed open a door. "Look!"

Lin Xun looked at the empty room. "What is this place?"

Sang Yi thought for a moment. "Dean said it's a music room."

"Where are the instruments?"

"They'll be here in a few years."

Lin Xun smiled and noticed the wall in the room was covered in photos. A photo for every child, with their name underneath. Sang Yi had one too.

But she also had two group shots, taken with Jiang Qing.

He looked at the people in the photos; both of them slightly younger.

In one, Jiang Qing was sitting on the steps outside the main gate, expressionless, head half-tilted toward the sky, smoking. His hand was open with two pieces of candy resting in the palm. A girl beside him, a little stiff, was reaching out cautiously to take them.

In the other, Jiang Qing had one leg crossed over the other and was sitting under a tree on the playground, playing a handheld game. The girl stood next to him, bent slightly at the waist, clearly trying to get a look at the screen.

"How long have you two known each other?" Lin Xun asked.

"I was fifteen then," Sang Yi said. "Qing-ge was twenty. Six years."

A bell rang. Children's laughter and shrieks flooded in from somewhere.

Lin Xun stepped out onto the corridor and looked down. He could see Jiang Qing walking out from the office in the other building, waving to the swarm of small figures below him with the energy of an emperor acknowledging his court. "At ease, children."

And then the court rushed the emperor all at once. Their teacher's voice carried from somewhere below: "Slow down, everyone! Be careful!"

Lin Xun braced his arms on the railing and watched from a distance.

Children of every size clung to Jiang Qing's clothes, and one particularly determined one had scaled him entirely, finally getting scooped up and held against his chest. Jiang Qing smiled a little. "Dinner first. I'm starving."

Lunch was a small occasion, three extra dishes put out in honor of the guests, six dishes and one soup in total, each served in a large communal bowl.

Jiang Qing took a small bowl to the serving table and glanced back at the large bowl Li Dajie had specially given Lin Xun.

"You eat less," Jiang Qing said.

Lin Xun: ......

The dining hall had four long tables, and each one needed an adult to keep an eye on things.

The moment the two of them sat down, the children at their table were visibly smug, shooting looks of superior satisfaction at the other tables before turning back and grinning up at them.

One bolder girl of about ten studied the newcomer Lin Xun with round, unblinking eyes. "Jiang Qing-gege, who's this brother?"

"A friend."

"Oh! Is he the kind of friend you marry?!"

Both Jiang Qing and Lin Xun inhaled wrong at the same moment. The other children didn't know what had set the adults off, but following along with the reaction seemed like the right move, so they started giggling too.

Lin Xun pressed his lips together, dropped his gaze to his rice bowl, and ate a few bites before he could get his expression under control.

Jiang Qing flicked the girl on the forehead. "Who told you friends are people you marry?"

"Li Dajie said it! She said she wants to go steady with someone, and then go get married."

Li Dajie, in the kitchen across the way, suddenly felt the temperature rise. Her dark cheeks flushed. "Xiao Wu, don't you go making things up!"

Dean Sang was laughing so hard his whole face quivered, then caught a pointed look from Jiang Qing and blinked innocently. "What?"

"Have you considered adding a health education curriculum?"

Dean Sang: ...

The teachers: ...

Li Dajie: ...I'm a little embarrassed, actually.

Even regular schools rarely tackled that topic properly, and in somewhere as remote as this, the older adults like Dean Sang and Li Dajie found it even harder to bring up with the children.

But Jiang Qing thought it was important. These children were already missing the warmth of a family. Without knowing how to protect themselves, their vulnerability to manipulation was significantly higher.

And they'd all grow up eventually. Better to face it than leave them as unprepared as Sang Yi still was, a full-grown person who barely knew what love was.

The adults went quiet with mild embarrassment; the children were too young to follow and went back to their food.

Lin Xun backed him up. "I think he's right. Our school ran health education from an early age. It's definitely worth introducing to children at the right age."

Dean Sang nodded, a little awkward, but when he thought it through properly, he knew it made sense.

Still, the topic had him thinking about something else entirely. He lowered his voice and leaned in with a conspiratorial expression. "Yi Yi, have you found someone yet?"

"Yes," Sang Yi said.

Everyone at the table: collective alarm.

Dean Sang got excited and looked at Jiang Qing, communicating urgently with his eyes: who is it?

Jiang Qing himself was stunned. He turned to her. "Who?! When did you start seeing someone and not tell me?"

Sang Yi looked up from her bowl, pointed at the person beside Jiang Qing, and said, perfectly matter-of-fact, "Xun-ge."

Jiang Qing: !!

Dean Sang: !!
