Lin Xun had barely seen it coming. He jolted back against the wall like someone had done something to him, looking as put-upon as possible. "It's not me. That's not what happened. Yi Yi is lying."

Jiang Qing's eyes narrowed. "Did you seduce her on purpose?"

"I genuinely had nothing to do with it. I wasn't pursuing her. If I were pursuing anyone, it would be..." Lin Xun stopped abruptly. He saw Jiang Qing's sly expression and realized, "You knew that wasn't what she meant."

Jiang Qing had meant to keep the act going a bit longer, but one look at Lin Xun's face and he broke. He laughed.

Of course he knew. Sang Yi was not going to fall in love with Lin Xun. As if Lin Xun's appeal could ever match his own.

In Sang Yi's ranking, it went roughly: Lin Xun < Jiang Qing < games.

Dean Sang, however, was still trying to evaluate his potential son-in-law. He fired off three questions in rapid succession. "Where are you from, young man? How old are you? What do you do for work? Do you have insurance?"

Jiang Qing lost it, doubled over the table, laughing until his stomach hurt.

The children caught the wave without understanding it and laughed right along.

After the meal, the children went off reluctantly to their afternoon nap and classes.

Jiang Qing brought Lin Xun along to take a walk around town. The two of them took a taxi to the center.

The sun was working hard. The streets were fairly quiet. The occasional pair of girls with parasols might glance over at two tall, long-legged men walking by, and by the time they looked back, there was only the retreating outline of their backs.

Lin Xun had no idea where Jiang Qing was headed, and though it looked aimless, there was probably a destination somewhere.

While he was thinking it over, he saw Jiang Qing stop at a roadside stall and pick up a few small things.

Eventually, the two of them walked into a shop.

Lin Xun looked up. A musical instrument store.

Jiang Qing, after the staff made introductions, selected one upright piano, twenty electronic keyboards, and a handful of guitars.

While it was being rung up, Lin Xun said quietly, "This piano's a bit ordinary. Want to go for a better one?"

Jiang Qing wasn't interested, paid, arranged for delivery, and said, "No point giving them something too fine. If everything comes too easily, it doesn't mean as much."

Lin Xun thought about it, and understood. Growing up with access to anything he wanted, he hadn't really had to consider that kind of thing.

He smiled. "Teacher Jiang is not only beautiful but also kindhearted."

"Kindhearted nothing. You haven't seen me when I discipline them." Jiang Qing said. "I'm terrifying when I'm angry. I've had kids cry for their parents. Not that it helps most of them, since they don't have any."

They made it back before long, and the delivery team from the shop arrived shortly after.

Dean Sang came down to take a look and when his eyes landed on the piano, they grew wet. He held onto Jiang Qing's hand and didn't let go. "Thank you. On behalf of all of them, thank you."

"It's nothing. Call it a dowry for Yi Yi."

Sang Yi: "I'm not getting married!" Games are better than marriage. This isn't even close.

The afternoon classes hadn't ended yet, but at the bell, the children came streaming out to see what was happening. At the sight of things they'd only ever seen on television, they erupted with delight.

The largest piece, the upright piano, was temporarily set up in the open courtyard while the staff waited to move it inside.

"Jiang Qing-gege, play something!" Xiao Wu started clapping, and the rest followed. "We've seen you play! You sound so good!"

Jiang Qing's piano playing was, in truth, not that impressive. What they'd seen was the version that existed in films.

He walked up, lifted the lid, and pressed a single key with one finger, testing the sound.

He looked back at the children's bright, expectant faces, smiled once, and pressed another key.

One finger at a time, slowly, but if you listened carefully, you could make out the shape of "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star."

It had been a while. He was rusty.

He moved his fingers around to warm them up, then put both hands on the keys, and let something take over, something that felt like muscle memory.

Funny, in a way. It was Jiang Huai who had taught him this piece.

He remembered being very small, when Jiang Huai was too occupied with work, and his mother was even busier.

Between them, they had arranged a full schedule of classes and tutors. The only faces he saw regularly were those of various teachers.

He had hated the piano teacher. The teacher was strict, wouldn't let him play with his building blocks, and sat next to him monitoring every note, reporting to his parents when he made mistakes.

Once, he'd lost his temper, and Jiang Huai came himself to teach him.

When sitting for too long made him sore, Jiang Huai would pick him up and put him on his lap.

He had deliberately refused to learn, and they spent six full months on a single piece.

Little Jiang Qing had thought that when his mother finally came home from her work, he would play it for her. She would tell him he was the most beautiful child in the world.

What he'd wanted didn't happen. The piece was never played for her. The piano ended up smashed.

A wrong note rang out.

The sound was obvious enough that even the children who couldn't read music sensed something had gone off.

He pulled his hands back, a little rueful, and turned to them with a smile. "I told you I'm no good."

A stillness fell. Children were the most attuned to what adults were feeling. They could tell something in Jiang Qing-gege's mood had changed. Maybe the wrong note, maybe something else.

Then the piano began again.

Everyone looked toward the newcomer. Lin Xun's hands moved across the keys with real ease, releasing a bright, fast-moving piece. His whole body swayed slightly with the rhythm; it was clear he was comfortable with this. Now and then he'd turn to look at Jiang Qing beside him.

"So good!" Xiao Wu took the lead, and the children clapped along and pushed in for a closer look.

Jiang Qing watched for a moment, then reached out and pressed a random key, interrupting the rhythm.

Lin Xun stopped, and then took the note Jiang Qing had played and pivoted seamlessly into something new.

Jiang Qing raised an eyebrow and pressed another key.

Lin Xun switched again without hesitation.

Jiang Qing: ...

"Together?" Lin Xun asked.

Jiang Qing unleashed his hands on the keys. No plan, just noise. Lin Xun matched it completely, chaos for chaos, playing along with genuine enthusiasm, until Dean Sang started backing away from the sounds.

After a while, Dean Sang reflexively reached for his camera. He kept it there.

Late-summer afternoon light filtered through the wutong tree above them, casting patchwork shadows across every face in the yard.

The children laughed and shrieked. And at the center of them, two adults who had briefly forgotten to be adults.

The two of them turned at the same moment and looked at each other. Their faces were alive, the sun behind them, their expressions unreadable from a distance, but the warmth in the set of their brows was there if you looked.

Like the light in the top of the trees, not yet blazing, but enough to leave a mark.

chapters.title: A Heart Out of Rhythm
chapters.content:
By dinner, the children had warmed up to Lin Xun considerably. The cautious reserve from earlier had melted into something much stickier.

As far as they were concerned, Jiang Qing-gege was the tallest and most capable person they'd ever known.

But this new big brother seemed, maybe, just a little bit more capable than Jiang Qing-gege.

They couldn't explain exactly how or why. But he could make Jiang Qing-gege angry, and that had to count for something. The same way Xiao-er-gege could pick on Xiao-san-jiejie, and Xiao-san couldn't do anything about it, which made Xiao-er the stronger one.

By that logic, Lin Xun-gege was clearly someone to reckon with.

On hearing the theory, Jiang Qing was so indignant he ate an entire extra bowl of rice.

I'll eat you all out of house and home.

Lin Xun was delighted and rewarded his new fans with a trip to the little shop down the road for snacks.

Jiang Qing came along. It was evening now and the first hints of autumn were in the air, the temperature dropping at either end of the day, a faint breeze running through.

The children were running ahead, not the least bit cold.

Jiang Qing was about to brush back his wind-blown hair when something latched onto his leg.

He looked down. Xiao Jiu.

Xiao Jiu was five or six, too slow to keep up with the older kids, so he'd turned back. He wrapped himself around Jiang Qing's leg and blinked his enormous, guileless eyes up at him, not saying a word.

Jiang Qing crouched and poked at his cheek, then swept him up onto one arm and tickled him.

Xiao Jiu laughed so hard he scrunched up into a ball, burrowing deeper into Jiang Qing's chest, not making a sound.

Lin Xun watched, and found the image unexpectedly moving.

Then something occurred to him. "Xiao Jiu, he..."

Jiang Qing had been gently scratching at Xiao Jiu's arm. He paused. "He can't speak."

The children here were not all whole and healthy.

Xiao Wu walked with an uneven gait, obvious in the way she moved.

Xiao Ba was a girl with a large blue-tinged scar across her face. Elders had called it an ill omen, said she'd never find a husband.

Xiao Liu had a congenital heart condition.

The money Jiang Qing sent covered some hardware costs, a building, educational supplies, but most of it went toward medical care for the children.

Lin Xun looked down, and then thought of Sang Yi. "What about Yi Yi?"

"Yi Yi has nothing wrong with her physically. Her only problems are mild social withdrawal and a tendency toward violence." Jiang Qing smiled a little. "You should have seen her at fourteen or fifteen. Terrifying. If a problem could be solved with her fists, she didn't bother using words. She carried pieces of brick and iron rods in her school bag."

"That's kind of cool, honestly."

Jiang Qing smiled and went back to fussing over Xiao Jiu.

Up ahead, Xiao Wu looked back and saw that Xiao Jiu was getting the better treatment. She turned and came back in her unsteady, determined gait, arms outstretched. "Lin Xun-gege, carry me!"

Lin Xun picked her up. Xiao Wu was thrilled. "Lin Xun-gege, you're so good. When I grow up, I'm going to marry you."

Jiang Qing: "Well. That's bold."

Lin Xun: "Why marry me? Isn't Jiang Qing-gege a good choice?"

"Jiang Qing-gege told me to give up on him!" Xiao Wu reported with great grievance.

Lin Xun looked at Jiang Qing. "You couldn't have let her down a little more gently?"

"You marry her then."

Lin Xun said, entirely serious, "Xiao Wu, I suggest you give up on me too."

"Wuwuwuwu!"

One small person, already twice rejected at this age. The injustice of it grew in her mind until she let out a proper wail.

Both men, beyond offering "don't cry," had absolutely nothing useful to contribute.

After trying for a while without success, Jiang Qing deployed his one real tool: "Xiao Wu, you are the loveliest child I've ever... ever seen. When you grow up, an absolutely wonderful, wonderful person is going to come and marry you."

"Really? Really?" Xiao Wu hiccupped and asked.

"Of course. You're clever and sweet. Who could resist you?"

"But my leg isn't right."

Jiang Qing: ...you are very forthright.

Lin Xun wiped her eyes gently. "You can draw people in with your strengths. When you come in first in a competition, do you think anyone notices your leg? When you've built something of your own, does anyone still care about your leg? You're the only one who thinks about it, and you don't have to. A clever girl like you knows that, right?"

Xiao Wu's expression was somewhere between understanding and not quite there. She wiped the last of her tears. "Okay... but will the person who comes for me be good-looking?"

"They will be," Lin Xun said, coaxing her.

Jiang Qing: ...the leg isn't the concern here. The romantic fixation is.

Xiao Wu looked up hopefully. "As good-looking as you two?"

"Not quite," Lin Xun answered honestly.

"Waaaa."

By the time Xiao Wu had cried herself out, her face was a mess.

Jiang Qing looked at the little tear-streaked face and laughed, and then something moved through him, and he said, almost to himself, "Wutong Village really does something for a person. Everyone here grows up so bright-eyed."

Lin Xun: "Like you?"

"Yes." Jiang Qing hadn't been thinking of himself, but since it was being handed to him, there was no reason not to accept it.

Maybe it was the mood of the evening, maybe it was the temporary distance from work and everything that came with it.

Coming back to the village felt like returning to something real, and the whole of him had settled down. There was a strange, rare urge to just say things out loud.

"Look at Xiao Jiu. He's such a pretty little thing. Yi Yi too; if she ever went into the industry she could absolutely get by on her looks alone. Which is a shame, really, because she's a walking hazard. The first few years, I genuinely worried she'd pull out a stun-baton and drop one of my more enthusiastic fans."

Lin Xun let out a real, full laugh.

"Still, the best-looking one was my mom. She was the local beauty from here. Not just the village, actually. The whole town. The whole city."

He laughed at himself a little. "There were so many people after her you could have lined them up from here to the capital. But she had bigger ideas. She didn't want to stay somewhere small."

"She left on her own for the capital, and there she met Jiang... her husband. They married young, and not long after, her career started to find its footing. She did very well."

"And after that?"

"After that?" Jiang Qing shrugged it off with a small smile. "She died. Not that you should make a face like that; dying is something everyone goes through. Though I do think she died too soon for someone who had been so beautiful, and by the end I couldn't even recognize her. Wasted away to nothing, not a trace of how she used to look."

He went quiet after that.

Lin Xun exhaled soundlessly and very quietly scratched Xiao Wu, who immediately broke the moment with a shriek: "Lin Xun-gege, you!"

"What do you want?" Lin Xun asked immediately.

"Ice cream!"

"No." Jiang Qing refused without hesitation.

At the small shop, Jiang Qing confiscated all the spicy and cold snacks they'd picked out, then divided them between himself and Lin Xun.

Xiao Wu was outraged. She refused to let Jiang Qing carry Xiao Jiu anymore and took it upon herself to carry Xiao Jiu on her own back, walking ahead with him piggyback in a stiff, wobbling march, back pointedly turned on all of them.

Jiang Qing bit into his ice cream. The cold hit him in a sharp jolt that made his brow twitch.

Click.

Lin Xun was there like he'd planned for this exact moment. He caught the expression on Jiang Qing's face before Jiang Qing could snatch the phone back, and slipped it safely into his pocket before making a run for it.

"Immature child!" Jiang Qing chased after him, shouting, ice cream still in hand, not willing to let it drop.

Xiao Wu watched their backs, the two of them chasing and yelling at each other, and clicked her tongue. "Xiao Jiu, don't they remind you of what Li Dajie said being in love looks like? Hmph. I curse them to never deserve me when they grow up!"

When they got back, Dean Sang had set a large round table up in the courtyard and switched on the outdoor lights.

Everyone gathered around to put the snacks out and sit together.

Jiang Qing reached over and picked up a piece of candy, then tossed it at Sang Yi, who had her head down looking at her phone. "Game, game, game. You're always on that thing."

Sang Yi felt around her head, picked the candy up off the ground, peeled it, ate it, and looked back at him with a small untroubled smile. Jiang Qing went back to finding something of his own to eat.

Lin Xun noticed that Jiang Qing's kindness was actually the kind that came with plausible deniability; he seemed to go out of his way to avoid being seen doing something nice for someone. The armor was almost always up, projecting the general air of I'm difficult, keep your distance.

"What are you smiling at," Jiang Qing said flatly, looking at him.

Lin Xun didn't stop smiling. "How did you and Yi Yi meet?"

Sang Yi, with no games to play and nothing else to do, looked up. "Fight."

Lin Xun: "Interesting."

"She was the one fighting, not me. Don't rope me in." Jiang Qing looked at Sang Yi pointedly.

Jiang Qing had been back in Wutong Village the year he'd taken home his Best Actor award. After getting the trophy, he'd spent ten days going back and forth on whether to go see Jiang Huai at all, and ultimately decided he might as well, if only to rattle him a little.

Jiang Huai had only glanced up briefly and said, in the same flat tone as always, "What's a Best Actor worth? Look at the one who took the Golden Duck award just the other week and ended up in custody."

That actor had won his award only a few days before Jiang Qing, and the story had become everyone's small talk at the time. Even Jiang Huai, who had no interest in the entertainment world, had heard about it.

The implication was clear: Best Actor or not, look at where it led.

It made Jiang Qing furious. He left, slamming the door. Since he had some time off, he bought a ticket and came directly to Wutong Village, giving himself a small break.

He didn't come here often. He'd been born in the capital, visited now and then with his mother, and met his grandfather only a handful of times. His grandfather had never wanted to leave the village.

But he didn't know why, in that moment, he'd just wanted to come see the place where his mother had lived.

On one of his days wandering around, he passed by a school and found himself in an alley where he stumbled across a case of bullying. A group of teenagers, bigger and older than their target, had cornered a girl and were demanding money from her, threatening to make her their girlfriend if she refused.

Jiang Qing had barely reached for his phone when the girl wordlessly pulled a rod out of her bag and brought it down on the ringleader's head.

The force behind it was evident from how much the ringleader bled.

The girl fought with a raw ferocity, not tracking who she was hitting or how much damage she was taking herself, just throwing herself in until the gang of troublemakers heard police sirens approaching and scattered.

Jiang Qing turned off his recording, walked over, and helped pick up her bag. Scattered on the ground were what amounted to a small arsenal.

The girl gave him one look, then walked off. No thank you. Nothing.

The next day, uneasy, he bought a pack of cigarettes and wandered back, and ran into her again.

This time there were more of them, and they didn't bother with threats. They got straight to it.

"What is this?" Jiang Qing had his sunglasses on, a cigarette between his teeth, and had pulled out a prop gun from a shoot, realistic enough to pass. He channeled everything he'd picked up from a lifetime of playing criminals and gangsters, strolled toward them with a slow, unhurried swagger, and said the kind of line only a character in a film would actually deliver. "This girl's under my protection. Anyone who tries anything answers to this."

They were teenagers playing at being tough. They'd never encountered this in real life. They ran.

Jiang Qing put the prop gun away and turned to leave, but a hand caught his arm.

He looked back. The girl who never said anything had finally spoken.

"Where did you get the gun?"

...... Are you planning to source a few for yourself?

He dug in his pocket, came up with two pieces of candy the shopkeeper had given him as change, and opened his palm. "Want some? I'll tell you if you take one."

The girl didn't move.

"You take one and I tell you. That's the deal."

The girl slowly extended her hand, peeled the wrapper, and put it in her mouth.

"Is it sweet?"

A long pause. Then she nodded.

He walked her to and from school for the rest of that month. He learned her name was Sang Yi, that she was not only a violent underachiever but an orphan.

When he had time, he'd stop by the orphanage and spend time with the children.

When he was leaving Wutong Village, he went to see Dean Sang and offered to fund a proper school building for the orphanage.

Back in the capital, he received a call from Dean Sang.

Dean Sang told him that when some other kids were in trouble, Sang Yi had gone to help and had gotten hurt in the process, and also been expelled. She was currently at the orphanage helping with construction.

Jiang Qing decided this couldn't continue. A young woman couldn't live like this her whole life. He suggested bringing Sang Yi to the capital to work as his assistant, since she clearly wasn't going back to school anyway.

He had had some thought, at the time, of Sang Yi possibly making it in the industry if a director happened to notice her looks.

And one did. A director had been interested. When they met, the director started putting his hands where they didn't belong. Sang Yi had beaten him thoroughly before Jiang Qing could even move.

After that, he stopped thinking about it.

Sang Yi hadn't wanted to leave the orphanage at first. It was only once the school building was finished and the younger ones no longer needed to go elsewhere for classes that she seemed to realize she might not be needed quite so urgently anymore.

When Jiang Qing found her again, he told her: come to the capital to make money, build something bigger later on, and in the meantime learn proper fighting technique, because sheer aggression only goes so far.

The last thing he did was drop an old handheld game into her hands. "First month's pay, in advance. You like fighting? Fight in here."

Lin Xun listened with interest, then asked, "So Yi Yi followed you because of the game?"

Jiang Qing: ...she's very perceptive.

He had no real defense against it. As humiliating as it was, the truth was that no offer of money or opportunity had worked, and it really had been a secondhand game console that clinched it.

Lin Xun laughed, and turned to look at Sang Yi, who had gone very quiet. He said, "Not because of the game. She went with you because of you."

"What do you mean?"

"Money didn't mean much to Yi Yi. Her whole sense of purpose was probably rooted in keeping the younger ones safe. But once the orphanage didn't need her to do that anymore, she was completely adrift. And maybe she realized somewhere in that time that someone else had started looking out for her. So the protective instinct shifted to you."

Jiang Qing went still, then turned to look at Sang Yi.

Sang Yi knocked her palm on the table, stood up, and walked away without turning around.

Jiang Qing: ...

Dean Sang laughed warmly. "Yi Yi's embarrassed!"

Sang Yi and Li Dajie had made up two beds in the east building. Dean Sang had initially suggested the two of them stay at a hotel in town.

But Jiang Qing couldn't be bothered, and Lin Xun didn't mind, so they agreed to take one of the spare dormitory rooms, new bedding and all.

After washing up, the children refused to let either of them go, wanting to play for a while longer.

The dorm floor was wood. Jiang Qing and Lin Xun settled down near the window, surrounded by children.

The girls had already gone to bed. This was a gathering of men.

One small but very earnest young man said, "Jiang Qing-gege, I want a bedtime story."

A whole group of very entitled little people.

Jiang Qing looked at them impassively. "What kind of story?"

"Sleeping Beauty!"

"Sleeping Beauty? At your age you're already thinking about things like that? There's no future for you."

Lin Xun let out a suppressed laugh.

The boy quickly reconsidered. "Then how about the Little Mermaid?"

"Half fish, half girl? That's not a princess. That's a monster. The kind that eats disobedient little boys who ask for bedtime stories."

A chorus of small voices: "Waaaaa."

Lin Xun was laughing hard enough to hit the floor.

Jiang Qing shot him a flat look. Lin Xun straightened up and said, "Do you not know any stories?"

"No." Jiang Qing, for once, was honest about it.

"What did you listen to when you were small?"

"Scripts." Jiang Qing said, resigned. "My mom loved films. The bedtime stories were all screenplays."

"That explains why you love acting so much. Early-stage immersion."

"And you? Don't tell me you grew up on Sleeping Beauty."

"No. I had the financial papers, science magazines, fashion weeklies, sheet music, medical journals, and various other things read to me."

"That many? What kind of extreme early education is that?" Jiang Qing had never felt better about his own childhood in that moment. Sure, it had been scripts, but compared to this, it was practically a holiday.

"Gege, I want a story," the boy wailed, with the full implication of we are not going to sleep until we get one.

Lin Xun patted his head. "I'll tell one. Everyone lie down."

The children celebrated and scrambled under their blankets, little eyes peeking out at the two adults by the window.

"Once upon a time there was a terrible dragon," Lin Xun began. "He was very ugly, and he had a great love of beautiful skirts."

Jiang Qing turned and looked at him with an expression that said please stop.

Lin Xun continued, untroubled. "The dragon's name was Shangguan·Milande·Kundera·Mingxi Xuan·Fenxue Wuying·Qianye Shang·Aotian. You may call him Little Wang Er."

Jiang Qing: ......

Children: "HAHAHAHAHAHA."

By the time the story ended, the children were more awake than before.

Jiang Qing shoved Lin Xun's outstretched leg with his foot. "Can you not tell something that will actually make them sleep? They're never going to settle down like this."

"Right, right." Lin Xun thought a moment, then started again with Sleeping Beauty, his voice low and unhurried, warm in tone, and within five minutes a number of children were already asleep, though they hadn't even registered it was Sleeping Beauty he was telling.

Because Lin Xun had told it entirely in English.

Jiang Qing: ...

I take everything back. That was genius.

At that point a small creature came crawling from somewhere near his feet. Xiao Jiu worked his way along Jiang Qing's leg, climbed into his lap, played there for a bit, then rolled over to Lin Xun instead.

Lin Xun patted the small back gently, glancing at Jiang Qing as he did so. The two of them looked at each other and, slowly, smiled.

Then Lin Xun kept quietly coaxing the children to sleep. After some time, Xiao Jiu finally stilled.

He stood, carried the boy back to his bed, and when he came back, found Jiang Qing with his head drooping forward, nodding off.

Moonlight fell through the window and lay flat across the floor, and Jiang Qing was sitting half in shadow.

A second later, Jiang Qing's head pitched forward.

Lin Xun reached over quickly and caught his face, then settled in beside him and shifted Jiang Qing's head carefully onto his own shoulder.

The texture of skin beneath his fingers was distracting. He hadn't been able to stop himself touching it.

He told himself not to. He already felt like something was wrong with him. But he didn't want to move his hand.

May as well deserve the hitting, he thought. Worth it.

But Jiang Qing didn't wake, possibly because of how tired the day had left him.

He traced his thumb lightly along Jiang Qing's jaw. Tilted his head and looked at the sleeping face from close up. Brushed back a strand of hair that had fallen across his cheek. Then his gaze caught, without his meaning it to, on the curve of a mouth.

Thin. Pink.

Looking at it, a thought formed that it might taste like something good.

He was turning into someone genuinely depraved, he realized.

He had the slightly perverse urge to know what would actually wake Jiang Qing up. Without quite meaning to, he pressed the pad of his thumb against the corner of that mouth, lightly. Jiang Qing didn't stir.

He really had passed out cold.

Lin Xun smiled at that, and then the smile faded into something steadier, and he kept his eyes on the mouth, not moving.

The light in the room wasn't bright. Even so, the dim glow of the moon seemed to pick out the outline of it with almost inconvenient clarity.

He wasn't sure what possessed him. But he bent down and pressed his lips to his own thumb, where it still rested at the corner of Jiang Qing's mouth.

Only a finger's breadth between them.

Then something in his chest struck a note so loud it nearly woke the room.

He pulled his head back sharply. He drew his hand back to himself, and his fingertips felt like they were barely keeping from burning.

After that, he didn't move again. He stared at the shadows on the floor.

He sat quietly listening to the soft breathing close to his ear, the warmth of it against his neck, and thought: this is actually intolerable.

He slipped his phone out and took a photo of the two shadows leaning against each other on the floor, then shifted the lens and took a blurred shot of the sleeping face.

A record of a heart gone off-rhythm.

He steadied himself, checked the time, and simply picked Jiang Qing up.

On the stairs down, Jiang Qing half-stirred, and his hand found its way around Lin Xun's neck of its own accord.

Lin Xun went rigid where he stood and didn't move for a moment.

The night was completely still. Wind moved through the branches of the wutong tree, a soft, dry brushing sound.

The east building where they were staying was across the courtyard. By the time he'd reached the middle of the open space, the person in his arms opened his eyes.

Jiang Qing blinked slowly. First he saw the moon hanging in the sky. Then a pair of eyes that held something in them the night couldn't quite name.

chapters.title: Partners
chapters.content:
Their eyes met. Neither of them spoke. Something moved in the space between them, a quiet, hidden current.

Lin Xun's throat moved. His whole body had gone very still. He watched Jiang Qing part his lips, and waited with his pulse held.

"You two are still not asleep?"

The door of the west building swung open. Sang Yi stood in the doorway, looking at them.

Jiang Qing came back to himself, dropped down from Lin Xun's arms, and walked ahead without looking back, though not before shooting Lin Xun a look over his shoulder.

Lin Xun turned back to Sang Yi and smiled. "Almost. Good night."

"Mm." Sang Yi went back inside, with a lingering sense that what she'd just walked in on was familiar in the specific way that scenes from television were familiar: man holding woman, leaning in, about to kiss.

She shook the image out of her head and opened her game, resolving to play a few rounds and then sleep. Just a few.

But her performance in the first round was off, and her teammates were harsh about it.

She'd been about to mute the voice channel when someone on the enemy team spoke up for her: "Come on, are you serious right now? You're blaming your own people? You play like garbage and then turn on your teammate? I'd rather have the mystery player on my team. Hey, was that a guy or a girl? Come join us, we'll go wreck these clowns together!"

Sang Yi blinked, uncertain. She said tentatively: "Yang-shushu?"

The voice on the other end went very still. "Yi Yi?"

"...Yes."

"I..." Yang Meng was about to say something, but Sang Yi's teammates cut him off.

"Little sister?! She sounds sweet! Hey Xiao Mei, come queue with us, we'll carry you!"

Sang Yi left the group and immediately received an invite from Yang Meng. She accepted. His laugh came through, warm and easy. "Come on, niece. Your uncle and you together, we'll dominate this canyon!"

Sang Yi: ...... Why is Xun-ge's friend like this?

Inside a villa somewhere in the capital, the door to an opulent bathroom opened. A woman with striking looks stepped out in sleepwear that left very little to the imagination, all soft curves and deliberate angles.

She moved to the living room and pressed herself against the man who was deep in a game, soft as water.

"Don't," Yang Meng said, eyes on the screen. He turned off the voice channel. "I didn't call you over."

The woman reached for his phone and closed the game. "Yang Meng. Is this what I came here for?"

"Give it back." Yang Meng rubbed his brow, and the warmth in his voice dropped several degrees. "Mu Ning. When did I ever say I liked you?"

"Yang Meng!" Mu Ning's carefully composed features fractured slightly. She pulled herself back, held it together, and asked in a cold, controlled tone, "What exactly is your relationship with Lin Xun? Why is he opening a studio directly above Ruian?"

Yang Meng's brow creased. His voice went sharp. "What exactly do you want to know?"

Mu Ning felt a flicker of fear behind his look, then reminded herself that he still had some feeling for her. Six months together, and he'd never sought anyone else's company, and had more or less given her what she asked for.

That gave her some courage. "I want to open a studio of my own."

"Mu Ning." Yang Meng picked up his phone, got up, and crossed to the door. "I don't need you tonight. You can go."

Mu Ning's expression went through several shades. She felt humiliated, and also afraid.

She let it drop. She stood and dressed slowly in front of him, watching for any reaction. Yang Meng said nothing.

She put on a serene expression as she reached the door and touched his face lightly, hoping he'd ask her to stay.

He did speak. "Don't come by for a while."

"Because I don't like Lin Xun?" Mu Ning went pale.

Yang Meng said nothing further and showed her out.

Lin Xun's identity wasn't fully out in the open, and he didn't feel like explaining.

He picked the game back up, but by then the niece had already gone offline.

Back at the orphanage, Jiang Qing and Lin Xun had both washed up and were in the room.

It was a small space, two narrow beds pushed along opposite walls, college-dormitory sized. The sheets smelled like sunshine and clean linen.

Both of them lay down, and the room went quiet.

After some time, Jiang Qing opened his eyes and stared at the wall.

He couldn't settle.

Every time he closed his eyes, the image came back: being carried, in someone's arms. He'd meant to be annoyed about it, but then he'd remembered that his own hand had found its way around the man's neck, and that knocked most of the indignation out of him.

He sat up quietly, wanting a cigarette, and patted his pockets. Nothing. He'd lost track of where he'd put it.

Happy moments and relaxed ones tended to make the cigarettes disappear.

He turned toward the window, pulled the curtain aside a little, and pushed it open a crack.

The night air hit his face, cool and clarifying.

"Can't sleep?" The voice from the other bed came without warning.

He paused, and nodded. "I'm not used to it."

"Not used to sleeping here?" Lin Xun sat up too, and opened the window fully, turning on the bedside lamp.

"No. Not used to sleeping with someone else in the room."

Lin Xun's first thought, immediate and unbidden, was that this was not encouraging news. Then he caught himself and reversed course. "Then I'll go wait outside until you fall asleep."

Jiang Qing saw him already getting up and reaching for his shoes, actually about to do it, and stopped him. "You don't have to. I'll just stay awake until I wear out."

Lin Xun stopped, sighed, and came to sit on the edge of Jiang Qing's bed. "No need to suffer like that. Here, I'll tell you a story."

"......" Jiang Qing said. "Maybe you should go wait outside after all."

Lin Xun laughed under his breath, then with firm, decisive hands found Jiang Qing's arms and guided him back under the covers. Jiang Qing, unexpectedly, didn't resist at all. He lay back without protest.

Lin Xun started in. "Supersymmetry is a symmetry between fermions and bosons; the two differ fundamentally in their basic physical properties. In supersymmetric theories, every fundamental particle is matched with a corresponding supersymmetric partner..."

Jiang Qing: ......

"...In supersymmetric theories, every fundamental particle has a corresponding superpartner with which it is paired..." Lin Xun continued, patient and low-voiced. Before long, the sound of steady breathing told him the matter had been settled.

He allowed himself a quiet smile, then reached over and scratched lightly under Jiang Qing's chin, his voice dropping to a murmur with the faint warmth of a laugh behind it. "Good night."

Once the breathing was even and undisturbed, Jiang Qing turned over in the dark.

His eyes opened in the blackness.

What the hell. What's with the scratching? Do friends do that to each other? Can someone with actual friends please come explain this to him?

He rubbed the spot that had been scratched. No stubble. Nothing.

On the other bed, Lin Xun kept his expression to himself and lay in silence.

The next morning, Jiang Qing was roused by the rhythmic sound of "left, right, left, right" coming from outside. He went to the window and looked down. Lin Xun and Sang Yi were in the courtyard below leading the children in laps.

The smell of breakfast drifted over from the kitchen. Dean Sang was crouched in front of the kitchen door brushing his teeth.

A moment later, someone came to stand beside him.

"Up early, are you." Dean Sang glanced over at Jiang Qing, who was brushing his teeth as well, and then looked back out at Lin Xun below. "That friend of yours is good. Excellent looking, good temperament. I approve."

"Mm." Jiang Qing gave a noncommittal answer and watched the movement in the courtyard.

Lin Xun had on a short-sleeved shirt and shorts. With the herd of short figures around him for contrast, he looked even more disproportionately tall than usual. He was shouting the cadence with real spirit, making a point of tapping hands with each child as they passed.

The formation had long since stopped resembling anything orderly. Really it was just Lin Xun running, and a cluster of admirers chasing him.

"Youth," Dean Sang said, nostalgic. Then he lowered his voice and, with the expression of someone who had been sitting on this for a while, asked, "So, does your friend have someone?"

"Probably not." Since the two of them had become neighbors, Jiang Qing had never seen Lin Xun bring anyone home or mention anyone.

Dean Sang's eyebrows lifted meaningfully. "Good. Very good. What do you think of him for Yi Yi?"

Jiang Qing inhaled wrong and nearly spat out a mouthful of toothpaste foam. He looked up to find a pair of feet in front of him, shoe tops flecked with the same foam.

He looked slowly upward. Lin Xun looked back at him.

"Sorry," Jiang Qing said, caught.

Lin Xun ruffled his hair, turned around, and went back to running laps with the children.

"You little brat," Jiang Qing called after him.

"Haha," Dean Sang laughed. "I suppose peers really do get along best. You and me and Yi Yi never cut loose the way you two do."

"Who's cutting loose with him? He's just immature."

"Ha, hard to say who's more immature. But immature's good, it means you've let your guard down a little."

"Hmph."

After breakfast, Lin Xun noticed Jiang Qing was nowhere to be seen. He asked Sang Yi, who told him Jiang Qing had gone back to his grandfather's house.

Jiang Qing made the trip every time he came to Wutong Village. He never brought anyone along.

He was back within two hours, and just as he walked through the gates he heard the piano.

He stood in the doorway of the music room, watching. The instruments had been arranged and set up. A man sat in front of the piano. His clothes were casual, and his eyes were closed, but there was something in his posture and the way he moved that made it feel like watching a performance.

The white curtains lifted in the breeze and settled, not disturbing the man at the keys at all. He was playing slowly, humming along under his breath.

Then his eyes opened. He looked at the children gathered around him and smiled. His gaze moved, caught the figure in the doorway, and that smile deepened. The tempo picked up, and he called out without ceremony, "Welcome home."

"Jiang Qing-gege's back!" Several children rushed over to pull him inside, dragging him to stand beside the piano.

Lin Xun finished the piece with a flourish, looked up brightly. "We're in the middle of a lesson. Want to sit in?"

Jiang Qing raised an eyebrow. "Sure."

For the rest of the afternoon, Jiang Qing sat beside the piano, listening to Lin Xun teach the basics and keeping an eye on the children to make sure they weren't getting out of hand.

Some of them, unable to follow along, began pressing keys at random.

Just like them, Jiang Qing thought. Good thing these are electronic.

Then Lin Xun's head turned toward Xiao Wu. He listened for a moment, an expression crossing his face, and went over to her. Jiang Qing followed.

A few seconds later, the two men looked at each other with the same quiet recognition.

Xiao Wu might be what Dean Sang had meant by "the one with a gift."

"Xiao Wu, do you like piano?"

"I love it," Xiao Wu said. "It's magical. It makes me happy."

"What kind of happy?"

Xiao Wu thought seriously. "The kind where I forget about my leg!"

Lin Xun ruffled her hair, warm and unhurried. "God gave you an artist's hands. You have to treasure that, you know."

Xiao Wu pursed her lips. Not really following.

Jiang Qing put it plainly: "It means your hands are how you make money and find your handsome husband."

Xiao Wu's eyes went wide with excitement.

Lin Xun: ...... Female hearts are not that hard to read, actually, once you know the formula.

The two of them talked it over and landed on piano lessons: plenty of programs available in the city, and there were options in the capital too, with Sang Yi there to keep an eye on things.

Lin Xun suggested the Zhu Li Piano Arts Center.

Zhu Li was a well-regarded concert pianist with a modest international profile who had performed at notable venues and for various dignitaries. She was rarely in the country, away almost constantly for engagements.

But the name was enough. The center was expensive; it was also known for producing results.

Jiang Qing had no objections. Proximity to home made logistics manageable.

When they shared the plan with Dean Sang and Sang Yi, both were visibly pleased.

Xiao Wu did not take the news as well. She cried and said she didn't want to go. Then Jiang Qing mentioned that the capital had many handsome men, and she said maybe seeing the wider world wasn't the worst idea after all. A person couldn't stay in one place forever.

"Dean Sang, maybe ease up on the television a bit," Jiang Qing said.

"Haha, she barely watches. What she watches is mostly your films."

"That's even worse. I've played a teenage murderer."

"......" The Dean's smile froze. He'd forgotten about that one.

When it was time to go, the children clung to both of them and cried themselves dramatic. Lin Xun took them all to buy snacks, which cured the separation anxiety immediately.

Jiang Qing handed Sang Yi a card. "For the Dean. Tell him it's your wages, so he takes it and goes to the doctor."

Sang Yi looked at him with quiet gratitude. "I'll work hard."

"Less gaming."

"I'll work very hard!" The gaming stays. That's non-negotiable.

"......"

Back in the capital, Lin Xun went straight to the company to deal with something Yang Meng had called about.

Jiang Qing took both kids to register at the arts center. They offered recreational and professional tracks. The professional track was three times the cost, but included full residential enrollment.

"Do you actually want to commit to this?" Jiang Qing asked Xiao Wu.

"No."

Same stubborn streak as Sang Yi.

Fine. Professional track it was.

After paying, he tucked the receipt into Xiao Wu's pocket and told her, "I'm lending this to you. Learn properly. I'm keeping a record, and one day you're going to pay me back with interest."

"Okay!"

Shu Tong heard they'd brought a child back and came to see. She found the girl simply dressed, took her and Xiao Yi and her own son out for a shopping trip.

Jiang Qing wasn't suited for a family excursion. He was heading home to prepare for the final recording.

But first, one thing needed to be handled.

He drove to the building that housed Ruian, but didn't go to Ruian itself. He went to the floor above.

Only one company occupied this level, clean and freshly fitted, the design bold and full of light. Just looking at it put you in a better mood.

The main door was open. Voices inside: Lin Xun and Yang Meng, and, he could tell even before seeing, someone else.

He hadn't gotten a clear look yet when Lin Xun spotted him and looked pleasantly surprised. "You're here?"

"Came to see for myself."

"Perfect timing. Let me show you around." Lin Xun pulled him in a different direction, pointing out the layout and setup of the space. "Satisfied?"

Jiang Qing let his gaze travel, then looked at Lin Xun. "It'll do."

Which was high praise, and Lin Xun knew it. "Three days are up. Is that your answer?"

Jiang Qing looked around once more, then said directly, "I'll join your studio. But I want to invest and come in as a partner."

Lin Xun paused. "A partner?"

Jiang Qing knew Lin Xun didn't need the money. But he also knew he didn't want to be a signed artist again.

After going over every option, investing for a share of ownership was the one that made the most sense.

If Lin Xun refused, he'd have to look elsewhere.

"Yes." Lin Xun said it without hesitation.

Jiang Qing was mildly surprised. "You're not going to think it over?"

"I've thought about it thoroughly."

Three seconds? That was thorough?

Lin Xun's expression broke into a smile. "If you're a partner, you'll be more invested. That's exactly what I want."

A bond that went deeper than being neighbors.

Partners. It had a good sound to it.

And a contract. Their names, side by side on the same document.

"You really thought this through," Lin Xun said, smiling so wide his eyes disappeared into it.

Jiang Qing blinked. If he'd known Lin Xun would agree this easily, why had he spent so many days rehearsing arguments?

chapters.title: A QQ Burner Account
chapters.content:
The two of them were talking when Yang Meng walked over with someone else in tow.

"What are you two chatting about?" Yang Meng asked.

"Jiang Qing agreed to join the studio." Lin Xun smiled, visibly pleased.

"Really?"

"And he wants to invest for a stake in it."

Yang Meng's eyes went wide. "You agreed? You actually agreed? I begged you so many times and you wouldn't budge! You have no heart!"

Jiang Qing found this hard to believe, and pretended not to hear.

"Fine, I agree, I agree." Lin Xun said.

"You seem thrilled about it." Yang Meng said, unamused.

"So are you putting money in or not?"

"Yes, yes."

Lin Xun smiled slightly, then moved on to business, introducing the unfamiliar man beside them. "This is Guan Jingshan, a high school classmate of Yang Meng's. He used to work at an advertising company and is now joining the studio as a talent manager. I mentioned before that Yang Meng has a professional team handling my resources and fan management. That's Guan Jingshan. Mm...... why are you looking at me like that?"

Jiang Qing had been stunned from the first moment he laid eyes on Guan Jingshan. He knew this person, and this was precisely who had become Lin Xun's manager in his past life.

He had never been a talent manager before, but his methods were formidable, with broad resources and connections, and he and Lin Xun had been a golden partnership.

Jiang Qing suddenly felt that this gamble had paid off.

Lin Xun found his expression a little too enthusiastic, and watched him reach out and shake Guan Jingshan's hand on his own initiative. "Hello, I'm Jiang Qing."

"Hello. I've watched your films, they're excellent." Guan Jingshan said. "Though the scripts you've taken on these past couple of years have been a bit lacking. What's the reason for that?"

"Constraints." Jiang Qing said.

"That's not uncommon. Actors often can't get the scripts or roles they want." Guan Jingshan said with understanding, and the two of them fell into their own conversation as though no one else was around.

Lin Xun stepped imperceptibly between the two of them and cut in with a casual remark. "Guan Jingshan has a partner."

Jiang Qing: ?

What of it?

Lin Xun added, "A girlfriend."

Guan Jingshan: ?

Is there some problem with that?

"Carry on." Lin Xun retreated sheepishly from their perfectly cordial exchange and drooped his head to look out the window.

A weight settled suddenly on his shoulder. He looked over with a small flicker of hope, saw it was Yang Meng, and his face fell again.

"Come on, little junior, you've just found a new collaborator and you're already giving me the cold shoulder?" Yang Meng said.

Lin Xun's brow creased slightly. "Let's redraft the contracts, and we can also start hiring employees officially."

"What about a company name? Just call it Lin Xun Studio?"

"No." Lin Xun glanced briefly at Jiang Qing. "Ask my business partner."

"Lazy to the bone, aren't you." Yang Meng turned away and went to chat with the other two.

Lin Xun checked his phone and saw a new message, from Du Yuening.

The two of them had exchanged WeChat contacts at the television station backstage last time, with her saying she'd send him some photos.

She had sent several dozen in one go, every single one of them featuring him and Jiang Qing, some taken openly, others candid shots.

He saved them all one by one and sent her a thank-you emoji.

Du Yuening: You're welcome, good luck at the grand finale!!!

Lin Xun smiled slightly. Noticing that Du Yuening seemed to have a particular fondness for him and Jiang Qing, he went ahead and asked on a whim, "Could you help me think of a name? Jiang Qing and I are opening a studio together."

Du Yuening: !!!

More sweetness incoming?!

The mentor-and-student relationship has leveled up directly to business partners!

That's such a monumental leap forward, it's basically the same as getting married!

It needs a great name!!!

Du Yuening squeezed her brain dry for a good while before finally arriving at one supremely perfect name.

Du Yuening: What about "Jiang Xun Fang Zhen" (Into the River, a Sturgeon)! The sea is wide for fish to leap, and the sky is vast for birds to fly free. Your studio is like a great sturgeon finally returning to the river and sea, swimming wherever it pleases, the future boundless and limitless!

Lin Xun: [Thumbs up]

Then he sent her a thank-you red envelope for 8,888 yuan.

Du Yuening excitedly tapped to collect it. Oh my goodness, does getting married also come with such a big red envelope! On behalf of your humble servant, I wish you a hundred years of happiness!

"How are the discussions going?" Lin Xun walked over to ask. Yang Meng shook his head. "Jiang Qing said whatever, and I suggested Hongqiang, and he still wouldn't have it!"

Lin Xun laughed. "I have a name. A naming master came up with it."

"Let's hear it." Yang Meng said.

Lin Xun had just opened his mouth when Jiang Qing's phone suddenly rang.

Jiang Qing stepped to one side to take the call. Shu Tong said over the phone, "Little Five has been taken back to the center. The little girl is quite endearing. I also picked up two sets of clothes for you while I was out. Are you home right now?"

"No. Head home first, wait...... actually." Jiang Qing glanced around the room. "I'll send you the address. Come here right now, I have something to talk to you about."

After hanging up, he heard Yang Meng let out a laugh, thought it over, and stepped forward proactively. "Shouldn't we talk through the contracts?"

In the bright open office, Yang Meng called the legal department upstairs from the floor below, and everyone sat together to discuss the terms of the new contracts.

Before long, Shu Tong came rushing over in a hurry, and only relaxed when she saw that Jiang Qing looked entirely unfazed.

Jiang Qing led her around on a tour, explaining his idea about the partnership.

Shu Tong let out a breath too small to detect, and after thinking it over, decided it wasn't a bad choice at all.

"Tong-jie, I'll sell you a small stake. Do you dare buy it?"

Shu Tong blinked, staring at him for a long moment, speechless.

She had worked for so many years, representing only one artist for the entire stretch of it. Although she had earned quite a bit in the early days, her income had clearly declined in the years since.

Jiang Qing had always assumed it was because she only managed one artist. In truth, it wasn't. She also had a family.

The life of a manager was already hectic. Handling one artist could keep you running flat out without a moment to spare. Taking on more would make it even harder to give her family the time they needed.

She was at an age now where she sometimes felt a creeping dissatisfaction with how things had gone.

Her earlier encouragement of Jiang Qing to open a studio had in part been for her own sake, too, but if it hadn't worked out, there was nothing to be done about it.

She had never once brought it up, but Jiang Qing had seen it all and kept it in mind.

This was his way of giving her an opening.

"Are you sure?" she asked.

Jiang Qing said casually, "It's not like I'm short on money. I just want a company that doesn't restrict my development. But think it over carefully. This is no small amount."

Shu Tong smiled. "What's there to be afraid of? If I go bankrupt, surely you won't abandon your stepmother?"

"Hmph, that's not necessarily guaranteed." Jiang Qing led her into the office, where the lawyers had already worked out a rough plan and were asking him how large a stake he wanted.

After a lengthy discussion, they finally settled on the numbers. Jiang Qing's investment would account for 30%, Yang Meng for 10%, and Lin Xun would be responsible for the rest. Shu Tong, after calculating her own assets, purchased 3% of the equity from Jiang Qing's share.

Lin Xun had no objections to this. He happened to need someone to manage the talent management division, and Shu Tong had the seniority, the experience, and a solid network of contacts. More than anything, her character was reliable.

Having spent this long in the industry alongside Jiang Qing without picking up any of its worse habits was itself enough to put his mind at ease.

She did have one critical weakness, though. She was too soft-hearted, especially when it came to her own artists.

But that was fine. There was still Guan Jingshan, the merciless tyrant, to balance things out.

The general division of responsibilities was worked out after that. Lin Xun would manage the company's core operations, while Shu Tong and Guan Jingshan would oversee the talent and resources division.

Shu Tong would be in charge of film and television, while Guan Jingshan would handle fashion resources.

Yang Meng would remain as nominal general manager, and Jiang Qing would be the priority artist the company would develop.

A small but well-funded team was assembled just like that.

Even by the time he got home, Jiang Qing still found it hard to fully believe that he had just gone into business with his mortal enemy from his past life.

Everything he knew about Lin Xun came from vague impressions of that life and their day-to-day interactions now. He had never seen him manage a company before. Would it really be alright?

Was this all too flippant?

Perhaps the image of Jiang Huai, who had been busy from dawn to dusk with seasoned methods and not a trace of lightness about him, had left too strong an impression. Looking at Lin Xun with his unruffled, indifferent manner, he couldn't help feeling a little worried.

"You already run so many companies. Can you actually handle it?" he couldn't stop himself from asking.

"Why wouldn't I be able to?" Lin Xun said. "I don't need to be in the building to keep things running. That's what professional managers are for. In fact, I majored in business at university, and I've been scouting talent since then. I also borrowed quite a few employees from my father. His people are excellent."

Jiang Qing was left speechless, and found himself suddenly curious. "If I may ask, just who is your esteemed father?"

Lin Xun: "Want to come see for yourself?"

"No time. Oh right, the grand finale of 'The Actor' is coming up. How's your preparation going?"

"Very well. I've prepared a good mindset." Lin Xun received a well-deserved eye roll in return, then asked, "Do you think I can win?"

Honestly speaking, probably not. But as a mentor, Jiang Qing felt it was his duty to give the person a little confidence. "Of, of course! In my heart, you are the best, the be... best of all! Keep it up, keep, keep it up!"

"Give me some specifics. What exactly is so good about me?"

Jiang Qing's fist tightened.

There was still a lot to do with the studio, but the most pressing matter for now was the upcoming grand finale of "I Am an Actor."

Lin Xun received word from the production team that they would be coming to his place to deliver the script and conduct a brief interview.

It was scheduled for the morning three days before filming, and on that day, Jiang Qing was woken up by hunger.

His morning temper flared instantly. He stomped to the door with the fury of a demon, then came to an abrupt stop.

Had he somehow gotten used to eating someone else's breakfast?

That was not right.

He counted the days and realized the production team was coming today. He might well be walking into an interview.

He rubbed his stomach, opened the refrigerator door, and found, as always, nothing but drinks.

Having apparently grown so accustomed to being fed, the refrigerator no longer held a single thing that could fill a stomach.

Without even noticing, he had somehow become habituated to mooching off someone else's meals.

After washing up, he was about to head out for breakfast when the production team called.

The producer explained that since the crew was already out anyway, they may as well interview him too, and since he and Lin Xun were in the same complex, it was convenient.

Jiang Qing: "......" Why didn't you say so sooner!

He strongly suspected the producer had done this on purpose.

At that moment, a staff member standing in the corridor called Jiang Qing. "Hello, Teacher Jiang, we're done with Lin Xun's interview. Would it be alright to come to your place now?"

The moment those words left her mouth, she heard the door next to her open, and the phone audio and the sound from behind her rang out simultaneously. "I'm right here."

Staff member: !!!

While she stood there in shock, Lin Xun stepped out, and right in front of her and the camera operator, handed the bag he was carrying to Jiang Qing. "Didn't get a chance to give this to you just now. Eat it while it's warm." Then he went back into his room, and gave the staff member a polite smile on his way in.

Staff member: !!!

What on earth! Was it always this obvious?! She had been corrupted by Du Yuening's influence and was now reading romance into everything herself!

Jiang Qing sat at the table, opened the bag, and said, "You don't mind if I eat first, right?"

"Of course not, we can film while you eat. Very relatable content."

"Up to you." He didn't quite understand what was worth filming about someone eating breakfast. He ate a few bites of a steamed bun, and when he no longer felt so hungry, remembered what had just happened. "That scene of us passing the breakfast through the door, cut that out."

"Why?" the staff member asked instinctively.

"Because it doesn't look great. I'm in my loungewear, and it wouldn't make for good viewing when broadcast, and there's no real need for it either. Don't you think?" Jiang Qing gave her a warm smile.

A beauty attack right to the face!

This job was incredible. A fresh morning with two beautiful men sighted in one go. What incredible luck.

The interview itself was straightforward. Give an evaluation of the remaining two team members, Lin Xun and Liu Huimin, then do a video call with each of them and offer some encouragement.

After saying his piece to Liu Huimin, Jiang Qing, under the staff member's wide-eyed and excited stare, made a video call to Lin Xun.

The other person picked up instantly, and a face of clean, sharp-edged beauty appeared on screen, truly flawless from every angle.

Jiang Qing felt a small pang of jealousy, glanced at his own appearance, and thought: even on the front camera with its mediocre resolution, these looks hold up just fine. Heh.

Lin Xun raised an eyebrow slightly, the corners of his eyes curving, and with perfectly easy familiarity asked, "Finished eating?"

"Mm." Jiang Qing's eye twitched, indicated that there were other people present, then swung the phone sideways for a moment. The staff member's silhouette flashed briefly on screen, and Lin Xun gave the faintest of nods.

"How's preparation going?"

"Not bad."

"Good luck."

"Okay."

Call ended.

"That's it? Is that really all?" The staff member couldn't believe it. "You talked with Liu Huimin for so long and even gave her pointers. Why didn't you say a few words to guide Lin Xun too?"

There was plenty of guidance, Jiang Qing retorted inwardly. That wretched Lin Xun came to him to study acting at every opportunity. He was supposed to be the boss now, and yet he was still here every day trying to poach his livelihood.

Of course none of this was appropriate to reveal right now, so all he said was, "I trust him. He won't disappoint me."

On the day of the official recording, Jiang Qing was on his way to the station while Lin Xun was already there doing his final rehearsal.

By this point, each mentor had two team members remaining. The six of them would be divided into two groups of three for a three-way performance showdown, after which each group would eliminate one contestant, leaving four to compete for the top three spots.

The first performance was Liu Huimin collaborating with two others in a Republic-era historical piece. Liu Huimin in a cheongsam had an exceptional quality about her, carrying real elegance.

The audience had finally discovered that this was a hidden gem of an actress. She could play dowdy, she could play vicious, and she could also be utterly captivating.

As Liu Huimin walked slowly to the center of the stage, Su Hongru suddenly noticed something about her posture that reminded him of Jiang Qing when he had played a woman before, and asked sideways, "Did you teach her that?"

"No." Jiang Qing hadn't expected it either. "She must have picked it up herself."

"Impressive. More feminine than you."

Jiang Qing laughed quietly.

The second performance was Lin Xun's spy thriller piece. He played a student who had studied abroad and returned home to meet with old friends, only to find that these old friends had suddenly begun speaking in veiled, pointed language, every sentence a probe, each one trying to draw information from the others, and each attempting to recruit this talented individual into their own organization.

Lin Xun portrayed the young man's spirited confidence with great skill, going from cheerfulness to suspicion at the dinner table, his expression gradually growing serious, until at last, with the old friends drawing their weapons on him, he remained entirely composed, and then reached under the table to produce a listening device, demanding to know who had planted it.

When the final round of eliminations came, Liu Huimin and Lin Xun had both made it through.

Jiang Qing had become the mentor with the most team members remaining.

This was something the audience hadn't anticipated. Even Su Hongru's powerhouse lineup had been whittled down to a single warrior, and yet Jiang Qing still had two players left on his team.

And one of them was a newcomer who had debuted as a domineering CEO in a romance drama, and the other was a female supporting actress who had spent years going nameless, and yet here they both were, having cut through round after round to reach this point.

The more you thought about it, the more unnerving it became.

Those who had been watching episode after episode, even those who had been in the audience at the venue, and even accounting for the element of luck in the groupings and scene selections here and there, had no choice but to acknowledge that these two had genuine ability.

And their strength hadn't been obvious from the start, which was exactly why Jiang Qing's team had been the least expected of all the championship contenders, making their current position all the more of a surprise.

If Liu Huimin had found a stage that suited her, one that finally let her shine with full force, then Lin Xun was an entirely different phenomenon altogether, operating in a terrifying upgrade mode all his own.

Attentive viewers could recall that in his very first performance, Lin Xun had been solid enough, not pulling anyone out of the scene, but nothing more. Yet from there, he had grown more and more at ease with each round, and even just now, going head to head with two seasoned veterans of real power, he had held his own, and at the moment of the final emotional peak, had taken full, steady, calm control of the entire stage.

Extraordinary. Truly extraordinary.

Su Hongru remarked, "Jiang Qing, you've genuinely given me a new perspective on you."

Those words were like a torch to a room full of people, and quite a few audience members immediately made the connection. It was because of Jiang Qing.

Jiang Qing had helped Liu Huimin discover a way to survive on this stage, and had guided Lin Xun through a masterclass approach to performance.

Lin Xun may have had natural talent, but without strong and proper guidance, it was very hard to achieve this level of transformation in such a short amount of time.

Jiang Qing, at the center of all this discussion, was completely unaware of what the audience was thinking. He was already heading backstage.

This was the mid-show break, and the remaining four contestants were making their way to the green room to prepare for the final performance of the night.

After long stretches of highly concentrated performance, both physical energy and emotional reserves had been depleted.

Lin Xun handed Liu Huimin a cup of water, and the two of them chatted for a while before Jiang Qing walked in, leaned against the makeup table, and said with a smile, "First, let me congratulate you both. Nervous about the performance coming up?"

Lin Xun: "Honestly..."

"Not nervous." Liu Huimin picked up where he started, and exchanged a smile with Lin Xun. "Getting to this point is already more than I could have hoped for. I'm happy."

Jiang Qing smiled too. "Good. Then just enjoy the stage for this last one. Keep your nerves steady. You've both already won."

They had barely rested before it was time to prepare for the final performance of the night.

Liu Huimin asked, "Jiang Qing, can I add you on WeChat?"

"Of course."

After they added each other, Liu Huimin started getting her makeup done and consulted him on some details of the upcoming performance, since what they were about to perform was "Old Friends."

Jiang Qing casually set his phone on the makeup table and moved to the seat beside Liu Huimin to chat with her.

Lin Xun glanced over at the two of them in the mirror, and just then the phone on the table in front of him lit up.

He reached out and pressed the screen to darken it, and in that instant, a bizarre group name flashed before his eyes.

A moment later the phone lit up again. New messages kept coming in, but the group name didn't change.

— Lin Zong's Lavender Garden No. 3.

This...... wasn't this his fan group?

Jiang Qing was in his fan group?

Jiang Qing was his fan?

By rough approximation, Jiang Qing liked him?

He didn't look at the messages any further. He got up and went to the restroom, sat on the toilet, heart pounding, and took out his phone to register a burner account, then entered "Garden No. 3."

Aside from an absolute avalanche of rainbow flattery, everyone was discussing tonight's recording, every single person cheering for him at full volume.

He opened the member list and first scanned through the male users, of whom there were very few, and whose messages didn't sound like Jiang Qing's voice at all.

He went back to the chat history and stared at the messages for a long time until his eyes were nearly crossing.

He checked the time. He needed to go get hair and makeup done soon. He was about to give up when suddenly a user with a hairclip avatar posted a photo of the two of them together.

He had seen this one before. It was one of the photos Du Yuening had sent him a few days ago.

No way.

Du Yuening, what have you done?

Du Yuening: "Don't worry everyone, with Jiang Laosi's help, Lin Zong is definitely going to take the championship!"

"Lin Zong is the best! Let's go girls!"

"Ahhh sis how do you always have so many photos! Any more? Let us have our fill all at once!"

"Stay on topic up there, this is the time to cheer Lin Zong on!"

"Jiang Qing will teach Lin Zong properly, right! I wonder if he actually likes Lin Zong. It looks like they have such a good relationship, but is it for the cameras or is he genuinely helping? (Just curious, no other meaning)"

A few more messages scrolled past, and then one particular message caught his attention.

Little Matchgirl: He will, doesn't like!

Because the messages were coming in so fast, this one came across as completely non-sequitur, and nobody seemed to notice anything unusual.

Lin Xun's lips curved slightly, a flicker of amusement passing through his eyes.

Found you.

Little Matchgirl.

chapters.title: The Grand Finale
chapters.content:
Jiang Qing had sent one message in the fan group and left it at that. Ever since joining, he had taken the occasional peek, sometimes even dipping into the chat to pass the time. Lurking was a great hobby.

A moment later, Lin Xun finally returned to the makeup room.

Jiang Qing looked him up and down. "Took you that long. Constipated?"

Lin Xun responded with a meaningful smile that made Jiang Qing's skin crawl.

While the performers were changing and getting their looks done, Jiang Qing wandered over to the director's area for a bit and exchanged a few words with the director.

"Old Friends" had a runtime of 156 minutes. The director's team had condensed the plot to 20 minutes, selecting several classic scenes as the key sequences, with props used to bridge and extend the timeline.

Su Hongru passed by and joined in, asking with a smile, "How are you feeling, Jiang Qing? Want to go up and perform it yourself?"

Jiang Qing waved the idea off. "No, no. I'm not that six-year-old child anymore."

"Ha ha, you could play a different role."

"Still, I'd rather not. Let it stay the way it is in my memory. That's enough. I don't want to go spending its sentiment." Jiang Qing said.

Su Hongru was quiet for a moment, and then gave him a firm clap on the shoulder. "Well said. I hope to have a work like that someday, something audiences love and actors hold dear."

"Teacher Su, you're still in your prime. The best years for a director come later in life. The older you get, the more depth you have, and the more of life you've seen, the more deeply your work can strike people."

"You really know how to make a person feel good, ha ha ha!" Su Hongru laughed, clapping him on the shoulder again.

"Those aren't my words, they were said by Old Master Guo Mingsheng." Jiang Qing smiled. "I pass them on to you. I look forward to even greater work from you."

"Alright, alright, I'll do my best." Su Hongru pulled him toward a corner and lowered his voice. "There's something I want to apologize to you about. At first, I didn't like you, because of the incident where you publicly criticized Yu Haoge."

"That was too rash of me." Jiang Qing said.

"No, I was generalizing unfairly. He and I are both directors, and honestly, I don't think I could have swallowed that either. You were a bit hasty about it, you know. The way you caused that scene scared off quite a few directors."

"I know." Jiang Qing laughed at himself.

"But having spent this time together, I've come to quite like you." Su Hongru clapped him on the shoulder again, seeming to come to a significant decision, and had just opened his mouth when the director behind them suddenly called out, "Teacher Su, Jiang Qing, we're ready to start recording."

"Coming." Jiang Qing called back, then turned to Su Hongru. "Was there something else, Teacher Su?"

"No, I'll find you for a proper chat when there's time. Make sure you set time aside for me."

"No problem. Right now what I have most of is time."

The audience was seated. The performers were ready.

This was the final recording session. Everyone had gathered themselves, ready to witness this last great performance together.

As the curtain rose, the hauntingly beautiful theme from "Old Friends" began to play. Then, with a sharp click, the music cut off.

A young and beautiful woman appeared at the center of the stage, wearing a Western-style little dress, her hair set in the most fashionable curls of the era. Her hand rested on a gramophone, and she said to the men and women dancing around her with mischievous charm, "This song doesn't sound nice. Let's change the music."

After she changed the record, she wove through the center of the dance floor like a sprite, her movements graceful and lively, impossible not to love.

The actress playing her was Teacher Wen Jiaxin's contestant, portraying the younger twin sister.

Fan Ling and Fan Li were a pair of twins, the celebrated socialite sisters of Shanghai.

The elder sister was composed and refined, fond of literature and the arts, known as a talented woman of Jiangnan.

The younger was spirited and vivacious, a social butterfly, and the toast of Shanghai.

At nineteen, the elder sister Fan Ling went abroad to study, and Fan Li saw her off at the pier. The two of them talked about when they would see each other again, never guessing that this parting would stretch into decades.

War broke out, and Fan Li followed her family northward to seek refuge with relatives in the northeast, but became separated from them along the way and was left entirely on her own.

After much hardship she finally managed to exchange letters with the relatives, only to be told that her family had been on the train that was bombed.

With nowhere to turn, she was rescued by the young son of a wealthy family, and became his wife.

After marriage, the husband's worse qualities came to light. He was ignorant, coarse, and hot-tempered, but he doted on her.

Her airs as a pampered young lady earned the mother-in-law's contempt, but her husband protected her.

Things went on this way for a few years, until the family caught wind of the land reforms and made the drastic decision to give away all their assets, becoming entirely impoverished peasants, and in doing so escaped disaster.

Fan Li, who had known only comfort and luxury from childhood, began a life of labor. At first she complained and wept, yearning for the lavish world of Shanghai she had known, but after her tears were spent, there was nothing to do but keep working.

And so, little by little with the passing days, she forgot the graceful dance steps she once knew, and remembered only how to swing a hoe with the least effort, how to calculate crop yields and work points, how to stretch the family rations and how to keep up with the children's schooling.

As her figure began to change, as her once-porcelain skin grew ever closer in color to the earth, as lines appeared at the corners of her eyes, she would sit often among the corn rows and tell her children to study hard, to be as accomplished as their aunt, to go abroad for their education, to find a good life for themselves.

The sister Fan Ling, whom she had envied, had indeed fared better. She had studied abroad and married a foreigner, but due to their different cultural backgrounds, the marriage ended in divorce two years later.

When she wanted to return home, domestic conflict had broken out, and she couldn't reach her relatives. Only her younger sister wrote letters urging her not to come back for the time being.

She later married a Chinese-descended supervisor, and the two of them were inseparable, sharing an intimate intellectual bond.

She also wrote a book, recording their love story, and under the influence of the foreign culture around her, it boldly documented their intimate life. The book even won an award.

The two of them had no children, believing a child to be merely the consequence of physical intimacy, and since they had already found joy in that intimacy, they saw no reason to seek the additional consequence.

The two of them lived freely and happily until her mother-in-law fell gravely ill and her husband's career suffered setbacks. Around that time, the war at home had ended and peace had finally come, so the two of them decided to return to China.

The mother-in-law's one dying wish was to hold a grandchild. After long and bitter argument, the couple finally had a son.

After the mother-in-law passed, Fan Ling became a high school teacher in her area. She had also reestablished correspondence with her long-estranged sister, and since the child was barely a month old and she couldn't travel, they made plans to spend the new year together at the end of the year.

Then an unforeseen catastrophe struck. Her home was raided. Every collection of poems and fiction she had preserved was burned. That award-winning book was put on public display, and she was spat upon, the name of "loose woman" fastened to her in humiliation.

But she had nowhere to cry out. She could not weep, or it would mean surrender.

The cattle pen and the shaved head became the recurring nightmares of her daily existence, and her child grew bigger, and the sound of his crying in the night grew louder.

One night she woke in the small hours and wept with a raw, tearing grief, holding her husband's thin and bony body in her arms.

The next morning, her husband took his own life.

Fan Li received a letter from her sister, insisting she must come see her.

She set out with a basket of flour borrowed from a neighbor, walked five days' worth of road, and arrived at five-thirty in the morning in the grey-light before dawn.

What she had not expected to find was her sister's cold body, lying in the cattle pen.

A beauty of her generation had perished, laid out in a filthy heap of stench, the woman who had loved romance and pursued perfection swallowed up by it.

She was gone, but in her arms she still held a sleeping child of five or six years old.

Fan Li broke into tears, the sound startling the child, who had not moved.

The child was still alive. He pushed himself up, rubbed his eyes, nudged Fan Ling's motionless body, and called out in a hoarse little voice, "Mama, time to get up."

Fan Li's tears burst free. She stepped forward and took the child in her arms. "There, there. From now on I'm your mama. I've come to take you home."

The child looked at the woman who was the image of his mother, and said nothing.

Fan Li held him and walked away, her steps heavy and slow. The child lay over her shoulder, staring back with fixed eyes at the figure growing further and further away, as the faintest hint of dawn began to break at the horizon.

The final shot of the film was a slow push-in on the child's face until it filled the entire frame, ending on a pair of bewildered, unseeing eyes.
