The child did not make a sound, looking into the lens in blank silence, and then a single tear fell.

What the child saw was never shown directly, but the space left open was enough to resonate with every audience member. Everything that had been suppressed for most of the film was released at last through one child's tear.

This ending was handled beautifully, leaving both a lingering grief and a depth of meaning.

What the child's eyes held, was it the sight of the old person now gone, or the sight of an entire old era now gone?

Perhaps both.

Jiang Qing had been asked this question many times before, and had also been asked how, at such a young age, he had managed the emotional shifts and expression control, and whether anyone had taught him anything of the sort. He had always just smiled and moved on, never giving a definitive answer.

Tonight's performance happened to feature exactly two men and two women: Liu Huimin as the elder sister Fan Ling, one of Su Hongru's team members, a forty-year-old powerhouse of a performer, as Fan Ling's husband, and Lin Xun as the husband of the younger sister Fan Li.

Both male performers did well. Jiang Qing watched Lin Xun's performance for a while, a deep smile settling in his eyes.

Having Lin Xun play this rakish young son of a wealthy family really was a piece of natural casting.

Add to that the way he doted on his wife, looking rough and a little bad on the outside while being soft on the inside, and the female viewers were going to love him.

The female performers, however, had a much harder time of it. Liu Huimin was older, and even with the support of her makeup, there was a slight incongruity to her playing the young Fan Ling.

The contrast with the other performer was even more stark. She had been captivating in the opening sequence playing a young girl, but as the years passed and the plot jumped rapidly forward in a short time, the psychological transitions and the physical shifts in manner weren't always keeping pace.

This made the sheer power of Teacher Ye Wu all the more apparent. She had been thirty when she performed this piece, playing both roles herself.

She had portrayed two young women with entirely opposite personalities with no trace of awkwardness. And the changes that each of the two main characters underwent across different times and different events were captured with precise exactness. A single look, a single small gesture, was all it took for the audience to know which character they were watching.

Ye Wu had also specifically learned two distinct speech patterns so that audiences could distinguish them by voice. The elder sister had a low, warm quality to her voice, the younger a sharp, bright, playful pitch. Later this extended to American English pronunciation and a northeastern Chinese accent.

The film covered a vast span of time, but told its story through a narrow lens, using the difficult lives of one pair of sisters to lay bare the lives of the "old people" of an entire era.

In that sense, it was Ye Wu who made the film what it was, and her death outside of it that elevated the film to an almost sacred status.

"Thank you to our performers for such a remarkable performance. How are you all feeling right now?" Du Yuening asked the performers onstage after the scene concluded.

Liu Huimin, with a light sweat on her face, said, "It wasn't easy. It really wasn't easy. This was a difficult piece, and I'm still struggling to quiet my emotions right now. I'm sorry, let me just take a moment."

Du Yuening gave the performers a moment to breathe, and said with a smile, "It really is an incredibly demanding piece. It's said that Teacher Ye Wu did everything herself when she performed this film. The dancing, the hoeing, the head-shaving, all without a stand-in. Truly admirable!"

With that, she looked toward the mentor's table. "Teacher Jiang also appeared in this film. Could you share something interesting from that time?"

Jiang Qing thought for a moment and said, "Mm...... Mama Ye Wu shaved her head and then suddenly ran into our green room to frighten us. Scared a few of us children to tears."

"Ha ha ha ha, so Teacher Ye Wu was quite the tease!" Du Yuening said laughingly. "I also heard there were six children at the time, and that you all called her Mama Ye Wu. Is that right?"

"Yes. We didn't have many scenes, but we were filming for a very long time. That final scene alone took seven or eight days, because they needed the light at around five or six in the morning. Mama Ye Wu was very kind to us, and after we'd been around long enough, we just started calling her what we called her in the script."

"As it happens, the date this episode airs is actually Teacher Ye Wu's birthday. We've also invited some old friends here tonight, to wish Teacher Ye together."

Jiang Qing looked toward the backstage area in startled disbelief, his eyes going wide.

The large doors opened, and five men and women walked out, greeting the audience.

Jiang Qing stood motionless for a moment before walking up to meet them, shaking hands one by one.

So many years had passed. These people had long since scattered across different fields and different walks of life. Some of them he could barely recognize. Only he was still drifting in and out of the entertainment world.

After Ye Wu's death, the parents of these children, afraid of being caught up in the fallout, had quickly had them withdraw from the industry. Among the parents, Jiang Huai had reacted with particular severity.

Each person shared something from their memories of filming, and spoke of how much they missed Ye Wu.

Afterwards, the large screen played photographs and videos of Ye Wu. After this tribute to the beloved screen legend, the program returned to the competition, and the voting began.

The audience vote came to a close, and the results appeared on the large screen.

Jiang Qing watched the numbers rise point by point, and felt, for once, a genuine flutter of nervousness and anticipation. When the numbers stopped, he quietly clenched his fist.

The audience broke into an uproar, followed immediately by thunderous applause.

"After round upon round of competition, we have finally selected the most outstanding performers to grace the stage of 'I Am an Actor.' Please join me in congratulating Duan Jiaxu, Lin Xun, and Liu Huimin!" Du Yuening led the applause. "Based on the final vote tallies, we will directly determine the champion, runner-up, and third place. First, congratulations to Liu Huimin, our third-place finisher, who receives the honor of 'Charismatic Performer.'"

Jiang Qing smiled and applauded, then looked toward Lin Xun. Their eyes met, and both smiled.

"Congratulations to Lin Xun, our runner-up, who receives the honor of 'Rising Star Performer.'"

Lin Xun accepted the trophy and flowers with gracious composure, and gave a wave in Jiang Qing's direction.

"Congratulations to Duan Jiaxu, who becomes the grand champion of 'I Am an Actor!'"

Duan Jiaxu was Su Hongru's team member, and his ability had always been formidable. The only thing that had held him back was the lack of standout work, but on this stage he had come into his full brilliance, and online he had already earned the reputation of a heavyweight talent.

Lin Xun, as a newcomer, had shattered the fixed impression everyone had of him as a pretty face with no substance, and vaulted in a single move to become the most respected of the trending stars in the eyes of the audience.

Including Liu Huimin, all three of them would find their path forward considerably easier from here.

"Duan Jiaxu, you're incredible!"

"Xun-ge, may your road be paved with flowers!"

"Liu Huimin, keep going!"

Amid the waves of cheering from the audience below, the recording officially wrapped.

The production team had arranged a closing dinner. A large table of fine food and wine was set up backstage, and everyone made their way in talking and laughing, then noticed there were still quite a few cameras, and knew this wasn't quite over.

Sure enough, Du Yuening began casually posing questions at the dinner table, and everyone had to eat while also keeping up with the host.

Du Yuening was seated beside Lin Xun and Jiang Qing. After wrapping up the questions she needed for the show, she covertly gave the lazy susan a spin, and a plate of boiled beef in spicy broth landed in front of Lin Xun. "Xun-ge, have some meat."

Lin Xun was just about to say something when Jiang Qing spun the turntable back without a second thought. "He doesn't eat spicy food."

Lin Xun looked at him with a long, searching look, and smiled. "That's right."

Du Yuening stared at Lin Xun's back turned toward her. On anyone else this would have been the most awkward thing in the world, but she was the founding member of the Lin-Jiang fan club!

Jiang Qing even knew Lin Xun didn't eat spicy food!

This was public dog-food feeding right in front of her face and she was absolutely living for it!

She couldn't let herself dwell on it. Too sweet, too sweet.

On the way back, Jiang Qing was quiet for a moment, then turned his head and said, "Congratulations."

"Thank you. And thank you for your guidance these past weeks." Lin Xun smiled, warmth brimming in his eyes. "I remember that when I asked you to teach me acting, you said you could ask for something in return, and you never did."

Jiang Qing thought for a while before remembering what had been said a month ago.

He had agreed offhand at the time. He hadn't given a single thought to what he might want in return.

"You're welcome to ask for anything. Whatever I can do, I'll agree to." Lin Xun said, with very strong implications.

Ask for anything! Even confessing right now would be fine!

Ever since learning that Jiang Qing was his fan, a heart that had been as still and quiet as standing water had begun to stir again, coming to life with new energy in the middle of what had otherwise been a dull and uneventful existence.

The other person surely had no idea that during the performance onstage just now, he had imagined who he had. He could win, and this little fan of his deserved half the credit. So asking for anything wasn't too much. Even asking for the person himself wouldn't be too much!

Jiang Qing watched Lin Xun looking at him with the eager eyes of a lapdog, and thought to himself: who exactly is the one making the demand here?

A moment later, meeting the other person's gaze, which carried a faint, barely concealed anticipation, he said, "I want you to be a little quieter."

"......"

Lin Xun was annoyed now, had taken a small sulk, had turned to look out the window and was refusing to acknowledge anyone.

Quite obedient, Jiang Qing thought, and then lowered his head to chat with his new friends.

He had just exchanged contacts backstage with those surprise guests, and everyone was sharing reminiscences, when a new notification came in on QQ.

[Little Mushroom Picking Girl] has sent you a friend request.

He opened it. Someone from Lin Xun's fan group.

An interesting name, with the same whimsical energy as his own Little Matchgirl.

The person immediately sent a sticker, a silly fan-made expression of Lin Xun.

[Little Mushroom Picking Girl]: Life is hard, Lin Xun sighs. jpg

Jiang Qing looked at this image and for some reason it struck him as funny. He replied with a haha laughing emoji, then accepted the request.

[Little Mushroom Picking Girl]: Are you a Lin Xun fan? Do you like him?

What kind of question is that. Anyone crawling over from a fan group would obviously be a fan. Unless the group had non-fan members?

...... Oh, well, it did. Wasn't he himself a fake fan?

So this was some form of periodic fan verification?

Good thing typing didn't cause a stammer. He quickly typed back a reply.

[Little Matchgirl selling matches]: Yes! I adore Lin Zong so much! Lin Zong is a little peach of a person, a sensual wild cat!

Lin Xun put away his phone. He wasn't annoyed anymore, the small sulk had dissolved. He turned his head back forward with a self-satisfied smile that thoroughly unnerved Sang Yi.

After the car stopped, Jiang Qing called out, "Lin Xun."

Lin Xun: "Meow."

Jiang Qing: "?"

What on earth has come over him?

chapters.title: "Drunk"
chapters.content:
Lin Xun's efficiency was impressive. Within a few days, the studio was ready to go, just waiting for official operations to begin.

Then he took Jiang Qing to meet Director Han of "New Homeland."

Han Yingguang was approaching fifty, short in stature, his hair thinning, but there was still a faint spark in his eyes.

The moment he laid eyes on Jiang Qing, that spark turned into a shower of crackling sparks.

"Jiang Qing, I've been trying to arrange a meeting with you for so long, but you were always tied up with the show. And honestly, I'm still a little afraid to believe it. You're really willing to appear in my film?" Han Yingguang gripped his hand and wouldn't let go, holding onto it as they both sat down at the table.

The biggest name he had ever worked with before this was a second-tier male artist, who had also been quite difficult to deal with.

Now here was Jiang Qing walking right through his door, and it felt like a gift from the heavens.

While he was still rejoicing, Han Yingguang felt a powerful stare falling on him from the side. He turned to look at Lin Xun. "Lin Zong, something to say?"

Lin Xun was staring at the two closely clasped hands, and said placidly, "We're all civilized people here. Let's not get so hands-on."

Han Yingguang let out a few ha-ha laughs and released the hand. "I'm sorry, I got carried away. I didn't frighten you, did I, Jiang Qing?"

He did.

Jiang Qing finally got his hand back. He was somewhat uncomfortable with excessive enthusiasm, and instinctively slid his hand under the table. "No, no. Director Han is very easy to talk to."

"I'm only like this with you. You're my kindred spirit."

Please don't.

Much more of this and things were going to get a little overwhelming.

"Let's get to business." Lin Xun said, and poured Jiang Qing a glass of water.

"Right, right." Han Yingguang got to the point at last, handing the script to Jiang Qing. "This is a script we've been working on for a long time. Take it home and have a careful read, and you're welcome to offer feedback at any time."

"I wouldn't dare. I agreed to take this project because I believe in the work." Jiang Qing opened the script and flipped through it briefly. Seeing that the key plot points matched what he remembered from the film in his past life with perfect accuracy, he relaxed. "Director Han, you absolutely must do this project justice."

Han Yingguang nodded solemnly. "I will. This is years of my life's work. I will finish it properly. I owe it to the first half of my life."

Lin Xun occasionally glanced at Han Yingguang's mounting excitement, and every time their conversation reached a particularly fervent point, he forced himself to look at the thin patches on Han Yingguang's head to calm himself back down.

When Han Yingguang reached for Jiang Qing's hand again, Lin Xun held on as long as he could, and then finally couldn't hold on any longer. He cut into the conversation. "Director Han, now that the lead is confirmed, shall we talk about production logistics?"

"Yes, yes. Lighting, props, and cinematography are all lined up, all the best possible, as you requested." Han Yingguang beamed, the heaviness that had hung over him completely swept away. "The special effects team is still being arranged. It's not urgent, but finding a quality team is no simple thing. Domestic post-production work in effects is still behind."

Lin Xun considered for a moment, then asked, "Could you contact a team from overseas?"

"That's very difficult. I've never worked with an overseas team, and even other directors rarely manage to bring in foreign teams. Everyone just makes do with what's available domestically."

"I'll reach out." Lin Xun said. "If all goes well, I should be able to find a few teams."

A few?!

Han Yingguang stared at him in disbelief for a full half minute.

For a science fiction film like this, the post-production effects were everything.

But the technical capabilities of domestic effects teams couldn't keep pace with Hollywood. The finished product naturally fell a good distance behind.

Audiences, given the choice between cheap, slapped-together effects and the polished productions of Hollywood studios, tended to lean heavily toward the latter.

And it wasn't only an unknown director like him who couldn't just casually go abroad and secure a few quality teams. Even top-tier directors wouldn't throw that out so lightly.

The first obstacle was money. It was often better to invest in deepening the story and developing the characters than to pour everything into post-production.

The second was that even with a high-enough offer, a foreign team might not have the availability, or might not agree to the arrangement at all. Why would they pass up mature film production companies in their own backyard?

And yet here was this young man, saying it with perfect calm, as though it were the most ordinary thing in the world. It was...... rather exhilarating, honestly.

Whether or not he could actually deliver, at least the intention was there.

"Lin Zong, let me raise a glass to you." Han Yingguang lifted a cup. "A thousand thank-yous, all of them in this drink!"

Lin Xun drank a few rounds with him, and finally managed to shift Han Yingguang's attention away from Jiang Qing.

Except that Jiang Qing had, at some point, developed a furrowed brow and a distracted look.

Lin Xun leaned in and asked quietly, "What's wrong?"

"I might not be playing the lead in 'New Homeland.'"

Jiang Qing dropped this bombshell, and the glass in Han Yingguang's hand nearly tilted over in shock.

Lin Xun was equally baffled. From the way Jiang Qing had lit up when talking about "New Homeland," it was clear he genuinely loved this project. He had specifically sought out the lead role for him. Why was he suddenly reconsidering?

"What I mean is, not the lead. I can take a supporting role." Since he'd said it, Jiang Qing went ahead and said it plainly. "Director Han, do you know someone named Zuo Xuan?"

Han Yingguang shook his head.

"He's been acting for a few years. He's had minor roles in over a hundred television productions and a few low-budget films."

Han Yingguang: ...... Not recognizing someone like that was completely understandable. Over a hundred productions and still in minor roles!

"His father has a gambling problem and racked up debt with loan sharks. He's in his thirties now, without a management company, and goes to shoot locations on his own looking for work. His looks aren't remarkable, so he rarely lands decent roles." Jiang Qing gave this brief summary of someone named Zuo Xuan, then said, "But he's better suited for the male lead of 'New Homeland' than I am. Go look him up and do a screen test. You won't be disappointed."

Han Yingguang was momentarily at a loss for words, simultaneously stunned by Jiang Qing voluntarily stepping down in billing and also wondering whether this was just a roundabout way of declining the invitation, with a conveniently produced name attached as cover.

But thinking it through, there was no reason for Jiang Qing to mislead him. The hundreds of millions in investment had come because of him. Would he really allow a film he had chosen to invest in and appear in to fail?

Impossible.

Han Yingguang thought carefully. The male lead was written as an unremarkable, middle-aged man whose fortunes had not gone well.

While Jiang Qing could certainly use makeup to play the role, his ordinarily striking features would make it difficult for audiences to believe he was a "perfectly ordinary" man.

Once this became clear to him, Han Yingguang pressed further. "Alright. I'll have him come in for a screen test in a few days. But how do you know this person?"

"Ah, I have a pr...... production, where he app...... appeared." Jiang Qing said, stumbling over the words, and didn't want to say any more on the subject.

Stuttering really was terrible for a person's image.

Zuo Xuan had never actually worked with him. He knew this person entirely because, in his past life, the lead in "New Homeland" had been Zuo Xuan.

At the time, Han Yingguang hadn't had the budget to hire expensive actors, so he had reached out to some lower-tier performers for screen tests. Zuo Xuan had, rather by accident, submitted a resume, went in and tested, and was cast in the lead just like that.

Zuo Xuan had become famous overnight because of the film, and shot to become one of the most beloved actors on screen, while also paying off every debt his family owed.

Without that film, he might have spent his whole life in minor roles, tormented year after year by interest compounding on interest.

Jiang Qing had wrestled with this for a long time before deciding to give that opportunity back to Zuo Xuan. After all, it was a film he loved, and getting to play a supporting role was more than enough for him.

Lin Xun's gaze on Jiang Qing grew increasingly deep, the admiration in his eyes growing more pronounced.

Jiang Qing seemed to notice, held his look for a few seconds, then leaned close and murmured, "Go sign Zuo Xuan. He should be cheap to sign right now."

Lin Xun nodded. "Alright."

Whatever you say.

After several rounds of drinks, Han Yingguang could no longer hold himself together and collapsed face-down on the table.

Lin Xun shook his head slightly, turned to look at Jiang Qing, who was sitting quietly beside him scrolling on his phone and drinking fruit juice, and reached out to cup the back of his head, drawing him forward.

Jiang Qing startled, and then a warm forehead pressed against his, and he couldn't move.

He looked up at the other person. The cheeks as fine and smooth as porcelain were faintly flushed, and the deep eyes held a glimmer of laughter scattered like light through water. His other hand closed around Jiang Qing's hand, his thumb moving slowly across the back of it.

"You're drunk." he said.

Lin Xun smiled, the faint scent of wine on his breath, and said quietly, "I'm not."

Then his head tilted, and came to rest on Jiang Qing's shoulder.

Worried the person might keel over sideways, he had no choice but to hold the back of the other's head in one hand, and with the other, free himself to call Han Yingguang's assistant, who was waiting outside.

The assistant walked in to find Jiang Qing with his back to the door, embracing Lin Xun in what was a very intimate-looking position.

The assistant was a worldly person who had seen plenty. He didn't dare look too long, and simply picked up the passed-out director and headed out.

Before leaving, he considerately pulled the door shut behind him.

Since they had come together, Jiang Qing hadn't brought Sang Yi along.

He held Lin Xun's arms around himself and pushed to his feet with effort.

In the midst of the scramble, he felt a warmth brush against his neck, and paused.

It was a fleeting thing, over in an instant. He touched his neck on reflex, and looking at the dazed, heavy-lidded Lin Xun, quietly reasoned it must have been an accidental brush.

"Lin Xun, wake up. Can you still walk?" He gave Lin Xun's face a few firm pats, and the already flushed cheeks quickly bloomed a shade deeper where his hand had landed.

The other person seemed to come around somewhat, eyelids barely open, and with most of his weight draped onto Jiang Qing, moved in shuffled steps alongside him out the door.

It was a struggle to reach the hotel entrance. The valet brought the car around. Once the person was deposited in the back seat, he finally let out a long breath.

He drove slowly, muttering under his breath, "I don't know what you were raised on, but you are heavy."

As the words left his mouth, a soft, brief laugh came from the back seat, there and gone in an instant, leaving him uncertain whether he had imagined it.

When they reached the complex, another ordeal of maneuvering followed. Inside the elevator, a large hand reached over and ruffled his hair, then proceeded to knead it thoroughly into a bird's nest.

He bore it helplessly and muttered under his breath, "Just you wait until you're sober. I'm going to pound you."

At the door, he realized he didn't know the password, and turned sharply to the side, intending to ask, and his nose ran right into the other man's cheek.

He rubbed his nose and pinched the face resting on his shoulder. "Wake up. What's the passcode."

It must have hurt enough, because Lin Xun opened his eyes the tiniest amount and said in a mumble, "Fingerprint......" and then went silent.

Jiang Qing took his hand and pressed his thumb to the sensor. Wrong. Index finger, also wrong. He worked through all the fingers on one hand, then shifted, propping the person on his other side, and tried the other hand.

The moment he picked it up, the other hand gripped his hard, and a low, threatening voice said, "Don't move."

Jiang Qing paused, waited a moment, and when nothing else happened, said helplessly, "You're out of your mind. Let go, it's time to go home."

"It's mine." Lin Xun said.

"Yes, yes, it's yours. Be good, let go."

Lin Xun obediently let go.

Jiang Qing continued pressing fingerprints and said, "Of course it's yours, a house this big."

Lin Xun was just about to retort when the door swung open.

Jiang Qing deposited him onto the bed in his room, stood there with his hands on his hips, and let out a long sigh to the ceiling. "If I ever agree to go out socializing with you again, I'll be a pig!"

He turned to leave, made it to the doorway, then doubled back to stand at the bedside. He took a deep breath, bent down and removed Lin Xun's shoes, then left with an expression of profound disgust.

The front door clicked shut.

The room returned to quiet. In the dark, Lin Xun's lips curved slowly upward. His lashes trembled, and he opened his eyes.

He turned on the bedside lamp, raised his hand, and looked at it for a long time. The warmth and texture of that touch seemed to still be there, lingering in his palm.

That hand had been slender and thin, yet not without strength. Held in his own, it was...... very difficult to stop thinking about.

He really was terrible, he thought, with some self-reproach.

He hadn't expected that there would come a day when he would have to find ways and means to hold someone's hand.

He couldn't pinpoint when exactly it had started, but somewhere along the way, his eyes had found themselves unable to pull away from Jiang Qing.

Since he couldn't control it, he may as well let it grow freely. He wasn't the kind of person who practiced rigid self-denial when it came to what he wanted.

But a person accustomed to the position of the pursuer would never rashly put himself in an awkward position.

He had no experience pursuing a romantic partner, but he knew that everything required a plan. Like founding a company, it had to be mapped out one reasonable step at a time in order to keep the whole situation in hand.

First, he needed to confirm the target market.

He picked up his phone, thought for a moment, opened QQ, and sent a message to his fan, Jiang Qing.

[Little Mushroom Picking Girl]: Good evening, Little Matchgirl. What kind of person do you think Lin Xun is?

Jiang Qing finished his shower, sniffed his own smell to confirm there was no trace of alcohol on him, then went to blow his hair dry.

When he absently touched his neck, he paused, his fingers tracing over a particular spot, and felt his emotions go unexpectedly unsettled.

His phone vibrated. He saw the new message from his online acquaintance, and quickly typed back a reply.

Lin Xun waited tensely for the new message. The moment it arrived, he opened it eagerly.

[Little Matchgirl selling matches]: A good person.

Being handed a Nice Guy card without warning, Lin Xun lost his grip, and the phone smacked him in the face.

He rubbed his nose, hugged the phone and rolled over, deeply conflicted.

[Little Mushroom Picking Girl]: Aren't you a fan? Don't you want to marry him? Don't you want him all to yourself?

[Little Matchgirl selling matches]: I'm just a fan hehe! Studies must come first, gotta be rational about it! [shy penguin emoji]

My goodness. Did someone else take over the account?

Lin Xun suspected he had either been hacked, or that he'd gotten the wrong person. He decided to test the waters: [You're right! But honestly, I like Jiang Qing more than Lin Xun.]

If this really was a die-hard Lin Xun fan, they should not be able to tolerate someone jumping ship and talking down about him like that.

The reply came back very quickly.

[Little Matchgirl selling matches]: Great taste, sis! Same. [penguin with a heart emoji]

Alright, case closed. It was definitely Jiang Qing.

But this badly disguised elementary-school persona was...... actually kind of adorable.

[Little Mushroom Picking Girl]: So what kind of person do you think Jiang Qing is? Why do you like him?

[Little Matchgirl selling matches]: A good person.

A good person too?

Rough approximation: saying himself and Lin Xun were equally excellent.

Which was indirectly confirming that Lin Xun held quite an important place in the equation as well.

Lin Xun was fully revived. After exchanging a goodnight with the other person, he opened his laptop and searched for a compilation of Jiang Qing's films.

Know yourself and know your enemy, and you shall not be defeated in any battle.

The next morning, Jiang Qing sat in the living room bright and early, waiting for breakfast to be delivered, while also running through a mental vocabulary of choice insults, fully prepared to unleash them on the person who had misbehaved so spectacularly last night.

He waited a long time. The doorbell never rang.

He sat on the sofa and shifted positions over a dozen times before finally couldn't take it anymore, walked over to the neighbor's door, was just about to press the bell, then stopped himself.

He paced back and forth for a moment in place, then turned around, went downstairs, and from a nearby dim sum restaurant packed up a portion of plain congee and some light, simple snacks, and ordered himself a custard lava bun and a meat bun.

He carried the food back, pressed the doorbell a few times, and found himself inexplicably restless while he waited.

Then he thought about how the other person came every single morning and stood at his door, never showing the slightest impatience, on the receiving end of his morning temper without a single complaint.

Tch. He couldn't think about that. Thinking about it only made the other person seem very good-natured.

He reset his mood before pressing the doorbell again.

And so, when Lin Xun dragged his exhausted body to the door and opened it, what he found was a face lit up with a bright, warm smile, carrying the smell of the morning sun, that in an instant washed away the fatigue of a sleepless night.

He had been staring at the other person's films all night long, until almost dawn before he finally slept. All manner of different characters had swirled through his mind, and in this moment they finally settled, coming to rest in one person.

No matter how many roles Jiang Qing had played, he was always still Jiang Qing.

"Good morning." Jiang Qing showed all eight teeth, the smile reaching the ends of his brows.

"Good morning." Lin Xun said, his voice still rough with sleep.

"Didn't rest well?" Jiang Qing took in the shadows under his eyes, walked in and set the breakfast on the table. "Eat first. Sleep again after eating. Serves you right for drinking that much last night."

He hadn't drunk that much. He was drunk on a person, was all, Lin Xun thought, and headed to the bathroom. "I'll wash up first."

Jiang Qing munched on his bun, and out of the corner of his eye noticed that a flower on the balcony had bloomed, and went to take a curious look.

When Lin Xun came back from his shower and sat down, he immediately felt that Jiang Qing's eyes were doing something strange, the expression in those peachy eyes full of impish mischief.

"What?" he asked.

The corner of Jiang Qing's mouth had lifted dramatically. "You just took a shower now, so why is there underwear hanging outside already!"

Lin Xun: "......"

"So that's why it took so long to answer the door! You were in there washing your underwear, weren't you~" Jiang Qing bit the straw of his soy milk and giggled.

He was laughing so hard Lin Xun couldn't even form a response. He buried his head in his congee, the tips of his ears going a little red.

Seeing this, Jiang Qing laughed out loud. "You're such a pure soul, how can you be turning red over this? It's the most normal thing there is."

Lin Xun thought privately: if you knew who I was dreaming about, you wouldn't be saying that.

chapters.title: The Fallout
chapters.content:
Lin Xun finished the last sip of his congee, calmly wiped his mouth, and smiled. "When was the last time you washed your underwear?"

Jiang Qing: "...... Come on, you can't bring that up at breakfast."

"I've watched all your films, and I noticed something quite serious."

The topic had shifted too fast. Jiang Qing hadn't followed, but hearing "films," he responded on instinct. "What's serious?"

"You have no kissing scenes and no bed scenes. At the very most you're holding hands." Lin Xun's smile deepened.

Jiang Qing: "......"

"Why?"

"Because I don't need them. I've always preferred other genres and types of stories over romance."

Things like the lives of Doctors Without Borders, war-themed works, stories about violence against minors, crime and law, the kind of films that could make audiences take something seriously.

When he was underage, the films he appeared in didn't require romantic scenes. But after becoming an adult, sometimes he still had to follow the market and work a romantic storyline into a production.

Take "Boundless," for example. He and Director Yu Haoge and the screenwriter had specifically discussed this, and the real dramatic core was between the character Jiang Qing played, the wealthy young man, and the older doctor among the medical team. The theme could have been far more profound.

But for the box office and for audiences, a love story had to be added in.

And then there was a personal reason, which was that he simply didn't believe in any such thing as love that endured until death.

If he didn't believe in it himself, how could he have any confidence in playing it convincingly?

After breakfast, he paid a visit to the Jiang family home.

Auntie Yu and the household staff were all standing at attention, busily making preparations, their nerves drawn taut for the moment the young master arrived.

But this time the young master seemed to have no interest in quarreling with Jiang Huai, and went off on his own to the garden with a large pair of shears.

Jiang Huai watched from upstairs.

Auntie Yu approached and asked, "Sir, shall we prepare incense for the young master's room?"

"Mm. He won't be staying tonight." Jiang Huai said.

Auntie Yu glanced out the window to find Jiang Qing with an easy, leisurely expression, trimming the garden plants in tranquil contentment. A picture of quiet, peaceful days.

What a pity, though. Clippings of weeds were scattered all over the ground.

"Oh!"

Auntie Yu let out a startled cry as she watched the young master swiftly and efficiently strip every last branch of the locust tree blossoms, which was the master's favorite, leaving nothing behind but a bare trunk.

When he was done, Jiang Qing looked up and cast a provocative glance in this direction.

"Sir, what are we to do?" Auntie Yu was a little afraid of Jiang Huai's temper.

"Never mind it. We'll plant new ones." Jiang Huai said, unbothered.

Lunch was abundant, a long table covered in all manner of dishes.

A newly arrived member of the household staff watched with envy. This was what life was like when you had money. A single meal like a royal banquet.

There were at least a dozen dishes that neither of the two men had touched, and an extra bowl sitting empty to the side, as though someone had picked it up by mistake.

The table was silent except for the sounds of eating.

Jiang Qing had little appetite and ate only a few bites before Jiang Huai suddenly broke the silence and asked, "You and that person called Lin Xun are neighbors now?"

He paused, and raised his eyes slowly, his expression turned cold. "You went and investigated again?"

Jiang Huai didn't answer his question directly. "His background isn't..."

"Will you stop it!" Jiang Qing put his bowl down hard, and the household staff braced themselves inwardly.

"How old am I? And you're still digging into things like this! Have you nothing better to do?"

"I'm only reminding you. He's not as simple as he seems." Jiang Huai said.

Jiang Qing stood up abruptly. The chair behind him toppled backward with a jarring clatter.

"Since when do I need you to remind me? Are my eyes not working? Is your idea of reminding me making sure I can't form any friendships at all? Don't think I won't call every one of your fair-weather friends right now and tell them exactly what you've done in your life that you're not proud of."

Jiang Huai looked at him steadily. "You care about him that much? The others I investigated before never got this kind of reaction from you."

"I was not in the mood for a fight today. But......" Jiang Qing took a deep breath, pulled the corner of his mouth sideways, walked up to him, bent close, and said quietly, "When I was little, I didn't report you because no one was going to believe a child. But I'm grown up now, and I have a voice. You had better not meddle in my affairs again, or don't blame me for going out of my mind."

Jiang Huai turned to look at him, his expression taut and combative, and said in a measured tone, "I would advise you not to go out of your mind at any moment you please. What separates that from an animal."

"Heh. And who made and raised the animal?" Jiang Qing dropped that one line and walked out of the Jiang family home.

Auntie Yu said hesitatingly, "Sir, the incense......"

"Throw it out. Who knows when it will be needed next." Jiang Huai continued eating, expression unchanged. He glanced at the empty bowl at some point, and something complicated moved across his face.

Auntie Yu waited to one side, and suddenly had the sense that the straight line of Master Jiang's spine had curved just slightly.

That evening, the final episode of "I Am an Actor" aired. Jiang Qing knocked on the neighbor's door with a few bottles of soda, said nothing about the Jiang family visit, and gave his full attention to the show.

It was almost a foregone conclusion that Lin Xun's second-place finish would stir up a wave of discussion, and that rival fanbases would be watching closely.

But barely a few minutes into the broadcast, the conversation had already gone sideways.

And the cause was that pre-broadcast interview segment.

Lin Xun's interview had been completely without issue. Jiang Qing's too.

Jiang Qing had asked the staff member at the time to cut the footage showing the two of them in the same frame as neighbors, and the production team had complied. Neither of them appeared together in any shot.

He had avoided the biggest risk, and had entirely overlooked that online viewers were the kind of people who watched video with a magnifying glass.

[Ahhh Lin Xun's bare face is SO handsome! Lin Xun when are you coming to marry me! I'm already lying down!]

[Jiang Qing's bare face is off the charts too! And he's in his loungewear ha ha ha! So soft and so unexpected, I want to sleep! Send the link to those clothes, by rough approximation I'm basically sleeping with Jiang Qing!]

[WAIT. Lin Xun and Jiang Qing's rooms look the same! The decor and the layout look identical!]

[WHAT. I nearly did a sit-up in place, and it's true, they really are!]

[The floors! The floors, same natural wood floors!]

[That breakfast! That breakfast sitting on the table! The one from Lin Xun's place! Jiang Qing ate it!]

[Look closely at the packaging on Jiang Qing's breakfast, it's definitely from Lin Xun's home!]

[Allow me to pose a math problem. Given that out of millions upon millions of people, the probability that two individuals' apartments look this similar AND that they share food from the same source simultaneously is roughly......]

[Oh my god, are they living together?!]

You truly cannot guard against everything. Jiang Qing pressed a hand to his forehead and turned to ask, "Why didn't you redecorate?"

"Lazy. When I first moved in I just wanted somewhere to sleep and wasn't planning to stay long." Lin Xun answered honestly. He hadn't expected Jiang Qing to be next door at the time, but he did have plans to stay long-term now. As for redecorating...... was there really anything wrong with matching interiors?

The footage cut to the scene of the mentor making a video call to a contestant.

[Oh, so they're not living together. You can see there's a small difference in the backgrounds when they're on video]

[The beauty of waking up and immediately getting a video call from a beautiful person, this is what bliss looks like!]

[Oh oh oh, the way Lin Zong is looking at Jiang Qing is so sweet, suddenly my own honey isn't as sweet anymore]

[These two people are genuinely too good-looking, I truly cannot imagine which two women could possibly have them. Maybe they should just keep it between themselves!]

[Another day in the life of a Lin-Jiang fan eating well! I'm so sad the show is ending! Once it's done there won't be any more opportunities for them to publicly give us candy like this!]

[Got my fix, got my fix, got my fix, got my fix, got my fix]

The show finally reached the competition segment. The stage production was more elaborate this time, and the performances grew stronger with each passing round.

[Liu Huimin is so incredible! I love this woman, you absolutely must blow up!]

[Make her famous, make her famous, make her famous...]

[Oh WOW, Lin Xun's performance is just so natural! His emotional control is incredible!]

[Lin Xun actually didn't get dominated by a force like Duan Jiaxu! He really does rise to any level of competition!]

[WAIT, both Liu Huimin AND Lin Xun made it through?! Honestly, I did not have either of them going to the finale at the start!]

[Same! Their performances this episode were seriously so good!]

[Is there a fix?]

[I was in the live audience and I can confirm there is no fix. Their live energy was even stronger! Liu Huimin and Lin Xun deserve your support! Every single performer was wonderful!]

"Have some water." Lin Xun handed Jiang Qing a glass, then checked Yang Meng's messages, asking when to announce the studio's launch.

He replied: "After this episode ends."

[AHHHH they're doing Old Friends! Forget it, I'm crying before it even starts!]

[Music starts and I've already got goosebumps! Such an iconic tearjerker of a classic]

[Not surprising, it's a classic, but it won't be easy to perform]

[Oh, the twins are being played by two different people. Liu Huimin has the right quality, though the girlishness is a little lacking. Overall, she's better as the older sister than the younger]

[AHHHH Lin Xun's character is such a domineering rogue, even this social butterfly of a younger sister is blushing and fluttering!]

[Ooh Lin Xun being grumpy is so good-looking too, so doting on his wife, I am green with envy!]

[Can't deny it, you can't compare without a benchmark, Ye Wu really is on another level!]

The performance concluded, and the episode moved to the tribute for Ye Wu. The barrage comments filled with a wave of "May heaven have no pain, may you live on in our hearts [candle emoji]."

Then came the announcement of results.

[Duan Jiaxu has to be first! If not, I'll suspect the show of rigging!]

[Liu Huimin get up there!]

[Lin Zong, let's go!]

[Liu Huimin is strong, third place is solid! Thank you to the production team for introducing us to so many hidden-gem performers]

[AHHHHHHH Xun-ge is the runner-up! Time for me to go run a giveaway!]

[Didn't expect a trending star to still slip in there. The power of capital, truly something]

[The person above sounds so sour. As a casual viewer, I thought Lin Xun genuinely stood out in this episode! Keep it up!]

The results sparked heated debate online quickly enough.

In the eyes of netizens, Duan Jiaxu and Liu Huimin had earned their honors fair and square, and it was right that these quietly capable performers were getting the recognition they deserved, pushing back against the culture of trending stars dominating everything.

But Lin Xun was more contested. Some said it was the power of capital and that someone had backed him. Others said his ability spoke for itself, no question.

Right in the middle of all the argument, someone dropped three paparazzi photos online.

They were taken the previous night of Jiang Qing supporting Lin Xun as they left the restaurant, and from the angle and the way the photos were shot, the two of them looked intimate, with even a hint of something that could be read as a kiss.

Whatever the interpretation, a secret late-night meeting and intimate physical closeness was enough to make people connect the dots to today's results.

What exactly was Jiang Qing's role during Lin Xun's time on the show?

Mentor? Friend? Backer?

Soon enough, marketing accounts and trolls were dissecting an alleged conspiracy between the two, analyzing every detail including their eye contact, and all manner of speculation and rumor began swirling.

Since Lin Xun had gained a good number of casual fans through this show, moving into territory that affected other fanbases' interests, the trolls multiplied in greater numbers than usual, and a slew of messy fabricated scandals surfaced.

Things like falsifying his education, with some rumor-account claiming Lin Xun had graduated from a prestigious university, while his public profile listed no school at all. If it really was a prestigious school, why not disclose it? Obviously fake!

And accusations of buying off the mentor, with numerous photos of his close interactions with Jiang Qing posted as evidence, with the implication it had all been orchestrated, because why else would the famously sharp-tongued Jiang Qing be showering Lin Xun with rainbow flattery every single episode?

There were also "couple breakfasts" shared by the two of them, endless CP shippers, and claims of deliberate fan-baiting and vote-fishing.

And then "ex-girlfriends" and "old classmates" came forward to post anonymous exposés.

Netizens were like a crowd of weasels ransacking a melon patch, each piece of gossip darker than the last, and the admiration that had barely begun to take root was swept away in an instant.

Jiang Qing sighed with exasperation. "Don't let it bother you. These people are just easily led. They hear the wind and call it rain, they see a melon and bite right into it."

"Mm." Lin Xun scrolled his phone, entirely unperturbed, with even a subtle curve at the corner of his mouth.

"What are you doing?" Jiang Qing leaned over to look.

Lin Xun raised his phone to block him.

He was quietly saving the intimate photos of him and Jiang Qing that had been posted online. Could he say that?

The fans were so thoughtful, really. Such great photos. Such stunning angles. So many of them. Delightful.

While saving them one by one, he received a message from his melon-watching friend, Yang.

[Oh god, go give Jiang Qing's Weibo a like right now! I'm basically ready to ship you two myself]

He opened Weibo with no idea what this was about. There were too many notifications, so he skipped them all and went straight to Jiang Qing's Weibo.

@Jiang Qing: Anyone questioning Lin Xun's ability is welcome to go ask the live audience and the other two mentors directly. Anyone accusing the production team of rigging is welcome to consult the production team. Be careful with your gossip consumption. Choke hazard. Eating too much rotten fruit can poison you.

Why is everyone reacting so intensely just because I praised someone? Did I only praise Lin Xun? Ask your conscience honestly. Doesn't he deserve to be praised?

As for "couple breakfasts"...... do you not eat steamed buns and soy milk and fried dough sticks? I'm basically in a relationship with all of humanity! Trolls, you've really hurt my feelings on that one. It's over between us. No more couple breakfasts tomorrow.

Finally, congratulations to @Lin Xun @Liu Huimin on their excellent results. @Gao Yuanqiao has also worked very hard. I hope everyone can see every performer who puts in genuine effort behind the scenes.

chapters.title: The Statement
chapters.content:
This Weibo post went up and the fans were shocked and thrilled all at once. The CP fans went so sweet they were bumping into walls. Casual viewers looked on in bafflement.

[AHHHHH today I am a groundhog! Jiang Qing gets attacked and Lin Xun goes to bat for him. Lin Xun gets attacked and Jiang Qing blows up the whole thing himself! What incredible friendship!!!!]

[Ha ha ha ha ha DEAD! God bless him for breaking up with the trolls! I don't care, I'm having couple breakfast with him tomorrow]

[Trolls go toe-to-toe with Jiang Qing then! Fair fight face to face! When it comes to roasting, Qing-ge is unmatched. When it comes to methods, it's your Xun-ge. Who told them to pick a fight with these two]

[No, this isn't even Jiang Qing at full power. A poet of his origins from the cradle of roasting, he must have exercised considerable restraint ha ha ha ha ha]

[I'm wide awake tonight, running on pure adrenaline. Is anything else going to happen? Let the storm rage even harder!]

[Lin Xun still hasn't said anything! He jumped out so fast when he was defending Jiang Qing, but when it's about himself he doesn't care...... oh god, saying this out loud actually moved me to tears]

[Lin-Jiang squad, never giving up! Sisters, let's go, the fan rankings are almost number one!]

......

Lin Xun looked at Jiang Qing in amusement. "Didn't Tong-jie change your Weibo password?"

"I got it back. My password, my call." Jiang Qing said lightly, turning his phone over in his hand. "No need to thank me. Consider it repayment for the times you've helped."

Lin Xun felt a warm swell in his chest. He typically handled his own problems, and it was rare for anyone to offer help on their own initiative. When it did happen, unexpectedly, he found it genuinely moving.

These comments had all been part of his plan from the start. He had even fanned the flames of the negative posts behind the scenes himself, waiting for the right moment for things to rebound.

But Jiang Qing's Weibo had ignited a new wave of momentum, and watching the online tide surge in exactly the direction he had anticipated, he felt none of the satisfaction of a scheme coming together. He sent Yang Meng a message and decided to move the plan forward.

Ten minutes later, while netizens were having a field day feasting on gossip, someone noticed a major announcement.

@Ryan Investment Co., Ltd.: There have been numerous inappropriate statements circulating online regarding our company's chairman, Lin Xun. After an internal resolution, we reserve the right to pursue legal action.

Regarding claims of academic fraud, this is categorically false. Lin Xun attended the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, completed the MBA program, and graduated with distinction.

As Lin Xun did not attend school in China, any alleged "old classmates" or "ex-girlfriends" are invited to produce graduation certificates from Penn or a school he attended prior to that as proof.

If there are any questions, you are welcome to comment. Please do not believe or spread rumors. Wishing everyone a pleasant day!

The internet detonated, more spectacular than any firework. The post shot up the trending charts at lightning speed and became the biggest explosion of the night.

[WHAT THE HELL! I can barely breathe! Ryan Investment chairman?! Is this the Ryan Investment, insanely rich, invested in like a dozen hit film and TV productions?!!!]

[Oh my god. Lin Xun's first drama was a Ryan Investment production. Wasn't there a rumor that Yang Meng was promoting him and they had some improper relationship? Ha ha ha ha what a contender for joke of the year! Lin Xun: I promote myself!]

[AHHHHHH I've lost my mind, what kind of big shot did I end up stanning?!]

[This account hasn't been hacked, has it?! Isn't Yang Meng the boss of Ryan Investment?! Someone tell me if this is real!]

Yang Meng, seeing the hype building, went to add a final confirmation.

@Yang Meng: Honestly, being a shopkeeper is tiring work too. When is the boss going to give me a raise? @Lin Xun

[WAIT YANG MENG PERSONALLY POSTED. THIS IS REAL!!!]

[I nearly got down from my chair to kneel, and I intend to stay kneeling! I bow to the great one!]

[Ryan Investment has been around for ten years and Lin Xun is still under 29. My god. What was I doing at eighteen or nineteen......]

[Lin Xun is incredible Lin Xun is incredible Lin Xun is incredible]

[Ha ha ha ha ha ha those supposed old classmates and abortion-having ex-girlfriends, where'd you all go? Come out and show us your certificates! Oh I'm sorry, you're not qualified!]

[Lin Xun really played this perfectly. A bombshell in the middle of the night, and I'm thoroughly satisfied!]

[Everyone telling me Lin Xun bought the mentor and rigged the show, come out here and take your beating. With this kind of net worth, would he really need to buy a second-place finish in one small show?!]

[The fan group has exploded! The Lavenders never saw this coming!!!]

[I'm switching fandoms, I'm joining the fan club! If I stan a big shot like this, do I really need to worry about anything ever?!]

After this news broke, every piece of rumor and gossip collapsed on its own. The trolls scattered.

And it wasn't just the netizens who were stunned. People inside the industry were shaken too.

Nobody had expected that this newcomer of under a year in the business, this person who had debuted as a domineering CEO in a romance drama, this person who was called a vase due to his looks, not only conquered everyone with his acting ability in a variety show, but was also a golden backer with deep pockets.

A number of dramas in the industry had Ryan Investment's fingerprints on them.

The rival camps who had been attacking him now started to feel afraid. Those who had disliked him disliked him even more. And a far greater number of people were kicking themselves for not having gotten close when they had the chance.

Mu Ning stared at Yang Meng's Weibo, her fingers trembling faintly.

No wonder Yang Meng had pushed her out. No wonder Yang Meng had always treated Lin Xun so well. How could she have listened to her plastic-friendship so-called sister and actually believed Yang Meng was keeping Lin Xun?

What was she going to do. The trolls she had arranged shouldn't be easy to trace back to her, right?

Probably fine. She hadn't been the only one attacking him.

Xu Jiacheng, who had performed "Boundless" with Lin Xun on the stage of "I Am an Actor," was sitting cross-legged on her bed, having spent the whole night as a spectator, and it was only now that she had truly gotten her fill.

Her manager called her and told her to reach out to Lin Xun and reconnect.

She said, dissatisfied, "What's there to reconnect over? We only worked together that one time. Who even knows if he remembers me. Why would I make a fool of myself chasing after someone?"

Her manager said in exasperation, "This is exactly why you're still crawling along in the second tier! Think about what you're doing!"

Maybe she'd had a little too much gossip to drink, because she found her nerve, and snapped back, "It's your fault! All you ever think about is finding me a rich backer or dragging me to events!"

"And who am I doing it for! I've said what I have to say. Do whatever you want." The manager hung up.

At the same time, in a certain hotel room, the sound of running water came from the bathroom. Wang Mingzhi sat in the living room watching the trending topics, his expression dark.

So Jiang Qing had been in such a hurry to dissolve his contract because he had already lined up a new home?

Ha. Just some Lin Xun who didn't understand anything. Having money, what use was that? Running a company wasn't that easy.

He let out a scornful laugh, but his brows were pressed into a deep crease.

"Come in." Bai Bangnan's voice sounded from inside the bathroom.

He twitched involuntarily at those words. He hated Bai Bangnan. He was straight, and every time he had to grit his teeth through the disgust to see things through, while pretending to enjoy it on the outside.

He walked in with degrading steps, telling himself this was the path he had chosen, and that the day he no longer needed Bai Bangnan, he was going to repay him very thoroughly.

Not just Bai Bangnan. Jiang Qing too.

If it hadn't been for Jiang Qing making him the laughingstock of the whole internet, he wouldn't have had to go and steal Gao Yuanqiao's project.

He was going to have a turn on top too! He was going to pin Jiang Qing to the floor, grip his waist and......

Meanwhile, Yu Minghan, who was supposed to be home playing games, had been nudged by Zhao Lianchuan to start paying attention to the online situation, but he had come to the party too late. If he had shown up earlier when everyone was piling onto Lin Xun, he would have loved to help, because he genuinely loathed that kind of baseless mud-slinging.

But Jiang Qing had already stepped in, which made him admire Jiang Qing even more.

By the time he finally got to the scene, he saw the announcement that Lin Xun was chairman of Ryan Investment, and his jaw practically dropped to the floor, like he was trying to bite through his own game controller.

This, this this...... what the hell...... so who was richer right now, him or Lin Xun?

Liu Huimin and Gao Yuanqiao also appeared, but they appeared in a private group chat of four.

From the moment the trolls started going after Lin Xun, the two of them had been sending messages of support, expressing their full confidence in him.

When the big revelation dropped, they were genuinely happy for him.

Liu Huimin sent a string of hahahahaha voice messages, gleeful and cathartic, making Gao Yuanqiao's voice after hers sound rather low by comparison.

Jiang Qing thought it had been a while since he'd seen the kid, and messaged him privately to ask how things were going.

The moment his message was sent, the other person replied with a big crying emoji.

He called Gao Yuanqiao, stepped out to the balcony, and his tone instinctively softened. "Hey, Xiao Qiao. Did something happen?"

Lin Xun sat in the living room and watched him for a while. His mood felt a little off. Even though the situation online was developing exactly as he had planned, he felt none of the pleasure of having the whole thing in the palm of his hand.

He opened Weibo, judged that the moment had built sufficiently.

According to the plan, this was the moment to announce the establishment of the studio he and Jiang Qing had co-founded, which would undoubtedly set off a wave of celebration and support among netizens, with maximum possible attention.

He planned everything he did step by step, but he looked at Jiang Qing on the balcony, gently encouraging someone else.

Jiang Qing had personally gone to bat for him online, but he also went to comfort other people.

If the person being attacked today were Gao Yuanqiao, Lin Xun was certain Jiang Qing would have shown up just the same.

It suddenly occurred to him that Jiang Qing was the unpredictable variable in all his plans, the one who kept him up at night, made his face flush and his heart race, and also made something possessive stir to life inside him.

The content he had been editing in Weibo was deleted, and instead he reposted Ryan's official clarification, adding a clarification of his own about another piece of gossip.

@Lin Xun: We're neighbors. @Jiang Qing

We won't be, for much longer, he thought, with perfect certainty.

Things had not been going well for Gao Yuanqiao lately.

His semi-final performance had been below par, though he had kept up appearances in front of Jiang Qing and the others.

But he had been far too naive about the termination of his contract. He had assumed paying a penalty fee would be sufficient, but after the falling out with Bai Bangnan, the people under him had made it very convenient to itemize every breach of contract fee, training expense, and exclusive styling cost to the last decimal, and the final figure that came back was astronomical.

This was the straw that broke everything.

All that genuine effort turned to bitter disappointment, and on top of it, he had a massive sum to pay. If not for thinking of the two elderly people at home, he might have already put an end to things for himself.

"Senior, I can't sleep." Gao Yuanqiao said in a hoarse voice. "Night after night I can't sleep. The moment I close my eyes I feel like I can't breathe."

Jiang Qing remembered he had once mentioned that his nerves were fragile, that he wouldn't even drink coffee for fear it would affect his sleep, and let out a breath too quiet to hear. "Are you on medication?"

"It's not helping." A long pause, and then Gao Yuanqiao asked in a drifting voice, "Senior, am I useless?"

"You ran into some bad luck." Jiang Qing said. "Are you free tomorrow? Let's meet."

"I'm not really up to seeing anyone right now...... you'd be shocked."

"You still have to see me. It's not like you're some rare exotic creature that can't be observed in person. That's settled then. Get some rest tonight, and tomorrow we'll go out and have some fun."

"Fun?"

"Mm." Jiang Qing glanced back toward the room. "I might bring a friend along too."

It took quite a while for Gao Yuanqiao to agree.

After hanging up, Jiang Qing went back to the living room and had barely sat down when Shu Tong called.

"Hey, I kept trying to reach you, the line was busy. Who were you on the phone with?"

"Gao Yuanqiao. Something up?"

"It's just that you've now made your neighbor situation public online. I wanted to check on the security setup at your complex. If any fansite stalkers track you down there, they'd be getting two for the price of one." Shu Tong said.

"Isn't the security in this area the best available?" Jiang Qing answered automatically, then caught up. "What do you mean made the neighbor situation public?"

"Lin Xun. He posted it online. I thought you two had discussed it together." Shu Tong laughed a little. "Honestly, it's fine. Better to be clear about it now than to have the trolls making material out of it later. The paparazzi would've found out eventually. May as well get some traction out of it now."

"Got it."

"By the way, we're planning to announce the studio launch tomorrow evening. Gives netizens a little time to breathe tonight, then tomorrow we get them going again."

"......" Jiang Qing could not find the words. "Who said that?"

"Ah, Yang Meng."

Of course. Thoroughly corrupted.

After ending the call, Jiang Qing glanced at Lin Xun sitting beside him, and was about to ask something. But as he turned his head, he found the other person seemed to have been watching him for some time, and the sustained gaze left him with nowhere to put himself. He looked down instinctively and opened his phone to check messages.

When he got to Lin Xun's Weibo, the comment count had already climbed toward three hundred thousand.

[AHHH Lin Zong you finally showed up! Let me get my fill of you! I'll be your dedicated fan for life!]

[Neighbors?! No wonder you're so close! Could you tell me the housing prices so I can properly let go of all hope!]

[I suppose this is what it means to be a big shot. Big shots just naturally cluster together. The places where they live are realms we ordinary people can only aspire to!]

[AHHHHHH today's sugar content has been dangerously high. I am expired but I am still climbing out of this coffin to shout: Lin-Jiang is real!!!]

"Why did you bring it up out of nowhere?" Jiang Qing asked, curious.

"Is that not allowed?" Lin Xun looked at him steadily.

"It's allowed." Jiang Qing said, and thought of what Shu Tong had said. Eventually someone would have found out regardless, and coming clean early saved a lot of trouble down the line. Plenty of artists had other artists as neighbors. It wasn't exactly world-shaking news.

"Also, are you free tomorrow?"

Lin Xun looked at him with a slight pause, uncertain. "I could be free or I could have plans, depending."

"Do you or don't you?" Jiang Qing raised an eyebrow. "If you're free, come out with me."

"I'm completely free. I have absolutely nothing going on." Lin Xun immediately looked at him with anticipation. This was the first time he'd been invited out to do something!

How wonderful.

Would they maybe go see a film together? Then a candlelit dinner, some red wine, pleasantly light-headed, and then......

No. The further he took it, the more swept up he got.

"Great, then it's decided. Gao Yuanqiao will be joining us too."

Lin Xun's smile abruptly froze. He was no longer swept up in anything. He was practically ready to cause a scene right here.

chapters.title: Fun
chapters.content:
The next morning, Jiang Qing set his own alarm clock.

Lin Xun was noticeably taken aback, with a faint sour note in his voice. "You're this excited to go out with Gao Yuanqiao?"

"That's not it. I just don't want to hear you waking up screaming anymore."

Lin Xun raised an eyebrow. "Screaming what?"

"That came out wrong! Never mind!" Jiang Qing set the breakfast down in front of him with some force, and pressed two glasses of fresh juice alongside it.

"If you want to hear it, I can. I imagine it would sound quite nice."

Jiang Qing gave him a languid look and smiled pleasantly. "Go ahead then. Let me hear it."

"It has to be done in bed to have any effect." Lin Xun said without a flicker of embarrassment, and then his eyes curved. "Your voice is quite nice, actually."

"Get out of my sight."

Gao Yuanqiao was renting his own place now. He had previously lived in company housing, with occasional stays at Bai Bangnan's, but now that he was terminating the contract, he had found a one-room apartment. The place was spotless.

When Jiang Qing and Lin Xun arrived at the address, they found him looking haggard, with deeper shadows under his eyes, and the genuine light that had once been in them gone. He was barely recognizable from the person they had seen a month ago.

"I've had nothing to do during the day so I've just been cleaning." Gao Yuanqiao led them inside.

The apartment had nothing much to see, so the three of them moved on to discussing where to go.

Gao Yuanqiao sat to one side and listened quietly, nodding at everything.

Lin Xun looked at him and suggested, "Racing?"

Jiang Qing's eyes lit up. Gao Yuanqiao slowly lifted his head.

"Alright, leave it to me. I'll arrange everything for today." Lin Xun took the two of them to a racing club, calling ahead on the way. There was no competition on today, and they had the whole place to themselves.

When they arrived at the club, the only people there were a handful of staff and one car.

"Get in." Lin Xun took Gao Yuanqiao to change into a racing suit, then tossed him the helmet.

Gao Yuanqiao looked at the car, steeled himself, and without thinking twice, climbed in.

The moment the engine turned over, he screamed. "AHHH WE'RE GOING TO DIE AHHHHH!"

The corner of Lin Xun's mouth curved, and he picked up speed, hurtling around the track. He raised his voice over the noise. "Scream all you want. I need to concentrate, I can't hear what you're saying!"

"AHHHHHH!" Gao Yuanqiao squeezed his eyes shut in terror, feeling as if his whole body were about to become airborne. His mind started to go completely blank with the speed, until there was nothing left but the raw sensation of being alive or not.

"BAI BANGNAN YOU SON OF A @#$%! AHHHHHH!"

"CRYING I AM GOING TO MAKE MY COMEBACK AHHHHHHHH!"

"This is insane oh my god I think I'm going to die of fright, my heart won't stop!"

"I THINK I'M HAVING A CARDIAC EVENT AHHHHH!"

Jiang Qing sat up in the viewing stand and watched the car weave through different lanes.

With no other vehicles around, Lin Xun drove with particular showmanship. Every time he swung past the viewing stand, he put on a dazzling display of moves that had Gao Yuanqiao nearly wetting himself.

Jiang Qing, however, found it thrilling to watch. He leaned over the railing and waved at them with enthusiasm.

The more enthusiastically he waved, the faster the car went, and the louder Gao Yuanqiao's yelling got.

In the end, Gao Yuanqiao had to be helped out of the car, sinking to his knees at the door. Lin Xun held him up and walked him back to the spectator area.

Jiang Qing saw his pathetic state and doubled over laughing.

Lin Xun handed Gao Yuanqiao a bottle of water, then turned to look at Jiang Qing. "Want to have a go yourself?"

Jiang Qing immediately lost his nerve. The laughter froze on his face.

"You're scared?" Lin Xun asked.

Jiang Qing looked at him for a long moment, then pressed his lips together. "Yeah. I am."

"You're not." Lin Xun walked over beside him, and ruffled his hair. "I've been driving for fifteen years, and I've competed in rally races. I've never had an incident. Trust me."

Jiang Qing looked at him sideways, and after a moment asked, "Then why did you never win?"

"...... Interesting question." Lin Xun said with a smile and explained, "Because my family didn't want me racing. I could only enter secretly, and then I'd deliberately not place. Come on."

Jiang Qing was still tangled up in the decision, and before he had reached any conclusion, Lin Xun had naturally taken him by the wrist and was already walking toward the car.

He glanced down at the hand, said nothing more, and fell into step. His mood had gone a little heavy, so much so that he didn't even notice the other person had quietly taken hold of his hand.

Lin Xun walked very slowly, a faint sweat gathering in his palm. He glanced back at their joined hands, and didn't want to let go.

"Let's go get changed first." Lin Xun steered him into the changing room.

About fifteen minutes later, Jiang Qing shuffled out, and at finding Lin Xun looking over at him, touched the back of his head awkwardly and muttered to himself, "Fits alright."

Lin Xun studied him for a moment, and said, "It fits. Looks good. Very sharp."

"Please." Jiang Qing pretended to be unimpressed as he turned away, but couldn't quite stop his mouth from curving, and felt a sudden surge of spirit. "Right, let's go for it."

Once in the car, a trace of nerves returned. "Actually, maybe keep it slow."

"Okay." Lin Xun, noticing that Jiang Qing consistently found high speeds alarming, drove carefully.

A few minutes later, Jiang Qing couldn't hold back. "This is way too slow! Look, that snail just made it to the finish line! Is this even a race car? This is a snail race!"

Lin Xun smiled and began to gradually build speed, letting the other person adjust gradually, until they were already into sharp-turn drifts.

"Oh my god, this is incredible!!!" Jiang Qing got completely swept up in the exhilaration, forgetting his fear entirely. "Lin Xun you're amazing! This is so cool!"

The corner of Lin Xun's mouth practically reached his temple. He felt wonderful all over, and started humming a song.

Getting out of the car, Jiang Qing was in slightly better shape than Gao Yuanqiao, though he did go down on one knee.

Lin Xun very "thoughtfully" moved in to help him up, nearly half-embracing him, every nerve in his body strung tight, afraid that if he pushed it even slightly the wire might snap.

Once Jiang Qing had recovered, he was just about to pull free, then decided having someone to lean on wasn't bad, and said nothing.

Gao Yuanqiao, fully rested by now, saw their posture and laughed with payback-level satisfaction. "Ha! Senior, you're worse than me."

"Oh please." Jiang Qing immediately pushed away his human crutch and struck the pose of a heroic champion. "Nonsense. I'm rock solid."

Lin Xun shot Gao Yuanqiao a deeply aggrieved look.

Gao Yuanqiao: ?

While changing back into their clothes, Jiang Qing spotted two caps sitting on a table, took a photo, and posted it to his Weibo burner.

@Ponytail Boy: Good mood, except for a certain sneaky little so-and-so. [image]

After everyone had wound down, Gao Yuanqiao felt considerably lighter, and followed them to the next destination.

Jiang Qing had no idea where they were going and was simply letting himself be led. This kind of no-brainer outing was the best kind!

Half an hour later, Jiang Qing and Gao Yuanqiao stood inside a live-fire shooting range, both looking completely blank.

Lin Xun brought over an instructor to walk them through loading, target acquisition, shooting, and safety.

Gao Yuanqiao held the gun, and every trace of his despondent moping vanished. All he wanted to do right now was shoot targets. One shot, one heartless scumbag!

Jiang Qing had handled guns before. He'd done a stretch of specialized training for a previous production. But seeing Gao Yuanqiao's intense enthusiasm to learn, he stayed along and listened to the instructor for a bit longer.

Out of the corner of his eye he noticed Lin Xun observing from the side, and threw out a challenge. "Let's see who does better."

"Sure." Lin Xun picked his gun, and the two of them stood in adjacent stalls, standing straight and tall, holding the weapons with proper form. Even the instructor couldn't help calling out in appreciation.

A series of shots rang out, one after another. A few minutes later, Jiang Qing looked at his result. 9.8 rings. He was satisfied with that.

Lin Xun finished his last round and didn't even look at his own score, going directly to the stall beside him to check Jiang Qing's result, then leaned against the doorframe and said with a smile, "You handle a gun well, handsome."

"......" Jiang Qing shot him an exasperated look, looked back down and turned the gun over, and felt his ears inexplicably warm.

Then he heard the instructor call out Lin Xun's score. Ten rings. Perfect.

"Right, you win." Jiang Qing said in irritated defeat, removing his ear protection and safety glasses.

Barely had the words left his mouth when a burst of rapid, indiscriminate gunfire sounded from nearby, and he flinched involuntarily, a shoulder shudder running through him.

At that moment, two hands reached over and covered his ears, warm and gentle.

The shooting range was loud, but through it all he heard clearly the other person say quietly, "It's alright."

The noise went on for a while. He stood where he was, looking at the person in front of him with a quiet, open smile, meeting his eyes. He unconsciously reached out and took hold of Lin Xun's wrist, not quite sure what he was thinking.

When the sound stopped, he removed Lin Xun's hands, and asked, "Do you think I'm very timid?"

"Aren't you?" Lin Xun, while genuinely fond of the way the other person pushed through everything with a brave face, also hoped he could be honest about it. "We're friends. So what if you're timid? Friends are the kind of people who can put up with each other's rough edges."

Jiang Qing pursed his lips. He found those words a little saccharine, and the toe of his shoe scraped at the floor, accidentally landing on Lin Xun's foot, and he went ahead and pressed down lightly, and didn't lift it until he'd left a clean shoe print on the spotless surface.

Lin Xun laughed quietly.

"AHHHH Senior, I missed the entire target!" Gao Yuanqiao let out a wail, snapping Jiang Qing out of it and giving him the perfect cover to slip away.

He took the opportunity to deliver a scathing remark. "You're hopeless. I hit 9.8 rings."

"Senior you're incredible! I'm so bad at this! I need more practice!"

Lin Xun watched the person make his quick retreat, then looked down at the shoe print, and did not wipe it away. Instead, he went to have a word with the instructor, making sure to give Gao Yuanqiao a thorough "education" later.

Serves that kid right for ruining a perfectly good moment.

After that they played archery and darts in other areas of the range. By the end of the day, Gao Yuanqiao's mood had gradually lifted. The intense activities had given his emotions somewhere to go, and after a full day of physical exertion, he now just wanted to find somewhere to rest.

Going out to dinner with three people was a little inconvenient, too easy to be photographed. So Lin Xun simply took them back to Yi Shui Bay and cooked himself.

On the way back, Jiang Qing received an unexpected call.

"Hey, Lao Jiang, it's Lao Yu." Yu Minghan said on the other end with the easy familiarity of someone they'd been friends with for years. "I'm in your complex, but I don't know your unit number. Come get me!" He hung up without giving him a chance to respond.

Jiang Qing: "......"

Lin Xun asked, "Who was that?"

"Yu Minghan. Says he's in our complex."

"..........!" Lin Xun's covert nemesis list had now added a second name to join Gao Yuanqiao. "What's he here for? How did he find the place? The security is clearly inadequate. To be safe, we should move as soon as possible."

Jiang Qing: "......?"

We?

In the back seat, impoverished Gao Yuanqiao shed a single tear of admiration. People who could casually say "let's just move to a bigger place" and mean it were truly something else.

He had no business being in this car. He should be underneath it.

The car pulled into the complex, and there was Yu Minghan, sitting cross-legged on a garden stone planter, earphones in, projecting studied nonchalance.

Jiang Qing got out of the car and flicked a few coins in front of him.

"Thank you for the tip, handsome. In return, this young man has nothing to offer but himself." Yu Minghan scooped up the coins in a flash and batted his lashes at him.

Lin Xun, who had followed right behind, watched this scene and had a strong impulse to poke both of his eyes out on the spot.

"What are you doing here? How did you find the place?" Jiang Qing asked.

"After you two caused such a ruckus last night, how could I miss out? I had someone look into it, and then bribed a little girl in the complex to let me in. Ha ha." Yu Minghan's hand shot out toward Jiang Qing's shoulder, but his arm was seized with considerable force before it could land. He winced visibly.

He turned around. It was Lin Xun.

"Ow, hey! That hurt!"

"Were you born without bones?" Lin Xun said flatly, and took Jiang Qing by the arm to walk forward.

"Hey hey, what are you two doing." Jiang Qing, walking ahead, had no idea what was happening behind him and just followed the pace.

"Fine, I'll let it go this once, given that you've got money too!" Yu Minghan grumbled at the air and gave it a petty kick, then suddenly noticed there was a straggler tagging along behind, and doubled back, crossing his arms and pushing his face close to inspect the newcomer. He recognized the person immediately.

"It's you. The one who stole our endorsement."

Gao Yuanqiao shrank back instinctively and said with an awkward smile, "Hi... hi."

"What's this, just some weakling. How did you even manage to steal our endorsement." Yu Minghan ran a hand through his hair with effortless swagger, and with nowhere else to put his hand dropped the full weight of it on Gao Yuanqiao's shoulder, bullying him by loading every bit of that weight onto him.
